cards.formal: For a probabilistic abstract rewriting system on a countable set, do almost-sure termination from every state under every reduction strategy and ordinary local confluence of the lifted multidistribution relation imply that all reductions from the same state have the same limiting distribution on normal forms?
cards.why: This asks for a probabilistic counterpart of a fundamental normalization principle.

cards.title: Fully abstract game semantics for pure call-by-value
cards.formal: Editorial effective arena-model variant: does the pure untyped call-by-value lambda calculus admit a compositional game interpretation satisfying the arena, effectiveness and interaction requirements below, whose equality of complete-play denotations is exactly termination-based contextual equivalence?
cards.why: Full abstraction would align a structured semantic model exactly with observable program behavior.

cards.title: Finite algebraic axiomatization of full guarded KAT
cards.formal: Does guarded Kleene algebra with tests admit a finite sound and complete algebraic calculus of the fixed-arity kind specified below for equality of guarded-string languages, uniformly over all finite sets of primitive actions and tests?
cards.why: A finite axiomatization would give a compact proof theory for structured program equivalence.

cards.title: Decidability of the infinite target discounted-sum problem
cards.formal: Is there an algorithm which, on any rational inputs \(0<\lambda<1\) and a,b,t, terminates and decides whether there exists an infinite sequence \(w\in\{a,b\}^{\mathbb N}\) satisfying \(\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}w_i\lambda^i=t\)?
cards.why: This elementary-looking arithmetic existence question is a barrier in discounted quantitative verification.

cards.title: Decidability of subsequence constraints with regular domains
cards.formal: For each fixed finite alphabet \(A\), consider the following decision problem. An input consists of a finite set \(X\) of variables, one regular expression \(r_x\) over \(A\) for every \(x\in X\), and a finite list \(C\) of constraints \(x\preceq y_1\cdots y_k\), where \(x,y_i\in X\) and \(k\ge0\). Does there exist, for every fixed \(A\), a deterministic Turing machine that halts on every such input and decides whether there is an assignment \(h:X\to A^*\) satisfying \[h(x)\in L(r_x)\quad(x\in X),\qquad h(x)\preceq h(y_1)\cdots h(y_k)\quad((x\preceq y_1\cdots y_k)\in C)?\] The same variable may occur repeatedly, and the directed dependencies between variables may contain arbitrary cycles.
cards.why: This question isolates the effect of cyclic reuse of unknown strings in a small constraint language. Regular domains and ordered concatenation are basic operations in string analysis, while subsequence constraints model loss of letters. A resolution would identify whether these ingredients alone retain effective satisfiability testing, clarifying a boundary obscured by undecidability results for richer interfaces.

cards.title: Decidability of termination for one left- and right-linear term rule
cards.formal: Is there an algorithm that, given one first-order rewrite rule \(\ell\to r\) over a finite ranked signature, with both \(\ell\) and \(r\) linear, decides whether its unrestricted rewrite relation terminates on every finite term?
cards.why: The problem asks whether simultaneous linearity of the two sides imposes enough structure to make global termination decidable for a single rule. It probes how little rewrite syntax can already encode unbounded computation, beyond the established left-linear and string-only boundaries.

cards.title: Relative completeness of Kleene induction for the positive calculus of relations
cards.formal: Is every equation valid in binary relations with union, intersection, composition, converse, constants \(0,1,\top\), and reflexive-transitive closure derivable from all valid closure-free equations in these operations together with the Kleene algebra axioms and induction rules specified below?
cards.why: This asks whether standard induction for iteration remains complete when programs can also be intersected and reversed as binary relations. A positive theorem would give a principled relative proof calculus for graph reachability expressions; a negative result would isolate an additional law of relational iteration.

cards.title: Exact multi-objective LTL achievability in stochastic games
cards.formal: Is exact multi-objective probabilistic LTL achievability decidable for finite full-observation turn-based stochastic games? Given such a rational game \(G\) with initial state \(s_0\), a finite list of LTL formulas \(\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_m\), and rational thresholds \(p_i\in[0,1]\), decide whether \[\exists\sigma\ \forall\tau\ \forall i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:\quad \Pr_{G,s_0}^{\sigma,\tau}(\varphi_i)\ge p_i.\] Both players may use arbitrary randomized strategies with unbounded history dependence. One deterministic algorithm must halt with the exact answer on every input. This is the decision target selected by the user on 16 September 2026 from the source's broader synthesis question.
cards.why: A controller often has several probabilistic requirements, such as reliability and eventual response, that must hold under the same policy against an adversarial environment. Exact achievability asks whether the stated requirements can all be guaranteed, including boundary thresholds that approximation alone may not decide. It is a central decision component of quantitative synthesis for stochastic systems.

cards.title: Decidability of weak bisimulation for normed BPA
cards.formal: Is there a deterministic Turing machine that, given any finite normed Basic Process Algebra system \(\Gamma\) and two finite process words \(\alpha,\beta\), always halts and decides whether \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are weakly bisimilar in the transition system generated by \(\Gamma\)? The equivalence is divergence-insensitive weak bisimilarity, with arbitrary finite sequences of silent transitions allowed before and after an observable transition, as defined below.
cards.why: Weak bisimilarity expresses that two recursive sequential systems can match every observable interaction while hiding internal computation. Normed BPA is a particularly small infinite-state model: a finite collection of rewrite rules acts on a sequential stack of variables, each able to terminate. Resolving this question would determine whether invisible computation alone defeats exact behavioral comparison in that model, beyond the related equivalences already known to be decidable.

cards.title: Decidability of restricted elementary real functions
cards.formal: Is the joint first-order truth problem for \(\mathcal R_0\) and \(\mathcal R_1\) decidable, where \(\mathcal R_0=(\mathbb R;0,1,+,-,\times,<,\mathrm{rexp},\mathrm{rsin},\mathrm{rcos})\) and \(\mathcal R_1\) additionally includes the unrestricted real exponential \(\exp\)? The three restricted functions agree with exponential, sine and cosine on the closed interval \([0,1]\), and equal zero outside it. Precisely, does one ordinary deterministic Turing machine halt on every pair \((b,\varphi)\), with \(b\in\{0,1\}\) and \(\varphi\) a first-order sentence in the corresponding language, and correctly decide whether \(\mathcal R_b\models\varphi\), without any unproved number-theoretic hypothesis or oracle?
cards.why: Real polynomial constraints admit exact decision procedures, while analytic functions can express descriptions needed for continuous-system verification. Determining whether the same kind of unconditional symbolic reasoning is possible for these restricted elementary operations would clarify the computational boundary of that extension. The problem concerns exact truth with arbitrary quantifier alternation, beyond numerical approximations to individual function values.

cards.title: Polynomial-time equivalence of free binary decision diagrams
cards.formal: Does there exist a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for equivalence of two explicitly given free binary decision diagrams? In full quantifiers, are there a deterministic Turing machine \(M\), constants \(C>0\) and \(k\in\mathbb N\) such that for every valid pair \((B_1,B_2)\), of total binary encoding length \(L\), the machine halts within \(C(L+1)^k\) steps and returns YES exactly when \[\forall a:X\to\{0,1\},\qquad f_{B_1}(a)=f_{B_2}(a),\] where \(X\) is the union of the variable labels appearing in the two inputs? No shared variable order is promised.
cards.why: FBDDs allow different branches to choose different variable orders and can be much more compact than ordered diagrams. Reliable equivalence testing is needed to compare independently compiled representations or optimized versions of a Boolean function. The question asks whether that representational flexibility can coexist with deterministic exact polynomial-time comparison, beyond the known randomized guarantee.

cards.title: Unconditional decidability of exact time-bounded CTMDP reachability
cards.formal: Is there an unconditional terminating algorithm that, for every finite rational-rate continuous-time Markov decision process with an absorbing state \(\mathrm{good}\), rational deadline \(T>0\) and rational threshold vector \(r\), decides whether \[\forall s\in\{1,\ldots,n\},\quad \sup_{\pi\in\Pi_T}\Pr_s^\pi[\text{reach }\mathrm{good}\text{ by time }T]>r_s,\] where \(\Pi_T\) consists of the measurable timed positional policies defined below?
cards.why: Settle a foundational exact-verification question for continuous-time controlled stochastic systems.

cards.title: Craig interpolation for Gödel logic with function symbols
cards.formal: In first-order Gödel logic over [0,1], without built-in equality and allowing function symbols, does every pair of sentences phi,psi with \(\varphi\models_1\psi\) admit a sentence theta in their common nonlogical vocabulary such that \(\varphi\models_1\theta\) and \(\theta\models_1\psi\)?
cards.why: The question asks whether common vocabulary still suffices to explain entailment once functions enter a many-valued logic.

cards.title: Perpetual reduction for the \(\lambda\sigma\) calculus
cards.formal: Editorial precise variant: does the untyped basic \(\lambda\sigma\) rewrite system specified below admit a total computable one-step strategy which follows an infinite reduction from every term that admits any infinite reduction?
cards.why: A perpetual strategy would expose nontermination in a foundational calculus of explicit substitution.

cards.title: Polynomial-time complementation of d-DNNFs
cards.formal:
Is there a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, given any d-DNNF circuit \(C\), outputs a d-DNNF circuit \(D\) over the same variables such that
\[\forall a:X\to\{0,1\},\qquad f_D(a)=1-f_C(a)?\]
The runtime is measured in the explicit binary input encoding and includes writing the entire output. The output may use different decompositions and share subcircuits arbitrarily, subject to the same d-DNNF conditions. It may omit irrelevant input variables, but may not introduce new variables, quantifiers or negation gates above leaves.

One uniform algorithm and one polynomial bound must work for all input sizes and all promised circuits. This is a construction question, distinct from the nonconstructive polynomial-size closure question.
cards.why: Complementation is a basic operation needed to reuse a compiled Boolean representation for exceptions, exclusions and opposite events. General d-DNNFs support useful counting and reasoning tasks, but it is unknown whether this logical transformation can always preserve their computational advantages with polynomial overhead. Resolving the construction question would clarify which operations can be performed directly on this succinct representation.

cards.title: Linear-length witnesses for reachability in each fixed vector addition system
cards.formal: For every integer \(d\geq1\) and finite set \(V\subseteq\mathbb Z^d\), does there exist a constant \(C_V\geq1\) such that every reachable pair \(s,t\in\mathbb N^d\) has a run of length at most \(C_V(\|s\|_1+\|t\|_1)\)?
cards.why: The conjecture isolates whether unbounded shortest-run growth is caused by changing the transition system or can already occur within one fixed system. This structural distinction is fundamental for understanding the complexity of reachability when only numerical configurations vary.

cards.title: Computable one-step normalization for finite confluent term rewriting
cards.formal: Does every finite, full, confluent first-order term-rewriting system \(R\) have a total computable one-step strategy \(F_R\) that reaches a normal form from every term having a normal form? The strategy depends only on the current term, may depend on the whole fixed system \(R\), and must also return a step on terms that have no normal form.
cards.why: This asks whether semantic uniqueness of outcomes guarantees an effective local way to reach an outcome whenever one exists. It isolates the interaction of confluence, finite syntax and memory-free evaluation beyond familiar orthogonal rewriting models.

cards.title: Elementary-time reachability for one-dimensional grammar-controlled VAS
cards.formal: Can reachability for one-dimensional grammar-controlled vector addition systems be decided in elementary deterministic time? More explicitly, do there exist fixed integers \(h\geq0\), \(c\geq1\) and one deterministic Turing machine deciding every instance of bit length \(n\) within \(O(e_h(n^c+c))\) steps, where \(e_0(z)=z\) and \(e_{j+1}(z)=2^{e_j(z)}\)?
cards.why: This asks whether one nonnegative counter interacting with context-free control can still be analyzed within a fixed-height exponential time bound. It separates existence of a decision algorithm from a meaningful complexity boundary and tests whether enormous reachable sets force equally enormous decision time.

cards.title: Polynomial-time recognition of abelian cores
cards.formal: Is there a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, given a finite algebra \(\mathbf A\) by full tables of its basic operations and promised that \(\mathbf A\) has an idempotent Taylor term, decides whether the core of \(\mathbf A\) is abelian? This selects the decision part of Theorem 3, whose quasipolynomial running time is the subject of the source’s open question.
cards.why: Measures the cost of recognizing algebraic structure that can make entire families of equation systems tractable. The question asks whether a useful structural classification can be found with polynomial preprocessing, rather than only being available as a theorem about each fixed algebra.

cards.title: Exponential witness bounds for three-dimensional VASS
cards.formal: Do there exist constants \(C,d\in\mathbb N\), with \(C,d\ge1\), such that every reachable instance \(I=(V,s,t)\) of a three-dimensional vector addition system with states has a legal run from \(s\) to \(t\) of length at most \[2^{C(L(I)+1)^d}?\] Here \(L(I)\) is the binary description size defined below, including the finite control graph, all transition updates, and both configurations. The constants must be independent of the instance. The target is the length of an actual sequence of transitions, not the size of a compressed representation of that sequence.
cards.why: Exact reachability in counter systems is decidable, but the length of the necessary witness can be vastly larger than the finite description. Dimension three is the first unresolved step beyond the exponential-witness theorem for binary two-counter systems. A positive result would yield a PSPACE upper bound for three-dimensional reachability and expose a strong structural limit on how much counter behavior finite control can force.

cards.title: Effective ultimate-positivity thresholds for simple recurrences
cards.formal: Is there a single deterministic Turing machine that, given any simple rational linear recurrence sequence \((u_n)_{n\ge0}\), always halts and returns either \(\mathrm{NO}\), meaning that the sequence is not ultimately nonnegative, or a natural number \(N\) satisfying \[\forall n\ge N,\qquad u_n\ge0?\] It must return \(\mathrm{NO}\) exactly when \(\forall N\in\mathbb N\ \exists n\ge N:u_n<0\). A valid natural-number output may be any sufficient threshold; it need not be the smallest one. The input recurrence length is unrestricted. Equivalently, because Ultimate Positivity for simple recurrences is already decidable, ask for a procedure that halts and outputs such a threshold on every ultimately nonnegative simple input, with no condition on other inputs.
cards.why: This problem isolates a precise gap between deciding an eventual property and computing a point after which it holds. An effective bound would make the exceptional prefix finite and accessible and would decide all-time Positivity for simple recurrences. The difference matters whenever an eventual mathematical guarantee must become an exact finite certificate about a concrete linear dynamical system.

cards.title: Effective prenex normalization for countable Gödel truth-value sets
cards.formal: Editorial conjecture variant of the classification question: for every countably infinite closed \(V\subseteq[0,1]\) containing 0 and 1, does Gödel logic over V admit a computable validity-preserving translation into its prenex fragment if and only if its set of valid sentences is arithmetical?
cards.why: A classification would explain when quantifier normalization remains algorithmically possible in many-valued semantics.

cards.title: Near-linear equivalence testing for propositional Horn theories
cards.formal: Can equivalence of two propositional Horn CNF formulas F and G be decided deterministically in \(O(N\log(N+2))\) time, where N is the total number of literal occurrences plus clause delimiters in their explicit input?
cards.why: A near-linear equivalence algorithm would make comparison of entire Horn consequence theories nearly as cheap as reading them.

cards.title: Cut elimination for \(\mu\mathrm{LK}_{p}^{+}\)
cards.formal: For every finite sequent Gamma, does derivability of \(\vdash\Gamma\) in the arithmetic calculus \(\mu\mathrm{LK}_p^+\) imply derivability of the same sequent using its rules with cut removed?
cards.why: Cut elimination would establish a fundamental proof-theoretic property of arithmetic with fixed points.

cards.title: A coanalytic upper bound for fair almost-sure termination
cards.formal: Does fair almost-sure termination for finitely branching probabilistic nondeterministic Turing machines admit a computable many-one reduction to well-foundedness of primitive-recursive trees on \(\mathbb N\)? That is, is there one total computable map sending each machine/input pair \((M,w)\) to such a tree \(T_{M,w}\) with \(M\) terminating with probability one under every fair scheduler exactly when \(T_{M,w}\) has no infinite branch?
cards.why: The target locates how much logical complexity fairness adds to probabilistic termination. A reduction to well-founded trees would connect general FAST reasoning to the established coanalytic framework; a negative answer would show that those certificates cannot cover this model through any computable translation.

cards.title: TOWER-hard reachability with seven nonnegative counters
cards.formal: Is reachability in unary-encoded seven-dimensional vector addition systems with states (7-VASS) \(\mathrm{TOWER}\)-hard under elementary-time many-one reductions?
cards.why: This seeks the dimension at which a small collection of nonnegative counters can already encode nonelementary computational difficulty. Reducing the eight-counter frontier would sharpen the low-dimensional boundary between tractable geometric behavior and extreme reachability complexity.

cards.title: Shortest runs in 3-D VASS
cards.formal: Is there no single-exponential bound on shortest runs in binary-encoded three-dimensional vector addition systems with states? Precisely, is it true that for every integer \(k\ge 1\), every real \(C>0\) and every \(N_{0}\ge 1\), there is a reachable instance I of encoding length \(N\ge N_{0}\) whose shortest source-to-target run has more than \(2^{C N^{k}}\) transitions?
cards.why: Isolates how much witness complexity three unbounded counters can force. Resolving the single-exponential threshold would clarify the gap between low-dimensional reachability and the much more expensive behavior possible when the number of counters grows.

cards.title: Exact finite-iteration reachability for Bellman operators
cards.formal: Is there an algorithm that, given a finite rational Markov decision process with no end components, its reachability Bellman operator \(\Phi:[0,1]^d\to[0,1]^d\), and rational vectors \(s,t\in[0,1]^d\), decides whether \(\Phi^n(s)=t\) for some integer \(n\geq0\)? The dimension is unbounded and several actions may be available, including several actions tight at the fixed point.
cards.why: Exact attainment is a sharper verification property than convergence of value iteration. Resolving it for Bellman operators would locate how much decidability survives the structured maxima of affine probability updates, beyond the already solved two-dimensional and single-policy cases.

cards.title: Decisiveness of static probabilistic Petri nets for finite targets
cards.formal: Is there a deterministic Turing machine that always halts and decides the following problem? The input is a finite Petri net with positive constant integer transition weights, an initial marking \(m_0\), and a finite explicitly listed set \(A\) of target markings. In the induced discrete-time Markov chain, let \(U_A\) consist of markings from which no marking in \(A\) is reachable by a finite sequence of enabled transitions. Decide whether \[\Pr_{m_0}\bigl[\exists n\in\mathbb N:\ M_n\in A\cup U_A\bigr]=1.\] This property is decisiveness from \(m_0\) with respect to \(A\). We retain the source's static-weight, finite-target question; its other, dynamic-weight variant is already resolved negatively and is described in the context.
cards.why: Decisiveness says that unresolved probability mass almost surely disappears: a run eventually either succeeds or enters a state from which success is impossible. This supports certified approximation of reachability probabilities in infinite-state systems. Deciding the property for ordinary constant-weight Petri nets would identify exactly when this general verification guarantee can be recognized from a finite concurrent-system description.

cards.title: Recognizing minimally false quantified formulas of fixed deficiency
cards.formal: Editorial tractability variant: for every fixed integer k≥2, is the language MF(k) of minimally false closed prenex CNF quantified Boolean formulas of raw deficiency k decidable in deterministic polynomial time?
cards.why: The target connects structural deficiency to the difficulty of recognizing minimal inconsistency under quantification.

cards.title: Decidability of the full alternating uniform one-dimensional fragment
cards.formal: Is satisfiability decidable for the full equality-free alternating uniform one-dimensional fragment AUF1 defined below, with arbitrarily many variables and arbitrary existential/universal alternation inside each permitted quantifier block?
cards.why: This asks whether a broad syntactic extension of a decidable logic retains an algorithmic satisfiability boundary.

cards.title: Cut elimination with digging in a linear modal fixed-point calculus
cards.formal: Editorial single-modality variant of the proposed digging extension: in the infinitary linear modal fixed-point calculus defined below, does every valid proof with cuts have a valid cut-free proof of the same end sequent?
cards.why: The question tests whether one proof-theoretic framework can encompass nested exponential structure as well as recursion.

cards.title: P versus NC
cards.formal: Is \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NC}\), where NC consists of decision languages recognized by logspace-uniform Boolean circuit families of polynomial size and polylogarithmic depth? Equivalently, does the Circuit Value Problem have such a circuit family?
cards.why: This asks whether a feasible computation can require intrinsically many sequential stages even when polynomially many processors are available. It is the central unresolved premise behind P-completeness as an explanation for resistance to parallelization, spanning graph algorithms, simulation, optimization, and language processing.

cards.title: Perfect matching in NC
cards.formal: Do there exist constants \(C,a,b>0\) and a logspace-uniform family of Boolean circuits which, on the adjacency matrix of every n-vertex simple undirected graph, output a perfect matching or correctly report that none exists, with at most \(C(n+2)^{a}\) gates and depth at most \(C(\log _{2}(n+2))^{b}\)?
cards.why: I include this because perfect matching is a basic polynomial-time graph problem for which randomization and parallelism interact in a particularly sharp way. The question asks whether randomness is needed to find globally compatible choices quickly, and whether the structural tools for odd cycles can be made as parallel as the algebraic ones.

cards.title: One-cycle versus two-cycles conjecture
cards.formal:
Is the following conjecture true? For every fixed sublinear local-memory exponent \(0<\delta<1\), every uniform randomized MPC algorithm \(A\) that distinguishes a single cycle of length \(n\) from two disjoint cycles of length \(n/2\), with high probability and linear total memory as specified below, requires \(\Omega(\log n)\) worst-case synchronous rounds. More precisely, for every fixed positive integer confidence parameter \(h\), there must be constants \(c_{A,h}>0\) and \(n_{A,h}\) such that
\[T_A(n,h)\ge c_{A,h}\log_2 n\]
for every even \(n\ge n_{A,h}\). Correctness has probability at least \(1-n^{-h}\) on each promised graph and every admissible initial placement of its edge list.
cards.why: I include this because the input removes most graph-theoretic complications and leaves the cost of assembling global connectivity information. It is a standard conditional-hardness benchmark for massively parallel algorithms, and a resolution would clarify whether limited memory creates an inherent logarithmic coordination cost even on degree-two graphs.

cards.title: Quantum 3-coloring of cycles in \(o(\log^{*}n)\) rounds
cards.formal:
Does there exist one uniform quantum-LOCAL protocol \(A\) and a function \(T:\mathbb N_{\ge3}\to\mathbb N\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge3\) and every injective identifier assignment \(\lambda:V(C_n)\to\{1,\ldots,n^2\}\), all nodes of the consistently oriented cycle \(C_n\) finish within \(T(n)\) communication rounds on every possible execution branch, and their classical outputs \(c_v\in\{1,2,3\}\) satisfy
\[
\Pr\bigl[\forall\{u,v\}\in E(C_n),\ c_u\ne c_v\bigr]\ge1-\frac1n,
\qquad
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{T(n)}{1+\log^{*}_2n}=0?
\]
The probability is over the protocol's quantum measurement outcomes. Initially the quantum state is a product of local zero states. Each node knows \(n\), its own identifier and the predecessor/successor ports, and communication in both directions is permitted.
cards.why: Cycle coloring is a basic distributed symmetry-breaking problem with a sharp classical locality threshold. Settling whether quantum communication beats that threshold would establish a concrete capability or limitation for coordinating neighboring processors with classical outputs.

cards.title: Directed reachability with nearly linear memory and polylogarithmic passes
cards.formal: Do there exist constants a,b,C and a uniform randomized streaming algorithm that decides directed s–t reachability on every n-vertex graph using at most \(Cn(\log (n+2))^{a}\) bits of memory and \(C(\log (n+2))^{b}\) passes, with success probability at least \(2/3\) for every adversarially ordered edge stream?
cards.why: Determine whether global directed reachability can be recovered from repeated sequential scans with only nearly linear memory, a central unresolved graph-streaming tradeoff.

cards.title: Polylogarithmic-space streaming Euclidean MST estimation
cards.formal:
Does there exist a uniform randomized one-pass insertion-only streaming algorithm A and absolute constants \(C\ge1\), \(K\ge1\) and integer \(k\ge1\) such that, for every \(n\ge2\), \(d\ge1\), \(\Delta\ge2\), and every stream of n distinct points in \(\{0,\ldots,\Delta\}^{d}\), A uses at most
\[K\bigl(d\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\lceil\log_2(\Delta+2)\rceil\bigr)^k\]
bits of working memory and returns a rational estimate Z satisfying
\[\Pr[\operatorname{MST}(X)\le Z\le C\operatorname{MST}(X)]\ge 2/3?\]
The stream order is arbitrary and fixed independently of the algorithm’s private random bits. The output estimates total Euclidean MST cost; it need not describe a tree. For polynomially bounded integer coordinates, the required space is \(\mathrm{poly}(d\log n)\), as in the community proposal.
cards.why: An MST measures the cost of connecting an entire geometric data set. A small summary that estimates this global quantity within a constant factor would clarify how much connectivity information survives a single streaming pass as dimension grows.

cards.title: Distributed Lovász Local Lemma in \(O(\log  \log  n)\) rounds
cards.formal: Does there exist an integer \(c\ge 2\) such that, for every fixed integer \(d\ge 2, a\) uniform randomized LOCAL algorithm \(A_{d}\) and a constant \(K_{d}\) solve every n-event variable Lovász Local Lemma instance of dependency degree at most d and maximum bad-event probability p with \(p\cdot d^{c}<1/2\), within \(K_{d}(1+\log _{2}\log _{2}(n+2))\) rounds, with probability at least \(1- n^{- 3}\) of avoiding all bad events simultaneously?
cards.why: The question asks whether sparse dependencies can always be resolved within a log-logarithmic communication radius under fixed polynomial slack. This would determine the complexity of a widely used distributed primitive and clarify a central scale in the LOCAL complexity hierarchy.

cards.title: Explicit superconstant lower bounds in the congested clique
cards.formal: Does there exist a Boolean predicate P of finite simple undirected graphs on \([n]\), decidable from the full adjacency matrix by one deterministic polynomial-time algorithm, such that every uniform deterministic unicast congested-clique algorithm computing P has worst-case round complexity \(R_{A}(n)=\omega (1)\)? Only node 1 is required to output the decision bit, and the input, bandwidth and limiting convention are fixed below.
cards.why: A central unbroken barrier in unconditional lower bounds for a powerful distributed model.

cards.title: Work-efficient parallel directed reachability
cards.formal:
Does directed single-source reachability admit nearly linear work and polylogarithmic depth simultaneously in the uniform randomized CREW PRAM model specified below? Precisely, is the following statement true?
\[
\forall c\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\ \exists A_c,K_c,a_c,b_c,q_c\ \forall n\ge2\ \forall G\ \forall s\in V(G),
\]
\[
\Pr\!\left[\begin{array}{l}
A_c(G,s)\text{ terminates with the exact reachability indicator,}\\
W\le K_c(n+m)L^{a_c}\ \text{and}\ D\le K_cL^{b_c}
\end{array}\right]\ge1-n^{-c},
\]
where \(G\) ranges over every directed graph on the labeled vertex set \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \(m=|E(G)|\), and \(L=\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\)? Here \(K_c\ge1\), \(a_c,b_c\ge0\) and \(q_c\ge3\) are integers independent of \(n,G,s\); \(A_c\) is one finite program independent of input size. The word length is \(q_cL\). The required event jointly bounds total work \(W\), depth \(D\), and correctness of the entire output on each fixed input. The confidence exponent is requested as a fixed constant before choosing the program. The one-vertex case has the prescribed output consisting of a single 1 and is omitted only to avoid a vacuous probability bound.
cards.why: Directed reachability is a basic graph operation with a linear-work sequential solution. The unresolved issue is whether its dependencies can be processed in polylogarithmic parallel time while retaining nearly that work bound on every input. A resolution would determine whether a fundamental sequential graph task admits efficient use of many processors, rather than a speedup purchased with polynomially more computation.

cards.title: Sublogarithmic distributed MIS
cards.formal:
Does there exist one uniform classical randomized LOCAL algorithm \(A\), taking a positive integer confidence parameter \(h\), such that for every fixed \(h\ge1\), on every \(n\)-vertex simple undirected graph with \(n\ge2\), its vertex outputs form a maximal independent set with probability at least \(1-n^{-h}\), and its worst-case elapsed round count \(T_A(n,h)\) satisfies
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{T_A(n,h)}{\log_2 n}=0?
\]
The guarantee ranges over all degrees, all valid distinct identifier assignments and all port numberings. Local computation, storage and message lengths are unrestricted; vertices have private random bits and may know \(n\) and the maximum degree.
cards.why: This isolates the communication needed for a basic symmetry-breaking task whose feasibility is easy to check locally. I include it because either outcome would change the benchmark for distributed graph algorithms: a faster algorithm would supply a stronger primitive, while a logarithmic lower bound would expose a substantial limitation of local coordination.

cards.title: Logarithmic-round deterministic maximal independent set
cards.formal:
Do there exist one uniform deterministic LOCAL algorithm \(A\) and an absolute constant \(C>0\) such that on every finite nonempty simple undirected graph with \(n\) vertices, and every valid identifier assignment and port numbering, all vertices output the membership bits of a maximal independent set within
\[C\log_2(n+2)\]
synchronous communication rounds? Vertices may know \(n\) and the maximum degree. No random bits are available, and the constant is independent of graph degree.
cards.why: This measures the quantitative cost of removing randomness from a basic distributed task. I include it separately from randomized sublogarithmic MIS because the algorithm must work against every identifier assignment with no failure probability. An \(O(\log  n)\) result would match the familiar randomized worst-case benchmark and propagate through reductions to other symmetry-breaking problems.

cards.title: Almost-linear-work parallel exact maximum flow
cards.formal:
For every fixed integer \(a\ge1\), do there exist one uniform randomized priority-CRCW PRAM algorithm \(A_a\), constants \(C_a\ge1\) and \(B_a\in\mathbb Z_{\ge a+3}\), and a function \(h_a:\mathbb Z_{\ge2}\to[1,\infty)\) with
\[
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log h_a(N)}{\log N}=0,
\]
such that the following holds? On every explicitly given directed graph with \(n\ge2\) vertices, \(m\) arcs, distinct terminals \(s,t\), and integral capacities \(0\le u_e\le n^a\), the algorithm outputs an exact integral maximum flow with probability at least \(2/3\), and every execution satisfies
\[
 W\le C_a(m+n)h_a(m+n),\qquad
 D\le C_a h_a(m+n).
\]
Here \(W\) is total work and \(D\) is parallel depth in the word model below. In asymptotic notation the requested simultaneous bounds are \((m+n)^{1+o(1)}\) work and \((m+n)^{o(1)}\) depth.
cards.why: This is a central unresolved parallelization problem for exact network optimization, asking whether near-optimal sequential work can coexist with subpolynomial dependence depth.

cards.title: Deterministic volume gap
cards.formal:
For every fixed locally checkable labeling problem \(\Pi\) on all finite graphs of some fixed maximum degree \(\Delta\), is the following implication true?
\[
\bigl[\exists\text{ correct deterministic VOLUME algorithm }A:\lim_{n\to\infty}V_A(n)/n=0\bigr]
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\bigl[\exists\text{ correct deterministic VOLUME algorithm }B\ \exists C>0\ \forall n\ge1:\ V_B(n)\le C(1+\log^* n)\bigr].
\]
The function \(V_A(n)\) is the largest number of distinct vertices visited to determine one requested output on an allowed input with at most \(n\) vertices. Algorithms know the exact size \(N\) of their input graph, and distinct vertex identifiers lie in \(\{1,\ldots,N^2\}\). The model and input class are defined below.
cards.why: This tests whether deterministic access to local solutions has only a tiny-information regime and an essentially global regime. Either outcome would substantially constrain the design and possible complexity classes of deterministic local computation algorithms.

cards.title: Optimal exact single-source shortest paths in CONGEST
cards.formal: For every fixed integer \(b\ge 1\), do there exist constants \(K,c>0\) and a uniform randomized CONGEST algorithm which, on every connected simple undirected graph with \(n\ge 2\) vertices, integer edge weights in \([0,n^{b}]\) and a designated source s, makes every vertex output its exact weighted distance from s in at most \(K(\sqrt{n}+D)(\log _{2}(n+2))^{c}\) rounds on every execution, with simultaneous correctness probability at least \(1- n^{- 3}\)? Here D is the diameter of the unweighted graph.
cards.why: This asks whether exact weighted shortest distances can be computed as quickly as the general communication lower bound permits, up to logarithmic factors. It separates the cost of exact optimization from the costs of network diameter and limited link bandwidth.

cards.title: Depth-first search in NC
cards.formal: Does there exist a logspace-uniform family of deterministic Boolean circuits of polynomial size and polylogarithmic depth that, on the adjacency matrix of every finite simple undirected graph, outputs a valid depth-first-search forest? The roots and the order of visiting neighbors may be chosen freely for each input.
cards.why: DFS is a basic graph structure whose standard construction has a long chain of sequential choices. Resolving this question would determine whether randomness can always be removed from its efficient parallel construction while retaining polynomial total resources.

cards.title: Two-dimensional sandpile prediction in NC
cards.formal: Is the language \(\mathrm{SP}_2\) defined below in logspace-uniform \(\mathrm{NC}\)? An instance explicitly supplies a finite stable rectangular array of sand grains and cells \(p,q\) inside that rectangle. Extend the array by zero to all of \(\mathbb Z^2\), add one grain at \(p\), and accept exactly when \(q\) eventually topples under the simultaneous four-neighbor rule. The question concerns one uniform circuit family with polynomial size and polylogarithmic depth for all input lengths.
cards.why: One extra grain can trigger a long deterministic cascade. Whether its eventual effect can always be computed in polylogarithmic parallel time is a canonical test of how much sequential dependence a simple physical process can express.

cards.title: Wait-free solvability of graph approximate agreement
cards.formal: For every finite nonempty connected simple undirected graph \(G\) and integer \(n\ge1\), define \(W(G,n)\in\{0,1\}\) to be \(1\) exactly when the \(n\)-process graph agreement task below has a deterministic wait-free solution using only atomic read/write registers, and \(0\) otherwise. Determine this solvability function on its entire domain. The benchmark accepts a real-valued function \(g\) with a Lean-checked proof that \[ \forall G\ \forall n\ge1:\quad |g(G,n)-W(G,n)|\le 1/100.\] A mathematically explicit necessary-and-sufficient characterization can specify \(g\); an algorithm deciding solvability from a graph is not additionally required.
cards.why: The question classifies which discrete relaxations of consensus can be implemented despite arbitrary process delays and crashes with the most basic shared-memory objects. Its full resolution connects the geometry of permitted output values with distributed computability, beyond separate algorithms and impossibility results for particular graph families.

cards.title: Lifting CSP sketching resistance to sublinear streaming resistance
cards.formal: For every finite family \(\Pi\) of Boolean predicates of a fixed arity, does the following implication hold? If no \(o(\sqrt n)\)-bit sketching algorithm nontrivially approximates Max-CSP(\(\Pi\)), then no \(o(n)\)-bit single-pass streaming algorithm nontrivially approximates it. Nontrivial approximation, sketching and the polynomial stream-length convention are defined below.
cards.why: A universal implication would upgrade a broad sketching classification to a fundamental limitation on all small-memory streaming algorithms. A counterexample would show that some CSPs admit an informative sequential summary even though every substantially smaller mergeable summary is approximation resistant.

cards.title: Optimal measurements and near-linear decoding for universal ℓ₂/ℓ₁ sparse recovery
cards.formal: Do there exist absolute constants \(C,B>0\), \(a\geq0\), and a deterministic recovery scheme such that, for every \(n\geq1\) and \(1\leq k\leq n\), one fixed matrix \(A_{n,k}\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) with \(m\leq Bk\log_2(en/k)\) permits recovery from \(A_{n,k}x\) in at most \(Bn\log_2^a(n+2)\) operations, with \[\|x-\widehat x\|_2\leq \frac{C}{\sqrt{k}}\min_{z:\,|\operatorname{supp}(z)|\leq k}\|x-z\|_1\] simultaneously for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\)?
cards.why: The target combines information-efficient sensing with fast, uniformly reliable reconstruction for arbitrary signals. Resolving it would show whether the strongest standard universal mixed-norm guarantee can be obtained without sacrificing near-optimal compression or practical asymptotic decoding time.

cards.title: Characterizing separable distances approximable in small streaming space
cards.formal: Characterize the functions \(\phi:\mathbb N_0^2\to\mathbb Q_{\geq0}\) in the domain below for which the separable dissimilarities \[d_\phi(f,g)=\sum_{i=1}^n\phi(f_i,g_i)\] admit arbitrarily accurate relative approximation by one-pass algorithms using space polynomial in \(\log(n+M+2)\) and \(1/\varepsilon\), under deletions that preserve nonnegative frequencies. Equivalently, determine the classification function \(\chi(\phi)\in\{0,1\}\), equal to one exactly for functions with such algorithms.
cards.why: A full classification would explain which local comparisons of large frequency vectors retain enough structure for accurate compression under deletions. It would connect individual distance estimators and impossibility results through a general mathematical criterion, including dissimilarities that are not norms or even metrics.

cards.title: Fast merging of summaries for symmetric streaming computations
cards.formal: Does every total, order-invariant Boolean stream function computable deterministically in polylogarithmic space and polylogarithmic time per item also admit a deterministic summary scheme with polylogarithmic message size, working space, and time per merge, correct for every binary merge tree? The uniform families, input lengths and costs in this question are specified below.
cards.why: Fast merging would allow any efficiently maintained order-independent statistic to be computed from independently processed pieces without an expensive reconstruction step. A separation would expose an inherent computational cost of parallel aggregation even when communication and memory are small.

cards.title: Wait-free exact FIFO queues in Common\(_{2}\)
cards.formal: For every fixed number \(n\ge 2\) of asynchronous processes, is there a deterministic wait-free linearizable implementation of an initially empty, unbounded FIFO queue using only atomic read/write registers and atomic Test&Set bits? Every process may perform both Enqueue and Dequeue, repeatedly and in any order. The implementation must satisfy exact FIFO semantics in every execution, including executions with arbitrary delays and crashes. This is the source’s Common\(_{2}\) question; “some objects with consensus number two” is not a free choice of base types that could include the desired queue itself.
cards.why: Would determine whether the familiar consensus-number-two primitives suffice for an exact queue with individual progress guarantees, clarifying the limitations of the consensus hierarchy as a guide to object implementation.

cards.title: Common2 membership of FIFO queues
cards.formal:
Is the following proposition true?
\[
\forall n\in\mathbb N,\ n\ge3\quad
\exists A_n:\quad A_n\text{ implements a linearizable wait-free FIFO queue for }n\text{ processes}
\]
using only the atomic read/write registers and one-shot test-and-set bits defined below? The queue is initially empty and has no capacity bound. Every process may perform arbitrarily many operations of either kind, with arbitrary finite binary strings as enqueued values. Each \(A_n\) is deterministic and has finite code; it may depend on \(n\). The quantifiers do not additionally require one compiler producing all \(A_n\).
cards.why: A queue orders work shared by concurrent processes. This question asks whether very weak synchronization suffices to guarantee that each continuing process finishes, even while others stop or interfere. It tests the distinction between consensus power and the ability to implement a reusable data type.

cards.title: One-pass approximation scheme for random-order streaming matching
cards.formal: For each \(0<\varepsilon\le1/2\), does there exist a one-pass random-order streaming algorithm returning a matching M with \(|M|\ge(1-\varepsilon)\nu(G)\) with probability at least 2/3, using at most \(C_\varepsilon n\log^c(n+2)\) bits of working space, for an absolute c and finite constants \(C_\varepsilon\)?
cards.why: The target asks how much random order can improve a severe streaming-memory constraint.

cards.title: LOCAL coloring below square-root degree dependence
cards.formal:
Do there exist a real constant \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)\), one uniform deterministic LOCAL algorithm \(A\), and a constant \(C>0\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge1\), every supplied integer degree bound \(\Delta\ge2\), and every finite simple undirected \(n\)-vertex graph of maximum degree at most \(\Delta\), the algorithm produces a proper vertex coloring with colors in \(\{1,\ldots,\Delta+1\}\) within
\[
C\bigl(\Delta^{1/2-\varepsilon}+\log^*n\bigr)
\]
synchronous communication rounds? The guarantee must hold for every assignment of distinct identifiers from \(\{1,\ldots,n^2\}\) and every local port numbering. All vertices know \(n\) and \(\Delta\); the same \(\varepsilon,A,C\) must work for all these inputs.
cards.why: I include this because the familiar greedy palette bound hides a distinct distributed coordination problem. A fixed improvement in the degree exponent would reveal new ways to resolve local conflicts, while an impossibility result would explain why the square-root dependence persists across different coloring methods.

cards.title: Randomized parity sketches versus one-way communication for XOR functions
cards.formal: Are there universal constants \(C>0\) and \(a\geq0\) such that, for every \(n\geq1\) and every Boolean function \(f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\{0,1\}\), \[R^{\mathrm{lin}}_{1/3}(f)\leq C\bigl(1+R^{\rightarrow}_{1/3}(f^+)\bigr)\log^a(n+2),\qquad f^+(x,y)=f(x+y)?\] Here the two complexities use worst-input error and shared randomness as defined below. This fixes the polylogarithmic-loss convention in the source’s conjecture.
cards.why: A positive result would justify proving lower bounds for arbitrary one-way XOR protocols by analyzing linear summaries, a much more structured class. A separation would identify Boolean information that a short nonlinear message preserves more effectively than nonadaptive random parities.

cards.title: Optimal one-pass randomized space for LIS length
cards.formal:
Determine, up to constant factors, the optimal randomized one-pass streaming space in bits for a factor-two estimate of the longest strictly increasing subsequence of a length-\(n\) sequence over \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\).

For every fixed input \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\{1,\ldots,n\}^n\), let
\[L(x)=\max\{r:\exists\,1\le i_1<\cdots<i_r\le n,\ x_{i_1}<\cdots<x_{i_r}\}.\]
An admissible algorithm reads \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) once in this order and, after the final item, outputs an integer \(\widehat L\) such that
\[\Pr\bigl[L(x)/2\le\widehat L\le L(x)\bigr]\ge2/3.\]
Find an explicit asymptotic function \(f(n)\) admitting a uniform algorithm with \(O(f(n))\) worst-case bit space and a matching \(\Omega(f(n))\) lower bound for every admissible randomized algorithm. Logarithmic factors are part of the requested answer.
cards.why: This problem tests whether randomness can substantially reduce the memory needed to retain ordered structure in a sequence. The large gap between what is known for deterministic algorithms and what is proved necessary for ordinary randomized algorithms makes it a basic unresolved question about one-pass computation.

cards.title: Full random walks with near-linear streaming space
cards.formal:
Can a randomized graph-streaming algorithm sample a whole \(L\)-step random walk, for every \(1\le L\le n\), with total-variation error at most \(1/100\), near-linear bit space and polylogarithmically many passes?

More precisely, do there exist one uniform algorithm \(A\), constants \(C_s,C_p>0\) and fixed nonnegative integers \(a,b\) with the following property? For every unweighted directed graph \(G\) on \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), every start \(s\), every \(1\le L\le n\) and every fixed ordering of its edges, \(A\), knowing \(n,L,s\) before reading the stream, uses at most
\[C_s n\bigl(\log_2(n+2)\bigr)^a\text{ bits and }\left\lceil C_p\bigl(\log_2(n+2)\bigr)^b\right\rceil\text{ passes}\]
and outputs a tuple \((Y_0,\ldots,Y_L)\) whose distribution \(\nu_{G,s,L}\) satisfies
\[\|\nu_{G,s,L}-\mu_{G,s,L}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le1/100?\]
Here \(\mu_{G,s,L}\) is the joint distribution of the ordinary directed random walk starting at \(s\), with the absorbing convention at a vertex of out-degree zero defined below.
cards.why: Random-walk sampling is a basic graph primitive, and this question asks whether its full trajectory can be recovered with both modest memory and few sequential scans. It isolates a gap between known constant-pass tradeoffs and the possibility of polylogarithmically many passes.

cards.title: Fault-adaptive Byzantine agreement at optimal resilience
cards.formal:
Does there exist a uniform deterministic synchronous protocol and an absolute constant \(C>0\) such that, for every integer \(t\ge0\), with \(n=2t+1\) named processes and trusted ideal signature setup as defined below, the protocol solves binary strong Byzantine agreement against every adaptive adversary corrupting at most \(t\) processes, and every execution with \(f\le t\) actual corruptions has total communication at most
\[
C\,n(f+1)
\]
words sent by processes while they follow the protocol? The protocol receives \(n,t\), identities and the setup, but not the eventual value of \(f\). The bound includes communication after a process decides. No bound on the number of rounds is imposed beyond eventual decision by every never-corrupted process.
cards.why: Worst-case quadratic communication can obscure much cheaper runs with few failures. This question asks for such savings all the way to the honest-majority resilience threshold, while preserving agreement and validity against adversarial behavior.

cards.title: Local certificate size versus verification radius
cards.formal: Determine the worst-case certificate-size function \[F(s,d)=\max\{c_d(P):P\text{ is a graph property and }c_1(P)\le s\},\qquad s\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0},\ d\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1},\] in the anonymous local-verification model defined below. Here \(c_d(P)\) is the minimum number of certificate bits per vertex permitting sound and complete verification of \(P\) at radius \(d\), uniformly over all finite graphs. This asks for the whole numerical tradeoff, with pointwise absolute accuracy \(1/100\), rather than only a yes-or-no answer to the source’s proposed inverse-radius scaling.
cards.why: Local certificates let every vertex check a global claim using a small neighborhood. Understanding their dependence on verification radius would distinguish properties for which additional communication reliably reduces stored proof information from properties that retain an irreducible local memory cost.

cards.title: Linear-round weighted APSP in CONGEST
cards.formal:
For every fixed integer \(b\ge1\), does there exist a uniform randomized CONGEST algorithm and a constant \(C_b\) that, on every connected simple undirected \(n\)-vertex graph with integer edge weights in \(\{0,\ldots,n^b\}\), outputs all exact weighted distances at their respective vertices within \(C_b n\) communication rounds, with probability at least \(2/3\) that all outputs are correct simultaneously?

The bound must hold on every execution, for all \(n\ge2\). “Linear” means \(O(n)\) with no factor growing with \(n\); a bound \(\widetilde O(n)=O(n\,\operatorname{polylog} n)\) does not meet the target.
cards.why: Exact APSP is a central global task in bandwidth-limited networks. Closing the remaining logarithmic gap would identify whether transmitting the necessary information is the only asymptotic obstacle, while respecting the established near-linear breakthrough rather than treating its older polynomial gap as open.

cards.title: Constant-round MIS in the congested clique
cards.formal: Does randomized maximal independent set admit a constant-round algorithm in the unicast Congested Clique? Precisely, for every fixed integer \(c\ge1\), do there exist a uniform randomized distributed algorithm \(A_c\) and positive constants \(R_c,B_c\) such that, on every simple undirected graph \(G\) with vertex set \([n]\), \(n\ge2\), the algorithm always terminates within \(R_c\) rounds, uses at most \(B_c\lceil\log_2 n\rceil\) bits per directed communication link per round, and outputs a maximal independent set with probability at least \(1-n^{-c}\)? Constants and program may depend on \(c\), but not on \(n\), the graph or its maximum degree.
cards.why: The question measures how much communication exact distributed symmetry breaking needs when every processor can directly contact every other processor. A constant-round solution would establish a sharp capability of this widely studied model. A general lower bound would expose a bandwidth limitation that survives unrestricted local computation and arbitrary global coordination.

cards.title: Linear-sketch complexity of the nuclear norm
cards.formal:
Determine the optimal number \(m_\varepsilon(n)\) of exact real linear measurements required to estimate the nuclear norm of an arbitrary real \(n\times n\) matrix with relative error at most \(\varepsilon\) and success probability at least \(2/3\), up to matching constant factors in \(n\), for every fixed \(0<\varepsilon<1\).

The sketch is randomized and chosen independently of the input matrix. It must satisfy, for every fixed \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\),
\[\Pr_\omega\!\left[(1-\varepsilon)\|A\|_*\le d_\omega(S_\omega A)\le(1+\varepsilon)\|A\|_*\right]\ge\frac23,\]
where \(S_\omega:\mathbb R^{n\times n}\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear and \(d_\omega\) is a decoder that receives only the sketch and the input-independent random choices. The quantity \(m_\varepsilon(n)\) is the smallest possible dimension \(m\).

Give an explicit asymptotic description \(g(n,\varepsilon)\) and prove that for every fixed \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) there exist \(0<c_\varepsilon\le C_\varepsilon<\infty\) and \(N_\varepsilon\) such that
\[c_\varepsilon g(n,\varepsilon)\le m_\varepsilon(n)\le C_\varepsilon g(n,\varepsilon)\qquad(n\ge N_\varepsilon).\]
The constants may depend on the fixed accuracy, but not on \(n\). Logarithmic factors in \(n\) must be resolved; determining only a polynomial exponent does not meet this target.
cards.why: Determining this complexity would explain whether summing singular values permits a materially smaller linear summary than storing a general matrix, and exactly how much compression is possible. It would also locate a central matrix norm within the sharply differing sketching behavior of the Schatten family.

cards.title: Subquadratic metric TSP cost estimation below factor two
cards.formal:
Do there exist an absolute constant \(\delta\in(0,1)\) and a classical randomized distance-query algorithm that estimates the minimum traveling-salesperson tour cost of every \(n\)-point metric within a factor \(2-\delta\), using \(o(n^2)\) distance queries?

For a metric \(d\) on \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with \(n\ge3\), define
\[\operatorname{TSP}(d)=\min_{\pi\in\mathfrak S_n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}d\bigl(\pi(j),\pi(j+1)\bigr),\qquad \pi(n+1)=\pi(1).\]
The algorithm knows \(n\) and can request \(d(i,j)\) for any chosen pair of labels. Its output \(Z\) must satisfy
\[\Pr\!\left[\operatorname{TSP}(d)\le Z\le(2-\delta)\operatorname{TSP}(d)\right]\ge\frac23\]
for every input metric. Only the number of oracle calls is bounded; the output is a cost estimate and need not describe a tour.
cards.why: This is a central test of how well a global optimization value can be estimated from incomplete metric information. Resolving it would determine whether the factor-two barrier is inherent to sparse distance access or reflects limitations of current estimators, with a sharp separation between learning a value and constructing a tour.

cards.title: Factor-two graph distances in logarithmically many passes
cards.formal:
Can a randomized streaming algorithm estimate the distance between two specified vertices of an undirected, unweighted graph within a factor of two using \(O(\log n)\) passes and \(O(n\operatorname{polylog}n)\) bits of memory?

More precisely, do there exist one uniform randomized algorithm \(A\), constants \(C_s,C_p>0\) and an integer \(k\ge0\) such that the following holds for every simple graph \(G\) on \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), every specified pair \(s,t\), and every ordering of its edges? The algorithm knows \(n,s,t\) before the stream begins, uses at most
\[C_s n\bigl(\log_2(n+2)\bigr)^k\text{ bits and }\left\lceil C_p\log_2(n+2)\right\rceil\text{ passes},\]
and, with probability at least \(2/3\), outputs \(D\) satisfying
\[d_G(s,t)\le D\le2d_G(s,t).\]
For disconnected \(s,t\), success means outputting the symbol \(\infty\). All passes read the same edge order.
cards.why: Shortest-path distance is a basic graph quantity whose global dependencies challenge small-memory sequential access. This question isolates the number of scans needed for a useful constant-factor estimate, between new near-logarithmic lower bounds and the best verified upper bounds.

cards.title: Constant-pass weighted matching with O(n log n) bits
cards.formal: For every fixed rational \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) and fixed integer \(c\geq1\), is there a randomized insertion-only streaming algorithm that, on every \(n\)-vertex simple undirected graph with integer edge weights in \([1,n^c]\), outputs a matching of weight at least \((1-\varepsilon)\operatorname{OPT}\) with probability at least \(2/3\), using at most \(p_{\varepsilon,c}\) passes and \(B_{\varepsilon,c}n\log_2(n+2)\) bits of memory, where \(p_{\varepsilon,c},B_{\varepsilon,c}\) do not depend on \(n\)?
cards.why: The question asks whether near-optimal weighted matchings can be found with memory comparable to the explicit output and a fixed number of scans of a dense graph. It isolates the remaining strict memory requirement from the already established existence of constant-pass algorithms with polylogarithmic overhead.

cards.title: Classification of robust chemical computation
cards.why: Chemical implementations often have uncertain reaction speeds. This question isolates what can be computed when every positive choice of fixed kinetic constants must lead to the same answer. A classification would distinguish robust computational content from behavior that depends on carefully selected reaction rates.

cards.title: Work-efficient parallel approximate flow
cards.formal:
Does at least one of the following two problems admit a uniform randomized parallel algorithm with nearly-linear work and polylogarithmic depth, in the precise regime below?

1. Edge-capacitated budgeted minimum-cost flow: given an undirected graph, terminals \(s,t\), edge capacities and nonnegative edge costs, and a total cost budget \(B\), output a feasible \(s\)-to-\(t\) flow whose value is at least \(\mathrm{OPT}/(1+\varepsilon)\), where \(\mathrm{OPT}\) is the largest flow value within both the capacities and budget.
2. Vertex-capacitated maximum flow: given an undirected graph, terminals \(s,t\), and vertex capacities, output a feasible \(s\)-to-\(t\) flow whose value is at least \(\mathrm{OPT}/(1+\varepsilon)\), where \(\mathrm{OPT}\) is the largest capacity-respecting value.

The assertion is a disjunction over the two entire problem classes. The algorithm may choose one class once and for all; choosing an easier alternative separately for each instance is not the assertion.
cards.why: A small depth bound makes an algorithm useful on many processors only when the total work also remains close to input size. The question asks whether cost budgets or vertex bottlenecks force an additional parallel cost for basic flow optimization. Its resolution would clarify the boundary between known efficient parallel flow primitives and more general constrained routing.

cards.title: One-pass semi-streaming depth-first search
cards.formal:
Does there exist one uniform randomized one-pass streaming algorithm and fixed constants \(C\ge1\), \(k\ge0\) that, for every connected simple undirected graph \(G\) on \(n\ge1\) vertices, outputs a depth-first-search spanning tree using at most
\[C n\bigl(\log_2(n+2)\bigr)^k\]
bits of working memory, with probability at least \(2/3\) for every ordering of its edge stream?

The stream lists each edge once, contains no deletions, and can only be scanned from beginning to end. The algorithm may choose the root and neighbor order of the DFS tree. The question concerns the memory and pass bounds, with no additional polynomial-time requirement.
cards.why: DFS is a basic graph decomposition tool whose required ancestor structure is stronger than connectivity or an arbitrary spanning tree. Resolving its one-pass feasibility would explain whether near-linear memory can retain enough information for this globally constrained traversal without revisiting edges.

cards.title: Optimal clique-detection rounds in CONGEST
cards.formal:
Determine the optimal randomized round complexity
\[
T_{\mathrm{det}}(n,\ell,b)
\]
of detecting an \(\ell\)-vertex clique in an \(n\)-vertex communication graph, when each directed use of an edge can carry \(b\) bits per round. The parameter domain is
\[
n\ge16,\qquad 4\le\ell\le\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor,\qquad b\ge1,
\]
with all three parameters integers.

The requested answer is an explicit asymptotic expression \(F(n,\ell,b)>0\) and absolute constants \(c,C>0\) such that, throughout this domain,
\[
cF(n,\ell,b)\le T_{\mathrm{det}}(n,\ell,b)
                 \le CF(n,\ell,b).
\]
The constants may not depend on \(n,\ell,b\). Polylogarithmic uncertainty is not sufficient. This full constant-factor target, rather than the historical question of whether a linear number of rounds is necessary, is the explicit user choice.
cards.why: A network can contain a dense local pattern without any one processor initially knowing all of its edges. The question measures how much communication is intrinsically needed merely to detect that pattern. Resolving the full parameter dependence would distinguish the cost of establishing existence from the cost of enumerating every occurrence.

cards.title: Register space of obstruction-free set agreement
cards.formal: For every integer pair \(n>k\ge1\), determine \(R(n,k)\), the minimum number of shared atomic read/write registers sufficient for deterministic obstruction-free one-shot \(k\)-set agreement among \(n\) named processes with input domain \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), in the model below. Supply a real-valued function approximating \(R\) with pointwise absolute error at most \(1/100\) registers throughout this domain.
cards.why: This measures how much shared memory is intrinsically needed for synchronization when processes may disagree on a bounded number of proposed values. Resolving the gap would connect the solvability of agreement tasks to their exact memory requirements, even under the weak guarantee of eventual progress in isolation.

cards.title: Bipartite maximal matching with polynomial-in-degree volume
cards.formal: Do there exist universal constants \(C>0\), \(k\in\mathbb N\) and one uniform deterministic local-query algorithm which, on every finite simple bipartite graph of maximum degree at most \(\Delta\), answers each vertex query after visiting at most \(C(\Delta+1)^k\) distinct vertices, such that all answers together specify one maximal matching? A proper two-coloring of the input graph is supplied. The bound has no dependence on the number \(n\) of graph vertices.
cards.why: This asks how much graph information is needed to answer a single matching query while remaining consistent with all other answers. A polynomial degree bound would give a deterministic local oracle for a basic graph primitive with cost independent of graph size. A superpolynomial lower bound would separate this information requirement from the known linear dependence on degree in communication rounds.

cards.title: Superlinear local certificates for hereditary graph classes
cards.formal:
Does there exist an isomorphism-invariant hereditary class \(\mathcal C\) of finite simple undirected graphs, with connected members of arbitrarily large order, and a fixed real exponent \(c>1\), such that every correct one-round proof-labeling scheme for membership in \(\mathcal C\) has worst-case certificate size \(\Omega(n^c)\) bits per vertex on connected \(n\)-vertex inputs?

More explicitly, for the optimal accepting-certificate size \(s_A(n)\) of a fixed correct local verifier \(A\), as defined below, require
\[\exists\mathcal C\;\exists c>1\;\forall A\text{ correct for }\mathcal C\;\exists a_A>0\;\exists N_A\;\forall n\ge N_A:\ s_A(n)\ge a_A n^c.\]
The exponent and graph class are common to all verifiers. This asks for a polynomial gap above linear certificate size, not merely for a bound that grows faster than \(n\).
cards.why: The question asks whether vertex-deletion stability imposes a fundamental information limit on distributed proofs. A polynomially superlinear example or a general obstruction would clarify how far local verification of structural graph properties can depart from the linear examples now known.

cards.title: Parallel sampling of planar perfect matchings
cards.formal:
Do there exist constants \(C,k\ge1\) and a uniform family of randomized Boolean circuits \((A_{n,t})_{n\ge0,t\ge1}\) that, for every simple unweighted planar graph \(G\) on \([n]\) with at least one perfect matching, output a distribution \(\mu_{G,t}\) satisfying
\[
d_{\mathrm{TV}}(\mu_{G,t},U_G)\le2^{-t},
\]
with circuit size at most \(C(n+2^t+2)^k\) and depth at most \(C(\log_2(n+2)+t)^k\)?
Here \(U_G\) is uniform over all perfect matchings of \(G\), and the complete input, output, uniformity and failure conventions are defined below. The same constants and uniform circuit generator must work for every graph and precision. This is the user-selected approximately uniform RNC sampling target.
cards.why: This is a concrete test of whether counting and sampling remain equivalent under strong parallel-time constraints. Planarity makes exact counting tractable, so the remaining issue isolates the cost of coordinating random choices rather than the hardness of evaluating the partition function. A resolution would clarify a central boundary in parallel randomized algorithms.

cards.title: Polynomial-in-optimum graph matching in \(\mathrm{AC}^{0}\)
cards.formal:
Do there exist constants \(c,\alpha>0\) and a DLOGTIME-uniform family of deterministic Boolean circuits \((C_n)_{n\ge1}\), of constant depth and polynomial size, such that every finite simple undirected graph \(G\) on \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) is mapped to a matching \(M(G)\subseteq E(G)\) satisfying
\[
|M(G)|\ \ge\ c\,\nu(G)^\alpha?
\]
Here \(\nu(G)\) is the maximum cardinality of a matching in \(G\). The same constants and circuit family must work for all \(n\) and all graphs. The output must identify the actual chosen edges. The scale \(c\,\nu^\alpha\), and the restriction to graph matching rather than general set packing, were explicitly selected by the user.
cards.why: A matching requires many output decisions to be mutually consistent: selected edges may not share vertices. This creates a concrete test of the constructive power of uniform constant-depth circuits. A resolution would clarify how much of combinatorial approximation survives when the number of sequential logical layers is bounded independently of input size.

cards.title: Deterministic linearizable objects for set agreement
cards.formal: Is it true that, for every pair of integers \(n>k>2\), no deterministic linearizable \((n,k)\)-set agreement object is computationally equivalent to the \((n,k)\)-set agreement task? The quantifier includes every proposal domain I with at least n values and every n-ported object satisfying the definitions below. Equivalence means mutual implementation with atomic read/write registers by deterministic wait-free algorithms. The object may depend on n,k and I, may use the chosen port in determining a response, and may be invoked repeatedly; it is not restricted to one call per port.
cards.why: Tests whether deterministic sequential semantics inevitably add coordination power to reusable set agreement objects, clarifying the relation between one-shot tasks and composable shared-memory abstractions.

cards.title: LOCAL lower bounds for 2-ruling sets
cards.formal:
Is it true that every randomized LOCAL algorithm \(A\) that computes a 2-ruling set on every \(n\)-vertex graph with global success probability at least \(1-1/n\), for all \(n\ge2\), has worst-case round complexity
\[
T_A(n)=\Omega\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log_2 n}{\log_2\log_2 n}}\right)?
\]
Precisely, the proposed assertion is that for every such \(A\) there are constants \(c_A>0\) and \(n_A\ge4\) such that the displayed lower bound with multiplier \(c_A\) holds for every integer \(n\ge n_A\). The maximum ranges over all simple graphs, legal identifier and port assignments, and random outcomes in the model below. No maximum-degree or arboricity restriction is imposed.
cards.why: The question tests how much a minimal relaxation of independence-based domination changes the locality of symmetry breaking. It separates the role of randomness, sparse structure and coverage radius from bandwidth restrictions, and would sharpen a central lower-bound boundary for distributed graph algorithms.

cards.title: Linear CONGEST lower bound with logarithmic LOCAL complexity
cards.formal: Do there exist a fixed maximum degree \(\Delta\), a locally checkable labeling problem \(\Pi\) on all connected simple graphs of maximum degree at most \(\Delta\), and a deterministic LOCAL algorithm solving \(\Pi\) in \(O(\log N)\) rounds, such that every randomized CONGEST algorithm solving \(\Pi\) with global failure probability at most \(1/N\) requires \(\Omega(N)\) worst-case rounds? The common size parameter \(N\ge2\) is known to every vertex, and each algorithm must meet its guarantee on every input with at most \(N\) vertices. Use the models and quantifiers below; no additional promise on the graph or input labels is allowed.
cards.why: Local verifiability limits what a problem can demand of a global solution, but it need not make that solution easy to construct with short messages. A logarithmic-versus-linear separation would show that bandwidth can cause a near-global delay even when graph distances and local verification permit a much faster solution. The requirement of one total bounded-degree LCL rules out explanations based on an arbitrary promise or an output whose size grows with the network.

cards.title: Maximum independent set in the congested clique
cards.formal: Determine, up to constant factors as \(n\to\infty\), the minimum worst-case round complexity \(T_{\mathrm{MaxIS}}(n)\) for computing an exact maximum independent set of an arbitrary simple undirected graph on \(n\) labelled vertices in the deterministic unicast congested clique defined below. The output is distributed: each processor outputs the membership bit of its own vertex in one common maximum independent set. Local computation and storage have no resource bound, but each local computation must terminate. Only synchronous communication rounds are charged.
cards.why: Exact independent set separates the cost of learning a global optimum from the cost of computing it once the input is known. The complete communication network removes distances and narrow cuts, yet each link still carries only logarithmically many bits. A tight characterization would identify whether this canonical optimization problem intrinsically requires substantially more information exchange than easier graph tasks in the same network. The circuit connections also make it a meaningful test of the limits of current distributed lower-bound methods.

cards.title: Streaming space for additive \(L_\infty\) estimation
cards.formal: Determine, up to universal constant factors, the optimal worst-case bit space for a one-pass randomized streaming algorithm that returns only an estimate \(z\) of \(\|f\|_\infty\), with \[\Pr\!\left[|z-\|f\|_\infty|\le\frac{\|f\|_p}{k}\right]\ge\frac23.\] The bound must describe its dependence on domain size \(n\ge2\), update budget \(M\ge2\), accuracy parameter \(k\ge4\), norm flag \(p\in\{1,2\}\), and update mode \(b\in\{\mathrm{insert},\mathrm{difference}\}\), in the model below.
cards.why: Separate the memory needed for one largest-magnitude estimate from the information needed to identify heavy coordinates, while accounting for error scale, domain size and cancellation.

cards.title: Breaking the quadratic color bound for bounded outdegree
cards.formal: Do there exist a constant \(\varepsilon \in\)(0,1], constants \(C_{1},C_{2}>0, a\) computable function \(f:\mathbb{N} _{+}\to \mathbb{N} _{+}\) and one deterministic LOCAL algorithm that, for every n-vertex graph supplied with an orientation of maximum outdegree at most \(\beta \ge 1\), computes a proper vertex coloring using at most \(\lceil C_{1}\beta ^{2- \varepsilon}\rceil\) colors within \(f(\beta )+C_{2}\log * n\) rounds?
cards.why: Would cross a basic locality barrier for coloring sparse oriented networks, making fewer colors achievable without paying global-size-dependent time beyond \(\log * n\).

cards.title: Polynomial-state protocols for Presburger arithmetic
cards.formal:
Do there exist positive integers \(C,k\) such that every Presburger formula \(\varphi(x_1,\ldots,x_d)\), including arbitrary nested quantifiers, has a leaderless pairwise population protocol \(P_\varphi\) with
\[
|Q_\varphi|\le C(1+|\varphi|)^k
\]
that computes its truth value on every input \(\mathbf a\in\mathbb N^d\) with \(\sum_i a_i\ge2\), reaching permanent unanimous agreement under every fair execution?
The size is that of the original quantified formula, using the syntax and encoding below. The constants are independent of the formula and population size. No running-time bound is required for constructing the protocol or for reaching consensus.
cards.why: The question compares the succinctness of logical descriptions with that of anonymous distributed computation. It asks whether quantifier compression forces an unavoidable increase in the number of local states, even when computation time is unrestricted. This separates representational power from synthesis and stabilization complexity.

cards.title: Subpolynomial detection of two-connected patterns
cards.formal: Does there exist a fixed finite simple 2-vertex-connected graph H, with at least three vertices, for which exact H-subgraph detection in the randomized CONGEST model can be solved in \(n^{o(1)}\) rounds on every n-vertex network? The pattern is fixed independently of n. Detection means that, with probability at least \(2/3\), every node outputs NO when the network contains no copy of H, and at least one node outputs YES when it does contain a copy.
cards.why: Asks whether any cyclic pattern can be detected almost as quickly as trees under per-edge communication limits. A resolution would clarify a broad boundary in distributed graph algorithms, and its negative direction includes the difficult triangle-detection barrier.

cards.title: Query complexity of the graph degree distribution
cards.formal:
Determine, up to universal constant factors, the function
\[
Q^\star(n,m,h,w)=
\inf_{A\in\mathcal A}\ 
\max_{G\in\mathcal G(n,m,h,w)}
\mathbb E[T_A(G)]
\]
on every feasible tuple defined below. Here \(\mathcal A\) consists of uniform randomized algorithms which receive only \(n\), access the graph through the three specified query types, and correctly estimate its entire complementary cumulative degree histogram with probability at least \(2/3\). The required simultaneous accuracy is
\[
\Pr\!\left[
\forall d\in\{1,\ldots,n-1\},\
\frac9{10}N_G\!\left(\frac{11}{10}d\right)
\le \widehat N(d)\le
\frac{11}{10}N_G\!\left(\frac9{10}d\right)
\right]\ge\frac23.
\]
The parameters \(m,h,w\) describe the graph on which cost is evaluated; their values, estimates and bounds are not supplied to the algorithm.
cards.why: The degree histogram distinguishes common low-degree vertices from rare hubs. Estimating its whole cumulative profile requires guarantees in the tail as well as where most vertices lie. A sharp query bound would identify which structural features permit reliable graph summaries with limited access.

cards.title: Two-stage group testing with arithmetic progressions
cards.formal:
Do there exist absolute constants \(C,D>0\) such that, for every pair of integers \(n\ge2\) and \(1\le k\le n\), an unknown set \(S\subseteq[n]\) with \(|S|\le k\) can be identified exactly by the following deterministic two-stage scheme?

The first stage uses at most \(Ck\log_2 n\) tests. Each test asks whether \(S\) meets a finite arithmetic progression contained in \([n]\), and every first-stage test is fixed before any answers are received. After seeing all first-stage answers, the second stage chooses at most \(Dk\) individual indices and learns their membership in \(S\). All second-stage indices must be chosen before receiving any second-stage answer. The final output must equal \(S\) for every admissible hidden set.

The constants must work simultaneously for all \(n,k,S\). The resource being bounded is the number of tests in each stage; neither constructing the scheme nor decoding the answers is subject to a running-time bound.
cards.why: This question tests how much measurement restrictions can cost in sparse identification even when one follow-up round is available. A resolution would distinguish what arbitrary pooling achieves from what regularly spaced queries can support, a distinction motivated by pattern matching rather than by a new statistical noise model.

cards.title: Strongly polynomial linear programming
cards.formal:
Does there exist one deterministic algorithm and fixed positive integers \(C,d,C',e\) with the following guarantee for every \(m,n\ge1\), \(A\in\mathbb Q^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb Q^m\) and \(c\in\mathbb Q^n\)? For the linear program
\[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x: x\in\mathbb R^n,\ Ax=b,\ x\ge0\},\]
the algorithm returns an exact rational optimal vector, or correctly reports infeasibility or an objective unbounded below.
