It uses at most \(C(m+n+1)^d\) elementary operations in the rational arithmetic model below, and every numerical value during the computation has binary encoding length at most \(C'(N+1)^e\), where \(N\) is the full input bit length. The same program and constants must work for all dimensions and coefficient values.
cards.why: Linear programming is a basic language for optimization across combinatorics, algorithms and applications. The question asks whether exact optimization needs a number of arithmetic decisions that grows with numerical precision, or whether the dimensions alone suffice. A positive answer would extend a central efficiency property of several combinatorial optimization problems to every rational linear program.

cards.title: Komlós conjecture
cards.formal: Is there a real constant \(C>0\) such that for every pair of integers \(m,n\ge1\) and every matrix \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) satisfying \(\sum_{i=1}^m A_{ij}^2\le1\) for each \(j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), there exists a single sign vector \(x\in\{-1,1\}^n\) for which \[\max_{1\le i\le m}\left|\sum_{j=1}^n A_{ij}x_j\right|\le C?\] The constant must be independent of both dimensions and all matrix entries.
cards.why: Komlós asks whether controlling the Euclidean size of each vector is enough to balance all coordinates by signs with a dimension-independent error. This is a central link between vector geometry and simultaneous rounding of linear constraints. It would imply the Beck–Fiala bound for sparse set systems and strengthen discrepancy-based guarantees in optimization.

cards.title: Nearly linear-time solution of general sparse linear systems
cards.formal:
For every fixed integer \(c\ge1\), do there exist a uniform randomized classical algorithm \(A_c\) and constants \(C_c,K_c\ge1\), \(d_c\ge0\), all integers, with the following guarantee? Every promised input consists of \(n\ge2\), a nonsingular rational matrix \(A\in\mathbb Q^{n\times n}\) with \(m\) nonzero entries, a nonzero vector \(b\in\mathbb Q^n\), and an integer \(1\le p\le c\lceil\log_2 n\rceil\). Every input numerator magnitude and positive denominator has at most \(c\lceil\log_2 n\rceil\) binary digits, and
\[\kappa_2(A)\le n^c.\]
On every run, \(A_c\) must halt within
\[C_c m\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil^{d_c}\]
word operations in the model below, with word length \(w=K_c\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\). With probability at least \(2/3\), its explicit rational output \(\widehat x\in\mathbb Q^n\) must satisfy
\[\|A\widehat x-b\|_2\le2^{-p}\|b\|_2.\]
The constants and the finite program may depend on \(c\), but must work for all promised dimensions, matrices, right-hand sides and accuracies. Matrices may be nonsymmetric and indefinite.
cards.why: This tests whether sparsity and moderate conditioning suffice for solving linear equations at essentially the cost of reading them. A resolution would clarify the limits of graph-based solvers, preconditioning and numerical subroutines used throughout algorithms and optimization.

cards.title: Exact semidefinite feasibility in polynomial time
cards.formal:
Does exact semidefinite feasibility belong to \(\mathrm P\) in the ordinary Turing model? The input is an explicitly listed tuple of symmetric rational matrices
\[A_0,A_1,\ldots,A_m\in\mathbb Q^{n\times n},\qquad n\ge1,\ m\ge0,
\]
and the required output is \(1\) if and only if
\[\exists x\in\mathbb R^m\quad A_0+\sum_{i=1}^{m}x_iA_i\succeq0.\]
More precisely, do there exist one deterministic finite-program Turing machine \(M\) and positive integers \(a,d\) such that, for every input string of total binary encoding length \(N\), \(M\) halts within \(a(N+1)^d\) steps and correctly decides the language defined below? Both matrix dimension and number of variables are unbounded input parameters. No numerical promise or approximation tolerance is supplied.
cards.why: Semidefinite constraints underlie many successful optimization relaxations, yet their unrestricted exact decision complexity is still unsettled. This problem isolates whether finite rational input admits a polynomial-time decision even when numerical separation and small explicit witnesses are unavailable.

cards.title: Single-exponential dependence on dimension for integer programming
cards.formal:
Do there exist a real constant \(C>0\), an integer constant \(c\ge1\), and one uniform classical deterministic Turing machine \(A\) such that, for every pair of integers \(m,n\ge0\), every explicitly given rational matrix \(Q\in\mathbb Q^{m\times n}\) and every rational vector \(b\in\mathbb Q^m\), the machine correctly decides whether
\[
 \exists x\in\mathbb Z^n\quad Qx\le b
\]
within at most
\[
 2^{Cn}(L+1)^c
\]
bit operations, where \(L\) is the total binary encoding length of the input? The inequalities are componentwise, and there is no boundedness or coefficient-size promise beyond the finite explicit encoding.
cards.why: Integer feasibility is a general optimization primitive. A fixed exponential base in the number of variables would sharpen the dimension dependence of a widely used fixed-parameter algorithmic tool without restricting the coefficients or constraint structure.

cards.title: Crouzeix’s sharp numerical-range inequality
cards.formal: For every integer n≥1, every complex matrix A∈C^{n×n}, and every scalar polynomial p∈C[z], does ‖p(A)‖₂≤2 max_{z∈W(A)}|p(z)| hold?
cards.why: A sharp dimension-independent bridge from scalar approximation on the numerical range to norms of functions of nonnormal matrices; retained as a recently resolved foundational problem.

cards.title: Polynomial-time simplex pivot rule
cards.formal:
Does there exist one deterministic primal-simplex algorithm and fixed positive integers \(C,d\) such that the following holds for every promised rational input \((A,b,c,B_0)\)? The linear program is
\[\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\in\mathbb R^n,\ x\ge0\},\]
where \(A\in\mathbb Q^{m\times n}\) has full row rank, \(1\le m\le n\), the maximum is finite, and \(B_0\) is any supplied feasible basis. Starting at exactly \(B_0\), the algorithm must reach and output a feasible basis \(B_t\) whose nonbasic reduced costs are all nonpositive, using only the legal improving pivots below, in at most \(C(L+1)^d\) total bit operations. Here \(L\) is the binary length of the complete input, including \(B_0\).
cards.why: Simplex is a central optimization method whose practical effectiveness has long exceeded its general worst-case guarantees. The question isolates whether exact polynomial-time linear optimization is compatible with its required improving basis exchanges, including degeneracy, and with efficiently choosing every exchange.

cards.title: Beck–Fiala conjecture
cards.formal: Is there a real constant \(C>0\) such that for every three integers \(m,n,t\ge1\) and every matrix \(A\in\{0,1\}^{m\times n}\) with \(\sum_{i=1}^m A_{ij}\le t\) for each column \(j\), there exists a single vector \(x\in\{-1,1\}^n\) satisfying \[\max_{1\le i\le m}\left|\sum_{j=1}^n A_{ij}x_j\right|\le C\sqrt t?\] The same constant must work for every dimension, frequency bound and matrix.
cards.why: The conjecture asks whether a local bound on how many constraints involve one element controls the error of balancing all constraints by the square root of that frequency. It is a central sparsity question in discrepancy theory, with a direct interpretation as simultaneously rounding half-integral choices in many overlapping constraints.

cards.title: Conforti–Cornuéjols conjecture
cards.formal: Does every finite clutter with the packing property have the max-flow min-cut property? Equivalently, if every deletion/contraction minor satisfies unweighted integral packing–covering equality, must weighted integral packing–covering equality hold for every nonnegative integer weight vector?
cards.why: Identify whether all obstructions to weighted integral packing–covering duality are already visible as unweighted failures in minors, a central issue in integer programming and combinatorial optimization.

cards.title: P-matrix linear complementarity in polynomial time
cards.formal:
Does there exist one uniform deterministic algorithm that solves every rational P-matrix linear complementarity problem in polynomial bit time? More precisely, are there a deterministic multitape Turing machine \(A\) and integers \(B,k\ge1\) such that, on every explicitly encoded rational input
\[n\in\mathbb N_{>0},\qquad M\in\mathbb Q^{n\times n},\qquad q\in\mathbb Q^n,\]
the machine halts within \(B(N+1)^k\) steps, where \(N\) is the full input length defined below, and whenever \(M\) is a P-matrix it outputs \(z,w\in\mathbb Q^n\) satisfying
\[w=Mz+q,\qquad z_i\ge0,\quad w_i\ge0,\quad z_iw_i=0\quad(1\le i\le n)?\]
A P-matrix has strictly positive determinant for every nonempty principal submatrix. No certificate of this promise is supplied, and the algorithm need not recognize it. The constants \(B,k\) and the program are shared by all dimensions and all rational coefficients.
cards.why: The P-matrix promise guarantees exactly one solution for every right-hand side, and that solution has a short rational description. The remaining difficulty is finding it efficiently despite the coupled choices of which coordinates vanish. A polynomial algorithm would resolve a central structured search problem that sits between tractable linear optimization and more general complementarity systems.

cards.title: Truly linear-time Laplacian solving
cards.formal: Does one randomized algorithm, for every connected weighted graph and zero-sum right-hand side, return \(\widehat x\) satisfying \[\|\widehat x-x^*\|_L\le\tfrac1{10}\|x^*\|_L\] with probability at least 2/3 in expected \(O(m)\) total arithmetic operations, where \(Lx^*=b\)? The constant must be independent of the graph size and edge-weight ratios.
cards.why: This asks whether approximate Laplacian solving can reach literal input-linear arithmetic complexity.

cards.title: Polynomial-time integer programming with bounded subdeterminants
cards.formal: For every fixed integer \(\Delta\ge1\), is there a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for integer linear optimization \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b,\ x\in\mathbb Z^n\}\), on inputs for which every square submatrix of A has determinant of absolute value at most Delta?
cards.why: This asks whether a bounded departure from total unimodularity guarantees tractable integer optimization.

cards.title: Linear bound in the flatness theorem
cards.formal: Does a universal real constant C>0 exist such that, for every integer n≥1 and every compact convex set \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) with nonempty interior and \(\operatorname{int}(K)\cap\mathbb Z^n=\varnothing\), its lattice width satisfies \(w(K)\le Cn\)?
cards.why: A linear flatness theorem would sharpen a foundational geometric limitation used in integer optimization.

cards.title: Limited-memory convex optimization
cards.formal: Determine, up to universal constant factors, the deterministic first-order oracle complexity \(T(d,M,\varepsilon)\) of minimizing a globally convex, Euclidean \(1\)-Lipschitz function with a global minimizer in the unit ball, when only \(M\) bits can be retained between queries. The target is the entire tradeoff for integers \(d\geq1\), \(M\geq0\) and real \(0<\varepsilon\leq1/4\), including the parameters for which \(T(d,M,\varepsilon)=\infty\).
cards.why: The tradeoff separates acquiring information about a convex objective from retaining that information for later decisions. A full answer would quantify when nearly linear storage can preserve fast convergence and when the geometry needed for a small number of queries forces substantially larger memory.

cards.title: Smale’s seventh problem
cards.formal: Do there exist real constants \(C,K>0\), an integer \(k\ge1\), and one deterministic real-number algorithm \(A\) in the model below such that, for every integer \(N\ge2\), \(A(N)\) outputs distinct points \(x_1,\ldots,x_N\in S^2\) in at most \(KN^k\) operations and satisfies \(E_N(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\le E_N^{\ast}+C\ln N\)?
cards.why: Connects the complexity of constructing global near-minimizers with discrete potential theory and the conditioning of polynomial-root problems. Its logarithmic total-energy tolerance is much sharper than leading-order equidistribution.

cards.title: Woodall’s conjecture
cards.formal: For every finite weakly connected loopless directed multigraph \(D\) that is not strongly connected, let \(\tau(D)\) be the minimum size of a directed cut. Do there exist \(\tau(D)\) pairwise arc-disjoint dijoins in \(D\)? All arcs have unit capacity, and a dijoin must meet every directed cut.
cards.why: Woodall’s conjecture asks whether the visible cut bottleneck completely determines the supply of disjoint directed-cut covers. It is a basic integral packing–covering question in combinatorial optimization, with exact structure beyond known approximation guarantees.

cards.title: Superpolynomial semidefinite extension complexity of perfect matching
cards.formal:
Is the semidefinite extension complexity of the perfect-matching polytopes of complete graphs unbounded by every polynomial in the number of vertices? Precisely, is
\[
\forall B,b\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\quad
\exists n\in\mathbb N\quad
\bigl(n\ge2\ \land\ 2\mid n\ \land\
\operatorname{xc}_{\mathrm{SDP}}(P_n)>Bn^b\bigr)
\]
true, for the exact real semidefinite lifts defined below?

This is a statement about the existence of representations, with arbitrary real coefficients and no symmetry or efficient-construction requirement. The quantifiers ask whether no single polynomial bounds the entire family; they do not require a specified exponential rate or a lower bound holding at every sufficiently large even size. Integer constants express the same assertion as the inherited formulation with every pair of positive real constants \(C,c\).
cards.why: Perfect matching is a canonical problem with efficient optimization algorithms and strong combinatorial structure. Deciding whether it nevertheless lacks polynomial-size exact semidefinite representations would clarify the limits of a major convex-optimization model beyond the established limits of linear programming. A polynomial-size family would instead demonstrate a substantial representational advantage over linear lifts for this central tractable polytope.

cards.title: Nearly quadratic oracle complexity for convex-body volume
cards.formal: Is there a randomized classical membership-oracle algorithm such that, for every fixed \(a\ge1\), every \(n\ge2\), and every convex body \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) with \(B_2^n\subseteq K\subseteq n^a B_2^n\), it returns \(V\) satisfying \[\Pr[|V-\operatorname{vol}_n(K)|\le\operatorname{vol}_n(K)/10]\ge2/3\] using at most \(C_a n^2(\log(2+n))^{c_a}\) membership queries in expectation? The polynomial-radius promise and origin are supplied; no isotropic position or uniform-sampling oracle is given.
cards.why: This targets the dimension dependence of a fundamental randomized integration problem.

cards.title: Polynomial-time linear convergence for geodesically convex optimization
cards.formal: In the geometric arithmetic model below, is there a deterministic first-order algorithm and absolute constants \(C,a,b>0\) that minimize every Lipschitz geodesically convex function on a strongly geodesically convex ball in a complete Riemannian manifold, using at most \(C(d+\zeta)^a\lceil\log(2/\varepsilon)\rceil\) objective-oracle queries and at most \(C(d+\zeta)^b\) additional operations between consecutive queries? Here \(d\) is the manifold dimension, \(\zeta=r\sqrt K/\tanh(r\sqrt K)\), with value one at \(K=0\), and the required additive objective error is \(\varepsilon Lr\). The same polynomial overhead bound applies before the first query and after the last.
cards.why: Euclidean cutting-plane methods show that high accuracy need not require a polynomial number of inverse-accuracy steps. Extending that efficiency to geodesic convexity would provide a general computational foundation for optimization on curved spaces, including matrix geometries used in scaling and statistical models.

cards.title: Deterministic near-linear-query approximation schemes for matroid intersection
cards.formal: Is there a deterministic algorithm and absolute constants \(C,a,b>0\) that, given independence-oracle access to any two matroids on a common \(n\)-element ground set and any rational \(0<\varepsilon<1\), finds a common independent set of size at least \((1-\varepsilon)r\) using at most \(Cn\log^a(n+2)\varepsilon^{-b}\) oracle queries, where \(r\) is the maximum size of a common independent set?
cards.why: The question asks whether random sampling is essential for information-efficient approximate intersection of arbitrary matroids. A positive answer would derandomize a central combinatorial optimization primitive at near-linear query cost; a negative answer would establish a separation in the power of adaptive deterministic and randomized oracle access.

cards.title: Superlinear randomized query lower bounds for submodular minimization
cards.formal: Let \(R(n)\) be the minimum worst-case number of value-oracle queries needed by a randomized algorithm to find an exact minimizer of every real-valued submodular function on \(n\) elements, with success probability at least \(2/3\). Is \(R(n)=\omega(n)\), meaning \(R(n)/n\to\infty\) as \(n\to\infty\)?
cards.why: Submodular minimization is a central tractable optimization problem, yet its information requirements remain far from its best general algorithms. A superlinear randomized lower bound would establish that even unlimited computation and adaptive random querying cannot reduce exact minimization to a linear amount of oracle information.

cards.title: Input-sparsity relative spectral low-rank approximation
cards.formal: Is there a randomized algorithm and absolute constants \(C,b>0\) that, for every real \(n\times n\) matrix \(A\), integer \(1\leq k<n\) and rational \(0<\varepsilon\leq1/2\), returns \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\) with orthonormal columns such that \[\|A-ZZ^{\mathsf T}A\|_2\leq(1+\varepsilon)\min_{\operatorname{rank}(B)\leq k}\|A-B\|_2\] with probability at least \(2/3\), using at most \(C\operatorname{nnz}(A)+Cn(k/\varepsilon)^b\) operations?
cards.why: Relative spectral approximation protects every direction of a compressed linear operator, making it useful where a small average error is insufficient. Resolving the question would determine whether this stronger guarantee can share the basic input-reading cost of fast Frobenius approximation, without rank or accuracy multiplying the sparse-data term.

cards.title: Flowing conjecture
cards.formal: Is every minimally nonideal binary clutter isomorphic to exactly one of the three obstruction types specified below: the Fano-line clutter, the odd-circuit clutter of K5, or the clutter of complements of nontrivial cuts of K5?
cards.why: A forbidden-minor characterization would explain integrality across a central class of covering problems.

cards.title: Explicit matroids with exponentially large extended formulations
cards.formal: Editorial algorithmic-explicitness variant: does there exist a uniform deterministic polynomial-time independence test defining matroids \(M_n\) on [n] for all n≥1, and constants c>0,n0, such that the linear extension complexity of each base polytope satisfies \(\operatorname{xc}(B(M_n))\ge2^{cn}\) for all n≥n0?
cards.why: This asks for concrete exponential extension-complexity obstructions where counting already proves existence.

cards.title: Gap-entropy conjecture
cards.formal: Are there absolute constants \(0<c\leq C<\infty\) such that, for every Gaussian best-arm instance \(I\) defined below and every \(0<\delta<1/10\), \[cH(I)\bigl(\log(1/\delta)+\operatorname{Ent}(I)\bigr)\leq L(I,\delta)\leq CH(I)\bigl(\log(1/\delta)+\operatorname{Ent}(I)\bigr)?\] Here \(L\) is the order-oblivious instance-wise optimum over globally correct sampling algorithms, not the performance of one algorithm required to attain the bound on every instance.
cards.why: The conjecture predicts the full instance-sensitive cost of identifying the best alternative, including the cost of learning which gap scales matter. Its entropy term would explain why instances with the same total inverse-square gap can have different exploration costs at fixed confidence.

cards.title: Constant-factor entrywise \(\ell_1\) rank-\(k\) approximation with variable \(k\)
cards.formal: Do a uniform randomized polynomial-bit-time algorithm \(A\) and an absolute constant \(C\ge1\) exist such that, for every rational matrix \(M\in\mathbb{Q}^{m\times n}\) and input integer \(0\le k\le\min(m,n)\), \(A\) returns rational factors \(U\in\mathbb{Q}^{m\times k}\), \(V\in\mathbb{Q}^{k\times n}\) satisfying \[\|M-UV\|_1\le C\operatorname{OPT}_k(M),\qquad \operatorname{OPT}_k(M)=\min_{\substack{B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\\\operatorname{rank}(B)\le k}}\|M-B\|_1,\] with probability at least \(2/3\) on every input?
cards.why: Determine whether robust low-rank compression remains computationally tractable with unrestricted target rank.

cards.title: Oertel’s mixed-integer centerpoint conjecture
cards.formal: For all integers n,d≥0 with n+d≥1 and every compact convex body \(C\subset\mathbb R^{n+d}\) with nonempty interior and positive mixed-integer volume, is there \(y\in C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)\) such that every closed halfspace H containing y satisfies \(\mu_C(H)\ge\mu_C(\mathbb R^{n+d})/(2^n e)\)?
cards.why: A universal mixed-integer centerpoint guarantee would link convex geometry to progress bounds for cutting-plane optimization.

cards.title: Seymour’s dyadic packing conjecture
cards.formal: For every ideal clutter C on a finite ground set E and every capacity vector \(w\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{E}\), does the packing linear program \[\max\{\textstyle\sum_{S\in C}y_S:y\ge0,\ \sum_{S\ni e}y_S\le w_e\ (e\in E)\}\] have an optimum all of whose coordinates are dyadic rationals?
cards.why: The conjecture asks whether integral covering geometry forces a special arithmetic form of optimal fractional packing.

cards.title: Log-squared query complexity of fixed-dimensional Tarski fixed points
cards.formal: For integers \(n\ge2\) and \(k\ge1\), let \(Q(n,k)\) be the minimum worst-case number of deterministic adaptive value queries needed to find a fixed point of an unknown monotone function \(f:[n]^k\to[n]^k\), where \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Is \[\forall k\ge1\ \exists C_k>0\ \forall n\ge2:\quad Q(n,k)\le C_k(1+\log_2 n)^2?\] A query at \(x\in[n]^k\) reveals the entire vector \(f(x)\) at cost one. Arbitrary finite computation between queries is allowed. The constant \(C_k\) may depend on \(k\) but not on \(n\) or \(f\); no polynomial bound on its dependence on \(k\) is required.
cards.why: Fixed points of monotone maps underpin equilibrium existence and program semantics. The oracle problem isolates how much information about a function is needed to find one. A dimension-independent logarithmic exponent would reveal a strong structural limit on that information requirement, even with dimension-dependent constants and unrestricted internal computation.

cards.title: First-order convergence to local minimax optima
cards.formal:
Consider sequential minimax optimization \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^p}\max_{y\in\mathbb R^q} f(x,y)\), with \(p,q\ge1\), \(f\in C^2(\mathbb R^{p+q},\mathbb R)\), and a supplied constant \(L>0\) satisfying
\[\|\nabla f(z)-\nabla f(w)\|_2\le L\|z-w\|_2\qquad\text{for all }z,w\in\mathbb R^{p+q}.\]
Does there exist one uniform deterministic first-order oracle method, in the model below, that produces iterates \(z_k=(x_k,y_k)\) from every initial point and has both of these properties for every such \(p,q,f,L\)?

First, for Lebesgue-almost every initial point \(z_0\), whenever the complete sequence \((z_k)_{k\ge0}\) converges to a finite point \(z^*\), that point is a local minimax point in the neighborhood definition below. Second, every strict local minimax point has an open neighborhood of initial points from which the method converges to that point. The second requirement excludes a method that satisfies the first merely by never converging.
cards.why: Sequential adversarial optimization needs the minimization and maximization roles to be respected at the limiting solution. Reaching a stationary point alone can select the wrong kind of equilibrium. A first-order selection theorem that remains valid with degeneracy would clarify what gradient information can guarantee beyond the curvature-restricted cases already analyzed.

cards.title: Smooth convex optimization with different domain and smoothness norms
cards.formal: For each fixed \(1\leq p<q\leq\infty\) and \(1<\kappa\leq2\), determine the optimal worst-case error \(\mathcal R_{p,q,\kappa}(n,T)\), up to constant factors, of deterministic algorithms making \(T\) exact first-order queries to minimize a convex function whose gradient is Hölder continuous in the \(\ell_q\) geometry over the unit \(\ell_p\) ball. The target covers every integer \(n\geq2\) and \(1\leq T\leq n\).
cards.why: The problem isolates whether the geometry of a constrained model can improve the fundamental convergence rate when smoothness is measured differently. Matching bounds would explain which gains in sparse and structured regression follow from geometry alone and which require access to additional problem structure.

cards.title: Polynomial-size constant-gap relaxation for minimum knapsack
cards.formal: Do universal constants C≥1 and k exist such that every feasible binary-encoded minimum-knapsack instance has an objective-independent rational extended LP relaxation of total encoding length at most (L+1)^k times a universal constant, with integrality gap at most C for every nonnegative cost vector?
cards.why: This separates efficient approximate optimization from the existence of a uniformly compact relaxation.

cards.title: Fully polynomial-size LP relaxation scheme for maximum knapsack
cards.formal: Does every maximum zero-one knapsack instance admit, for every rational \(0<\varepsilon<1\), an objective-independent rational extended LP relaxation of total bit size polynomial jointly in the input length L and \(1/\varepsilon\), whose gap is at most \(1+\varepsilon\) for all nonnegative profit vectors?
cards.why: A fully polynomial formulation scheme would provide one compact geometric certificate for all objectives.

cards.title: Second-order cone lift dimension of semialgebraic convex hulls
cards.formal: Determine the function \(a(S)\) giving the minimum number of auxiliary real scalar variables in an exact second-order cone representation of \(\operatorname{conv}(S)\), for every semialgebraic set \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and every integer \(n\geq1\). Set \(a(S)=\infty\) when no finite such representation exists. For finite values, the benchmark accepts a real approximation within absolute error \(1/100\); infinite values require proof of nonrepresentability.
cards.why: Second-order cone lifts expose nonlinear convex structure through a class of conic constraints with effective optimization methods. Understanding both representability and the minimum added dimension would distinguish intrinsic geometric obstacles from the overhead of particular reformulations, while keeping those questions separate from numerical relaxation quality.

cards.title: Deterministic competitive ratio for matching with delays
cards.formal: Determine, up to universal constant factors as \(n\to\infty\), the optimal deterministic competitive ratio \(\rho(n)\) for online minimum-cost perfect matching with linear waiting costs on a known \(n\)-point metric. The ratio must depend only on \(n\), uniformly over the number and timing of requests and all distances in the metric.
cards.why: This question measures the unavoidable cost of making irrevocable pairings while deciding how long to wait for future demand. A sharp deterministic ratio would separate the value of randomization from the difficulty of balancing spatial matching cost and elapsed waiting time in general metric spaces.

cards.title: Polynomial-size split closures in fixed dimension
cards.formal: Editorial bit-size variant: for each fixed dimension d≥3, does a polynomial p_d exist such that the split closure of every rational polyhedron P in R^d has a rational inequality description of total binary encoding length at most p_d(L), where L is the encoding length of the supplied inequality description of P?
cards.why: This asks whether a standard cutting-plane closure retains a compact representation in fixed dimension.

cards.title: Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits conjecture
cards.formal: Does there exist a real constant \(C>0\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge1\), every isotropic log-concave probability measure \(\mu\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), and every locally Lipschitz function \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) with \(\int f^2\,d\mu<\infty\) and \(\int\|\nabla f\|_2^2\,d\mu<\infty\), \[\operatorname{Var}_{\mu}(f)\le C\int_{\mathbb R^n}\|\nabla f(x)\|_2^2\,d\mu(x)?\] The same constant must work for all dimensions, measures and admissible functions. This is the Poincaré formulation of the Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits conjecture.
cards.why: KLS asks whether covariance normalization alone controls the relation between global variation and local change for every log-concave distribution. Its equivalent geometric expansion principle is central to concentration inequalities and the analysis of random walks used for sampling, integration and convex optimization.

cards.title: Gupta–Newman–Rabinovich–Sinclair conjecture
cards.formal:
Is the following proposition true? For every finite simple graph \(H\), there exists a real constant \(C_H\ge1\) such that, for every nonempty finite connected simple undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) with no \(H\) minor and every edge-length function \(w:E\to\mathbb R_{>0}\), there exist an integer \(m\ge1\) and a map \(f:V\to\mathbb R^m\) satisfying
\[
d_{G,w}(u,v)\le
\sum_{j=1}^{m}|f(u)_j-f(v)_j|
\le C_H\,d_{G,w}(u,v)
\qquad\text{for every }u,v\in V?
\]
The constant may depend only on \(H\). The dimension and map may depend on the whole weighted graph, with no bound on dimension or on the time needed to construct them.
cards.why: Determine whether excluded graph minors exactly prevent unbounded \(\ell\)\(_{1}\) distortion and multicommodity flow–cut gaps in proper minor-closed graph families.

cards.title: Unknot recognition in polynomial time
cards.formal:
Do there exist a deterministic Turing machine \(M\), a real constant \(C>0\), and an integer \(k\ge1\) such that, for every valid explicit knot-diagram encoding \(D\) of bit length \(N\), the machine halts within \(C(N+1)^k\) steps and outputs
\[
M(D)=1
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\text{the knot represented by }D\text{ is ambient isotopic to the unknot}?
\]
It must output zero for every nontrivial knot. The same machine and constants must work for all diagrams, without auxiliary certificates or advice.
cards.why: Determine whether triviality of an explicitly given knot can be decided efficiently, a foundational test of the gap between topological certificates and algorithms.

cards.title: Planar k-set extremal function
cards.formal:
For a finite set \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^2\), let
\[
\mathcal S_k(P)=\bigl\{S\subseteq P:\ |S|=k,\ 
\exists(a,b)\in\mathbb R^2\setminus\{(0,0)\}\ 
\exists t\in\mathbb R:\ 
a x+b y<t\ \forall(x,y)\in S,\ 
a x+b y>t\ \forall(x,y)\in P\setminus S\bigr\}.
\]
For integers \(n\ge2\) and \(1\le k\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor\), define
\[
K_2(n,k)=
\max_{\substack{P\subseteq\mathbb R^2,\ |P|=n\\
                 \text{no three points of }P\text{ are collinear}}}
|\mathcal S_k(P)|.
\]
Determine a positive real-valued function \(F(n,k)\), together with universal real constants \(0<c\le C<\infty\), such that
\[
cF(n,k)\le K_2(n,k)\le CF(n,k)
\quad\text{for every }n\ge2,\quad
1\le k\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor.
\]
cards.why: A central unresolved counting problem in computational geometry, it controls the complexity of levels and line-separated ranges. Its persistent gap tests the strength of crossing-number methods and geometric constructions, with consequences for output-sensitive and parametric algorithms.

cards.title: Polynomial Hirsch conjecture
cards.formal:
Is the following proposition true? There exist a real constant \(C>0\) and an integer \(k\ge1\) such that for every integer \(d\ge1\) and every nonempty, full-dimensional, pointed convex polyhedron \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), writing \(n\) for its number of facets,
\[
\operatorname{diam}G(P)\le C(n+d)^k?
\]
The same \(C\) and \(k\) must work for all dimensions, all facet counts and all real coefficients defining \(P\). Both bounded and unbounded polyhedra are included.
cards.why: Determine whether all polyhedral feasible regions have uniformly short edge routes, a central structural question underlying linear programming.

cards.title: Optimal \(\ell_1\) distortion of planar Earth Mover Distance
cards.formal: Determine, up to universal constant factors as \(n\to\infty\), the least distortion \(D(n)\) of a bi-Lipschitz embedding into \(\ell_1\) of all probability measures on the planar grid \(X_n=\{0,1,\ldots,n-1\}^2\), equipped with Euclidean Earth Mover Distance. This asymptotic target was resolved in 2026: \(D(n)=\Theta(\log n)\).
cards.why: The result identifies the optimal loss when representing planar transport by coordinatewise absolute differences. It closes a longstanding metric-embedding gap relevant to image comparison and nearest-neighbor methods, and shows that the logarithmic loss of classical representations is inherent. The completed result belongs in the historical archive rather than the active open benchmark.

cards.title: Lang–Plaut problem
cards.formal: For every integer \(K\geq2\), do there exist a finite integer \(N(K)\geq1\) and a finite real constant \(D(K)\geq1\) such that every \(K\)-doubling subset \(X\) of real Hilbert space admits a map \(F:X\to\mathbb R^{N(K)}\) satisfying \[\|x-y\|_2\leq\|F(x)-F(y)\|_2\leq D(K)\|x-y\|_2\qquad(x,y\in X)?\]
cards.why: The problem asks whether intrinsic local metric dimension completely controls Euclidean dimensional reduction once Hilbert embeddability is available. Its resolution would clarify a central obstruction to finite-dimensional metric representation and the limits of geometry-based compression independent of dataset size.

cards.title: Optimal size of weak \(\varepsilon\)-nets for convex ranges
cards.formal: For every fixed integer \(d\geq2\), determine the asymptotic order of \(f_d(\varepsilon)\) as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), up to multiplicative constants depending only on \(d\). Here \(f_d(\varepsilon)\) is the smallest worst-case number of auxiliary points required to hit every convex set containing at least an \(\varepsilon\) fraction of a finite point set in \(\mathbb R^d\).
cards.why: Weak nets quantify how many representatives can preserve every large convex part of an arbitrary finite configuration. Sharp bounds would settle a basic gap in discrete geometry and clarify the geometric cost underlying transversal, selection and approximation results.

cards.title: Decidability of PL four-sphere recognition
cards.formal:
Does there exist one deterministic Turing machine \(M\) with the following property? For every finite abstract simplicial complex \(K\), encoded by its facets as below and promised to be a nonempty closed combinatorial \(4\)-manifold, \(M\) halts and outputs a bit satisfying
\[
M(\operatorname{enc}(K))=1
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
K\cong_{\mathrm{PL}}\partial\Delta^5.
\]
Here \(\partial\Delta^5\) is the standard PL \(4\)-sphere. Output zero is required on every promised input that is not PL homeomorphic to it. There is no running-time or space bound, and connectedness is not part of the promise.
cards.why: Locate the remaining decidability boundary for recognizing spheres in the piecewise-linear category.

cards.title: Euclidean minimum spanning tree complexity
cards.formal: For each fixed integer \(d\geq3\), determine up to constant factors the optimal deterministic worst-case time for computing an exact Euclidean minimum spanning tree of \(n\geq2\) distinct points in \(\mathbb R^d\). The input is the array of coordinates of the points \(p_1,\ldots,p_n\); the output is a list of \(n-1\) pairs of indices forming a connected acyclic graph \(T\) that minimizes \(\sum_{\{i,j\}\in T}\|p_i-p_j\|_2\) over all spanning trees on these labels. Include logarithmic factors in the requested complexity, and use the real-arithmetic model below.
cards.why: The problem asks how effectively fixed-dimensional geometry can accelerate one of the most basic graph optimization tasks. Sharp complexity bounds would clarify the algorithmic cost of exact geometric connectivity and its relation to proximity searching.

cards.title: Dürer’s conjecture
cards.formal: For every bounded three-dimensional convex polytope \(P\subset\mathbb R^3\) with nonempty interior, is there a connected edge unfolding whose distinct face interiors do not overlap in the plane?
cards.why: This long-standing question asks whether every convex three-dimensional shape has an edge-based planar net, a basic unresolved principle in geometric folding and representation.

cards.title: Exact planar Euclidean matching
cards.formal: Determine, up to constant factors including logarithmic factors, the optimal deterministic worst-case running time for computing a minimum-length perfect matching of \(2n\) distinct points in \(\mathbb R^2\), for all integers \(n\geq1\), in the exact real-arithmetic model below. The output is a list of \(n\) unordered pairs of input indices, every index occurring exactly once, minimizing \(\sum_{\{i,j\}\in M}\sqrt{(x_i-x_j)^2+(y_i-y_j)^2}\) among all perfect matchings. The input consists only of the point coordinates; the complete graph is implicit.
cards.why: Exact Euclidean matching is a basic geometric optimization primitive. Its unresolved complexity tests how far geometric structure can reduce the cost of optimization over an implicit complete graph, beyond the easier approximation guarantees.

cards.title: Decidability of contractibility for finite two-dimensional complexes
cards.formal: Is there an algorithm that, on every finite nonempty simplicial complex \(K\) of dimension at most two, halts and decides whether \(K\) is simple-homotopy equivalent to a point? Equivalently, can contractibility of all such \(K\) be decided?
cards.why: This is a basic boundary of algorithmic topology: whether a finite two-dimensional description admits any reliable procedure for recognizing a space with no nontrivial homotopy. It separates unrestricted computability from practical simplification and from resource-bounded versions of topological reduction.

cards.title: Constant-distortion Steiner point removal
cards.formal: Is there an absolute constant \(C<\infty\) such that, for every finite connected undirected graph \(G\) with nonnegative real edge lengths and every terminal set \(K\subseteq V(G)\) with \(|K|\geq2\), there is a reweighted terminal-preserving minor \(H\) with vertex set exactly \(K\) satisfying \[d_G(s,t)\leq d_H(s,t)\leq C\,d_G(s,t)\qquad(s,t\in K)?\]
cards.why: Steiner point removal asks how much of a network’s geometry and topology can survive when only designated terminals remain. A universal constant would establish a strong form of graph compression; an unbounded lower bound would show that the topology of general graphs forces a growing loss even when edge lengths may be redesigned.

cards.title: Polynomial-time recognition of the 3-sphere
cards.formal:
Is there a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm deciding whether a finite simplicial triangulation of a closed connected piecewise-linear \(3\)-manifold is piecewise-linearly homeomorphic to the standard \(3\)-sphere?

Precisely, let \(\mathcal P\subseteq\{0,1\}^{*}\) be the promised encodings below, and let \(S(x)\) assert that the encoded complex is PL-homeomorphic to \(\partial\Delta^{4}\). Does there exist one uniform deterministic Turing machine \(M\), an integer \(C\ge1\), and an integer \(d\ge0\) such that
\[
\forall x\in\{0,1\}^{*}\ \exists b\in\{0,1\}\
\left[
H_{M}\bigl(x,C(|x|+1)^{d},b\bigr)
\ \land\
\bigl(x\in\mathcal P\ \Rightarrow\ (b=1\Longleftrightarrow S(x))\bigr)
\right]?
\]
Here \(H_{M}(x,t,b)\) means that \(M\) halts within \(t\) transitions with output bit \(b\). The running-time bound holds on every binary string, including malformed encodings and inputs outside the manifold promise; correctness is required on \(\mathcal P\). The machine and both polynomial constants are fixed before the input is chosen.
cards.why: Recognizing the simplest closed three-dimensional manifold is a basic test of whether global topological structure can be determined efficiently from local combinatorial data. A polynomial-time algorithm would also give polynomial-time unknot recognition for diagram input, while separating decidability and short certificates from efficient decision in a central example of computational topology.

cards.title: Linear-size universal point sets for planar graphs
cards.formal: Does there exist a universal real constant \(C>0\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge1\), some set \(U_n\subset\mathbb R^2\) of at most \(Cn\) distinct points supports a crossing-free straight-line drawing of every simple planar graph on \(n\) vertices?
cards.why: This asks whether a linear geometric host can represent all planar combinatorial structures of a given size, rather than dedicating a separate layout to each graph.

cards.title: Flip graph connectivity in three dimensions
cards.formal:
For every finite point set \(P\subset\mathbb R^3\) with \(|P|\ge4\) and no four points coplanar, is the graph of all geometric tetrahedralizations of \(P\) connected under \(2\leftrightarrow3\) bistellar flips?

A tetrahedralization must use exactly the vertices \(P\), consist of straight, nondegenerate tetrahedra meeting along common faces, and cover \(\operatorname{conv}(P)\). A legal flip replaces two tetrahedra filling a convex triangular bipyramid by the three tetrahedra with the same five vertices and the same union, or performs the reverse replacement. Every intermediate tetrahedralization must retain all points of \(P\) as vertices.

Equivalently, for every such \(P\) and every pair \(T,T'\) of its tetrahedralizations, must there exist a finite sequence \(T=T_0,T_1,\ldots,T_m=T'\) in which each consecutive pair differs by one legal flip?
cards.why: This is a basic reachability question for three-dimensional meshes: can local bistellar moves explore every tetrahedralization without changing the underlying points? A resolution would identify a fundamental difference, or an essential commonality, between planar triangulation algorithms and their three-dimensional counterparts.

cards.title: NP certificates for homeomorphism of three-manifolds
cards.formal: Does homeomorphism of connected compact triangulated 3-manifolds, allowing boundary and nonorientable manifolds, have polynomially bounded certificates verifiable in polynomial time? Precisely, do there exist a polynomial \(p\) and a uniform deterministic polynomial-time verifier \(V\) such that for every promised pair \((T,U)\in\mathcal D\) of total encoded length \(N\), \[H(T,U)\iff\exists w\in\{0,1\}^{\leq p(N)}\;V(T,U,w)=1?\] This is the NP-certificate question for the promised homeomorphism problem below.
cards.why: Short certificates would separate the cost of discovering topological equivalence from the cost of checking it. An NP upper bound would place a fundamental classification problem within the standard theory of efficient verification.

cards.title: Optimal input-sparsity subspace embeddings
cards.formal: Is the optimal-dimension sparse oblivious subspace-embedding conjecture true? Precisely, does there exist a universal constant \(C\ge1\) such that for every pair of integers \(n\ge d\ge1\) and every \(0<\varepsilon,\delta\le1/3\), there are an integer \(m\) and a probability distribution \(\mathcal D\) over real \(m\times n\) matrices with \[1\le m\le\left\lceil C\,\frac{d+\log(1/\delta)}{\varepsilon^2}\right\rceil,\qquad s=\left\lceil C\,\frac{\log(d/\delta)}{\varepsilon}\right\rceil,\] such that every matrix in the support has at most \(s\) nonzero entries per column and, for every \(d\)-dimensional linear subspace \(W\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \[\Pr_{\Pi\sim\mathcal D}\bigl[\ \forall x\in W:\ (1-\varepsilon)\|x\|_2\le\|\Pi x\|_2\le(1+\varepsilon)\|x\|_2\ \bigr]\ge1-\delta?\] The row and column-sparsity bounds must hold simultaneously, with no additional growing factors.
cards.why: Subspace embeddings compress a matrix’s column space while preserving the lengths of all its linear combinations. Small output dimension reduces later computation, and sparse embedding columns reduce the arithmetic needed to apply the map to sparse data. The conjecture asks whether these two advantages can be attained together at the stated dependence on accuracy and failure probability.

cards.title: Klee’s measure problem
cards.formal: For every fixed integer \(d\ge 3\), determine the optimal deterministic worst-case running time, up to constant factors as \(n\to \infty\), for computing the exact d-dimensional volume of the union of n axis-aligned boxes in the arithmetic real-RAM model below. The dimension may affect constants and the algorithm, but is not an input parameter in this running-time question.
cards.why: A basic measure-computation problem underlying geometric union and coverage algorithms.

cards.title: General unfolding of nonconvex polyhedra
cards.formal:
Does every closed embedded polyhedral surface in \(\mathbb R^3\), including nonconvex surfaces, admit a general nonoverlapping unfolding into one connected planar piece?

Precisely, for every compact connected polyhedral two-dimensional manifold \(P\subset\mathbb R^3\) without boundary, do there exist a finite union \(C\) of straight segments on its surface and a continuous injective map
\[f:P\setminus C\longrightarrow\mathbb R^2\]
such that \(P\setminus C\) is connected and \(f\) is a rigid Euclidean placement on each triangle of a finite subdivision of the surface away from the cuts?

Cuts may cross original faces. They have zero width, no area of the surface is discarded, and the whole uncut surface must remain connected. Coincidence between copies of cut-boundary points in the planar closure is allowed; overlap between distinct uncut surface points is not. No restriction to genus zero is imposed.
cards.why: This asks whether nonconvex geometry can obstruct every possible connected planar net even when cuts are unrestricted within faces. Resolving it would identify a fundamental limit of cutting and flattening polyhedral surfaces, and distinguish geometric impossibility from the shortcomings of particular meshing or fabrication algorithms.

cards.title: Output-sensitive convex hull complexity
cards.formal: For every fixed integer \(d\geq4\), determine up to constant factors the optimal deterministic output-sensitive running time for constructing the convex hull of \(n\geq d+1\) points in \(\mathbb R^d\) in general position, as a function of \(n\) and the actual number \(f\) of hull facets. The coordinate array is the input. Output the complete facial structure of the hull, as specified below. The required complexity must cover every realizable pair \((n,f)\), including small hulls, and retain logarithmic factors.
cards.why: Sharp output-sensitive hull bounds would connect the work of discovering a geometric boundary to its actual combinatorial size. This matters for hull construction, polyhedral representations and geometric computations whose input contains many nonextreme points.

cards.title: Earth mover distance sketching complexity
cards.formal: Determine, up to universal constant factors, the minimum sketch length \(s(n,c)\) for approximating planar earth mover distance for every integer \(n\geq2\) and real approximation factor \(c\geq1\). Inputs are subsets \(A,B\subseteq[n]^2\) of equal cardinality, with unit mass at each occupied grid point, and \[\operatorname{EMD}(A,B)=\min_{\pi:A\to B\ \mathrm{bijection}}\sum_{a\in A}\|a-\pi(a)\|_1.\] Each set must be encoded independently using the same public randomness. From the two \(s\)-bit encodings the decoder must return \(\widehat d\) satisfying \(\operatorname{EMD}(A,B)\leq\widehat d\leq c\operatorname{EMD}(A,B)\) with probability at least \(2/3\) for every fixed pair.
cards.why: EMD sketching asks how much information must be retained to compare geometric mass distributions without keeping the original data. Sharp tradeoffs would clarify the limits of metric compression and the distinction between embeddings, sketches and full-input transport algorithms.

cards.title: Efficient constant-distortion cut-cone approximation
cards.formal:
Do there exist an absolute constant \(C\ge1\), a family of closed convex cones
\[
K_n\subseteq\mathbb R^{\binom n2}\qquad(n\ge2),
\]
and one uniform deterministic algorithm for exact membership and strong separation, as defined below, satisfying both
\[
\mathrm{CUT}_n\subseteq K_n\subseteq\mathrm{MET}_n
\]
and
\[
\forall d\in K_n\quad\exists\rho\in\mathrm{CUT}_n
\quad\forall\,1\le i<j\le n,\qquad
d_{ij}\le\rho_{ij}\le C\,d_{ij}?
\]
The constant \(C\) is independent of \(n\) and \(d\). The membership/separation algorithm must run in polynomial bit time for every rational query point, with a single polynomial bound independent of \(n\).
cards.why: Cut metrics encode graph partitions, and their nonnegative combinations capture finite ℓ₁ distances. The question seeks a tractable convex domain that retains this geometry to constant distortion. It separates a broad algorithmic possibility from the limitations of the best-studied semidefinite candidate.

cards.title: Simultaneous embedding with fixed edges for two graphs
cards.formal: Is there a deterministic algorithm that, given any two finite simple planar graphs \(G_{1}=(V,E_{1})\) and \(G_{2}=(V,E_{2})\) on the same labeled vertex set, decides in polynomial time whether they admit planar topological drawings that coincide on every shared vertex and every shared edge?
cards.why: A central simultaneous graph-drawing problem about making overlapping structures geometrically consistent.

cards.title: Truly subquadratic exact Euclidean bipartite matching
cards.formal: Does there exist a uniform algorithm and absolute constants \(\delta,C>0\) that, for every \(n\ge1\) and every pair of labelled planar point lists \(R=(r_1,\ldots,r_n)\), \(B=(b_1,\ldots,b_n)\), returns a permutation \(\pi\in S_n\) minimizing \(\sum_{i=1}^n\|r_i-b_{\pi(i)}\|_2\), using at most \(Cn^{2-\delta}\) operations in the real-arithmetic model below, with probability at least \(2/3\) on each input? Deterministic algorithms qualify. Coordinates are arbitrary real numbers and there is no separation, spread or grid promise.
cards.why: The question tests whether exact geometric bipartite optimization can break the quadratic barrier.

cards.title: Polygon visibility graph recognition
cards.formal: Is there a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, given a finite simple undirected graph \(G\) on \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and a cyclic order \(C=(v_1,\ldots,v_n)\) of its vertices, decides whether some simple polygon with these labelled vertices in boundary order \(C\) has visibility graph exactly \(G\)? Here \(n\geq3\), the graph is given by its complete adjacency matrix and the cyclic order by an explicit list. Both visible and nonvisible pairs must be realized, and the polygon has no holes or additional vertices.
cards.why: The problem is a central inverse question about geometric visibility: whether pairwise sight-line information and a boundary order can be tested for realizability efficiently. It connects graph recognition with geometric representation complexity.

cards.title: Near-quadratic Voronoi complexity of lines in three dimensions
cards.formal: For every real \(\varepsilon>0\), does there exist a real \(C_\varepsilon>0\) such that every regular Euclidean Voronoi diagram of \(n\ge2\) distinct affine lines in \(\mathbb R^3\), under the exact stratum convention below, has total complexity at most \(C_\varepsilon n^{2+\varepsilon}\)?
cards.why: This is a central unresolved complexity gap for a fundamental three-dimensional proximity structure, closely connected to lower-envelope and arrangement bounds.

cards.title: coNP certificates for three-manifold homeomorphism
cards.formal: Does nonhomeomorphism of connected compact triangulated 3-manifolds have polynomially bounded certificates verifiable in polynomial time? Allow boundary and nonorientable manifolds. Precisely, do there exist a polynomial \(p\) and a uniform deterministic polynomial-time verifier \(W\) such that for every promised pair \((T,U)\in\mathcal D\) with total input length \(N\), \[\neg H(T,U)\iff\exists w\in\{0,1\}^{\leq p(N)}\;W(T,U,w)=1?\] This is the coNP-certificate question for the promised homeomorphism problem.
cards.why: The question asks whether topological difference always has efficiently checkable finite evidence. Its reduction from graph isomorphism ties the difficulty of distinguishing 3-manifolds to a central unresolved certificate problem in complexity theory.

cards.title: Polynomial flip-distance bounds for three-manifold triangulations
cards.formal:
Does every compact connected piecewise-linear three-manifold, with or without boundary, have a polynomial bound on the number of local moves needed to pass between any two of its finite simplicial triangulations?

Precisely, let \(\mathcal M_3\) be the finite combinatorial three-manifold triangulations defined below, let \(t(K)\) count tetrahedra, and write \(K\simeq_{\mathrm{PL}}L\) when their realizations are piecewise-linearly homeomorphic. Prove or refute
\[
\forall R\in\mathcal M_3\ \exists C,k\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\
\forall T,U\in\mathcal M_3:\quad
\bigl(T\simeq_{\mathrm{PL}}R\ \land\ U\simeq_{\mathrm{PL}}R\bigr)
\Longrightarrow
\exists\text{ a legal move sequence from }T\text{ to }U
\text{ of length at most }C\bigl(t(T)+t(U)\bigr)^k.
\]
The constants may depend on the fixed reference triangulation \(R\), equivalently on its manifold type, but must work for every pair \(T,U\) of that type. No common polynomial for different manifolds, effective procedure to obtain the constants, or efficient algorithm to find a move sequence is required. Intermediate triangulations may have more tetrahedra than either endpoint.

The card uses the standard combinatorial version: finite abstract simplicial complexes, interior bistellar moves, and elementary shellings and their inverses on the boundary. This explicitly repairs the boundary convention in the original question and specifies a simplicial representation. The source also discusses more general face-pairing encodings; no unproved equivalence between their quantitative move bounds and this specified version is part of the claim.
cards.why: Polynomial move bounds would provide short, locally checkable certificates relating arbitrary triangulations of each fixed three-manifold. A counterexample would exhibit intrinsic superpolynomial reconfiguration distance in one fixed topological space. The question measures representation changes, rather than the performance of a particular recognition algorithm.

cards.title: Fast Johnson–Lindenstrauss transforms for sparse vectors
cards.formal:
Do there exist absolute constants \(C_1,C_2>0\), an integer \(q\ge0\), and uniform sampling and application algorithms with the following property? For every integer \(d\ge1\) and every \(0<\varepsilon,\delta<1/2\), the sampling algorithm produces an input-independent representation of a random linear map \(A:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^k\), where
\[
1\le k\le\min\{d,\lceil C_1\varepsilon^{-2}\log_2(1/\delta)\rceil\}.
\]
For every fixed \(x\in\mathbb R^d\), its distribution satisfies
\[
\Pr_A\bigl[(1-\varepsilon)\|x\|_2\le\|Ax\|_2
                 \le(1+\varepsilon)\|x\|_2\bigr]\ge1-\delta.
\]
Given a sampled representation and the list of the \(s\) nonzero coordinates of any \(x\), the application algorithm must return all coordinates of \(Ax\) in at most
\[
C_2(s+k)\bigl(\log_2(d+2)\bigr)^q
\]
operations in the arithmetic model below, for every sampled representation and input. The same constants and algorithms must work for all parameters. The matrix distribution is independent of \(x\), including its support.
cards.why: An affirmative answer would make optimal Euclidean dimension reduction almost as cheap as reading a sparse vector and writing its sketch. This would strengthen a general primitive used in similarity search, randomized linear algebra and high-dimensional geometry. A general obstruction would identify a computational cost that dimension bounds alone do not reveal.

cards.title: Instance-optimal outer approximation of convex polytopes
cards.formal: Editorial finite-input variant: for every fixed \(d\ge2\), is there a deterministic algorithm which, given a full-dimensional polytope \(K\subseteq B_2^d\) by N vertices and \(0<\varepsilon\le1/2\), constructs a polytope P with \[K\subseteq P\subseteq K+\varepsilon B_2^d,\qquad f(P)\le C_d\operatorname{OPT}(K,\varepsilon),\] in time polynomial in N and 1/epsilon? Here f counts facets and C_d depends only on dimension.
cards.why: Instance-optimal approximation would adapt representation size to the geometry of the particular polytope.

cards.title: Efficient average-distortion embeddings of polyhedral norms
cards.formal: Is there a uniform deterministic polynomial-time construction of a globally defined Euclidean embedding of the square-root metric of every rational polyhedral norm, with quadratic average distortion at most \(C\sqrt{\log_2 d}\) on any given finite rational point set, for one universal constant \(C\)? The construction must produce a finite description permitting polynomial-time evaluation to any requested precision. This is the explicitly encoded polyhedral-norm branch of the source’s algorithmic average-John question; the exact guarantees and complexity parameters are below.
cards.why: Average-distance preservation can be much better than preservation of every distance from below. Constructing such maps would make a strong structural theorem in metric geometry algorithmically usable. The global nonexpansion requirement matters because a later query point need not belong to the original data set.

cards.title: Exact planar Euclidean maximum TSP
cards.formal:
Is there a deterministic algorithm that finds an exactly longest Euclidean tour through any finite set of rational points in the plane in time polynomial in the full binary input length?

For an explicitly listed set \(P=(p_1,\ldots,p_n)\) of distinct points in \(\mathbb Q^2\), with \(n\ge3\), define the length of a cyclic ordering \(\pi\) by
\[\ell_P(\pi)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sqrt{(x_{\pi(i)}-x_{\pi(i+1)})^2+(y_{\pi(i)}-y_{\pi(i+1)})^2},\qquad \pi(n+1)=\pi(1).\]
Do there exist one deterministic Turing machine \(A\), a constant \(C>0\) and an integer \(a\ge0\) such that, on every valid input of bit length \(B\), the machine returns a permutation \(\pi\) of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) satisfying
\[\ell_P(\pi)=\max_{\sigma\in S_n}\ell_P(\sigma)\]
within \(C(B+1)^a\) bit operations?
cards.why: This is a sharply focused boundary in geometric optimization: nearby versions are tractable under polygonal norms or hard in higher Euclidean dimension, while accurate approximation is available. Settling exact planar optimization would clarify how the geometry of a distance function and the arithmetic of exact lengths affect efficient computation.

cards.title: Point location in three-dimensional subdivisions
cards.formal: Do there exist uniform deterministic preprocessing and query algorithms that, for every explicitly represented polyhedral subdivision of a three-dimensional box of total boundary complexity \(n\), store \(O(n)\) words and answer every point-location query in \(O(\log(n+2))\) worst-case time? A query gives an arbitrary point \(q\in\mathbb R^3\) and must return the label of a subdivision region whose closure contains \(q\), or the exterior label for points outside the box. Constants are universal, the guarantee is exact, and the subdivision may have nonconvex regions.
cards.why: Point location is a basic spatial-search operation. Resolving the simultaneous storage and query bounds would establish whether arbitrary three-dimensional partitions admit the same asymptotic search economy as planar subdivisions.

cards.title: NP recognition of closed hyperbolic three-manifolds
cards.formal: Does there exist a deterministic polynomial-time verifier V and a polynomial p such that, for every finite PL-triangulation T of a compact connected three-manifold M, M is closed and admits a hyperbolic metric if and only if there exists a binary certificate w with |\(w|\le p(|T|)\) and \(V(T,w)=1\)?
cards.why: Would show that a global constant-curvature geometry can always be certified using polynomially bounded discrete evidence from an arbitrary triangulation. It would sharpen the complexity of a central geometric recognition problem beyond mere decidability.

cards.title: Constant-factor streaming approximation of planar Earth Mover Distance
cards.formal:
Do there exist a uniform randomized one-pass streaming algorithm \(A\), real constants \(C\ge1\), \(B>0\), and an integer \(q\ge1\), such that for every integer \(n\ge1\), every integer \(\Delta\ge2\), and every stream consisting of \(n\) red and \(n\) blue point arrivals in \([\Delta]^2\), the algorithm uses at most
\[
B\bigl(1+\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil+\lceil\log_2(\Delta+1)\rceil\bigr)^q
\]
bits of working memory and returns a nonnegative rational number \(\widehat E\) satisfying
\[
\Pr\!\left[
\operatorname{EMD}(R,B_{\mathrm{pts}})
\le\widehat E
\le C\,\operatorname{EMD}(R,B_{\mathrm{pts}})
\right]\ge\frac23?
\]
Here \(R\) and \(B_{\mathrm{pts}}\) are the red and blue multisets, respectively, and
\[
\operatorname{EMD}(R,B_{\mathrm{pts}})
=\min_{\pi:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\{1,\ldots,n\}\ \mathrm{bijection}}
\sum_{i=1}^n\|r_i-b_{\pi(i)}\|_1.
\]
The constants and algorithm are independent of \(n,\Delta\), coordinates and stream order.
cards.why: Determine whether transportation distance can be estimated from one scan using only polylogarithmic memory, beyond the limitations of standard metric embeddings.

cards.title: Half-snowflake embeddings into Wasserstein p-space
cards.formal: For every fixed real \(p\in(2,\infty)\), does there exist a finite constant \(C_p\ge1\) such that every finite metric space \((X,d)\) admits a map \(F:X\to\mathcal P_p(\mathbb R^3)\) and a scale \(s>0\) satisfying \(s\sqrt{d(x,y)}\le W_p(F(x),F(y))\le C_p s\sqrt{d(x,y)}\) for all \(x,y\in X\)? The constant may depend on p but must be independent of X, its number of points and its distances.
cards.why: Asks how richly a fixed three-dimensional transport space can represent arbitrary finite metric geometry after taking square roots of distances. The proposed exponent would improve the known universality range beyond what follows directly from the transport-cost exponent.

cards.title: Minimum-weight triangulation in NP
cards.formal: Does the following language belong to NP? An instance consists of a finite set \(S\subset \mathbb{Q} ^{2}\) of explicitly given points and a rational bound B; it is a yes instance exactly when S has a triangulation whose total Euclidean edge length, counting every edge once, is at most B.
cards.why: Asks whether exact geometric optimization has short certificates despite the algebraic cost of verifying lengths.

cards.title: Counting simple polygonalizations
cards.formal:
Is there a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, given a finite planar point set \(S\subset\mathbb Q^2\) in binary rational coordinates, outputs the exact number \(\operatorname{poly}(S)\) of simple polygonalizations of \(S\)?

A simple polygonalization is a non-self-intersecting closed polygonal curve that visits every point of \(S\) exactly once and joins consecutive points by straight segments. Two cyclic orders count as the same polygonalization precisely when one is obtained from the other by changing the starting point or reversing the traversal. Collinear points are allowed, but crossings, overlapping edges and contacts between nonadjacent edges are forbidden.

The running time must be polynomial in the total binary input length, including the coordinate encodings, and the output count is written in binary.
cards.why: This is a basic exact-counting question for a geometric family of Hamiltonian cycles. A resolution would clarify whether planarity of the drawing and freedom to choose its edges make counting fundamentally easier than familiar hard graph-counting problems, and would separate compact numerical output from exhaustive geometric enumeration.

cards.title: Minimum-Link Path in 2D
cards.formal:
Does there exist a single deterministic algorithm \(A\) in the real-RAM model specified below and a function \(T:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N\) such that, for every valid planar polygonal-domain input \((P,s,t)\) with \(n\) boundary vertices, \(A\) outputs a minimum-link polygonal path from \(s\) to \(t\) contained in \(P\), using at most \(T(n)\) operations, and
\[
\forall\eta\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\ \exists N\ge1\ \forall n\ge N:
\qquad T(n)\le\eta n^2?
\]
The source's word “subquadratic” is interpreted here literally as \(o(n^2)\). The target permits logarithmic-factor savings and does not require a fixed power saving \(O(n^{2-\varepsilon})\).
cards.why: The number of straight portions of a route captures the cost of changing direction, independently of how far the route travels. This question asks whether exact optimization of that basic geometric objective can avoid a quadratic operation count in environments with many obstacles, where the planar Euclidean shortest-path objective has a different complexity.

cards.title: NP-hardness of three-manifold homeomorphism
cards.formal: Is homeomorphism of connected compact triangulated 3-manifolds NP-hard under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions? Use the domain \(\mathcal D\) below, allowing boundary and nonorientable manifolds. Equivalently, is there one uniform polynomial-time Turing machine \(R\) which, on every binary string \(x\), outputs a valid pair \((T_x,U_x)\in\mathcal D\), such that \[x\in\mathrm{3SAT}\iff H(T_x,U_x)?\] Outputs must satisfy the manifold promise on both satisfiable and unsatisfiable inputs.
cards.why: NP-hardness would locate a central topological classification task relative to general combinatorial search. It would supply a stronger complexity obstruction than the currently known reduction from graph isomorphism.

cards.title: Optimal space–query tradeoff for approximate Voronoi diagrams
cards.formal: For each fixed dimension \(d\ge2\), determine the worst-case minimum storage \(S_d(n,t,\varepsilon)\) of the box-based approximate Voronoi diagrams defined below, for \(n\ge2\), \(1\le t\le n\), and \(0<\varepsilon\le1/2\). Seek matching upper and lower bounds up to powers of \(\log(n/\varepsilon+2)\), uniformly over the full parameter domain.
cards.why: The tradeoff quantifies the geometric storage needed to reduce approximate nearest-neighbor queries to a small candidate set.

cards.title: Lower-left anchored rectangle packing constant
cards.formal: Determine the universal lower-left anchored rectangle packing constant \(\alpha\) to absolute error at most \(1/100\). For each finite point set \(P\subseteq[0,1)^2\) containing \((0,0)\), let \(A(P)\) be the supremum of the total area of all valid packings of one positive-area axis-aligned rectangle per point, each anchored at that point as its lower-left corner and contained in the unit square. Rectangles must have disjoint interiors. Define \(\alpha=\inf_{P\subseteq[0,1)^2,\;P\text{ finite},\;(0,0)\in P}A(P)\). Area is measured as a fraction of the unit square, so the tolerance is one percentage point of its area.
cards.why: The question asks how much area arbitrary anchors inevitably permit one to occupy. Its mathematical interest comes from the universal guarantee over every finite configuration, including degeneracies, rather than the optimal value of one instance. The half-area conjecture would identify the extremal value, while rigorous estimates of the constant quantify the remaining gap.

cards.title: Does every point set admit an oriented t-spanner with t < 2?
cards.formal: Is there a real constant t<2 such that, for every integer d≥1 and every finite set P⊆ℝ^d with |P|≥3, some oriented graph on P has oriented dilation at most t? Edges may join arbitrary pairs, with Euclidean lengths, but opposite directed edges on the same pair are forbidden.
cards.why: The historical question tested how much detour is forced by one-way connections when every pair needs a short round trip. The 5/3 theorem crosses its proposed threshold and now serves as a benchmark for stronger dilation, sparsity and optimization questions.

cards.title: Linear-size sample compression
cards.formal: Is there a universal integer \(C\ge1\) such that every nonempty Boolean concept class \(H\subseteq\{0,1\}^{X}\) on an arbitrary set \(X\), with finite VC dimension \(d\ge1\), admits a labeled sample compression scheme with nonnegative integer kernel and side-information bounds \(k,b\) satisfying \[k+b\le Cd?\] The scheme is exact on every finite \(H\)-realizable sample, stores an unordered subset of labeled sample records plus \(b\) bits, and may reconstruct a predictor outside \(H\). Its compressor, reconstructor, \(k\), and \(b\) may depend on the complete class, but the same scheme and bounds must work for all sample sizes. Only \(C\) must be universal. This preserves the card’s previously selected linear-size, counted-side-information formulation.
cards.why: A central question connecting the combinatorial complexity of prediction with how many observations suffice to represent all training decisions. Its universality across concept classes, and its links to learning, extremal set systems and graph geometry, make the linear-versus-exponential gap fundamental.

cards.title: Learning parity with noise in polynomial time
cards.formal: For every fixed rational \(\eta\in(0,1/2)\), does there exist a uniform classical randomized polynomial-time algorithm that exactly recovers every hidden parity vector from independent uniform examples with independent label noise of rate \(\eta\)? More explicitly, is the following assertion true? \[\forall\eta\in\mathbb Q\cap(0,1/2)\ \exists A_\eta,\ C_\eta,k_\eta\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\ \forall n\ge1\ \forall s\in\{0,1\}^n:\quad \Pr[A_\eta^{\operatorname{EX}_{n,s,\eta}}(1^n)=s]\ge\frac23,\] where every execution takes at most \(C_\eta(n+1)^{k_\eta}\) bit-computation steps, including all example requests and output writing, and \(\operatorname{EX}_{n,s,\eta}\) returns a fresh pair \[ (a,b),\qquad a\sim U_n,\quad e\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\eta),\quad b=\langle a,s\rangle\oplus e.\] All vectors, errors and machine coins are independent except for the displayed dependence of each label on its input and the same fixed secret. This retains the existing every-fixed-rate, every-secret search-LPN target.
cards.why: A canonical computational learning problem where a tiny amount of independent label noise defeats the obvious algebraic method, connecting efficient learning, random-code decoding and cryptographic hardness.

cards.title: Polynomial-time distribution-free PAC learning of DNF
cards.formal:
Does there exist one uniform classical randomized learner \(A\) and absolute positive integers \(a,d\) such that the following holds for every pair of integers \(n,s\ge1\), every Boolean function \(f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}\) representable by a DNF with at most \(s\) terms, every probability distribution \(D\) on \(\{0,1\}^n\), and every pair of integers \(t,b\ge2\)? Given only \((n,s,t,b)\) and access to independent labeled examples \((x,f(x))\) with \(x\sim D\), the learner halts within
\[a(n+s+t+b+1)^d\]
steps on every run and outputs an explicitly encoded deterministic Boolean circuit \(h\) on \(n\) inputs such that
\[\Pr\!\left[\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}D(x)\,\mathbf 1[h(x)\ne f(x)]\le\frac1t\right]\ge1-2^{-b}?\]
The outer probability includes the learner’s coins and sampled examples. Membership queries, equivalence queries and descriptions of \(f\) or \(D\) are not supplied. The output need not be a DNF; it must be an efficiently evaluable circuit as defined below.
cards.why: DNF learning is a central question about whether compact Boolean rules can be inferred efficiently from observations. Polynomial sample complexity is available, but achieving polynomial computation for arbitrary input distributions remains the difficulty. A positive answer would also cover important target classes such as decision trees and juntas through their DNF representations.

cards.title: Efficient learning of well-separated Gaussian mixtures
cards.formal: Is there an end-to-end polynomial-time, polynomial-sample algorithm for learning the parameters of well-separated spherical Gaussian mixtures at the source’s square-root-logarithmic separation scale? More precisely, do there exist one uniform randomized learner \(A\) and universal constants \(C_{\rm sep},B,a\ge1\) such that the following holds for every integer \(k\ge3\), \(d\ge1\), \(s\ge k\), \(R\ge1\), \(t\ge3\)? For every mixture \[P=\sum_{i=1}^{k}\pi_i N(\mu_i,\sigma_i^2 I_d),\qquad \pi_i\ge1/s,\quad \frac{\max_i\sigma_i}{\min_i\sigma_i}\le R,\] whose means satisfy \[\|\mu_i-\mu_j\|_2\ge C_{\rm sep}\max\{\sigma_i,\sigma_j\}\sqrt{\log(sR)}\quad(i\ne j),\] the learner, given only \(d,k,s,R,t\) and independent unlabeled samples from \(P\), returns \(k\) estimated component parameters with probability at least \(2/3\) for which some permutation \(\tau\) of \([k]\) satisfies, for every \(i\), \[\frac{|\widehat\pi_{\tau(i)}-\pi_i|}{\pi_i}\le\frac1t,\qquad \frac{\|\widehat\mu_{\tau(i)}-\mu_i\|_2}{\sigma_i}\le\frac1t,\qquad \frac{|\widehat\sigma_{\tau(i)}-\sigma_i|}{\sigma_i}\le\frac1{t\sqrt d}.\] Require at most \(B(d+k+s+R+t)^a\) samples and total arithmetic operations, including output. The learner receives no initial estimates of the means, weights or variances. It need not attain the source’s sharper near-linear sample bound; the selected question asks for polynomial sample complexity and polynomial time simultaneously.
cards.why: Identifiable clusters need not be easy to locate. This problem asks whether the separation that makes parameter recovery statistically feasible also permits an efficient global algorithm. It is a basic test of the computational cost of fitting latent-variable models when the number of components grows.

cards.title: One-way functions from hardness of learning P/poly
cards.formal: Does worst-case computational hardness of distribution-free PAC learning of polynomial-size Boolean circuits from random labeled examples imply the existence of one-way functions? Precisely, let \(\mathsf{Learn}_{\mathrm{circ}}\) be the size-parameterized uniform learning assertion below, and let \(\mathsf{OWF}\) mean the existence of an ordinary uniformly computable one-way function secure against every uniform probabilistic polynomial-time inverter. The target is \[\neg\mathsf{Learn}_{\mathrm{circ}}\ \Longrightarrow\ \mathsf{OWF}.\] Equivalently, would the nonexistence of all such one-way functions guarantee an efficient learner for every target circuit and every example distribution? Hardness here is the failure of efficient learning in the worst case over targets and distributions; no efficiently samplable distribution of hard target descriptions, depth promise on those descriptions, or hardness reduction from SAT is assumed.
cards.why: One-way functions provide the basic computational ingredient for much of classical private-key cryptography. The question asks whether failure of a general-purpose circuit learner is already enough to supply that ingredient, without assuming that hard target functions can be efficiently generated at random.

cards.title: Learning Boolean juntas from uniform random examples
cards.formal: Does there exist one uniform classical randomized learner \(A\) and universal positive integers \(B,C\) such that every Boolean \(k\)-junta on \(n\) variables can be learned from independent uniform noiseless examples in time polynomial in \(n,2^k\) and inverse error? Explicitly, for all integers \(n\ge1\), \(0\le k\le n\), \(t\ge3\), and every \(k\)-junta \(f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}\), the learner receives \(1^n,1^k,1^t\) and an independent-example oracle \(\operatorname{EX}_f\). Every execution takes at most \(B(n+2^k+t)^C\) steps and outputs an ordinary Boolean circuit \(h\) for which \[\Pr_{A,\,\operatorname{EX}_f}\left[\Pr_{x\sim U_n}[h(x)\ne f(x)]\le\frac1t\right]\ge\frac23.\] The exponent \(C\), constant \(B\) and machine are independent of \(n,k,t,f\). This preserves the existing full \(\operatorname{poly}(n,2^k,1/\varepsilon)\) target; it is not merely a separate polynomial-time statement for every fixed \(k\).
cards.why: Determine whether arbitrary dependence on a small hidden set of variables can be learned efficiently from ordinary observations, separating computational search from sample sufficiency.

cards.title: Learning decision trees from uniform random examples in polynomial time
cards.formal: Does there exist one uniform classical randomized learner \(A\) and universal positive integers \(B,C\) such that, for every \(n,s\ge1\), \(t\ge3\), and every Boolean function \(f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}\) represented by a decision tree with at most \(s\) nodes, \(A\), given \(1^n,1^s,1^t\) and independent uniform examples labeled by \(f\), runs on every execution for at most \(B(n+s+t)^C\) steps and outputs a Boolean circuit \(h\) satisfying \[\Pr_{A,\,\mathrm{examples}}\left[\Pr_{x\sim U_n}[h(x)\ne f(x)]\le\frac1t\right]\ge\frac23?\] The hypothesis may be an arbitrary efficiently evaluable circuit. The target remains the previously selected polynomial-time sample-only uniform-PAC question; reciprocal-integer error \(\varepsilon=1/t\) makes the accuracy encoding explicit.
cards.why: Settle the sample-only computational learnability of a canonical interpretable Boolean model.

cards.title: NP-hardness of improper learning of \(\mathrm{P}/\mathrm{poly}\)
cards.formal: Is there an integer \(a\ge1\) such that, for every integer \(b\ge a\), there are an integer \(r\ge1\) and a uniform randomized polynomial-time oracle reduction \(R_b\) which decides SAT with success probability at least \(2/3\) using the following agnostic circuit-learning oracle? A query is a Boolean sampling circuit producing a distribution \(D\) on \(\{0,1\}^{m}\times\{0,1\}\). Every oracle reply must be a circuit \(h\) of size at most \((m+1)^{b}\) satisfying \[L_D(h)\le\min_{g\in\operatorname{SIZE}_{m}((m+1)^{a})}L_D(g)+(m+1)^{-r}.\] The reduction must succeed for every sequence of valid replies. The exponent \(r\), reduction and its running-time polynomial may depend on \(b\), but not on the SAT instance. No cryptographic or unproved complexity assumption is part of the target. This selects the source's agnostic, efficiently samplable-distribution reduction formulation.
cards.why: This asks whether learning general small circuits remains hard when the learner is free to use a different and polynomially larger representation. Establishing such hardness from SAT would connect worst-case NP difficulty with a central general learning task, while the known links to witness encryption expose consequences beyond learning itself.

cards.title: Time complexity of Gaussian agnostic halfspace learning
