cards.formal: Determine the optimal joint running-time dependence on dimension \(n\) and inverse excess error \(t=1/\varepsilon\) for agnostically learning affine halfspaces from Gaussian examples. Retain the source’s deterministic Boolean target-function model: for every measurable \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\{-1,+1\}\), a learner sees independent \((x,f(x))\) with \(x\sim\gamma_n=N(0,I_n)\), and must output a predictor \(h\) such that \[\Pr\left[\operatorname{err}_f(h)\le\operatorname{OPT}_n(f)+\frac1t\right]\ge\frac23,\qquad \operatorname{err}_f(h)=\Pr_{x\sim\gamma_n}[h(x)\ne f(x)],\] where \[\operatorname{OPT}_n(f)=\inf_{w\in\mathbb R^n,\ b\in\mathbb R}\Pr_{x\sim\gamma_n}[\operatorname{sgn}(\langle w,x\rangle+b)\ne f(x)].\] The parameters range over \(n\ge2\), \(t\ge3\). More precisely, characterize the asymptotically attainable uniform time bounds \(T(n,t)\) defined below, with matching algorithmic upper and general lower bounds in each stated parameter regime. The source’s subsidiary question about \(n^{O(\log t)}\) is recorded in context; it does not replace the broader optimal-time target. The real-arithmetic convention and its distinction from a finite-bit implementation are explicit parts of this formulation.
cards.why: Gaussian inputs remove many distributional complications, yet arbitrary labels can still make even the best linear predictor difficult to match. The question asks for the precise computational cost of decreasing excess error, allowing any output representation. It separates the number of examples needed for learning from the much larger time used by current algorithms.

cards.title: Fully polynomial learning of halfspace intersections under Gaussian and uniform inputs
cards.formal: Resolve the following two distribution-specific questions, separately. For \(D_n=\gamma_n=N(0,I_n)\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), and for \(D_n=U_n\), the uniform measure on \(\{-1,+1\}^n\), does there exist a uniform randomized learner \(A_D\) and constants \(B_D,C_D\ge1\) such that, for all integers \(n,k\ge1\), \(t\ge3\), and all intersections \(f\) of at most \(k\) affine halfspaces, \(A_D(n,k,t)\), using only independent examples \((x,f(x))\) with \(x\sim D_n\), outputs a predictor \(h\) satisfying \[\Pr\!\left[\Pr_{x\sim D_n}[h(x)\ne f(x)]\le\frac1t\right]\ge\frac23\] in total training, output-writing and evaluation cost at most \(B_D(n+k+t)^{C_D}\)? The Gaussian branch uses the explicit real-arithmetic convention below; the Boolean-cube branch uses bit computation. The learner may be improper. Both the number of halfspaces and inverse accuracy are variable parameters: a polynomial whose exponent depends on \(k\) or \(t\) does not answer either branch affirmatively. A full resolution reports an answer to each branch, rather than treating failure of one as a classification of both.
cards.why: Simple independent input coordinates do not identify which inequality caused a negative label. The question asks whether that ambiguity creates a computational barrier even when the distribution is completely known. Its uniform dependence on the number of inequalities and desired accuracy separates practical polynomial learning from algorithms efficient only for fixed parameters.

cards.title: Distribution-free learning of two margin halfspaces
cards.formal: Does there exist one uniform randomized learner and one polynomial \(p\) with the following guarantee? For every dimension \(d\geq 1\), every \(0<\gamma,\varepsilon<1\), and every distribution \(D\) satisfying the realizability and margin promises below, the learner receives independent labeled examples from \(D\) and, within \(p(d,\lceil1/\gamma\rceil,\lceil1/\varepsilon\rceil)\) operations, outputs a hypothesis \(h\) such that \[\Pr_{\text{samples, learner}}\!\left[\Pr_{(x,y)\sim D}[h(x)\ne y]\leq\varepsilon\right]\geq 2/3.\] The hypothesis may be improper, but its evaluation on a new point must also take polynomial time in these parameters. No factorization or other restriction on the example distribution is imposed beyond the stated promises.
cards.why: This asks whether the simplest intersection of linear classification rules remains efficiently learnable from ordinary examples under arbitrary distributions. A positive answer would remove a distributional assumption from a central margin-learning model; a negative answer would establish a computational obstruction even when the learner may use any efficiently evaluable representation.

cards.title: Distribution-free improper learning of two unrestricted halfspaces
cards.formal: Is there a single randomized learner that, for every distribution \(D\) on \(\{0,1\}^n\), every target \(f\) expressible as the intersection of two integer-weight halfspaces of total description length at most a supplied bound \(B\), and every rational \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\), uses only independent labeled examples from \(D\) to output a Boolean circuit \(H\) with \(\Pr_{x\sim D}[H(x)\ne f(x)]\le\varepsilon\) with probability at least \(2/3\), in time polynomial in \(n+B+\lceil1/\varepsilon\rceil+\operatorname{len}(\varepsilon)\)?
cards.why: Determine whether combining two elementary classifiers already defeats efficient distribution-free learning.

cards.title: Optimal multiclass regret versus Littlestone dimension
cards.formal: Determine, up to universal constant factors, the function \[R(d,T)=\sup\bigl\{R_T(H):\ X,Y\text{ nonempty sets},\ \varnothing\ne H\subseteq Y^X,\ \mathrm L(H)\le d\bigr\}\] for all integers \(T\ge d\ge1\). The supremum permits infinite instance sets, infinite label sets and arbitrary hypothesis classes. For the prediction game defined below, \[R_T(H)=\inf_A\ \sup_{(x_1,y_1),\ldots,(x_T,y_T)\in X\times Y}\left\{\sum_{t=1}^T(1-p_t(y_t))-\min_{h\in H}\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbf1\{h(x_t)\ne y_t\}\right\}.\] Here \(p_t=A_t((x_1,y_1),\ldots,(x_{t-1},y_{t-1}),x_t)\) is a probability distribution on labels. The infimum ranges over all causal prediction rules, without computational restrictions. Retain all logarithmic factors. This is the previously authorized quantitative reformulation of the source conjecture, which predicts \(R(d,T)=\Theta(\sqrt{dT})\).
cards.why: Would determine whether Littlestone dimension alone controls the exact minimax cost of multiclass sequential prediction, beyond the already known learnability characterization.

cards.title: Littlestone-dimension regret bounds for unrestricted classes
cards.formal: Do universal real constants \(0<c\le C<\infty\) exist such that, for every nonempty set \(\mathcal X\), every nonempty Boolean concept class \(\mathcal H\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\mathcal X}\) of finite Littlestone dimension \(d\ge1\), and every integer horizon \(T\ge d\), the optimal adversarial online regret satisfies \[c\sqrt{dT}\le R_T(\mathcal H)\le C\sqrt{dT}?\] Here \[R_T(\mathcal H)=\inf_A\ \sup_{(x_1,y_1),\ldots,(x_T,y_T)\in\mathcal X\times\{0,1\}}\left\{\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell(p_t,y_t)-\min_{h\in\mathcal H}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbf1\{h(x_t)\ne y_t\}\right\},\] where \(p_t=A_t((x_1,y_1),\ldots,(x_{t-1},y_{t-1}),x_t)\in[0,1]\), \(\ell(p,0)=p\), and \(\ell(p,1)=1-p\). The infimum ranges over all such causal prediction rules. No restriction of countability, topology, compactness, or measurability is imposed on \(\mathcal X\) or \(\mathcal H\). The unresolved issue in the source is whether the upper bound holds with this full generality; the matching lower scale is already known.
cards.why: Littlestone dimension already characterizes whether adversarial online classification is learnable. This question asks whether that single combinatorial number also controls the sharp regret for every class. Removing the remaining regularity assumption would complete that quantitative characterization; a counterexample would exhibit a genuine limitation of a purely dimension-based prediction theorem.

cards.title: Sample-optimal Gaussian graphical model learning in polynomial time
cards.formal: Can general Gaussian conditional-independence graphs be learned in uniform polynomial time using, up to a universal constant factor, the information-theoretically optimal number of independent observations? For integers \(p\ge2\), \(1\le d\le p-1\), \(r\ge2\), and rational \(0<\kappa<1\), let \(\mathcal G(p,d,\kappa)\) be the Gaussian family defined below and let \(m^*(p,d,\kappa,r)\) be its minimax sample count for exact graph recovery with failure probability at most \(2^{-r}\), allowing unrestricted measurable estimators. Is there one uniform randomized algorithm \(A\) and constants \(C,B,a\ge1\) such that, for every parameter choice and every \(P\in\mathcal G(p,d,\kappa)\), \(A(p,d,\kappa,r)\) returns its exact graph with probability at least \(1-2^{-r}\), draws at most \(\lceil C m^*(p,d,\kappa,r)\rceil\) independent samples, and uses at most \[B\bigl(p+d+\lceil\kappa^{-1}\rceil+r+L\bigr)^a\] real-arithmetic operations, including sample loading and output, where \(L\) is the binary encoding length of \(\kappa\)? The exponent and constants must be independent of every parameter and of the unknown distribution. This retains the general sample-optimal computational question from the source’s conclusion; bounded-degree recovery is already treated there. The minimax definition does not presume that the commonly quoted \(d\log p/\kappa^2\) sample scale is sharp in all joint parameter regimes.
cards.why: Sparse conditional dependence can be statistically identifiable even when variables are extremely correlated. Recovering that graph from few observations is useful only if the necessary search is computationally affordable. The problem asks whether uniformly efficient computation must pay an extra sample cost without regularity assumptions on the covariance.

cards.title: Nontrivial agnostic membership-query learning of \(\mathrm{ACC}^{0}\)
cards.formal: Can polynomial-size constant-depth modular circuits be agnostically learned under uniform inputs using membership queries in time \(2^n/n^{\omega(1)}\)? Precisely, for every fixed depth bound \(d\ge1\), fixed modulus \(m\ge2\), and fixed integer size exponent \(k\ge1\), do there exist one uniform randomized oracle Turing machine \(A_{d,m,k}\), an integer \(n_0\), and a saving function \(\sigma:\mathbb N_{\ge2}\to[0,\infty)\) such that \(\sigma(n)/\log_2 n\to\infty\) and the following holds? For every \(n\ge n_0\) and every joint distribution \(D\) on \(\{0,1\}^n\times\{-1,+1\}\) whose first marginal is uniform, \(A_{d,m,k}\), given \(1^n\) and the conditional-label oracle described below, runs in worst-case time at most \(2^{n-\sigma(n)}\) and outputs a hypothesis \(h\) satisfying \[\Pr\left[\operatorname{corr}_D(h)\ge \max_{c\in\operatorname{ACC}_{d,m,k}(n)}\operatorname{corr}_D(c)-2^{-n^{99/100}}\right]\ge\frac13,\qquad \operatorname{corr}_D(g):=\mathbb E_{(x,y)\sim D}[g(x)y].\] All machine coins and oracle responses are included in this probability. The success constant \(1/3\) is the literal consequence of the source’s full-learning convention \(1-\delta\) and its assignment \(\delta=2/3\); it is recorded explicitly rather than silently exchanged with the separate weak-learning convention.
cards.why: Constant-depth circuits with modular gates are a central boundary class in circuit complexity. The question asks whether their predictive structure can be exploited even when labels need not come from that class and the learner may choose its queries. The requested saving must beat every fixed polynomial factor relative to the exponential scale while retaining the source’s high-accuracy guarantee.

cards.title: Linear conditional-information bounds for VC learning
cards.formal: Does there exist a universal constant \(c>0\) such that the following holds? For every nonempty Boolean hypothesis class \(H\subseteq\{0,1\}^{X}\) of finite VC dimension \(d\ge1\), and every integer \(n\ge d\), there is a proper randomized learner \(A:(X\times\{0,1\})^n\to H\) satisfying both \[\forall P,\quad \operatorname{CMI}_{P}(A)\le cd\] and \[\forall s\in(X\times\{0,1\})^n,\quad \mathbb E_{W\sim A(s)}\widehat L_s(W)\le\inf_{h\in H}\widehat L_s(h)+c\sqrt{d/n}?\] The first quantifier ranges over all labeled-data distributions in the measurable model below, including nonrealizable distributions. The second ranges over every deterministic sample, including samples with conflicting labels. The same learner must satisfy both guarantees; it may depend on \(H,n\), but not on \(P\). This is the original source’s main agnostic Conjecture 6, recovered from the imported introduction excerpt, not its different realizable or improper variants.
cards.why: Classical VC theory controls prediction error through the richness of a class. This question asks whether the same optimal scale can always be realized by a learner whose whole output reveals only a dimension-proportional amount about which examples were used. The joint information and empirical-accuracy requirements make it a statement about the learner itself.

cards.title: PAC learning of finite automata under the uniform distribution
cards.formal: Are deterministic finite automata efficiently PAC learnable from independent uniformly distributed words and their acceptance bits? Use the ordinary finite-word, fixed-length uniform model. Does there exist one randomized classical Turing machine \(L\) and one polynomial \(p\) such that, for every alphabet size \(q\ge2\), word length \(n\ge1\), state bound \(s\ge1\), integers \(a,b\ge3\), and deterministic finite automaton \(M\) with at most \(s\) states over \(\Sigma_q=\{0,\ldots,q-1\}\), the following holds? Given \(1^q,1^n,1^s,1^a,1^b\) and access only to independent examples \((w,M(w))\) with \(w\sim U_{q,n}\), \(L\) runs in worst-case time at most \(p(q+n+s+a+b)\), and outputs a finite predictor \(h\) satisfying \[\Pr_{L,\,\mathrm{examples}}\left[\Pr_{w\sim U_{q,n}}[h(w)\ne M(w)]\le\frac1a\right]\ge1-\frac1b?\] The predictor may use any efficiently evaluable representation; it need not be an automaton. A 2021 theorem rules out this guarantee under a specified local-pseudorandom-generator assumption, already for binary alphabets. This card retains the unconditional algorithm-existence question, while recording that published conditional negative answer explicitly.
cards.why: Finite-state machines give very small descriptions of potentially complicated behavior on long strings. This question isolates whether uniformly random training words make that behavior computationally learnable from acceptance labels alone. It separates the simplicity of the sampling distribution from the difficulty of recovering a useful predictor.

cards.title: Minimax sample complexity of proper agnostic online reinforcement learning
cards.formal: Editorial quantitative finite-state variant: determine, up to universal constant factors, the minimax episodic sample complexity N(Pi,H,epsilon) for proper agnostic online reinforcement learning in the model below, uniformly over all finite deterministic policy classes Pi and 0<epsilon<1/2.
cards.why: A structural characterization would distinguish statistically tractable online reinforcement learning from settings needing stronger access.

cards.title: Dimension complexity of distribution-independent SQ learning
cards.formal: Is there a universal constant \(C>0\) with the following property? For every nonempty set \(X\), every nonempty binary concept class \(\mathcal H\subseteq\{-1,+1\}^{X}\), every integer \(m\ge1\), tolerance \(0<\tau<1\) and error \(0\le\varepsilon<1/4\), suppose a single randomized statistical-query learner makes at most \(m\) queries of tolerance \(\tau\) and, for every input distribution \(D\), target \(h\in\mathcal H\) and admissible oracle response rule, returns \(\hat h\) with \(\mathbb E[\Pr_{x\sim D}(\hat h(x)\ne h(x))]\le\varepsilon\). Must \(\operatorname{dc}(\mathcal H)\le C m/\tau^{2}\)? The learner is selected before the distribution, target and oracle replies. The constant is independent of all these objects and of the accuracy, domain size and class.
cards.why: This asks whether learning successfully from noisy expectation information under every distribution forces all targets to share a small linear representation. It connects a general information-access model with the geometric capacity of linear predictors, and tests whether known advantages of learned representations depend essentially on the input distribution.

cards.title: Proper decision-tree learning in polynomial time
cards.formal: Is there a uniform randomized membership-query algorithm that properly learns Boolean decision trees under the uniform distribution in polynomial time? For every \(n,s\geq1\), every integer \(m\geq2\), and every \(f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}\) representable by a decision tree with at most \(s\) leaves, the learner is given \(n,s,m\) and oracle access to \(f\). It must output an explicitly represented decision tree \(h\), with probability at least \(2/3\), such that \[2^{-n}|\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:h(x)\ne f(x)\}|\leq1/m.\] Its worst-case running time must be polynomial in \(n,s,m\).
cards.why: The question tests whether efficient prediction can be achieved while retaining a decision-tree representation in a basic, well-specified query model. Its resolution would clarify the computational cost of proper learning beyond sample complexity alone.

cards.title: Recursive teaching dimension conjecture
cards.formal: Does there exist a universal real constant \(K>0\) such that, for every finite set \(X\) and every finite Boolean concept class \(\mathcal C\subseteq\{0,1\}^X\), \[\operatorname{RTD}(\mathcal C)\leq K\operatorname{VCdim}(\mathcal C)?\] Both dimensions are the combinatorial quantities defined below. The constant must be independent of the number of concepts, the domain size and the class itself.
cards.why: A universal linear bound would connect sample-based combinatorial complexity with the number of examples needed for structured teaching. It asks whether recursive teaching can always be controlled at the same scale as VC dimension.

cards.title: Memory–sample tradeoffs for noisy parity learning
cards.formal: Do there exist absolute constants \(c_{1},c_{2}>0\) and \(n_{0}\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge n_{0}\), every \(0<\varepsilon <1/2\) and every one-pass learner recovering a uniformly random \(x\in \{0,1\}^{n}\) with probability at least \(2/3\) from the noisy parity samples defined below, its worst-case memory S and maximum sample count T satisfy \(S\ge c_{1}n^{2}/\varepsilon ^{2}\) or \(T\ge 2^{c_{2}n}\)? Constants are independent of \(n, \varepsilon\) and the learner, and \(\varepsilon\) may tend to zero with n. This states the bounded-error recovery interpretation of Conjecture 1; it does not additionally require a lower bound at exponentially small success probability.
cards.why: Would quantify how observation noise increases the storage needed for a central learning problem, strengthening unconditional limits relevant to streaming learning and bounded-storage cryptography.

cards.title: Proper unlabeled compression of ample classes
cards.formal: Does every nonempty ample concept class \(C\subseteq \{0,1\}\)ᵁ on a finite domain U admit a proper unlabeled sample compression scheme of size at most \(d=\operatorname{VC}(C)\)? Precisely, do there exist maps \(\kappa :RS(C)\to \{A\subseteq U:|A|\le d\}\) and \(\rho :\{A\subseteq U:|A|\le d\}\to C\) such that, for every realizable labeled partial sample \(s, \kappa (s)\subseteq dom(s)\) and \(\rho (\kappa (s))\) agrees with every label in s? The stored object is only an unordered subset of the sample’s input points. The bound is d, not an unspecified multiple of d.
cards.why: Would extend sharp label-free sample compression from maximum classes to the larger class characterized by equality of shattering and strong shattering, clarifying how far the VC dimension controls lossless reconstruction of consistent samples.

cards.title: Multiclass sample compression from binary compression
cards.formal: Is the following implication valid for every function \(f:\mathbb N_0\to\mathbb N_0\)? Suppose every nonempty binary concept class \(B\subseteq\{0,1\}^{U}\) on every nonempty domain \(U\), with finite VC dimension \(v\), admits an exact realizable sample compression scheme of size at most \(f(v)\). Must there exist an integer \(A_f\ge1\) such that every nonempty multiclass concept class \(H\subseteq Y^X\), on arbitrary nonempty sets \(X,Y\) and with finite graph dimension \(d\), admits such a scheme of size at most \[A_f f(d)?\] The constant may depend on the chosen binary bound \(f\), but not on \(X,Y,H,d\), the sample size or the labels occurring in a sample. Label sets may be infinite. No properness, majority-vote form, stability, effectiveness or computational efficiency of the compression schemes is assumed. This restores the hypothesis omitted from the imported source sentence: the question concerns transfer of an arbitrary universal binary compression bound, not just existence of some graph-dimension bound.
cards.why: A general transfer theorem would carry any improvement in binary sample compression to multiclass prediction without a penalty for the number of labels. It would separate the combinatorial difficulty of binary compression from additional requirements imposed by multiclass reconstruction. This matters even though bounded compression at an exponential graph-dimension scale is already known.

cards.title: Polynomial-time robust spectral estimation
cards.formal: For every fixed \(q\in[2,\infty]\), is there a polynomial-time algorithm that always recovers a robust low-rank representation of an unknown clean matrix from bounded perturbations to every data point, with the spectral-error guarantee available information-theoretically in Proposition 27? Specifically, do there exist, for each fixed \(q\), a uniform algorithm \(\mathcal A_q\) and constants \(b_q,C_q,B_q,a_q\ge1\) such that the following holds for all integers \(n,m\ge1\), \(0\le r\le n\), real \(\kappa,\delta\ge0\), and matrices \(A,\widetilde A\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\) satisfying \(\|\widetilde A_j-A_j\|_q\le\delta\) for every column \(j\)? Given only \((\widetilde A,r,\kappa,\delta)\), the algorithm must output an orthogonal projection \(\widehat\Pi\) with \[\operatorname{rank}(\widehat\Pi)\le r,\qquad \|\widehat\Pi\|_{q\to2}\le b_q\kappa,\] and, for every \(\eta>0\), \[\|(I_n-\widehat\Pi)A\|_{2\to2}\le C_q(1+\eta^{-1})\left(\operatorname{OPT}_{q,r,\kappa}(A)+\sqrt m\,\delta\kappa\right)+\sqrt{2\eta}\,\|A\|_{2\to2}.\] The same output must satisfy every \(\eta\); \(\eta\) is an analysis parameter, not an extra source of clean-data information. Require at most \(B_q(n+m+1)^{a_q}\) operations in the explicit fixed-\(q\) real-arithmetic model below. The output must be a projection, even when the observed matrix has large spectral distortion; reporting only that the input was poisoned is insufficient.
cards.why: A representation can be stable against future perturbations and still be difficult to learn from already corrupted data. This question asks whether worst-case robust spectral reconstruction is computationally attainable whenever it is information-theoretically possible. It isolates a gap that is hidden if an algorithm may simply report severe corruption.

cards.title: Local regularization for multiclass learning
cards.formal: Does every realizably PAC-learnable multiclass hypothesis class H admit a fixed local regularizer \(\psi :H\times X\to \mathbb{R} \ge 0\) such that every learner induced by \(\psi\), under the pointwise minimum-score rule below, PAC learns H? This is the existence part of the source question; optimal sample complexity is a separate refinement.
cards.why: Tests whether a fixed preference over hypotheses at each prediction point is a general principle for multiclass learning. A negative answer would identify a limit of regularization even when improper prediction is allowed; a positive answer would give a common template for all learnable multiclass classes.

cards.title: Compression overhead for adversarial robustness
cards.formal: Is there a universal constant \(K>0\) such that the following implication holds for every nonempty domain \(X\), every nonempty total binary concept class \(\mathcal C\subseteq\{0,1\}^{X}\) of finite VC dimension, every integer \(k\ge1\), and every perturbation map \(U:X\to2^{X}\) satisfying \(x\in U(x)\)? If \(\mathcal C\) admits an ordinary labeled sample compression scheme of size at most \(k\), must it admit an adversarially robust labeled sample compression scheme of size at most \(\lceil Kk\rceil\)? The constant is independent of the class, domain, perturbation sets and sample length. Perturbation sets may be infinite. This makes the size-overhead assertion in Open Problem 28 explicit, with \(k\) denoting the available ordinary compression bound.
cards.why: Sample compression asks how much of a training set determines a predictor consistent with all its constraints. Adversarial robustness replaces each example by an entire set of required predictions. A constant-overhead theorem would connect these two information requirements without charging separately for the number of possible perturbations.

cards.title: Learning PH/poly from learning NP/poly
cards.formal: Does efficient distribution-free PAC learnability of \(\mathrm{NP/poly}\) from random labeled examples imply the same learnability for every fixed level of \(\mathrm{PH/poly}\)? In the size-parameterized model below, write \(\mathsf{Learn}_r\) for efficient learning of Boolean concepts represented by circuits with \(r\) alternating witness blocks, starting existentially. The target is the single implication \[\mathsf{Learn}_1\ \Longrightarrow\ \forall r\in\mathbb N_{\ge1},\ \mathsf{Learn}_r.\] The learner for each fixed \(r\) may be different and have a different polynomial running-time bound. This does not request one polynomial uniform over arbitrarily many alternations. Both sides use ordinary Boolean circuits as output hypotheses and only independent random examples of the unknown target.
cards.why: The question asks whether solving one level of a powerful prediction task automatically solves every fixed level above it. An affirmative answer would give a structural collapse for efficient learning, beyond the familiar collapses for deciding languages or merely representing them by small circuits.

cards.title: Non-clashing teaching dimension versus VC dimension
cards.formal: For every finite set X and every nonempty concept class \(C\subseteq 2^{x}\), is \(NCTD(C)\le \operatorname{VC}(C)\)? Equivalently, if C has VC dimension d, does there exist a teaching map assigning at most d correctly labeled examples to each concept such that no two distinct concepts are mutually consistent with one another’s assigned examples? Both positive and negative examples are allowed. The target constant is exactly one, not merely a bound \(O(d)\).
cards.why: Would show that every finite concept class can be taught with at most its VC dimension many examples per concept in the non-clashing model, giving a sharp link between learning capacity and teaching complexity.

cards.title: Learning speedups from random examples
cards.formal: Does the low-end learning speedup hold using only independent uniform labeled examples? For each circuit family C specified below, suppose every polynomial-size subfamily has a randomized weak learner under the uniform distribution, with confidence \(1- 1/n\) and worst-case running time \(2^{n}/n^{\omega (1)}\). Must every polynomial-size subfamily then have, for every fixed \(\varepsilon >0\) and \(a\ge 1, a\) randomized learner with error at most \(n^{- a}\), confidence at least \(1- 1/n\), and worst-case running time \(O(2^{n^{\varepsilon}})\), still using only independent uniform labeled examples?
cards.why: Tests whether the sharp gap in possible circuit-learning runtimes is a structural feature of passive learning, or relies on being able to choose labels to request. It connects the computational cost of statistical prediction with major circuit classes while keeping the distribution and available information fixed.

cards.title: Agnostic direct-sum learning rates
cards.formal: Does the single-instance agnostic learning rate determine all Cartesian-power learning rates up to constant factors? Precisely, for every two nonempty concept classes \(\mathcal C\subseteq Y^{X}\) and \(\mathcal D\subseteq Z^{W}\) on nonempty countable input and label sets, suppose there are \(a,b>0\) such that \[a\,e_{\mathcal D}(n)\le e_{\mathcal C}(n)\le b\,e_{\mathcal D}(n)\qquad\text{for every integer }n\ge1.\] Must there then be \(a',b'>0\), allowed to depend on the two classes but not on \(n\) or \(r\), such that \[a'\,e_{\mathcal D^{r}}(n)\le e_{\mathcal C^{r}}(n)\le b'\,e_{\mathcal D^{r}}(n)\qquad\text{for every }n,r\ge1?\] This is the constant-factor rate-determination form of the source's agnostic Open Question 3. The countable-domain convention and constant-factor interpretation are explicit editorial choices; the source paper also asks separate realizable-learning and compression questions.
cards.why: A direct-sum law would explain whether learning several tasks together has a statistical cost determined by the difficulty of one task. In the agnostic setting, whole-tuple loss and unrestricted correlations can make that question depend on class structure not visible in its ordinary learning rate.

cards.title: Monotone empirical risk minimization
cards.formal: Does every nonempty Boolean concept class \(\mathcal H\subseteq\{0,1\}^X\) of finite VC dimension on a countable domain \(X\) admit a possibly randomized empirical risk minimizer whose expected population error never increases with sample size, under every data distribution? Precisely, for each such \(X,\mathcal H\), require learning rules \(A_n\), \(n\geq1\), that always return an empirical risk minimizer in \(\mathcal H\), and for every distribution \(D\) on \(X\times\{0,1\}\) satisfy \[\mathbb E_{S\sim D^{n+1},R}L_D(A_{n+1}(S,R))\leq\mathbb E_{S\sim D^n,R}L_D(A_n(S,R))\quad(n\geq1).\] The learner may depend on \(\mathcal H\), but not on \(D\).
cards.why: The problem asks whether exact empirical fitting is inherently compatible with the intuition that more independent data should improve expected predictions. It separates the behavior of ERM from general statistical consistency and from monotone wrappers that change the learning rule.

cards.title: Improper compression for Gaussian-mixture reconstruction
cards.formal: Does there exist one uniform randomized learning procedure with the following guarantee? For all integers \(d\ge1\), \(k>d\) and \(t\ge2\), and every Borel probability distribution \(D\) on the closed Euclidean unit ball \(B_d\), it learns a shared model \(w\) and an encoder–decoder pair \(E_w:B_d\to\{0,1\}^{b}\), \(Q_w:\{0,1\}^{b}\to B_d\) such that, with probability at least \(2/3\), \[\mathbb E_{x\sim D}\|Q_w(E_w(x))-x\|_2^{2}\le\operatorname{OPT}_k(D)+1/t,\qquad \operatorname{OPT}_k(D)=\inf_{\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_k\in B_d}\mathbb E_{x\sim D}\min_{i\in[k]}\|x-\mu_i\|_2^{2}?\] Training, sample count, model storage, encoding and decoding must all be polynomial in \(d,k,t\), while the number of bits per encoded point satisfies \(b\le C(1+\log_2 k+\log_2 t)^{q}\) for universal \(C,q>0\). This is the explicitly normalized, bounded-data version of the source's first reconstruction question, in the overcomplete regime \(k>d\).
cards.why: The task asks whether efficient unsupervised reconstruction can compete with a small optimal codebook while using only a polynomial in the logarithms of its size and accuracy per point. It separates the cost of discovering original mixture parameters from the cost of learning a useful compact representation.

cards.title: Statistical-query complexity of sparse halfspaces
cards.formal: Do there exist absolute constants \(C\ge 2\) and \(a,b>0\) such that, for every \(n\ge 2\) and \(1\le r\le n, SQ-DIM(Hn,r, 1/[C(r \log _{2} n)^{a}])\le C n^{b}\), where Hn,r is the class of r-sparse halfspaces on \(\{0,1\}^{n}\) and SQ-DIM is the distribution-worst-case correlation parameter defined below?
cards.why: Clarifies whether a statistical-query learner can exploit sparsity while tolerating coarse, sample-efficient estimates. The problem isolates an informational obstruction from the cost of reading many irrelevant coordinates, without assuming a favorable data distribution.

cards.title: Uniform convergence under Dobrushin dependence
cards.formal: For every \(a\in\)[0,1), does there exist a finite constant \(C_{a}\) such that the following holds uniformly? Let \(m\ge 1\), let H be a nonempty class of measurable binary functions on a measurable instance space X with finite VC dimension d, and let \(\mathrm{P}_{m}\) be a joint law of \(S=(Z_{1},\ldots ,Z_{m}), Z_{i}=(X_{i},Y_{i})\in X\times \{0,1\}\), whose marginals all equal D and whose total-variation Dobrushin coefficient is at most a. For every \(\delta \in (0,1)\), require \(\Pr _{S\sim \mathrm{P}_{m}}[\sup _{h\in H}|\mathrm{L}_{S}(h)- \mathrm{L}_{D}(h)|>C_{a}\sqrt{(d+\log (2/\delta ))/m}]\le \delta\). Here \(\mathrm{L}_{S}\) and \(\mathrm{L}_{D}\) are zero-one losses and the conditional-kernel and measurability conventions below are part of the model. This card reads the source’s proposed extension quantitatively, using the iid-order finite-VC rate stated in equation (18) of its full version; it is not merely a claim that some unspecified convergence rate exists.
cards.why: Would determine whether the standard weak-influence condition suffices for the uniform statistical guarantees that make finite VC dimension useful, beyond the already-known existence of a successful learner.

cards.title: Polynomial-time proper learning of Poisson binomial distributions
cards.formal: Is there a randomized proper learner which, given n≥1, rational \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\) and independent samples from an unknown sum of n independent Bernoulli variables, outputs with probability at least 2/3 a Poisson binomial distribution within total variation epsilon, using time and samples polynomial in \(\log(n+1)\) and \(1/\varepsilon\)?
cards.why: This asks whether the structural requirement on the output imposes more than polynomial learning cost.

cards.title: Longest-example memory for automatic learning
cards.formal: For every automatic language family learnable in the limit from positive texts by an automatic learner with unrestricted memory, does there exist an automatic learner for that family with memory length at most the length of the longest nonpause example seen so far plus a fixed constant?
cards.why: This asks whether extra memory genuinely increases the power of finite-state-style learning.

cards.title: Automatic iterative learning versus hypothesis-sized memory
cards.formal: Does there exist an automatic language family learnable in the limit from positive texts with automatic hypothesis-length-bounded memory, but not learnable by any automatic iterative learner even after changing to another automatic hypothesis space?
cards.why: The comparison isolates the informational power of auxiliary memory in constrained learning models.

cards.title: Identifiable elicitation complexity
cards.formal: Determine the identifiable elicitation-complexity function \(E(\mathcal P,\Gamma)\) defined below, throughout its full domain of nonempty convex families of real-outcome distributions and finite-dimensional statistical properties. Its value is the smallest positive number of intermediate real reports needed to recover \(\Gamma\) through an elicitable, identifiable property, or \(\infty\) if no finite number suffices. The numerical benchmark requires a real-valued approximation with absolute error at most \(1/100\) at every finite value, and a proof identifying exactly the infinite-value cases.
cards.why: A loss can recover a richer prediction than the statistic ultimately needed. The minimum dimension of that prediction measures an expressive limitation of loss-based estimation, independently of optimization time. A general classification would connect statistical functionals, forecast evaluation and the design of indirect prediction objectives.

cards.title: One-way functions from \(\mathrm{P} \ne  \mathrm{NP}\)
cards.formal:
Does \(\mathrm P\ne\mathrm{NP}\) imply the existence of a classical one-way function secure against uniform probabilistic polynomial-time inversion? Precisely, under that premise alone, must there exist one total deterministic polynomial-time computable function
\[f:\{0,1\}^{*}\longrightarrow\{0,1\}^{*}\]
such that, for every uniform probabilistic polynomial-time inverter \(I\) and every real constant \(c>0\), there is an integer \(N\ge1\) for which every \(n\ge N\) satisfies
\[\Pr_{x\sim U_n,\,r}\!\left[z\in\{0,1\}^{n}\ \land\ f(z)=f(x),\quad z=I(1^n,f(x);r)\right]\le n^{-c}?\]
Here \(U_n\) is the uniform distribution on length-\(n\) binary strings, and \(r\) denotes the inverter’s independent fair random coins. Finding any length-\(n\) preimage counts as successful inversion. The function must be fixed before the inverter and security exponent are chosen.
cards.why: One-way functions are a basic foundation for computational pseudorandomness and cryptography. This question asks whether a worst-case separation between decision and verification already forces a function whose efficiently generated outputs resist inversion on average, without a separate cryptographic assumption.

cards.title: Noninteractive SZK versus SZK
cards.formal: Does NISZK equal SZK? Equivalently, does there exist a uniform deterministic polynomial-time reduction that maps every promised pair of sampling circuits X,Y to a sampling circuit Z, preserving the near/far promises specified below?
cards.why: Determine the intrinsic role of interaction in information-theoretic zero-knowledge proofs.

cards.title: Public-key encryption from one-way functions
cards.formal: Does the existence of a classical cryptographic one-way function imply the existence of a classical public-key encryption scheme for one-bit messages, with negligible correctness error and security against every uniform probabilistic polynomial-time chosen-plaintext adversary, in the plain model specified below? This is an unrelativized existence implication. The construction and its security proof may inspect the program of the one-way function and need not be black-box.
cards.why: This asks whether the minimal generic assumption supporting private-key cryptography also supports encryption to a receiver whose encryption key is public. It tests whether the apparent need for additional structure in public-key constructions reflects a true difference in existence or only the known reductions. The distinction controls the foundational assumptions needed for confidential communication without a pre-existing shared secret.

cards.title: Circuit obfuscation from polynomial-hard LWE
cards.formal:
Does ordinary polynomial-hard decisional Learning With Errors imply indistinguishability obfuscation for all polynomial-size Boolean circuits, with no additional hardness, circular-security or leakage-resilience hypothesis?

Precisely, let \(H_{\mathrm{LWE}}\) be the fixed classical nonuniform decisional-LWE assumption below, with prime modulus \(q(n)\ge n^4\) and Gaussian width \(n\). Let \(I_{\mathrm{circ}}\) assert the existence of the uniform classical probabilistic obfuscator defined below, with security against all classical polynomial-size circuit families. The proposition to establish or refute is the implication
\[H_{\mathrm{LWE}}\ \Longrightarrow\ I_{\mathrm{circ}}.\]
All modulus, error, sample, correctness and security quantifiers are fixed in the definitions. Neither subexponential hardness nor additional information supplied about the LWE secret or errors is part of the premise.
cards.why: General indistinguishability obfuscation supports cryptographic capabilities well beyond ordinary encryption. Deriving it from one standard noisy-linear-equation assumption would connect that broad power to a much simpler foundation. The precise quantitative premise matters: an implication from stronger security or from secret-dependent hints does not determine the power of ordinary polynomial-hard LWE.

cards.title: Unleveled fully homomorphic encryption from LWE alone
cards.formal:
Does the ordinary polynomial-modulus decisional Learning With Errors assumption specified below imply the existence of a classical compact fully homomorphic public-key encryption scheme whose keys are generated without a bound on the size or depth of the circuits subsequently evaluated?

The scheme must be secure against nonuniform polynomial-size classical adversaries given both its encryption and evaluation keys. Its only hardness assumption may be the stated ordinary LWE assumption; no independent circular-security or key-dependent-message assumption is allowed.
cards.why: Determine whether ordinary LWE alone supports compact encrypted computation at arbitrary polynomial depth with one fixed key set.

cards.title: Sub-square-root share-size exponents in perfect secret sharing
cards.formal: Do there exist real constants \(K>0\) and \(0<c<1/2\) such that, for every \(n\ge 1\) and every monotone access structure \(\Gamma\) on \([n]\) with \(\varnothing \notin \Gamma\) and \([n]\in \Gamma\), there exists a perfect secret-sharing scheme for a uniform one-bit secret with \(\max _{i} \log _{2}|S_{i}|\le K\cdot 2^{cn}\), where \(S_{i}\) is the finite alphabet of participant i’s share?
cards.why: A worst-case storage benchmark for information-theoretic access control, separating the power of general secret sharing from linear schemes. The newly reported bound directly addresses its strict exponential threshold.

cards.title: Existence of one-way functions
cards.formal: Does there exist a total deterministic polynomial-time computable function \(f:\{0,1\}*\to \{0,1\}\)* such that, for every uniform probabilistic polynomial-time algorithm I and every integer \(d\ge 1\), there is \(n_{0}\) with \(\Pr [f(I(1^{n},f(X)))=f(X)]\le n^{- d}\) for all \(n\ge n_{0}\), where X is uniform on \(\{0,1\}^{n}\) and the probability also includes the independent random coins of I?
cards.why: Asks for the unconditional existence of the basic computational asymmetry underlying much of modern cryptography.

cards.title: Existence of public-key encryption
cards.formal: Do there exist uniform classical probabilistic polynomial-time algorithms Gen, Enc and Dec forming a public-key encryption scheme for one-bit messages with negligible correctness error and IND-CPA security against every uniform classical probabilistic polynomial-time adversary, with these properties proved without an unproved hardness assumption?
cards.why: Would establish the existence of secure public communication from a mathematical theorem rather than a computational assumption.

cards.title: Private PAC sample complexity from VC and Littlestone dimensions
cards.formal: Do there exist universal integers \(A,k\ge1\) such that every nonempty finite Boolean concept class \(\mathcal C\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\mathcal X}\) on a nonempty finite domain \(\mathcal X\), with \(v=\operatorname{VC}(\mathcal C)\ge1\) and \(d=\operatorname{LD}(\mathcal C)\ge1\), has a positive integer sample size \[m\le A\bigl(1+v+\log^{*}d\bigr)^{k}\] and a possibly improper learner \(L\) that is \((1,1/(100m^{2}))\)-differentially private and realizes the following PAC guarantee? For every distribution \(D\) on \(\mathcal X\) and every target \(h^{*}\in\mathcal C\), when \(L\) receives \(m\) independent samples \((x_i,h^{*}(x_i))\) with \(x_i\sim D\), its output \(\widehat h\) satisfies \[\Pr\!\left[\Pr_{x\sim D}[\widehat h(x)\ne h^{*}(x)]\le1/10\right]\ge9/10.\] The same \(m,L\) must work for all \(D,h^{*}\) for the chosen class. Their choice can depend on the complete class, but \(A,k\) cannot. Computation is unrestricted. This is the previously selected concrete polynomial-overhead version of the source question; the constant accuracy, confidence and sample-dependent privacy parameters are editorial specifications, not parameter values asserted in the source.
cards.why: The theorem characterizing whether private learning is possible leaves an enormous quantitative gap. This question asks whether the extra data needed for privacy is controlled by ordinary statistical complexity and an exceptionally slowly growing function of sequential complexity. A positive answer would put a uniform bound on that privacy overhead across all finite concept classes.

cards.title: Oblivious transfer from public-key encryption
cards.formal:
In the classical plain model, does the existence of public-key encryption secure against chosen-plaintext attacks imply the existence of 1-out-of-2 bit oblivious transfer secure against static semi-honest corruption of either party?

Let \(E\) assert the existence of the bit-encryption scheme defined below, and let \(T\) assert the existence of the two-party protocol and simulators defined below. The target is the unrelativized implication
\[E\ \Longrightarrow\ T.\]
All honest algorithms and simulators are uniform probabilistic polynomial-time classical machines; security is against arbitrary nonuniform polynomial-size classical circuit families. The implication may use the full code of the encryption algorithms, non-black-box reasoning and polynomially many messages. It must not assume an additional property of encryption unless that property is proved to follow from the stated premise.
cards.why: Public-key encryption protects a message from someone without its decryption key. Oblivious transfer must also protect a sender from a receiver who is entitled to learn one selected message, while hiding that selection from the sender. Determining whether the first capability already implies the second would clarify a basic boundary between secure communication and general private computation.

cards.title: Key agreement from one-way functions
cards.formal: Does the existence of a classical one-way function imply the existence of a classical two-party key-agreement protocol in the plain public-channel model below? The parties must output \(\lambda\)-bit keys with negligible disagreement, and either honest key must be computationally indistinguishable from an independent uniform key given the entire public transcript. This is the unrelativized existence implication, allowing arbitrary constructions and security proofs, including those that inspect the program implementing the one-way function.
cards.why: This asks whether generic computational one-wayness suffices for two strangers to establish a shared classical secret through publicly visible interaction. It separates the minimal hardness underlying symmetric cryptography from the additional structure used for secret establishment, while allowing more interaction than public-key encryption. A resolution would determine whether that foundational gap concerns existence itself or the known forms of cryptographic reductions.

cards.title: One-way permutations from one-way functions
cards.formal: Does the existence of a classical one-way function secure against every nonuniform polynomial-size classical adversary imply the existence of an efficiently generated public-key family of one-way permutations on full Boolean cubes, with the same adversary convention? Require a bijection on the entire cube for every key the generator can output, and negligible inversion probability averaged over an honestly generated public key and a uniform input. No trapdoor is required.
cards.why: Determine whether basic average-case inversion hardness necessarily supports efficient bijections, a rigid primitive at the foundation of cryptographic constructions.

cards.title: Collision-resistant hashing from one-way functions
cards.formal:
In the ordinary classical computational model, is the following existence implication true?
\[\bigl(\exists f\;\operatorname{OWF}(f)\bigr)\ \Longrightarrow\ \bigl(\exists\operatorname{Gen},H\;\operatorname{CRH}(\operatorname{Gen},H)\bigr).\]
The predicates are defined below. The honest functions and algorithms are uniform and polynomial-time, and security is against every nonuniform family of polynomial-size classical Boolean circuits. The hash family has a freshly sampled public key \(k\) and maps \(H_k:\{0,1\}^{2\lambda}\to\{0,1\}^{\lambda}\) for every positive integer security parameter \(\lambda\). Both members of a proposed collision may be chosen after the key is known. The implication permits unrestricted constructions and proof techniques, including use of a one-way function's implementation.
cards.why: Determines whether a fundamental compressing cryptographic primitive needs assumptions beyond ordinary one-wayness, while exposing the gap between known black-box barriers and unrestricted constructions.

cards.title: Noninteractive zero knowledge from one-way functions
cards.formal: Does the existence of a classical one-way function imply the existence of a reusable, adaptively secure noninteractive zero-knowledge argument for Boolean circuit satisfiability in the honestly generated common-reference-string model? Require computational soundness and computational zero knowledge against every nonuniform polynomial-size classical adversary, with negligible errors and one public proof message per statement. The implication may use the code of the one-way function and has no black-box restriction.
cards.why: Determine whether the minimal assumption supporting basic cryptography is sufficient for reusable, publicly verifiable proofs that reveal no witness and require no online interaction.

cards.title: Fully homomorphic encryption from public-key encryption
cards.formal: Does the existence of IND-CPA-secure public-key bit encryption imply the existence of an IND-CPA-secure, compact, unleveled fully homomorphic bit-encryption scheme for every polynomial-size Boolean circuit, with the algorithms and security convention below?
cards.why: Determine whether computation over encrypted data requires fundamentally more than public-key confidentiality.

cards.title: Succinct noninteractive arguments for NP from LWE alone
cards.formal: Does the specified ordinary LWE assumption imply a noninteractive succinct argument for every NP relation in the common-reference-string model, with adaptive soundness and proof length polynomial in lambda and log T for T-step witness verification?
cards.why: This asks whether one standard assumption suffices for very short general computational proofs.

cards.title: Polynomial-time private release of all marginals
cards.formal: Do there exist an integer \(C\ge1\), a function \(\alpha:\mathbb N_{\ge2}\to[0,1]\) with \(\lim_{d\to\infty}\alpha(d)=0\), a uniform randomized mechanism \(M\), and a uniform deterministic evaluator \(E\) satisfying the following statement? For every integer \(d\ge2\), put \(n=d^{C}\). For every explicitly given database \(D\in(\{0,1\}^{d})^{n}\), \(M(d,D)\) runs in worst-case time polynomial in \(n+d\), satisfies \((1,1/(100n^{2}))\)-differential privacy under replacement of one row, and outputs a finite binary synopsis \(S\). With probability at least \(2/3\) over \(M\)'s random bits, this one synopsis satisfies \[\left|E(d,S,J,a)-q_{J,a}(D)\right|\le\alpha(d)\] simultaneously for every \(J\subseteq[d]\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}^{J}\). The evaluator runs in worst-case time polynomial in \(d+|S|\), outputs a binary-encoded rational, and has no further access to the database. The synopsis may be arbitrary: it need not be synthetic data or describe a consistent probability distribution.
cards.why: Marginals are basic summaries of relationships among attributes. The question asks whether the large information-theoretic usefulness of private high-dimensional data can be captured by a compact, efficiently evaluated object using polynomially many records. It isolates a statistical-versus-computational gap for a concrete query family while allowing outputs more flexible than synthetic datasets.

cards.title: Chosen-ciphertext security from ordinary public-key encryption
cards.formal: Does the existence of an IND-CPA-secure public-key encryption scheme imply the existence of an IND-CCA2-secure public-key encryption scheme in the plain model, with correctness and classical security as defined below, against all nonuniform polynomial-size adversaries? The sole premise is ordinary chosen-plaintext-secure public-key encryption, and the conclusion is full adaptive chosen-ciphertext security with no fixed bound on an attacker's polynomial number of decryption queries.
cards.why: Determine whether public-key confidentiality alone can always be strengthened to resist adaptive decryption attacks, without importing another cryptographic assumption.

cards.title: One-way functions from errorless average-case NP hardness
cards.formal: Is the following implication true? \[(\mathrm{NP},\mathrm{PSamp})\not\subseteq\mathrm{AvgP}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\text{there exists a classical one-way function}.\] Here the antecedent means that some fixed NP language, under some fixed polynomial-time samplable distribution ensemble, has no deterministic exact decider with average polynomial running time in the moment sense below. The conclusion asks for a total polynomial-time computable function \(f:\{0,1\}^{*}\to\{0,1\}^{*}\) such that, for every uniform probabilistic polynomial-time inverter \(I\) and every integer \(c\ge1\), there exists \(n_0\) for which, for every \(n\ge n_0\), \[\Pr_{x\sim U_n,\ I}\bigl[|z|=n\ \land\ f(z)=f(x)\bigr]\le n^{-c},\qquad z\leftarrow I(1^n,f(x)).\] The statement is unrelativized and has no additional hardness, derandomization or cryptographic assumption.
cards.why: A problem can be difficult to decide on typical efficiently generated inputs without obviously providing an efficiently computed map that is hard to invert. Connecting these two kinds of difficulty would clarify the minimum computational assumptions needed for classical cryptography. The precise decision-error and security-length conventions are essential to that comparison.

cards.title: Average-case RSA inversion versus factoring for exponent 65537
cards.formal: For the fixed exponent \(e=65537\) and the balanced-prime ensemble below, does the existence of a uniform randomized polynomial-time RSA inverter with inverse-polynomial average success imply the existence of a uniform randomized polynomial-time factoring algorithm with inverse-polynomial average success?
cards.why: Identify the computational assumption underlying one of the central public-key primitives.

cards.title: Public-key quantum money from LWE alone
cards.formal: Does quantum hardness of the fixed decisional Learning with Errors distributions below imply the existence of a reusable, unforgeable public-key quantum money scheme in the plain computational model? The scheme must have a static classical public key, polynomial-time quantum minting and verification, and security against every nonuniform polynomial-size quantum adversary with classical advice.
cards.why: Ground publicly verifiable unclonable quantum states in a standard lattice assumption, resolving a central assumption gap in quantum cryptography.

cards.title: Witness encryption from plain LWE
cards.formal: Assuming the specified polynomial-modulus decisional LWE hardness, does every polynomial-time NP witness relation admit standard-model witness encryption with correctness for valid witnesses and message indistinguishability on false instances?
cards.why: This asks for the minimal assumptions needed to encrypt against the existence of mathematical witnesses.

cards.title: General functional encryption from plain LWE
cards.formal: Does the specified ordinary decisional LWE assumption imply public-key functional encryption for all polynomial-size Boolean circuits, with adaptive indistinguishability security against arbitrarily polynomially many colluding functional-key queries?
cards.why: This asks whether a central lattice assumption supports general fine-grained access to encrypted data.

cards.title: Optimal error for pure-DP continual counting
cards.formal: Determine, up to universal constant factors as \(T\to \infty , E(T)=\inf _{M} \max _{x\in \{0,1\}^{T}} E_{Y\sim M_{x}}[\max _{1\le t\le T}|Y_{t}- \sum_{i=1}^{t} x_{i}|]\), where the infimum is over all causal \((1/2,0)\)-differentially private mechanisms defined below.
cards.why: Determines the minimax cost of repeatedly publishing a running count while protecting each individual event under pure privacy. It separates guarantees for the whole observed trajectory from per-time or average accuracy.

cards.title: Additive privacy cost for adversarial bandits
cards.formal: Does there exist a pure centrally \(\varepsilon\)-differentially private adversarial-bandit algorithm, absolute constants \(C,p\ge0\), and a finite nonnegative function \(F(K,\varepsilon)\), independent of the horizon, such that for every \(K\ge2\), \(T\ge1\), \(0<\varepsilon\le1\) and oblivious loss array, its expected regret is at most \[C\sqrt{KT}\,(\log(2+KT))^p+F(K,\varepsilon)(\log(2+T))^p?\] This is the broad additive-separation question; no particular polynomial dependence of \(F\) is required.
cards.why: This asks whether privacy adds a separate cost or fundamentally multiplies the difficulty of adversarial learning.

cards.title: Pseudorandom functions from worst-case hardness of learning
cards.formal:
For every circuit class
\[
\mathcal C\in\{\mathrm{AC}^0,\ \mathrm{AC}^0[p]\ (p\text{ any fixed prime}),\
\mathrm{ACC}^0,\ \mathrm{TC}^0,\ \mathrm{NC}^1,\
\mathrm{Formula},\ \mathrm{Circuit}\},
\]
does the following implication hold?
\[
\neg\operatorname{Learn}_{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathcal C)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{PRF}_{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathcal C).
\]
Here learning means uniform randomized polynomial-time improper learning under the uniform input distribution, with adaptive membership queries. The conclusion is a uniformly polynomial-time samplable family of functions computed by polynomial-size \(\mathcal C\)-circuits, secure against every uniform probabilistic polynomial-time oracle distinguisher. Both notions are defined below.

The hypothesis is only worst-case failure of learning: each candidate learner may fail on its own target function. No efficiently samplable common distribution of hard targets is assumed.
cards.why: A function class may resist every efficient learner without coming with a usable way to sample difficult targets. Cryptographic pseudorandomness requires a single efficient sampling procedure whose outputs defeat every efficient observer. The question asks whether the first obstruction alone supplies the second object within the same class.

cards.title: Low-noise LPN hardness from Nearest Codeword hardness
cards.formal:
Does the following implication hold?
\[
\operatorname{NCP}_2\notin\mathrm{BPP}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\forall D\in\mathrm{PPT}\ \forall c>0\ \exists n_0\ge9\ \forall n\ge n_0:
\quad n\text{ a square}\ \Longrightarrow\ \operatorname{Adv}_D(n)<n^{-c}.
\]
Here \(\operatorname{NCP}_2\) is the unrestricted binary Nearest Codeword decision problem defined below. The distinguisher receives either \((A,As+e)\) or \((A,u)\), with a uniform \(n^2\times n\) binary matrix, independent uniform secret and comparison vector, and independent noise bits of probability \(1/\sqrt n\). The conclusion requires negligible advantage at all sufficiently large square dimensions for every uniform classical probabilistic polynomial-time distinguisher.
cards.why: A basic security assumption would obtain an explanation through independently studied hardness. The extra assumption in the new reduction makes the remaining target concrete.

cards.title: Unbounded fully homomorphic encryption from polynomial-factor GapSVP
cards.formal: Does there exist a classical compact fully homomorphic public-key encryption scheme, with keys generated without any circuit-depth bound, and an integer \(a\ge1\), such that there is a quantum polynomial-time reduction from solving worst-case Euclidean \(\mathrm{GapSVP}_{n^a}\) to breaking its chosen-plaintext security, in the precise sense below? The scheme must support every polynomial-size Boolean circuit using the same key-generation algorithm. No independent circular-security or other cryptographic assumption may be used. A quantum reduction is permitted, while key generation, encryption, homomorphic evaluation and decryption are classical.
cards.why: Leveled encryption chooses its keys for a known computation depth. This asks for one reusable key setup supporting arbitrary polynomial-depth computation, with a security proof grounded entirely in a standard worst-case lattice problem.

cards.title: One-way functions in \(\mathrm{NC}^{0}\) from one-way functions
cards.formal:
Does the existence of a classical one-way function imply the existence of a classical one-way function computed by a polynomial-time uniform \(\mathrm{NC}^{0}\) circuit family? With the definitions below, the proposition is
\[
\bigl[\exists f\;\mathrm{OWF}(f)\bigr]
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\bigl[\exists g\;\mathrm{OWF}(g)\land\mathrm{PUniformNC}^{0}(g)\bigr].
\]
Both sides require security against every nonuniform polynomial-size classical circuit family. The conclusion asks for the existence of some such \(g\), with some constant depth and some polynomial bounds. These constants may depend on \(g\), but not on its input length or on an adversary. There is no additional assumption on the starting function's circuit depth, no requirement that \(f\) and \(g\) have the same input or output lengths, and no requirement of a black-box construction or an efficient compiler from descriptions of \(f\).
cards.why: The question tests whether the minimal computational assumption underlying much of cryptography already guarantees functions with constant-depth local evaluation. A positive answer would make this extreme parallelism available under the general one-way-function assumption; a negative answer would separate local cryptographic hardness from unrestricted polynomial-time cryptographic hardness.

cards.title: Verifiable random functions from one-way functions alone
cards.formal: Does the existence of arbitrary one-way functions imply a standard-model verifiable random function on all lambda-bit inputs with adaptive pseudorandomness and perfect uniqueness even for malformed public keys?
cards.why: The question tests whether public verifiability requires stronger assumptions than ordinary private pseudorandomness.

cards.title: Blind signatures from one-way functions alone
cards.formal: Does the existence of arbitrary one-way functions imply a classical plain-model blind-signature scheme with concurrent blindness and one-more unforgeability, allowing polynomially many interaction rounds and non-black-box constructions?
cards.why: This asks how little computational hardness suffices for anonymous authenticated transactions.

cards.title: Optimal regret for private stochastic online learning
cards.formal: Determine, up to universal constant factors, the optimal expected pseudo-regret \(R^{*}(K,T,\varepsilon,\Delta)\) for pure differentially private stochastic full-information online learning. The domain is integers \(K\ge2\), \(T\ge1\), and real parameters \(\varepsilon>0\), \(0<\Delta\le1\). For independent loss distributions \(P_1,\ldots,P_K\) on \([0,1]\), let \(\mu_j=\mathbb E_{P_j}[L]\); require a unique minimizer \(j^{*}\) and \(\mu_j-\mu_{j^{*}}\ge\Delta\) for every \(j\ne j^{*}\). At round \(t\), select \(I_t\in[K]\) using only earlier observations and private randomness, incur loss \(L_{I_t,t}\), and then observe the entire vector \(L_t\), where all \(L_{j,t}\sim P_j\) are independent across actions and rounds. Put \[R^{*}(K,T,\varepsilon,\Delta)=\inf_A\sup_{(P_1,\ldots,P_K)}\mathbb E\!\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T}(\mu_{I_t}-\mu_{j^{*}})\right],\] where the supremum ranges over the promised product distributions and the infimum over the causal \(\varepsilon\)-private strategies defined below. The requested rate retains every dependence on \(K,T,\varepsilon,\Delta\), including logarithmic factors and the small-horizon regime.
cards.why: This asks how protecting one round of observations changes the achievable accuracy of sequential decisions even when the environment is stationary and all actions are observed. A sharp rate would identify the statistical price of pure privacy and whether the remaining dependence on the number of actions is necessary.

cards.title: PZK versus SZK
cards.formal: Is \(\mathrm{PZK}=\mathrm{SZK}\) for classical single-prover interactive proofs of promise problems in the precise input-only simulation model below? Both classes use uniform polynomial-time verifiers and simulators, negligible completeness and soundness errors, and zero knowledge against every uniform probabilistic polynomial-time verifier. Perfect simulation may output a failure symbol with probability at most \(1/2\); conditioned on success its distribution must be exactly correct. Statistical simulation permits negligible total variation distance.
cards.why: Determine whether allowing any negligible statistical simulation error increases the expressive power of information-theoretic zero-knowledge proofs.

cards.title: Identity-based encryption from arbitrary public-key encryption
cards.formal: Does the existence of IND-CPA-secure public-key bit encryption imply an adaptively IND-ID-CPA-secure identity-based bit-encryption scheme for identity space \(\{0,1\}^{\lambda}\) with polynomial-size public parameters, under the classical standard-model conventions below?
cards.why: Compare the assumptions needed for basic encryption and large-scale identity-based access control.

cards.title: Dual pseudorandom functions from arbitrary one-way functions
cards.formal: Does the existence of arbitrary one-way functions imply a uniformly efficiently computable dual pseudorandom function family F_lambda:{0,1}^lambda × {0,1}^lambda to {0,1}^lambda with adaptive oracle security in each orientation?
cards.why: Dual pseudorandomness tests how much symmetric cryptographic structure follows from the weakest standard hardness primitive.

cards.title: Compact general-circuit homomorphic secret sharing from DDH
cards.formal: Editorial independent-client variant: does DDH imply two-server, one-private additive homomorphic secret sharing for arbitrary polynomial-size Boolean circuits, with independently shared input bits and output shares of size independent of the evaluated circuit?
cards.why: This asks whether general secure evaluation can be supported under a substantially different assumption from those used for full homomorphic encryption.

cards.title: Constant-round concurrent zero knowledge from LWE alone
cards.formal: Does the specified ordinary LWE assumption imply a constant-round plain-model concurrent zero-knowledge argument for every NP relation, with no a priori bound on polynomially many interleaved sessions and with expected-polynomial-time simulation?
cards.why: The target combines minimal assumptions, concurrency and a constant interaction cost.

cards.title: Doubly efficient PIR with quasilinear server preprocessing
cards.formal: Under the specified Ring-LWE assumption, is there unkeyed single-server PIR on every N-bit database with deterministic server-only preprocessing time and storage N times poly(lambda,log N), and worst-case online client/server time, communication and client workspace poly(lambda,log N)?
cards.why: The question asks whether privacy-preserving database access can have almost optimal preparation as well as fast queries.

cards.title: Polynomial-time computationally sound verification of \(\#\mathrm{SAT}\)
cards.formal: Do there exist deterministic uniform algorithms \(P,V\), integers \(C>c\ge1\), and a constant \(K\ge2\) giving the following plain-model argument system for exact \(\#\mathrm{SAT}\), without unproved hardness assumptions? On a Boolean formula \(\Phi\) encoded in \(N\) bits, \(P\) produces a proof of length at most \((N+1)^C\) in time \(T_P(N)=2^{K(N+1)^c}\). The verifier runs in time \(K(N+1)^C\) and outputs either the exact number of satisfying assignments or the rejection symbol \(\bot\). Completeness requires \(V(\Phi,P(\Phi))=\#\mathrm{SAT}(\Phi)\) on every valid formula. Soundness requires that every uniform randomized adversary running in any fixed polynomial in \(T_P(N)\) has only negligible probability, as a function of \(T_P(N)\), of generating a length-\(N\) formula and a proof on which \(V\) outputs an incorrect number. This card fixes the unconditional version of the source question; conditional constructions are recorded below.
cards.why: Exact counting requires certifying that no satisfying assignments were missed, as well as that counted assignments exist. This question tests whether computational soundness can give deterministic short verification of such global information while retaining an honest prover with a specified running time. It connects the power of proof systems with derandomization and the distinction between uniform computational attacks and arbitrary false witnesses.

cards.title: Exponentially hard weak versus strong one-way functions
cards.formal: Does the existence of an exponentially hard weak one-way function imply the existence of an exponentially hard strong one-way function, in the following nonuniform-adversary, negligible-success formulation? The premise is that there exist a uniform polynomial-time computable length-preserving function \(f\), a real \(a>0\), an integer \(k\ge1\), and \(n_0\), such that \[\operatorname{Inv}_f(C,n)\le1-n^{-k}\] for every \(n\ge n_0\) and every circuit \(C\) with \(n\) inputs, \(n\) outputs and at most \(2^{an}\) gates. The desired conclusion is that there exist another uniform polynomial-time computable length-preserving function \(g\) and a real \(b>0\) such that, for every integer \(d\ge1\), there is \(n_d\) with \[\operatorname{Inv}_g(C,n)\le n^{-d}\] for every \(n\ge n_d\) and every such circuit with at most \(2^{bn}\) gates. The constants and function in the conclusion may depend on those witnessing the premise.
cards.why: Ordinary hardness amplification equates weak and strong one-wayness at polynomial security scales. Preserving hardness exponential in the actual input length would extend that equivalence to a much stronger regime and clarify how fine-grained average-case hardness supports cryptographic security.

cards.title: Linear-seed pseudorandom generators from one-way functions
cards.formal:
Can every efficiently evaluable length-preserving one-way function be converted into a fully explicit pseudorandom generator with seed length linear in the function's input length, while retaining the following quantitative security?

Precisely, for every integer \(b\ge1\), do there exist integers \(A,K,q,r\ge1\), \(\ell_0\ge4\), and one deterministic compiler \(\mathcal B_b\) such that the following holds? Its input is a Boolean circuit \(F:\{0,1\}^{\ell}\to\{0,1\}^{\ell}\) of size at most \(\ell^b\), integers \(\ell\ge\ell_0\), \(1\le s\le2^{2\ell}\), \(m>A\ell\), and \(1\le e\le2\ell\). Write
\[
 \varepsilon=2^{-e},\qquad
 t=\left\lfloor\frac{s}{K(m2^e)^q}\right\rfloor,
\]
and require \(t\ge1\). Suppose every inversion circuit \(I\) of size at most \(s\) satisfies
\[
 \Pr_{x\leftarrow U_{\ell}}[F(I(F(x)))=F(x)]\le\frac12.
\]
The compiler must produce a circuit \(G:\{0,1\}^{d}\to\{0,1\}^{m}\), with \(1\le d\le A\ell<m\), in at most \(K(m+1)^r\) bit operations, such that every Boolean distinguishing circuit \(T\) of size at most \(t\) satisfies
\[
 \left|\Pr[T(G(U_d))=1]-\Pr[T(U_m)=1]\right|\le\varepsilon.
\]
The construction may depend on \(s\) and \(\varepsilon\): a separate generator is permitted for each requested pair of these parameters.
cards.why: The amount of true randomness needed by a cryptographic generator can determine whether a hardness assumption yields an efficient deterministic simulation. The question asks whether arbitrary one-way functions support the same linear seed scale available in more structured cases without discarding the quantitative hardness guarantee.

cards.title: Optimal private sample complexity for nonsmooth nonconvex optimization
cards.formal: Editorial zero-order variant: determine the sample complexity of uniformly polynomial-time central \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-private algorithms returning \(X\in\mathbb R^d\) with \[\mathbb E\,\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial_\alpha F(X))\le\beta\] for all population objectives in the normalized class below. Determine matching upper and lower bounds up to factors polynomial in \(\log(2+d+1/\alpha+1/\beta+1/\varepsilon+1/\delta)\). Expectation includes the independent dataset and algorithm randomness.
cards.why: The tradeoff connects privacy, statistical sample size and a general notion of stationarity beyond smooth optimization.

cards.title: Efficient split-state non-malleable codes approaching capacity
cards.formal: Do uniform polynomial-time two-share nonmalleable codes exist with k message bits, equal share length ell(k), negligible statistical error in k, and rate k/(2 ell(k)) tending to 1/2 as k tends to infinity, against all independent tampering functions on the two shares?
cards.why: This asks whether efficient split-state coding can reach its information-theoretic capacity.

cards.title: Subpolynomial-key perfectly secure three-server DPFs
cards.formal: Does there exist a fixed finite Abelian group \(G\), with \(|G|\ge2\), and a uniform three-server distributed point function with perfect correctness, perfect privacy against any one server, and worst-case key length \(\ell(N)=N^{o(1)}\)? For every integer \(N\ge2\), location \(\alpha\in[N]\), and value \(\beta\in G\), key generation must produce three binary keys \((k_0,k_1,k_2)\) such that \[\sum_{i=0}^{2}\operatorname{Eval}_i(k_i,x)=\begin{cases}\beta&x=\alpha,\\0_G&x\ne\alpha\end{cases}\qquad\text{for every }x\in[N]\] with probability one. For each individual \(i\), the distribution of \(k_i\) must be identical for all pairs \((\alpha,\beta)\) with the same \(N\). Every generated key must have at most \(\ell(N)\) bits. The fixed output group may be chosen as part of a positive answer; requiring all output groups is the source's separate question.
cards.why: Distributed point functions compress secret shares of a sparse vector while letting each holder evaluate its share locally. Resolving the three-server question would locate a basic boundary for information-theoretic compression and privacy, with consequences for private retrieval and secure computation that use additive reconstruction.

cards.title: Unconditional zero knowledge for gap circuit complexity
cards.formal: Is there a fixed rational \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)\) for which \(\mathrm{Gap}_{\varepsilon}\mathrm{MCSP}\) admits a computational zero-knowledge interactive proof system without a computational hardness assumption? Given the length-\(N=2^n\) truth table of a Boolean function, the promise distinguishes circuit size at most \(N^\varepsilon\) from size greater than \(N^{1-\varepsilon}\). This card selects the MCSP branch of the original question and the gap family used by Hirahara and Nanashima; it does not claim equivalence with every MINKT or other gap variant.
cards.why: Would provide a natural unconditional zero-knowledge protocol for a central problem about circuit descriptions. It probes the connection between worst-case complexity, average-case cryptographic hardness and verification that reveals no efficiently usable information beyond the claim.

cards.title: Sublinear communication for perfectly secure two-party computation
cards.formal: Is there a uniform two-party protocol in the trusted correlated-randomness model that perfectly computes every Boolean circuit \(C:\{0,1\}^n\times\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}\) with polynomial setup and computation, and online communication \(O(n+g(s))\) for some function \(g(s)=o(s)\), where \(s\) is the circuit's supplied size? More precisely, seek fixed algorithms, constants \(K,q\ge1\), and \(g:\mathbb N_{\ge1}\to\mathbb R_{\ge1}\) with \(\lim_{s\to\infty}g(s)/s=0\), such that every circuit and every pair of inputs satisfy the correctness and privacy conditions below; dealer computation, total setup length and both parties' computation are at most \(K(n+s+1)^q\), while at most \(K(n+g(s))\) bits are exchanged online. The circuit is arbitrary, without a layering or depth restriction. The additive input-length term fixes the source's sublinearity question in a form that also covers circuits of linear size.
cards.why: Standard perfectly private evaluation pays communication proportional to circuit size, even after preprocessing. A general sublinear protocol would show that polynomial preprocessing can reduce this online cost without relying on conjectured cryptographic hardness. A lower bound would expose a fundamental limit on what preprocessing can achieve, beyond the extreme regime of exactly optimal communication.

cards.title: Quantum PCP conjecture with classical reductions
cards.formal:
Do there exist fixed positive integers \(k,d\) and a rational constant \(0<\varepsilon<1\) for which the following promise problem \(\mathrm{LH}_{k,d,\varepsilon}\) is QMA-hard under deterministic classical polynomial-time many-one reductions? An instance specifies \(n\geq1\) qubits, \(1\leq m\leq(n+1)^d\) local terms \(H_1,\ldots,H_m\), and rational thresholds \(0\leq a<b\leq1\) with \(b-a\geq\varepsilon\). Each term acts on at most \(k\) qubits, has rational real and imaginary matrix entries, and satisfies \(0\preceq H_i\preceq I\). For the normalized Hamiltonian
\[H=\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m H_i,\]
distinguish \(\lambda_{\min}(H)\leq a\) from \(\lambda_{\min}(H)\geq b\). The classical reduction requirement preserves the saved card’s variant; the cited survey’s standard formulation permits quantum reductions.
cards.why: This asks whether coarse average-energy estimation retains the full difficulty of verification with an arbitrary quantum witness. The per-term normalization prevents a numerical rescaling from creating the required gap. A positive result would give a robust quantum analogue of classical constraint-satisfaction hardness, with consequences for the computational structure of low-energy states. The saved classical-reduction version additionally requires that the hard physical instance be produced without quantum computation.

cards.title: BPP versus BQP
cards.formal:
Is \(\mathrm{BPP}\subsetneq\mathrm{BQP}\)? Equivalently, does there exist one total decision language
\[L\subseteq\{0,1\}^{*}\quad\text{such that}\quad L\in\mathrm{BQP}\ \text{and}\ L\notin\mathrm{BPP}?\]
Both classes require a correct membership bit with probability at least \(2/3\) separately on every input. The quantum and classical models are uniform and have fixed polynomial resource bounds as defined below. The established containment \(\mathrm{BPP}\subseteq\mathrm{BQP}\) makes equality the other possible answer.
cards.why: This asks whether quantum computation expands the set of efficiently decidable total problems beyond classical randomization. It identifies the exact classical lower bound needed to turn an efficient quantum decision algorithm into an unconditional separation of computational power.

cards.title: Information-theoretic classical verification of quantum computation
cards.formal:
Can a completely classical verifier check arbitrary efficient quantum computation by interacting with one efficient quantum prover, with soundness against every computationally unbounded cheating prover?

The common input is an explicitly encoded quantum circuit \(C\) over \(\{H,T,\mathrm{CNOT}\}\), with all qubits initially zero and a designated output qubit.
