Write \(N\) for its description length and \(p(C)\) for the probability that measuring that output in the computational basis gives one. The promise is
\[C\in\mathrm{YES}\iff p(C)\ge 2/3,\qquad C\in\mathrm{NO}\iff p(C)\le 1/3.\]
Does there exist one uniform interactive protocol \((P,V)\) and positive integer constants \(a,d\) with the following properties? The verifier \(V\) is a classical probabilistic machine; the honest prover \(P\) is a quantum machine with classical control. They exchange only classical messages with no setup or extra prover. Both honest computations, the verifier against every cheating strategy, the number of messages and total communication have the polynomial bounds specified below. For every promised circuit,
\[C\in\mathrm{YES}\ \Longrightarrow\ \Pr[V\text{ accepts in interaction with }P\text{ on }C]\ge2/3,\]
\[C\in\mathrm{NO}\ \Longrightarrow\ \forall P^*\quad\Pr[V\text{ accepts in interaction with }P^*\text{ on }C]\le1/3.\]
Here \(P^*\) ranges over all adaptive response strategies, without any computational bound. The protocol and the constants precede the quantifiers over inputs and cheating strategies.
cards.why: The question isolates the resources needed for a classical user to trust a quantum answer. Known protocols obtain trust by giving the verifier some quantum capability, separating several devices, or assuming that particular computations are hard for an attacker. Resolving the stated conjunction would determine whether any of those additional resources is necessary when the honest server itself remains efficient.

cards.title: NP outside BQP
cards.formal:
Is \(\mathrm{NP}\not\subseteq\mathrm{BQP}\)? That is, does there exist a total decision language
\[L\subseteq\{0,1\}^{*}\quad\text{with}\quad L\in\mathrm{NP}\ \text{and}\ L\notin\mathrm{BQP}?\]
Equivalently, is the total language \(3\text{-}\mathrm{SAT}\) defined below outside \(\mathrm{BQP}\)? The negation is that every language with polynomially bounded classical certificates and a polynomial-time classical verifier has a uniform bounded-error quantum polynomial-time decider. This is noncontainment, not merely inequality of two classes.
cards.why: This asks whether efficient classical verification always permits efficient quantum decision. Noncontainment would identify a limit even for ideal scalable quantum computers and would also imply P differs from NP. Containment would place all classically verifiable decision problems within quantum polynomial time.

cards.title: QMA versus QCMA
cards.formal: Is \(\mathrm{QMA}=\mathrm{QCMA}\) for ordinary promise problems without an oracle? Equivalently, does every promise problem that has a uniform polynomial-time quantum verifier with polynomially many quantum witness qubits also have such a verifier with only polynomially many classical witness bits, with completeness at least \(2/3\) and soundness at most \(1/3\)? The converse inclusion is available by measuring a purported classical witness in the computational basis, so the requested equality is exactly the inclusion \(\mathrm{QMA}\subseteq\mathrm{QCMA}\).
cards.why: This asks whether an untrusted quantum state can certify something that no short classical message can certify, even when the recipient already has a quantum computer. It isolates the power of the evidence itself from the power of the verifier and is a basic boundary in quantum complexity.

cards.title: Computability of quantum channel capacity
cards.formal: Does there exist a single deterministic classical Turing algorithm that, for every valid finite description of a memoryless finite-dimensional quantum channel \(\Phi\) specified below and every positive rational \(\varepsilon\), halts and outputs a rational \(r\) satisfying \(|r-Q(\Phi)|\le\varepsilon\)? Here \(Q\) is unassisted, vanishing-error quantum capacity in qubits per channel use. The algorithm must work for all valid descriptions and all positive requested accuracies; there is no time or space bound beyond eventual halting.
cards.why: Determine whether the fundamental reliable quantum communication rate is algorithmically accessible even without efficiency constraints.

cards.title: QMA versus \(\mathrm{QMA}(2)\)
cards.formal: Is \(\mathrm{QMA}(2)=\mathrm{QMA}\) for ordinary uniform promise problems without an oracle? A QMA(2) verifier receives two polynomial-length quantum witnesses that are promised to be unentangled across the two witness registers, even on a no-instance. A QMA verifier receives one arbitrary polynomial-length quantum witness. The easy inclusion \(\mathrm{QMA}\subseteq\mathrm{QMA}(2)\) follows by ignoring a second witness; the question is whether every QMA(2) promise problem is also in QMA under the definitions below.
cards.why: This asks whether a promise of independence between two untrusted quantum messages can increase what an efficient quantum computer can verify. It connects computational verification with the geometry of entanglement and separates the value of unentanglement from simply supplying more qubits.

cards.title: Dihedral hidden subgroup problem in BQP
cards.formal: Does there exist one uniform quantum algorithm and integers \(C,c\ge1\) such that, for every integer \(N\ge2\), every integer \(\ell\ge1\), every subgroup \(H\le D_N\), and every function \(f:D_N\to\{0,1\}^{\ell}\) hiding \(H\) as defined below, the algorithm outputs a finite list generating exactly \(H\) with probability at least \(2/3\), using at most \(C(\lceil\log_2N\rceil+\ell+2)^c\) total operations? The only external quantum oracle is the reversible evaluation of \(f\). The bound is uniform over subgroup and hiding-function choices and includes both oracle calls and all other computation.
cards.why: A central test for quantum algorithms beyond abelian Fourier sampling. The information can be acquired with few queries, but extracting the subgroup efficiently remains a fundamental computational challenge with lattice-related consequences under the appropriate reductions.

cards.title: Graph isomorphism in BQP
cards.formal: Does the ordinary graph-isomorphism decision problem belong to \(\mathrm{BQP}\), bounded-error quantum polynomial time? That is, do there exist one uniform quantum algorithm and integers \(C,c\ge1\) such that, for every pair of finite simple graphs given by their complete binary adjacency matrices, the algorithm decides whether a vertex bijection preserves adjacency, with error at most \(1/3\), using at most \(C(n+2)^c\) total elementary operations, where \(n\) is the larger vertex count? No distributional or structural promise is imposed on the graphs.
cards.why: A canonical test of whether quantum computation can efficiently recognize equivalence of explicit combinatorial structures, beyond the algebraic problems already handled by standard period finding.

cards.title: Quantum query-to-communication lifting
cards.formal: Do there exist constants \(C\ge1\) and an integer \(k\ge0\) such that, for every \(n\ge2\), there is a total nonconstant Boolean communication gadget \(g_n:\{0,1\}^{a_n}\times\{0,1\}^{b_n}\to\{0,1\}\), with finite positive integers \(a_n,b_n\), for which every partial Boolean function \(f:D\to\{0,1\}\), \(D\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), satisfies \[\frac{Q_{1/3}(f)}{C(\log_2n)^k}\ \le\ Q^*_{1/3}(f\circ g_n^n)\ \le\ C(\log_2n)^k Q_{1/3}(f)?\] Here \(Q_{1/3}\) is quantum query complexity and \(Q^*_{1/3}\) is two-party quantum communication complexity with unrestricted prior entanglement. Both have worst-case error at most \(1/3\). The gadget depends on \(n\), but not on \(D\) or \(f\), and the constants are common to the entire family.
cards.why: Quantum query complexity captures information obtainable from an oracle, while communication complexity measures information exchanged between separated parties. A universal lifting theorem would tightly connect these two models across all Boolean promise problems. The demand for only polylogarithmic loss is substantially stronger than transferring a weaker lower-bound measure or obtaining an arbitrary polynomial relation.

cards.title: Quantum versus classical nonuniform advice
cards.formal: Is \(\mathrm{BQP/qpoly}=\mathrm{BQP/poly}\) as classes of languages without an oracle? Explicitly, for every language decidable by a uniform polynomial-time quantum algorithm supplied with a polynomial-size quantum advice state depending only on input length, does some uniform polynomial-time quantum algorithm with polynomial-length classical advice decide the same language with error at most \(1/3\) on every input? The algorithm and polynomial advice bound may change. The reverse inclusion follows by encoding a classical advice string in the computational basis.
cards.why: This compares the computational value of quantum and classical information stored in advance for an entire input length. It asks whether a short quantum state can support useful computations that no polynomial-length classical record can support, even when preparing either kind of advice is free. The shared-advice requirement makes this a different resource comparison from per-instance witnesses.

cards.title: Efficient approximation of the optimal dihedral measurement
cards.formal: Can the specific pretty good measurement \(\{E_0,\ldots,E_{N-1},E_{\bot}\}\) defined below be approximated by uniform polynomial-size quantum circuits to every requested inverse-polynomial accuracy? Precisely, does there exist one deterministic circuit generator and a polynomial \(p\) such that, for every integer \(N\ge2\), number of copies \(k\ge1\), and precision parameter \(m\ge2\), it runs in time at most \(p(\lceil\log_2N\rceil+k+m)\) and produces a circuit with at most that many gates and ancilla qubits whose output distribution satisfies \[\sup_{\sigma}\frac12\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z_N\cup\{\bot\}}\left|\Pr[C_{N,k,m}(\sigma)=j]-\operatorname{Tr}(E_j\sigma)\right|\le\frac1m?\] The supremum ranges over all input density matrices on \((\mathbb C^2\otimes\mathbb C^N)^{\otimes k}\). The circuit receives one such state and returns one classical outcome. The selected target concerns this concrete measurement, without requiring a particular unitary realization or a Subset Sum algorithm.
cards.why: This isolates the cost of extracting the information already present in dihedral coset states. An efficient implementation would turn a provably optimal measurement into an algorithmic resource, while a general impossibility theorem would distinguish measurement optimality from computational feasibility.

cards.title: A finite quantum gate set with decision power strictly between P and BQP
cards.formal:
Does there exist a finite set \(G\) of constant-arity unitary quantum gates with algebraic complex matrix entries such that
\[
\mathrm P\subsetneq Q_G\subsetneq\mathrm{BQP},
\]
and \(G\) is not contained in any common one-qubit conjugate of the Clifford gates? The bounded-error decision class \(Q_G\), the circuit interface, and the conjugation exclusion are defined below. Both strict containments are unconditional parts of the assertion.
cards.why: A genuine intermediate decision class generated only by a finite gate set would expose a computational regime beyond deterministic classical computation but below universal quantum computation. It would distinguish gate-induced limitations from restrictions on depth, state preparation or geometry.

cards.title: Parity versus \(\mathrm{AC}^{0}\) with shallow quantum preprocessing
cards.formal: Does every polynomial-size constant-depth classical \(\mathrm{AC}^0\) circuit with polynomial-size constant-depth quantum preprocessing have asymptotically zero correlation with parity? Precisely, for every polynomial \(p\), constant \(d\in\mathbb N\), and sequence \((C_n,f_n)_{n\ge1}\) satisfying the model and bounds below, is \[\left|2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}\ \sum_{y\in\{0,1\}^{n+m(n)}}\Pr[C_n(x)=y]f_n(y)(-1)^{\sum_{i=1}^nx_i}\right|\longrightarrow0\quad(n\longrightarrow\infty)?\] Here \(m(n)\le p(n)\) zero-initialized ancillary qubits are allowed, both circuit stages have depth at most \(d\), and both have polynomial size bounded by \(p(n)\). There is no geometric locality, uniformity or clean-ancilla condition.
cards.why: Parity is a basic test of global information processing. Resolving this conjecture would show whether very shallow quantum preprocessing can give weak classical decision circuits a persistent advantage on a canonical Boolean function, beyond known quantum search and sampling separations.

cards.title: Area law for gapped two-dimensional Hamiltonians
cards.formal: For every choice of integers \(q\ge2\), \(r,g\ge1\) and real numbers \(J,\Delta>0\), does there exist a finite constant \(C=C(q,r,g,J,\Delta)\ge0\) with the following property? For every square-lattice size \(L\ge1\), every Hamiltonian satisfying the locality, norm, incidence, unique-ground-state and global-gap conditions below, and every subset \(A\subseteq\Lambda_L\), its ground state satisfies \[S(\rho_A)\le C\,|\partial A|.\] The constant must be independent of \(L\), the region and the particular interaction matrices. This is an entropy area law for general uniformly gapped two-dimensional local systems.
cards.why: A central problem in quantum Hamiltonian complexity: whether locality plus a uniform gap controls the quantum information in ground states in two dimensions. It would sharpen the structural foundations of tensor-network methods and separate the task of bounding entanglement from the further task of computing the state.

cards.title: NPT bound entanglement
cards.formal: Does there exist a negative-partial-transpose state that is undistillable for every finite number of copies? Precisely, are there integers \(a,b\ge2\) and a density matrix \(\rho\) on \(\mathbb C^a\otimes\mathbb C^b\) such that \(\rho^{\Gamma_B}\) has a strictly negative eigenvalue and \[\langle\psi,(\rho^{\Gamma_B})^{\otimes k}\psi\rangle\ge0\] for every integer \(k\ge1\) and every unit vector \(\psi\in(\mathbb C^a)^{\otimes k}\otimes(\mathbb C^b)^{\otimes k}\) of Schmidt rank at most two across the displayed bipartition? The same dimensions and the same state must satisfy the condition for all \(k\).
cards.why: A defining question about whether partial-transpose negativity completely captures the possibility of converting bipartite entanglement into useful Bell pairs. Its precise all-copy quantifier connects quantum resource theory to tensor-stable matrix inequalities.

cards.title: Asymptotically good quantum locally testable stabilizer codes
cards.formal: Do there exist real constants \(r,\delta,s>0\) and positive integers \(w,b\) such that, for every integer \(N\ge1\), some stabilizer code on \(n\ge N\) qubits has an admissible list of checks as defined below and satisfies \[k\ge rn,\qquad d\ge\delta n,\qquad H\succeq\frac{s}{n}D_Q?\] Here \(k\) is its number of logical qubits, \(d\) its code distance, each listed check acts on at most \(w\) qubits, and each qubit occurs in at most \(b\) listed checks. All five constants are fixed for the unbounded family. This is the bounded-degree stabilizer version of asymptotically good quantum local testability.
cards.why: A central missing object connecting quantum error correction to robust verification. It asks whether sparse quantum constraints can simultaneously protect a linear amount of information and detect global corruption with constant normalized soundness.

cards.title: Passive quantum memory in three dimensions
cards.formal: Do there exist constants \(B,R>0\), a fixed finite inverse temperature \(\beta>0\), strictly increasing qubit counts \(n_j\to\infty\), local three-dimensional stabilizer Hamiltonians \(H_{n_j}\), and fixed encoding maps \(\operatorname{Enc}_{n_j}\), all satisfying the definitions below, for which \[\tau_{n_j}(\beta)\longrightarrow\infty?\] The dynamics couple every single-qubit Pauli error to the same specified positive-temperature bath, with no intervention during storage. This card retains a claimed affirmative resolution from May2026; the complete preprint proof has not been independently verified here.
cards.why: A foundational question about whether quantum information can enjoy passive thermal protection in physical three-dimensional space. The recent claimed solution makes careful separation of storage, initialization, bath restrictions and stability especially important.

cards.title: Quantum capacity of the qubit depolarizing channel
cards.formal: Determine the unassisted quantum-capacity function \(Q(q)=Q(\mathcal D_q)\) for every real \(q\in[0,1]\), where the qubit depolarizing channel is \[\mathcal D_q(\rho)=(1-q)\rho+\frac q3(X\rho X+Y\rho Y+Z\rho Z).\] The parameter \(q\) is the total probability of a nonidentity Pauli error. Capacity uses the operational definition below and is measured in qubits per independent channel use. The quantitative benchmark accepts a function with absolute error at most \(1/100\) throughout the whole domain.
cards.why: The unresolved communication limit of a canonical quantum-noise model. It tests whether quantum coding theory can turn regularized existence formulas into sharp quantitative limits despite degeneracy and multi-copy advantages.

cards.title: Quantum entropy inequalities beyond strong subadditivity
cards.formal:
Is there an unconditional homogeneous linear inequality for finite-dimensional quantum subsystem entropies that does not follow from the standard von Neumann inequalities? Precisely, do there exist an integer \(n\ge4\), real coefficients \((c_J)_{\varnothing
e J\subseteq[n]}\), and a vector \(v\in\mathcal V_n\), as defined below, such that \[\sum_{\varnothing
e J\subseteq[n]}c_J S(ho_J)\ge0\] for every choice of finite local dimensions and every \(n\)-party density matrix \(ho\), while \[\sum_{\varnothing
e J\subseteq[n]}c_Jv_J<0?\] The same coefficients must work in every local dimension. The party count is any one finite \(n\ge4\); the target is not restricted to exactly four parties or to a special class of states.
cards.why: This asks whether the established linear laws of quantum entropy are complete. A new unconditional inequality would reveal a universal restriction on sharing quantum information; completeness would characterize every finite-party entropy cone by finitely many standard inequalities, after taking closure.

cards.title: Exponential repetition of two-player entangled games
cards.formal: Does every finite two-player, one-round game \(G\) with entangled value \(\omega^{*}(G)<1\) admit a constant \(c_{G}>0\) such that \[\omega^{*}(G^{\otimes n})\leq \exp(-c_{G}n)\qquad\text{for every integer }n\geq1?\] The repetition uses the unchanged game and requires winning every coordinate. The 2016 paper proves convergence to zero at a polynomial rate; an August 2026 manuscript claims the exponential bound, with verification limits recorded below.
cards.why: Determines how reliably independent challenges amplify soundness against quantum players who may coordinate across all copies. The universal question isolates the effect of entanglement without adding auxiliary tests or restricting the form of the game.

cards.title: Bell nonlocality from finitely many copies of every entangled state
cards.formal: For every finite pair of local dimensions \(d_A,d_B\ge2\) and every entangled state \(\rho\) on \(\mathbb C^{d_A}\otimes\mathbb C^{d_B}\), do there exist a finite integer \(k\ge1\), local filters with strictly positive joint success probability, and finite families of local measurements for which the successfully filtered state obtained from \(\rho^{\otimes k}\) has Bell-nonlocal correlations? Both filters act before the measurement settings are chosen. No auxiliary shared entangled state is supplied. The number of copies, filters, output dimensions and measurement families may depend on \(\rho\).
cards.why: A positive answer would give every entangled bipartite state an intrinsic Bell-nonlocal manifestation using only repeated access to that same state. A negative answer would exhibit entanglement that remains Bell-local under every finite collective local test and preliminary filter. This separates the mathematical resource of entanglement from the observable nonlocal correlations used in device-independent information tasks.

cards.title: Maximum randomized-versus-quantum gap for total functions
cards.formal: Determine the optimal polynomial separation exponent \[\alpha_{\mathrm{RQ}}=\inf\bigl\{a\ge0:\exists C>0\ \forall n\ge1\ \forall\text{ nonconstant }f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\},\ R(f)\le C\,Q(f)^a\bigr\}.\] Here \(R(f)\) and \(Q(f)\) are randomized and quantum bit-query complexities with worst-case error at most \(1/3\). The constant \(C\) must be independent of both \(n\) and \(f\). The known range is \(3\le\alpha_{\mathrm{RQ}}\le4\). This card makes the source's maximum-gap question precise at the level of its polynomial exponent; logarithmic factors are not part of this numerical target.
cards.why: This quantifies the greatest possible quantum query advantage when an algorithm must handle every input, without a promise. It tests a basic limitation on quantum speedups and distinguishes the role of classical randomization from that of deterministic computation.

cards.title: Locality-preserving quantum gap amplification
cards.formal:
For every fixed integers \(k,q\ge2\), do there exist integers \(D\ge q\) and \(C\ge1\), a rational \(0<\gamma\le1\), and a deterministic classical polynomial-time transformation \(T_{k,q}\) with the following property? Given any explicit \(k\)-local projective Hamiltonian
\[
 H=\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m P_j
\]
on \(n\) sites of local dimension \(q\), it outputs an explicit projective Hamiltonian
\[
 H'=\frac1{m'}\sum_{j=1}^{m'} P'_j
\]
with \(1\le m'\le Cm\), whose terms each act on at most \(k\) sites and whose site dimension is \(D\), such that
\[
 \lambda(H)=0\ \Longrightarrow\ \lambda(H')=0,
 \qquad
 \lambda(H')\ge\min\{2\lambda(H),\gamma\}.
\]
Here \(\lambda\) denotes the lowest eigenvalue of the normalized Hamiltonian. In particular, whenever \(0<\lambda(H)\le\gamma/2\), its normalized energy is at least doubled. All output-dimension, term-growth and energy-threshold constants are independent of the input instance and its size.
cards.why: Checking a few quantum particles remains useful only if amplification does not make each check involve more and more particles. The question asks whether the energy penalty can grow while each individual constraint retains its original arity.

cards.title: QMA versus \(\mathrm{QMA}_1\) over Clifford+T
cards.formal: Is \(\mathrm{QMA}=\mathrm{QMA}_1^{\mathcal G}\) for the exact gate set \(\mathcal G=\{H,\mathrm{CNOT},T\}\) defined below? Both classes concern promise problems on finite binary strings and use polynomial-size, uniformly generated verification circuits with polynomially many witness qubits. In \(\mathrm{QMA}\), every yes-instance has a witness accepted with probability at least \(2/3\); in \(\mathrm{QMA}_1^{\mathcal G}\), it has a witness accepted with probability exactly \(1\). In both classes, every witness for a no-instance is accepted with probability at most \(1/3\). The one-sided class in this question is explicitly the Clifford+T version.
cards.why: This determines whether certainty on yes-instances changes the power of efficient quantum proof verification. It separates arbitrarily reliable verification from exact acceptance and affects the relation between quantum satisfiability and general quantum witness problems.

cards.title: Classical hardness of approximate Boson Sampling
cards.formal: Is the following classical sampling impossibility statement true? There is no single probabilistic classical Turing machine \(M\) and polynomial \(p\) such that, for every valid ideal Boson Sampling input \(B\) defined below and every integer \(k\ge2\), the machine \(M(B,1^k)\) outputs an occupation vector with law \(Q_{B,k}\), always halts in at most \(p(|B|+k)\) steps, and satisfies \[d_{\mathrm{TV}}(Q_{B,k},D_B)=\frac12\sum_{s\in\Omega_{m,n}}|Q_{B,k}(s)-D_B(s)|\le\frac1k?\] The target distribution is \[D_B(s)=\frac{|\operatorname{Per}(A_s)|^2}{\prod_{j=1}^{m}s_j!},\qquad A=\operatorname{GS}(B),\qquad \Omega_{m,n}=\{s\in\mathbb N_0^m:\sum_js_j=n\}.\] Thus the approximation must meet every requested error tolerance, in time polynomial in the explicit network description and the inverse tolerance. The claim is unconditional and concerns all valid inputs, rather than only typical random optical networks.
cards.why: This asks for an unconditional boundary between classical sampling and a concrete, restricted quantum optical experiment. It would clarify whether reproducing an entire physically defined distribution can require superpolynomial classical resources even when universal quantum computation is not part of the device model.

cards.title: Quantum query complexity versus bounded approximate degree
cards.formal: Determine, up to universal multiplicative constants, the extremal function \[M(n,d)=\max\bigl\{Q(f):\varnothing\ne D\subseteq\{0,1\}^n,\ f:D\to\{0,1\},\ \operatorname{bdeg}_{1/3}(f)\le d\bigr\}\] for all integers \(n\ge1\) and \(1\le d\le n\). The bounded approximate degree \(\operatorname{bdeg}_{1/3}(f)\) is the least total degree of a real polynomial \(p\) satisfying \[|p(x)-f(x)|\le1/3\quad(x\in D),\qquad 0\le p(x)\le1\quad(x\in\{0,1\}^n).\] The query measure \(Q\) has worst-case error at most \(1/3\). This makes the source's largest-gap question a two-parameter extremal query bound. The source's additional question of whether an exponential gap exists was answered affirmatively in 2023.
cards.why: Bounded approximate degree is the main numerical object behind the polynomial method for quantum query lower bounds. Determining its worst possible discrepancy from actual quantum query complexity would quantify how much algorithmic difficulty this method can miss under promises.

cards.title: One-way state generators versus EFI pairs
cards.formal: Does the existence of EFI pairs imply the existence of efficiently verifiable one-way state generators in the ordinary quantum circuit model defined below? Both primitives have uniform polynomial-time honest algorithms and security against polynomial-size quantum circuits with classical nonuniformity. The implication is between existence assertions; no oracle is supplied to any algorithm.
cards.why: The question asks whether computational indistinguishability alone supplies quantum search hardness with an efficiently checkable secret. Its answer determines whether two central minimal assumptions for quantum cryptography have the same power once the cost of verification is included.

cards.title: Remote state preparation from quantum-secure one-way functions
cards.formal:
Does the existence of classical one-way functions secure against quantum polynomial-time inversion with quantum advice imply the existence of a protocol for parallel remote preparation of BB84 states with the inverse-polynomial rigidity guarantee defined below? In symbols, decide
\[
\bigl(\exists F\;\operatorname{QOWF}(F)\bigr)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\bigl(\exists\Pi\;\operatorname{RSP}_{\mathrm{rig}}(\Pi)\bigr).
\]
The protocol has one classical client and one quantum server, uses only classical communication, and has no trusted setup or initially shared resource. The client chooses a basis string \(\theta\in\{0,1\}^{n}\), and upon acceptance obtains a string \(v\in\{0,1\}^{n}\). For an honest server, its designated output register contains the corresponding BB84 product state
\[
|\psi_{v,\theta}\rangle=\bigotimes_{i=1}^{n}H^{\theta_{i}}|v_{i}\rangle,
\qquad H=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},
\]
with uniformly random \(v\), up to negligible correctness error. Against any efficient malicious server, the accepted joint output must satisfy the computational rigidity condition below, up to an efficient isometry on the server’s space and an auxiliary state independent of \(v,\theta\). A unary accuracy parameter \(t\) permits soundness error \(1/t\) plus a negligible term, with resources polynomial in the security parameter \(\lambda\), \(n\), and \(t\).

This is a documented selection of the original paper’s own inverse-polynomial, isometry-based guarantee from its broader question about an RSP-like protocol. The target is an implication between existence statements, not a prescribed black-box reduction or a requirement for negligible simulation error.
cards.why: Remote preparation asks how a classical participant can cause an untrusted quantum device to hold useful hidden quantum states using only classical messages. Identifying whether ordinary one-way-function hardness suffices would clarify which cryptographic resources are essential for this form of classical control, beyond the more structured assumptions in known constructions.

cards.title: Simulation or postselection universality for algebraic two-qubit interactions
cards.formal: For every fixed Hermitian \(4\times4\) matrix \(H\) with complex algebraic entries, does at least one of the following hold: all of its basis-input, basis-output circuits admit polynomial-time classical sampling to arbitrary inverse-polynomial total-variation accuracy; or \(\mathrm{PP}\subseteq\operatorname{Post}(H)\), with the circuit, uniformity and postselection conventions below?
cards.why: Seeks a boundary between classically manageable quantum dynamics and postselection universality using only one fixed two-qubit interaction. The restriction to basis preparation and measurement makes computational power depend on more than ordinary unitary controllability.

cards.title: \(\mathrm{QMA}(2)\) versus NEXP
cards.formal: Is \(\mathrm{QMA}(2)=\mathrm{NEXP}\) for ordinary promise problems without an oracle? Equivalently, does every promise problem decidable by a nondeterministic classical Turing machine in time \(2^{p(n)}\), for some polynomial \(p\), admit a uniform polynomial-time quantum verifier with two polynomial-length unentangled witnesses, completeness at least \(2/3\), and soundness at most \(1/3\)? The known inclusion \(\mathrm{QMA}(2)\subseteq\mathrm{NEXP}\) makes the reverse containment the unresolved direction. The verifier, its running time and both witness lengths must remain polynomial in the original binary input length.
cards.why: Two short quantum messages may contain a highly structured encoding of a much longer computation, while their independence restricts how a dishonest prover can cheat. This question asks whether that resource reaches the full power of nondeterministic exponential time despite a polynomial-time verifier and a constant reliability gap. It locates the upper end of the unusually wide known range for QMA(2).

cards.title: Polynomially many EPR pairs for bounded-error Boolean communication
cards.formal:
Do there exist universal constants \(C\ge1\), \(A\ge1\) and an integer \(d\ge1\) with the following property? For every \(n\ge1\), every promise set \(D\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\times\{0,1\}^n\), every Boolean function \(f:D\to\{0,1\}\), and every two-party quantum protocol computing \(f\) with worst-case error at most \(1/4\) using at most \(Q\ge1\) communicated qubits and arbitrary prior entanglement, there exists a protocol computing \(f\) with error at most \(1/3\), using at most \(CQ\) communicated qubits and at most
\[
 \lfloor A(n+1)^d\rfloor
\]
shared EPR pairs initially? Both protocols may use arbitrary two-way interaction. The replacement may change all local operations and the message pattern; it need not reproduce the original shared state or its internal evolution.
cards.why: Communication complexity counts the messages but usually gives the parties their shared entangled state for free. This question asks whether that hidden resource can always be bounded polynomially while keeping almost the same communication cost.

cards.title: Entanglement without distillable secret key
cards.formal: Do there exist finite integers \(a,b\ge2\) and an entangled density matrix \(\rho\) on \(\mathbb C^a\otimes\mathbb C^b\) with zero distillable secret-key rate, \(K_D(\rho)=0\), under arbitrary local quantum operations and two-way public classical communication? The rate is the standard asymptotic, vanishing-error rate defined below. There is no restriction to one-way communication, perfect finite-block output, a chosen measurement, or efficient protocols.
cards.why: This question determines whether every entangled bipartite state has some usable private correlation when arbitrary collective quantum processing is allowed. An entangled zero-key state would establish an additional form of irreversibility beyond ordinary bound entanglement; a universal positivity theorem would identify entanglement itself as the exact boundary for asymptotic key usefulness.

cards.title: Black-box unitary synthesis
cards.formal: Is there one polynomial-time uniform family of polynomial-size quantum oracle circuits \(\{A_n\}_{n\ge1}\) such that, for every \(n\)-qubit unitary matrix \(U\), some Boolean function \(f_U:\{0,1\}^{m(n)}\to\{0,1\}\) makes the channel implemented by \(A_n^{f_U}\) approximate \(\rho\mapsto U\rho U^\dagger\) within diamond distance \(1/10\)? The oracle input length \(m(n)\), total number of qubits, number of ordinary gates, and number of oracle calls must all be bounded by one fixed polynomial in \(n\). The circuit family is chosen before \(U\); only the Boolean oracle may depend on \(U\). This is the fixed-constant-error version of black-box unitary synthesis.
cards.why: The question asks whether implementing arbitrary quantum transformations can be reduced efficiently to evaluating Boolean functions. A negative answer would establish a black-box obstruction to explaining all quantum transformation complexity through classical function computation, a central issue for unitary complexity and quantum cryptography.

cards.title: Quantum games PCP with efficient honest provers and short messages
cards.formal: Does every promise problem \(\mathrm{L}=(\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{yes}},\mathrm{L}_{no})\) in QMA admit a one-round entangled multiprover proof with a uniform classical polynomial-time verifier, a constant number r of provers and polylogarithmic-length classical questions and answers, such that: \((i)\) on every \(x\in \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{yes}}\), some polynomial-size quantum witness permits uniform quantum polynomial-time preparation and local execution of an honest strategy accepted with probability at least \(2/3\); and \((ii)\) on every \(x\in \mathrm{L}_{no}\), every entangled strategy, with no computational bound on the dishonest provers, is accepted with probability at most \(1/3\)?
cards.why: Would connect efficient verification of quantum witnesses to succinct classical interaction with entangled provers. The honest-prover requirement preserves the computational meaning of the witness, which unrestricted entangled proof-system containments do not ensure.

cards.title: Completeness and soundness amplification in StoqMA
cards.formal: For every pair of efficiently computable threshold functions \(a(n),b(n)\) with \(1/2\le b(n)<a(n)\le 1\) and \(a(n)- b(n)\ge 1/q(n)\) for some polynomial q, and every integer-valued polynomial \(\ell\)\((n)\ge 2\), is \(StoqMA(a,b)\) contained in \(StoqMA(1- 2^{- \ell (n)}, 1/2+2^{- \ell (n)})\)? Here n is the classical input length. The new verifier must remain in the same one-witness stoquastic circuit model, with polynomially many gates, witness qubits and ancillas.
cards.why: Would determine whether the stoquastic verification model has ordinary exponential error reduction and, through the published equivalence, whether its proof power collapses to classical Merlin–Arthur verification.

cards.title: Succinct entangled proofs with efficient provers
cards.formal: Does quantum circuit acceptance admit a uniform two-prover, one-round proof with a classical polynomial-time verifier, total classical communication \(O((\log(N+2))^k)\) for some fixed \(k\), completeness at least \(2/3\), and soundness at most \(1/3\) against arbitrary entangled provers, such that the honest provers can prepare and execute their strategy in quantum polynomial time given polynomially many copies of an accepting witness? Here \(N\) is the explicit circuit-instance length, and the instance, efficiency and soundness requirements are defined below.
cards.why: This asks whether a classical verifier can check general quantumly provable claims using very little communication while keeping the honest quantum resources polynomial. It joins three substantial demands—two separated provers, unconditional soundness and succinct communication—and would clarify the practical content of entangled proof systems beyond their unconstrained complexity-class power.

cards.title: Universal quantum stability of seeded extractors with output-linear error loss
cards.formal:
Is there a universal integer \(C\ge1\) such that every classical \((k,\varepsilon)\) seeded extractor
\[
 F:\{0,1\}^n\times\{0,1\}^d\longrightarrow\{0,1\}^m
\]
is quantum-proof with conditional min-entropy requirement
\[
 K=C\bigl(k+\log_2(1/\varepsilon)\bigr)
\]
and trace-distance error at most \(C m\sqrt{\varepsilon}\)? Quantify over all integers \(n,m\ge1\), \(d\ge0\), real \(0\le k\le n\), and \(0<\varepsilon\le1/2\). Use the general, or weak, seeded-extractor definition below: the uniform independent seed is averaged out, and \(m\) counts the entire retained classical output.
cards.why: An adversary can store information about a weak random input in a quantum state. The question asks whether a classical extractor’s guarantee alone controls how much this changes the quality of its output, with a loss that grows only linearly in output length.

cards.title: \(\mathrm{QMA}(2)\) versus \(\mathrm{BQEXP}\)
cards.formal: Is \(\mathrm{QMA}(2)\subseteq\mathrm{BQEXP}\)? In promise-problem terms, does every pair \(\Pi=(Y,N)\) of disjoint sets of binary strings that has a polynomial-time quantum verifier with two unentangled polynomial-size proofs also admit a uniform quantum algorithm running in time \(2^{p(n)}\), for some polynomial \(p\), with error at most \(1/3\) on every promised input? The algorithm receives no proofs. The polynomial may depend on \(\Pi\) and its verifier, but not on the individual input of length \(n\).
cards.why: Unentangled quantum proofs add a nonconvex constraint to quantum verification. An exponential-time quantum simulation would place a meaningful algorithmic limit on this model and clarify whether its power can be explained without nondeterministic exponential-time witness search.

cards.title: Constant-round quantum refereed games versus \(\mathrm{PSPACE}\)
cards.formal: Does \(\mathrm{QRG}_{\mathrm{const}}\subseteq\mathrm{PSPACE}\)? For every promise problem \(\Pi=(Y,N)\) admitting a quantum refereed game with a uniform polynomial-time verifier, two competing provers and some fixed constant \(k\) of interaction cycles, must there be a deterministic algorithm deciding \(\Pi\) using polynomial space? For \(x\in Y\), a yes-prover must have a strategy that makes the verifier accept with probability at least \(2/3\) against every no-prover strategy. For \(x\in N\), a no-prover must have a strategy that makes it reject with probability at least \(2/3\) against every yes-prover strategy. The constant \(k\) and the polynomial bounds may depend on the problem and verifier, but not on input length.
cards.why: These games combine efficient quantum verification with competition between two powerful provers who have different information. Locating constant-length games would clarify whether repeated alternation of private interaction can increase computational power beyond polynomial space, even when only a few exchanges are allowed.

cards.title: Optimal quantum query complexity of uniformity testing
cards.formal: Determine \(Q(d,\varepsilon )\), the optimal worst-case quantum query complexity of distinguishing \(p=u_{d}\) from \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(p,u_{d})>\varepsilon\) with success probability at least 0.99, up to universal constant factors jointly for all integers \(d\ge 2\) and real \(0<\varepsilon \le 1/4\). Access is to an arbitrary distribution synthesizer with the precise oracle convention below.
cards.why: Would identify the optimal joint dependence on domain size and accuracy for one of the basic distribution-testing tasks with coherent sampler access, clarifying the extent of quantum advantage over classical samples.

cards.title: Limiting optimized QAOA energy in the SK model
cards.formal: Determine \(A=\sup _{p\ge 1} \sup _{\gamma ,\beta \in \mathbb{R} ^{p}} a_{p}(\gamma ,\beta )\), where \(a_{p}(\gamma ,\beta )=\lim _{n\to \infty} n^{- 1} E_{J}[\langle \psi _{p,J}(\gamma ,\beta )|H_{J}|\psi _{p,J}(\gamma ,\beta )\rangle ]\) for the Gaussian Sherrington–Kirkpatrick Hamiltonian and QAOA state defined below. The benchmark requires absolute error at most \(1/100\) in energy per spin.
cards.why: The limiting optimized energy of QAOA asks whether a central quantum optimization ansatz can reach the statistical-mechanics optimum after taking the infinite-instance limit.

cards.title: Strong quantum IOPs with polynomial communication
cards.formal: Does every QMA promise problem have a strong quantum interactive oracle proof with polynomial communication, constantly many messages and a constant total number of queried message qubits? More precisely, for every \(L\in\mathrm{QMA}\), do there exist a polynomial \(p\), constants \(r,q\in\mathbb N\), and one uniform verifier under the strong access rules below such that, on every input \(x\) of length \(n\), its running time and total incoming prover-message length are at most \(p(n)\), the total number of messages is at most \(r\), the total query cost is at most \(q\), and \[x\in L_{\mathrm{yes}}\Rightarrow\sup_P\Pr[V_x\leftrightarrow P\text{ accepts}]\ge2/3,\] \[x\in L_{\mathrm{no}}\Rightarrow\sup_P\Pr[V_x\leftrightarrow P\text{ accepts}]\le1/3?\] Here \(P\) ranges over all allowed prover strategies, with no computational bound. Strong means that the verifier returns each incoming quantum register in full and sends no additional quantum register of its own.
cards.why: This asks whether very local interactive verification of quantum evidence can avoid enormous communication while obeying the strong return rules. Resolving it would clarify the joint limits of proof length, local access and interaction for QMA.

cards.title: Bosonic quantum computation in PP
cards.formal: Does \[\mathrm{CVBQP}[X^3]\subseteq\mathrm{PP}\] hold for the Gaussian-and-cubic bosonic model below, with no additional restriction on energy during the computation? For every language \(L\subseteq\{0,1\}^*\) decided by the stated polynomial-time uniform bosonic circuit family with polynomial total evolution time and the separated output intervals below, must there be a classical probabilistic polynomial-time machine accepting each \(x\in L\) with probability strictly greater than \(1/2\) and each \(x\notin L\) with probability at most \(1/2\)? The target is the inclusion itself, rather than an unspecified improvement of an exponential-space upper bound.
cards.why: This tests whether an infinite-dimensional optical model with cubic nonlinearity still fits within a familiar classical counting class. Its answer would clarify how much computational power can be hidden in very high intermediate photon numbers despite polynomial evolution time and a bounded-error final decision.

cards.title: Oracle separation of BQP from efficient-prover interactive proofs
cards.formal: Does there exist a classical Boolean oracle A and a language \(\mathrm{L}\subseteq \{0,1\}\)* such that \(\mathrm{L}\in \mathrm{BQP}^{A}\) but \(\mathrm{L}\notin \mathrm{IP}_{\mathrm{BQP}}^{A}\), where \(\mathrm{IP}_{\mathrm{BQP}}^{A}\) requires a polynomial-time quantum honest prover and classical interaction with a polynomial-time classical verifier?
cards.why: Distinguishes the existence of a classical interactive proof from the ability of an efficient quantum device to carry out its honest strategy. It tests whether verification can match the computational resources of the device while retaining soundness against all cheating provers.

cards.title: Quantum query–space tradeoffs for collisions and distinctness
cards.formal: Determine, up to universal multiplicative constants, the functions \(T_b(n,m,S)\) for \(b\in\{\mathrm{collision},\mathrm{distinctness}\}\): the minimum worst-case number of quantum queries needed by an algorithm with at most \(S\) qubits of total retained memory to solve the specified decision problem with error at most \(1/3\). The input is an oracle for \(f:[n]\to[m]\). In the collision problem, \(n\) is even and \(f\) is promised to be either injective or exactly two-to-one; distinguish these cases. In element distinctness there is no promise; decide whether \(f\) is injective. The full parameter domain is \(m\ge n\ge2\) and \(S\ge4(\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil+\lceil\log_2(m+1)\rceil)+10\), with integer parameters. This card selects the source's total-memory tradeoff, allowing all retained memory to be quantum; separating classical and quantum memory budgets is a further variant.
cards.why: Quantum collision and distinctness algorithms gain speed while retaining substantial information about queried values. Their optimal time/space tradeoffs would quantify how much memory is necessary for those advantages and develop lower-bound methods for problems whose output contains only one bit.

cards.title: Complement of quantum approximate counting in \(\mathrm{QMA}(2)\)
cards.formal: Is the following complementary quantum approximate-counting promise problem in \(\mathrm{QMA}(2)\)? The input is a finite quantum verification circuit \(V\) with \(w\) witness qubits, together with a binary integer \(1\le K\le2^w\). Let \(A_V\) be its acceptance operator on the witness space and let \(D_a(V)\) count its eigenvalues at least \(a\), with multiplicity. Distinguish \[\text{YES: }D_{1/3}(V)\le K/2\qquad\text{from}\qquad\text{NO: }D_{2/3}(V)\ge K,\] promised that one of these conditions holds. Membership asks for one uniform polynomial-time quantum verifier using two polynomial-size, mutually unentangled witnesses, with completeness at least \(2/3\) and soundness at most \(1/3\). The two spectral thresholds deliberately leave a buffer; the selected target is the complement of this buffered counting problem.
cards.why: This asks whether two unentangled quantum certificates can verify that a quantum verifier has only a small accepting space. It connects the power of independent quantum witnesses to approximate counting and distinguishes proving scarcity from merely proving existence.

cards.title: Exact quantum fanout in constant depth with unrestricted circuit size
cards.formal: Does there exist a fixed integer d such that, for every \(n\ge 1\), some finite QAC circuit of depth at most d exactly implements FANOUT\(_{n}\) on one control qubit and n target qubits, allowing arbitrarily many clean ancillas and no size bound?
cards.why: Determines whether unbounded-arity quantum AND operations and one-qubit gates can express coherent fanout in bounded depth at any finite size. It isolates a basic limitation of shallow unitary computation that cannot be explained solely by insufficient circuit width.

cards.title: Zero-free quantum partition functions with a tensor-product perturbation
cards.formal:
For every fixed integers \(q\ge2\), \(k,d\ge1\), positive rational \(J\), and rational \(R>1\), does there exist a deterministic classical algorithm with the following guarantee? Its input specifies a bounded-occurrence local Hamiltonian \(H=\sum_{j=1}^m h_j\) on \(n\ge1\) sites of dimension \(q\), a tensor-product Hermitian perturbation
\[
 H'=A_1\otimes\cdots\otimes A_n,\qquad \|H'\|\le1,
\]
and a rational accuracy \(0<\varepsilon<1\). Each \(h_j\) acts on at most \(k\) sites, has operator norm at most \(J\), and each site occurs in at most \(d\) terms. Under the promise
\[
 Z(z):=\operatorname{Tr}\exp(-zH+H')\ne0
 \quad\text{for every }z\in\mathbb C\text{ with }|z|<R,
\]
the algorithm must output a rational \(\widehat Z\) satisfying
\[
 |\widehat Z-Z(1)|\le\varepsilon Z(1)
\]
in time polynomial in the binary input length and \(1/\varepsilon\). The polynomial may depend on the fixed parameters \(q,k,d,J,R\), but not on the instance or its accuracy.
cards.why: Zero-free complex regions often turn a difficult counting problem into an efficient approximation problem. A tensor-product perturbation has a short description but disrupts the factorization behind the known algorithm, testing whether zero-freeness alone remains sufficient.

cards.title: Sequential randomness certification against non-signaling adversaries
cards.formal: Is the randomness certifiable from a single pure entangled pair of qubits universally bounded against time-ordered no-signaling adversaries, even when Bob measures his qubit arbitrarily many times? Precisely, does a real constant \(B\ge0\) exist such that \[H_{\mathrm{NS}}(P,\mathbf y^0)=-\log_2 G_{\mathrm{NS}}(P,\mathbf y^0)\le B\] for every finite sequence length, every experiment in the single-pair model below, and every fixed generation input string \(\mathbf y^0\)?
cards.why: The question tests how much repeated randomness certification depends on quantum theory beyond no-signaling. It separates the physical resource available to the honest experiment—a single pair of qubits—from assumptions about an adversary. A universal bound or unbounded family would clarify whether recycling one entangled system can retain its qualitative advantage under this stronger adversarial model.

cards.title: Quantum–classical communication gaps for total functions
cards.formal:
Do there exist real constants \(a\ge1\), \(\delta>0\), an integer \(b\ge1\), and an infinite set \(\mathcal N\subseteq\{2,3,\ldots\}\) such that, for every \(n\in\mathcal N\), some total Boolean function
\[f_n:\{0,1\}^n\times\{0,1\}^n\longrightarrow\{0,1\}\]
has bounded-error communication complexities satisfying
\[Q^*_{1/3}(f_n)\le a(\log_2 n)^b,
\qquad R_{1/3}(f_n)\ge a^{-1}n^\delta?\]
Here \(R_{1/3}\) permits classical public randomness and unrestricted interaction, and \(Q^*_{1/3}\) permits quantum communication and arbitrary finite prior entanglement. Only communication is charged. The constants are fixed independently of the input length and the function chosen at that length.
cards.why: This asks whether the large quantum savings known for promise problems can persist for a Boolean function defined on every input pair. A positive family would refute any universal polynomial simulation of quantum communication by randomized classical communication, even when local computation is unrestricted.

cards.title: Oracle separation of BQP from IP
cards.formal: Does there exist a classical Boolean oracle A and a language \(\mathrm{L}\subseteq \{0,1\}\)* such that \(\mathrm{L}\in \mathrm{BQP}^{A}\) but \(\mathrm{L}\notin \mathrm{IP}^{A}\)?
cards.why: Determines whether classical single-prover verification of efficient quantum computations survives arbitrary oracle access. The distinction is sharper than a quantum speedup over direct classical computation: even an unrestricted interactive helper must fail in the separating world.

cards.title: Martin’s conjecture
cards.formal: Assume \(\mathsf{ZF}+\mathsf{DC}+\mathsf{AD}\). Is the following conjunction true for all total Turing-invariant functions \(f:2^{\omega}\to2^{\omega}\)? Part I: every such \(f\) is constant in Turing degree on a cone or computes its input on a cone. Part II: the relation \(\leq_M\) of Turing reducibility on a cone prewellorders the set \(\mathcal F\) of all such functions above the identity on a cone, and for every \(f\in\mathcal F\), its pointwise Turing jump \(f'\) has rank exactly \(\operatorname{rank}_M(f)+1\) in that same prewellorder. All functions, cones, ordinals and quantifiers are interpreted within the stated set-theoretic universe.
cards.why: Turing degrees encode relative computational power and have a highly non-linear structure. Martin’s conjecture asks whether invariance under mutual computability nevertheless forces every nontrivial operation into an ordered hierarchy once behaviour is compared on cones under determinacy. It gives a precise structural target behind the observed regularity of many degree operators, and connects computability with descriptive set theory and analogous hierarchies of logical strength.

cards.title: Busy Beaver \(\mathrm{BB}(6)\)
cards.formal:
Determine the exact six-state binary Busy Beaver runtime \(\mathrm{BB}(6)=S(6)\) by giving a concrete machine \(M_*\in\mathcal M_6\) and proving
\[M_*\text{ halts on the blank tape},\qquad
\forall M\in\mathcal M_6:\ M\text{ halts on the blank tape}\ \Longrightarrow\ T(M)\le T(M_*).\]
Here \(\mathcal M_6\) is the finite class of deterministic six-nonhalting-state, two-symbol Turing machines defined below, and \(T(M)\) is the number of transitions through the first entry into the separate halting state. The complete transition table of \(M_*\), together with proofs of its halting and universal maximality, specifies the answer exactly as \(S(6)=T(M_*)\).
cards.why: The halting behavior of a finite set of exceptionally short programs is still beyond complete classification. This problem makes the boundary of current computability knowledge concrete: one additional nonhalting state separates the established five-state maximum from an unresolved maximum with enormous certified examples and difficult residual halting questions. A solution would give a universal exact upper bound for every halting program in this precisely fixed class.

cards.title: Rigidity of the Turing degrees
cards.formal:
Let \(D_T=\mathcal P(\mathbb N)/{\equiv_T}\) be the set of all Turing degrees, ordered by Turing reducibility. Is this order rigid? The exact assertion is
\[\forall\pi:D_T\to D_T,\quad \Bigl[\pi\text{ is bijective}\ \land\ \forall a,b\in D_T\,\bigl(a\le_T b\iff\pi(a)\le_T\pi(b)\bigr)\Bigr]\ \Longrightarrow\ \forall a\in D_T\,\pi(a)=a.\]
The domain is the full quotient of all subsets of the standard natural numbers. The quantifier over \(\pi\) ranges over arbitrary functions on this quotient in ordinary classical set theory, with ZFC as the set-theoretic background.
cards.why: Rigidity asks whether the entire ordering of relative computational power has any nontrivial global symmetry. Its connection with intrinsic definability and second-order arithmetic makes it a central structural question in computability, beyond the classification of individual computable problems.

cards.title: Kolmogorov–Loveland randomness versus Martin-Löf randomness
cards.formal:
Is every Kolmogorov–Loveland random infinite binary sequence Martin-Löf random for the fair-coin product measure? In the precise model below, determine whether
\[\forall X\in\{0,1\}^{\mathbb N},\qquad
\operatorname{KLR}(X)\Longrightarrow\operatorname{MLR}(X).\]
The reverse implication is known, so this is equivalently equality of the two randomness classes. Betting strategies may choose fresh coordinates adaptively, need not visit every coordinate, and are ordinary partial computable procedures without an oracle.
cards.why: Determines whether adaptive computable fair betting detects every effective measure-theoretic failure of randomness in an individual infinite sequence. Equality or separation would connect two foundational ways to formalize unpredictability.

cards.title: Computability of the Mandelbrot set
cards.formal:
Is the Mandelbrot set a computable compact subset of the plane?

Precisely, does there exist a single deterministic Turing machine \(A\) such that for every integer \(k\ge0\), \(A(k)\) halts and outputs a finite nonempty set \(S_k\) of points with dyadic rational coordinates satisfying
\[
d_H(S_k,M)\le 2^{-k},
\]
where
\[
M=\{c\in\mathbb C:\ (z_j(c))_{j\ge0}\text{ is bounded}\},\qquad
z_0(c)=0,\quad z_{j+1}(c)=z_j(c)^2+c?
\]
The assertion is unconditional and places no complexity bound on \(A\).
cards.why: The defining iteration is simple and finite images are ubiquitous, yet those facts do not establish a uniform algorithm with certified error at every resolution. The problem tests whether the global geometry of a natural dynamical parameter set is effectively recoverable from its definition.

cards.title: Reversal of Hindman’s theorem to the \(\omega\)-jump
cards.formal:
Does the following formal provability statement hold?
\[
\mathrm{RCA}_0+\mathrm{HT}\ \vdash\
\forall X\,\exists Y\,
\bigl[Y_0=X\ \wedge\ \forall j\,(Y_{j+1}=Y_j')\bigr].
\]
Here \(\mathrm{HT}\) is Hindman's theorem for every finite coloring of the positive integers and all nonempty finite sums of distinct members of one infinite set. The conclusion says that every set has its coded \(\omega\)-jump. Equivalently, does full Hindman's theorem imply \(\mathrm{ACA}_0^+\) over \(\mathrm{RCA}_0\)?
cards.why: The problem asks how much set existence is forced by a basic theorem about finite sums. A reversal would identify unrestricted finite-sums homogeneity with closure under all finite Turing jumps recorded in one set; a separation would show that this known upper theory is stronger than necessary.

cards.title: Universality of Turing equivalence
cards.formal: Is unrestricted Turing equivalence universal among countable Borel equivalence relations? Precisely, is the following proposition true: for every standard Borel space \(X\) and every Borel equivalence relation \(E\subseteq X\times X\) whose equivalence classes are at most countable, there exists a Borel map \(f:X\to2^{\mathbb N}\) such that \[\forall x,y\in X,\qquad x\,E\,y\ \Longleftrightarrow\ f(x)\equiv_T f(y)?\] The map may depend on \(X\) and \(E\); both implications must hold on every pair.
cards.why: A central bridge between computability and descriptive set theory, asking whether equality of computational power can encode every countable Borel classification problem.

cards.title: NP-hardness of conditional polynomial-time pKt
cards.formal:
Does conditional probabilistic time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity admit the following unconditional, uniform padding-compatible NP-hardness reduction in the polynomial-time regime?

For every integer \(\kappa\ge1\), there must exist one randomized polynomial-time map \(R_\kappa\) such that for every integer \(c\ge2\), there exist polynomially bounded, polynomial-time computable length functions \(n_c,m_c:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N_{\ge2}\) with the following property. For every Boolean 3-CNF formula \(z\) of encoded length \(v\ge2\),
\[
R_\kappa(z,1^{n_c(v)},1^{m_c(v)})=(x,y,1^s),
\qquad |x|=n_c(v),\quad |y|=m_c(v),
\]
and, with probability at least \(1-v^{-\kappa}\) over the reduction's random bits,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 z\text{ satisfiable}
 &\ \Longrightarrow\
 \mathrm{pK}_{2/3}^{\,\tau_c(|x|,|y|)}(x\mid y)\le s,\\
 z\text{ unsatisfiable}
 &\ \Longrightarrow\
 \mathrm{pK}_{1/3}^{\,\tau_c(|x|,|y|)}(x\mid y)>s,
\end{aligned}
\qquad
\tau_c(n,m)=(n+1)^c(m+1)^c.
\]
The same \(R_\kappa\) must work for all \(c\); \(c\) affects the chosen output-length schedules and is not a separate input or advice string to the reduction. The schedules may also depend on \(\kappa\). This is the quantified polynomial-regime target underlying the source's Corollary 55.
cards.why: When a short program cannot inspect most of its conditional input, there is a provable source of hardness. Allowing it polynomial time to read and process the whole input removes that obstruction. Establishing the stated uniform hardness reduction would make a major connection between worst-case reductions and the existence of cryptographic hardness.

cards.title: Unconditional coding theorem for randomized Kolmogorov complexity
cards.formal:
Is the following coding statement true without a computational hardness or derandomization assumption?
\[
\forall D\in\mathrm{PSamp}\ \exists c,d\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\
\forall n\ge2\ \forall x\in\operatorname{supp}(D_n):
\quad
\mathrm{rK}^{(n+2)^d}(x)
\le
\left\lceil\log_2\frac1{D_n(x)}\right\rceil
+c\left\lceil\log_2(n+2)\right\rceil .
\]
Here \(D=\{D_n\}_{n\ge2}\) ranges over uniformly polynomial-time samplable distributions on \(n\)-bit strings, and \(\mathrm{rK}^t\) uses private random bits and success probability at least \(2/3\), as defined below. The constants \(c,d\) may depend on the fixed sampler but must work for every length and every string in its support.

The target is existence of short polynomial-time randomized descriptions. No efficient algorithm for finding a description from \(x\) is required.
cards.why: A sampler may assign a string high probability without providing an obvious short description that a fast decoder can use. The question asks whether information content nevertheless always predicts description length, allowing private randomness and logarithmic overhead. A resolution would clarify a recurring gap between information-theoretic coding and computational descriptions.

cards.title: Mortality of \(2\times 2\) integer matrix semigroups
cards.formal: Is there a deterministic Turing machine that, for every finite list \(A_{1},\ldots ,A_{m}\) of \(2\times 2\) integer matrices, halts and correctly decides whether there exist \(\ell\)\(\ge 1\) and indices \(i_{1},\ldots ,i_{\ell}\in \{1,\ldots ,m\}\) with \(A_{i_{1}} A_{i_{2}} \cdots  A_{i_{\ell}}=0_{2}\)?
cards.why: A minimal-dimensional undecidability frontier for matrix products and discrete dynamical systems.

cards.title: Rigidity of the computably enumerable degrees
cards.formal: Is every order automorphism of R, the c.e. Turing degrees, the identity?
cards.why: Rigidity would say that the reducibility position of a computably enumerable degree determines the degree itself.

cards.title: Biinterpretability of computably enumerable degrees with arithmetic
cards.formal: Does R admit a parameter-free first-order interpretation of standard arithmetic together with a parameter-free definable map assigning each degree an index of a c.e. set of that degree?
cards.why: Full biinterpretability would recover individual computability degrees from order-theoretic information.

cards.title: An algorithmic Ahlswede–Körner lemma
cards.formal: Is there a constant \(a>0\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge 2\) and all finite binary strings x,y,z with \(C(x,y)\le n\), some finite binary string \(z'\) satisfies \(C(z' |x,y)\le a \log _{2} n\) and |\(C(w|z)- C(w|z' )|\le a \log _{2} n\) for each \(w\in \{x,y,\langle x,y\rangle\}\)?
cards.why: Tests how far a central information-theoretic replacement principle extends to individual strings, including highly non-stochastic data. Preserving the whole two-string conditional profile would clarify which information relationships can be represented by side information determined almost entirely by the data itself.

cards.title: Shannon feasibility from algorithmic network coding
cards.formal: For every fixed finite acyclic directed network with correlated finite-alphabet sources and specified source-reconstruction demands, does high-probability algorithmic feasibility on independent source blocks imply Shannon achievability at the same edge rates? The algorithmic model permits sample-dependent local programs of length \(O(\log N)\) and \(O(\log N)\) extra bits on each edge for a block of \(N\) samples. The Shannon model requires fixed local encoding and decoding maps for each block length, with vanishing error and arbitrarily small rate slack, as defined below.
cards.why: The question compares information transmission for random sources with transmission of their individual realized strings. A positive answer would show that logarithmic sample-dependent algorithmic descriptions cannot create new asymptotic network rates. A negative answer would expose a concrete operational distinction between Shannon and Kolmogorov descriptions of distributed information.

cards.title: Scaling joint Kolmogorov-complexity profiles
cards.formal: For every fixed integer \(k\ge 1\) and real \(\lambda >0\), does there exist a constant \(c>0\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge 2\) and every tuple of binary strings \(a_{1},\ldots ,a_{k}\) of length at most n, there are finite binary strings \(b_{1},\ldots ,b_{k}\) satisfying |\(C(b_{S})- \lambda  C(a_{S})|\le c \log _{2} n\) for every nonempty \(S\subseteq \{1,\ldots ,k\}\)? The same tuple b must satisfy all \(2^{k}- 1\) inequalities simultaneously.
cards.why: Scaling complete algorithmic-information profiles asks whether shared information has a universal homogeneous geometry, across arbitrary tuples rather than one example.

cards.title: Low-\(n\) Boolean algebra conjecture
cards.formal: For every integer n≥1, does every countable Boolean algebra with a low-n presentation have a computable presentation?
cards.why: This tests whether a weak noncomputable presentation of an algebra can always be replaced by a computable one.

cards.title: Universality of recursive isomorphism on binary sequences
cards.formal: Is recursive isomorphism on binary sequences universal among countable Borel equivalence relations?
cards.why: This asks whether a very concrete computable symmetry relation represents all countable Borel classification problems.

cards.title: Algorithmic networks characterized by cut inequalities
cards.formal:
Characterize the finite directed acyclic network patterns \(\mathcal N\) for which the information-flow inequalities across all cuts are sufficient, with logarithmic precision, for transmitting arbitrary correlated input strings to their requested destinations.

Precisely, determine a necessary-and-sufficient condition on \(\mathcal N\) for the property
\[
\forall a\in\mathbb N\ \exists b,B\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\
\forall n\ge2\ \forall x_1,\ldots,x_k\
\forall (u_e)_{e\in E_{\rm fin}}:
\quad
\operatorname{Cut}_a(\mathcal N,x,u,n)
\Longrightarrow
\operatorname{Code}_{b,B}(\mathcal N,x,u,n),
\]
where \(|x_i|\le n\) and \(u_e\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\). The definitions below specify both predicates. The constants \(b,B\) may depend on the fixed pattern and on \(a\), but not on \(n\), the strings or the capacities.

Equivalently, determine the Boolean characteristic function that assigns one exactly to patterns with this property. The characterization must be a condition on the finite network pattern, including source placement and demands, rather than a restatement of the quantification over strings and codes.
cards.why: A cut counts how much information must enter a group of processors, but it does not describe whether the information can be packaged consistently for all destinations. The requested characterization would identify precisely when these numerical constraints capture the whole coding problem for individual correlated strings.

cards.title: Deciding the two-quantifier theory of c.e. degrees
cards.formal: Is the set of true universal-existential sentences of the pure order R decidable?
cards.why: This locates an important decidability boundary below the known undecidability of the full theory.

cards.title: Deciding finite-lattice embeddability into c.e. degrees
cards.formal: Is there an algorithm deciding whether a finite lattice embeds into R preserving binary joins and meets?
cards.why: This asks for an effective description of the finite algebraic patterns realizable by relative computability.

cards.title: Topological computable categoricity of infinite Polish spaces
cards.formal: Does there exist an infinite Polish space with a computable metric presentation that is topologically computably categorical?
cards.why: This asks whether an infinite complete separable space can have a fully effective topological identity.

cards.title: Degree of topological categoricity of Baire space
cards.formal: Does Baire space have a least Turing degree of topological categoricity?
cards.why: A least degree would measure the computational information required to identify arbitrary effective presentations of a basic space.

cards.title: Strong extractors for infinite sequences
cards.formal:
Does there exist one deterministic oracle Turing machine \(F\) such that for every pair of infinite binary sequences \(x,y\) with
\[\dim(x)=\dim(y)=\tfrac12\]
and global algorithmic independence as defined below, all computations \(F^{x\oplus y}(i)\), \(i\ge0\), halt with a bit, and the resulting sequence \(z(i)=F^{x\oplus y}(i)\) satisfies
\[\dim^x(z)=\dim^y(z)=1?\]
Here \(\dim^a\) is effective Hausdorff dimension measured with the entire sequence \(a\) available as an oracle. The same machine must work for all promised pairs; it receives no description of their independence constants.

This card takes the explicit dimension-one-half instance in the 2012 question and uses “independent” in the global oracle sense of Calude–Zimand's Definition 2.1. The weaker finitary prefix-independence notion is distinguished below; it is not silently substituted for this premise.
cards.why: The question asks whether two imperfectly random infinite sources can yield information of full asymptotic density that remains incompressible even after either entire source is disclosed. It tests how far the strong-extraction principle from finite information extends to arbitrary individual sequences. The distinction matters because an infinite oracle can expose information beyond any fixed pair of input prefixes.

cards.title: Existence of strings without simple optimal hypotheses
cards.formal:
For every polynomial sampling budget, do infinitely many lengths contain a string with no simple optimal statistical hypothesis, when its reference description is allowed a larger polynomial time budget?

The selected unconditional proposition is
\[
\forall U\in\mathcal U\ \forall c\in\mathbb N_{\ge2}\
\exists d\in\mathbb N_{>c}\
\forall N\in\mathbb N_{\ge2}\
\exists n\in\mathbb N_{\ge N}\quad
\operatorname{Bad}_U(c,d,n).
\]
Here \(\mathcal U\) is the explicitly defined class of polynomially universal finite machines below. Write
\[
\begin{split}
\operatorname{Bad}_U(c,d,n)\ \Longleftrightarrow\
\exists x\in\{0,1\}^n\ \forall\mu\in\mathcal D_n\quad
\bigl[
&\operatorname{Simple}_U(\mu;n^c,c\log_2 n)\\
&\Longrightarrow\
\mu(x)\le n^{-c}2^{-C_U^{n^d}(x)}
\bigr].
\end{split}
\]
The set \(\mathcal D_n\) consists of rational probability distributions on \(n\)-bit strings. Simplicity requires an exact sampler with description length strictly less than \(c\log_2 n\), halting within \(n^c\) steps on every choice of its fair random bits. The quantity \(C_U^{n^d}(x)\) is the length of a shortest deterministic description producing \(x\) within \(n^d\) steps. Optimality requires the strict reverse likelihood inequality, so the displayed weak inequality expresses its failure.

The exponent \(d\) may depend on \(U,c\), but must be chosen before the length threshold \(N\), the witness length \(n\), and the string \(x\). The same exponent \(c\) sets the sampling time, logarithmic description budget and inverse-polynomial likelihood slack. No algorithm generating the witness strings is required.

This is the explicitly selected editorial formulation of the source question. The original Question 3 does not state this quantifier order or tie these three budgets to one exponent, and its presentation also invites conditional results. The target here is the displayed unconditional proposition, not a claim that the source already states exactly this variant.
cards.why: This target asks whether computation limits can create an intrinsic gap between descriptions of individual data and simple probabilistic models of that data. It concerns existence of explanatory models, beyond the success of one model-selection or learning algorithm. A resolution would clarify how exact randomized sampling and time-bounded algorithmic information constrain statistical explanation. The selected asymptotic regime makes this structural question precise while leaving its scientific status separate from the editorial choice.

cards.title: Low-two supersets lattice conjecture
cards.formal: For every coinfinite c.e. low-two set A⊆N, is L*(A) isomorphic to E* as a bounded lattice?
cards.why: The question connects computational weakness of a set to the global structure of its supersets.

cards.title: Classifying sets with countable infinite-time decision complexity
cards.formal: Characterize exactly the sets A⊆2^ω having a parameter-free infinite-time decider with a countable uniform time bound, by a necessary-and-sufficient condition on Borel codes expressed through the constructible hierarchy.
cards.why: The problem asks which sets can be recognized with transfinite time budgets, beyond merely locating time suprema.

cards.title: Communication rate for secret-key agreement at fixed Hamming distance
cards.formal:
Determine the function
\[
 R:[0,1]\longrightarrow\mathbb R_{\ge0}
\]
to pointwise absolute accuracy \(1/100\). Here \(R(\theta)\) is the optimal asymptotic public-communication rate, in bits per input bit, for two parties with independent private randomness to agree on a secret key of maximal algorithmic-information length. Their inputs are pairs of \(n\)-bit strings at distance \(\lfloor\theta n\rfloor\) with nearly maximal joint Kolmogorov complexity in that Hamming layer. The precise family, secrecy condition and rate quantifiers are defined below.
cards.why: Determine how the geometry of correlated binary data controls the public communication needed to realize all of its algorithmic mutual information as a shared secret. A sharp rate distinguishes inputs with the same information profile but different communication requirements.

cards.title: Random-oracle invariance of fully extractable common information
cards.formal:
Is the following implication true? For every integer \(c\ge1\) there exists an integer \(d\ge1\) such that for every \(n\ge2\) and every pair of binary words \(x,y\) with \(|x|,|y|\le n\), put \(\ell_n=\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\). If
\[
 \Pr_{X}\!\left[\exists b\in\{0,1\}^*:\
 \begin{array}{l}
 C^X(b\mid x)\le c\ell_n,\quad C^X(b\mid y)\le c\ell_n,\\
 |C^X(b)-I^X(x:y)|\le c\ell_n
 \end{array}\right]\ge2/3,
\]
where \(X\) is an infinite fair random binary oracle, must there exist a finite binary word \(z\) such that
\[
 C(z\mid x)\le d\ell_n,\qquad C(z\mid y)\le d\ell_n,\qquad
 |C(z)-I(x:y)|\le d\ell_n\ ?
\]
The coefficient \(d\) may depend on \(c\) and the fixed description conventions, but not on \(n,x,y\).
cards.why: Mutual information is a number; representing it by a word recoverable from either input is a stronger property. This asks whether an unlimited independent random resource can change that property, even though ordinary complexity values are stable up to small losses with high probability.

cards.title: Two-quantifier theory of the local enumeration degrees
cards.formal: Is the universal-existential theory of the Σ⁰₂ enumeration degrees decidable in the pure order language?
cards.why: The target would identify the complexity of a low-quantifier theory of a fundamental reducibility structure.

cards.title: Admissibility of gaps in infinite-time decision times
cards.formal: In the specified ITTM model, is every nonzero limit ordinal beginning a bounded gap in the spectrum of least countable decision times admissible?
cards.why: A positive theorem would connect gaps in computational time spectra to the structure of admissible set theory.

cards.title: Frege versus Extended Frege
cards.formal:
Does ordinary Frege polynomially simulate Extended Frege in proof size? For the two fixed systems and binary size convention below, determine whether
\[\exists C,k\in\mathbb{N}_{\ge1}\ \forall\varphi\ \forall\pi\;\bigl(\operatorname{EFProof}(\pi,\varphi)\Rightarrow\exists\rho\,[\operatorname{FProof}(\rho,\varphi)\land |\rho|\le C(|\pi|+2)^{k}]\bigr).\]
Here \(\varphi\) ranges over all finite propositional formulas in the ordinary variables, and \(\pi,\rho\) range over finite binary strings. The constants are independent of the formula and of both proofs. This asks for existence of short Frege proofs of the same conclusions; it does not require a polynomial-time algorithm that finds them. Equivalently, for every tautology \(\varphi\), is its minimum Frege proof size \(s_{\mathrm F}(\varphi)\) bounded by one fixed polynomial in its minimum Extended Frege proof size \(s_{\mathrm{EF}}(\varphi)\)?
cards.why: This asks whether naming and reusing intermediate formulas can shorten rigorous propositional proofs by more than every polynomial factor. It is a central comparison between strong proof systems and between reasoning with formula trees and shared circuit representations. A separation would yield superpolynomial lower bounds for unrestricted Frege; an equivalence would show that the extension rule changes shortest-proof lengths by at most polynomial factors.

cards.title: Superpolynomial Extended Frege lower bounds
cards.formal: Is classical Extended Frege not polynomially bounded? Precisely, for every pair of integers \(C\ge1,c\ge1\), does there exist a propositional tautology \(\varphi\) such that every Extended Frege proof \(\pi\) of \(\varphi\) has binary encoding length \(|\pi|>C(|\varphi|+2)^c\)? The formula and proof encodings and the fixed proof rules are specified below.
cards.why: Extended Frege captures a powerful form of efficient propositional reasoning with reusable definitions. A superpolynomial lower bound would cross one of the central barriers in proof complexity and clarify whether a standard, highly expressive certificate language necessarily fails on some short true statements.

cards.title: Existence of p-optimal proof systems
cards.formal: Does there exist a Cook–Reckhow proof system P for propositional tautologies such that, for every Cook–Reckhow proof system Q for the same tautologies, there is a deterministic polynomial-time translation \(t_{Q}\) satisfying \(\mathrm{P}(t_{Q}(\pi ))=Q(\pi )\) for every finite binary proof string \(\pi\)?
cards.why: Asks whether one efficiently checkable proof formalism can efficiently absorb every other such formalism.

cards.title: Superpolynomial lower bounds for unrestricted Frege proofs
cards.formal:
Is ordinary Frege not polynomially bounded? For the fixed calculus and complete binary encoding below, determine whether
\[\forall C,k\in\mathbb{N}_{\ge1}\ \exists\varphi\;\bigl(\operatorname{Taut}(\varphi)\land\forall\pi\,[\operatorname{FProof}(\pi,\varphi)\Rightarrow |\pi|>C(|\varphi|+2)^k]\bigr).\]
Here \(\varphi\) ranges over finite propositional formulas, and \(\pi\) over finite binary strings. Equivalently, for every fixed polynomial bound, some tautology has minimum Frege proof size \(s_{\mathrm F}(\varphi)\) exceeding that bound in its own encoded length. Neither a polynomial-time construction of hard tautologies nor any algorithm for finding their shortest proofs is required. The depth and length of intermediate formulas and the reuse of previous lines are unrestricted.
cards.why: This asks whether a standard, robust language of propositional deduction must sometimes use certificates larger than every polynomial in the statement proved. It is a central unresolved lower-bound question for formal reasoning, beyond the restricted proof systems for which strong size lower bounds are known. It concerns the size of the best possible proof, independently of the resources used to discover it.

cards.title: Weak automatability of Resolution
cards.formal: Is there a deterministic algorithm, running in time polynomial in \(|F|+s\), that on input a CNF formula \(F\) and a unary proof budget \(1^{s}\) distinguishes the following two promised cases: \(F\) is satisfiable, or \(F\) has a Resolution refutation with at most \(s\) clauses?
