cards.title: Tight ETH lower bounds for binary Nearest Codeword at every constant factor
cards.formal:
Does the deterministic Exponential Time Hypothesis imply the following statement? For every fixed rational \(\gamma>1\), there do not exist computable functions \(f:\mathbb N_{\ge1}\to\mathbb N_{\ge1}\) and \(g:\mathbb N_{\ge1}\to\mathbb Q_{\ge0}\) with \(\lim_{k\to\infty}g(k)/k=0\), and a uniform deterministic algorithm that solves \(\gamma\)-Gap-\(k\)-Nearest Codeword over \(\mathbb F_2\) in at most
\[
f(k)(L+2)^{g(k)}
\]
bit operations on every valid encoded instance of length \(L\)? The parameter \(k\) bounds the number of erroneous coordinates, and the two promised cases are distance at most \(k\) versus distance greater than \(\gamma k\).
cards.why: This asks whether ordinary satisfiability hardness already yields the tight parameter dependence for arbitrarily coarse constant-factor decoding. It would close a specific gap between ETH and Gap-ETH in the fine-grained theory of error-correcting codes.

cards.title: Slice-wise Polynomial Space Conjecture
cards.formal: Is it true that no XNLP-hard parameterized decision problem has a single deterministic algorithm with both worst-case time \((n+2)^{f(k)}\) and working space \(f(k)(n+2)^{c}\), for any total computable function \(f:N\to N\) and any absolute constant c? Here k is the parameter, n is the bit length of the ordinary input, and both resource bounds must hold on the same execution. Hardness uses parameterized logspace many-one reductions defined below.
cards.why: Would explain a broad barrier to reducing the memory of parameterized dynamic programming while keeping polynomial time for each fixed parameter, connecting practical table-size tradeoffs with a uniform complexity-class obstruction.

cards.title: Job-shop approximation parameterized only by machines and accuracy
cards.formal:
Do there exist a total computable function \(F:\mathbb N_{\ge1}^2\to\mathbb N_{\ge1}\), an integer \(c\ge1\), and one uniform deterministic algorithm \(A\) such that, for every number of machines \(m\ge1\), accuracy parameter \(q\ge1\), and job-shop instance \(I\) defined below, \(A(I,q)\) returns a feasible schedule \(S\) satisfying
\[
C_{\max}(S)\le(1+1/q)\operatorname{OPT}(I)
\]
in at most \(F(m,q)(L+1)^c\) Turing-machine steps, where \(L\) is the complete binary input length? The number of operations per job is unbounded and may not be an additional parameter of \(F\).
cards.why: Machine count alone is a natural measure of shop complexity, but long job routes can still encode difficult interactions. An approximation scheme with no separate route-length parameter would clarify whether near-optimal schedules remain tractable on a fixed shop even when individual jobs revisit machines many times.

cards.title: Polynomial kernel for Planar Edge Deletion
cards.formal:
Does Planar Edge Deletion admit a deterministic polynomial kernel parameterized by the edge-deletion budget \(k\)?

An instance consists of a finite simple undirected graph \(G\) and an integer \(k\ge0\). Write
\[
\operatorname{PED}(G,k)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists F\subseteq E(G):\ |F|\le k\ \text{and}\ G-F\ \text{is planar}.
\]
Here \(G-F\) retains all vertices and removes exactly the edges in \(F\). There is no promise on the input graph.

Precisely, do there exist one deterministic multitape Turing machine \(M\) and fixed integers \(C,a,b\ge1\) such that, on every valid input of bit length \(L\), \(M\) halts within \(C(L+1)^a\) bit steps and outputs a valid instance \((G',k')\) of this same problem satisfying
\[
\operatorname{PED}(G,k)\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \operatorname{PED}(G',k'),
\qquad
|\operatorname{enc}(G',k')|+k'\le C(k+1)^b?
\]
The program, constants and exponents are independent of \(G\) and \(k\). There is no complexity-theoretic assumption in this existence question.
cards.why: Planar Edge Deletion is a concrete test of whether a graph close to a central minor-closed class can be reduced efficiently to polynomially many relevant bits. A polynomial kernel would bound the information needed for exact edge repair solely by the repair budget, despite an arbitrarily large input graph. Its position between fixed-parameter algorithms, graph-minor structure and the broader forbidden-minor edge-deletion question gives it significance beyond one reduction rule.

cards.title: Independent set algorithms from tropical circuit size
cards.formal: Do there exist one deterministic multitape Turing machine \(A\), a real constant \(K>0\) and an integer \(a\ge1\) such that, for every finite simple graph \(G\) on \(n\ge1\) labeled vertices and every nonnegative integer weight vector \(w\), the machine outputs the exact value \(\operatorname{MWIS}(G,w)\) within \(K(\tau(G)+n+L+1)^a\) bit operations? Here \(L\) is the total encoded length of the weights and \(\tau(G)\) is the minimum tropical-circuit size defined below. The input contains only \(G,w\), without a circuit, a decomposition or the value of \(\tau(G)\).
cards.why: A compact circuit can express a dynamic program for every weight assignment to one graph without explaining how to discover it. This question asks whether the existence of that compact representation always yields an effective uniform algorithm, connecting nonuniform computation with exact graph optimization.

cards.title: Converting CNF to DNF
cards.formal:
Determine the worst-case minimum DNF term count of a Boolean function representable by a \(k\)-CNF on \(n\) variables. More precisely, for integers \(1\le k\le n\), let \(\mathcal C_{n,k}\) be the set of Boolean functions on \(\{0,1\}^n\) representable as a conjunction of clauses, each containing at most \(k\) literals. Define
\[
d(f)=\min\{\text{number of terms in }D:D\text{ is a DNF on the same variables and }D(x)=f(x)\text{ for every }x\in\{0,1\}^n\},
\]
\[
M(n,k)=\max_{f\in\mathcal C_{n,k}}d(f).
\]
Supply a mathematical description of a real-valued function \(g\) on \(\mathcal D=\{(n,k)\in\mathbb Z^2:1\le k\le n\}\), with a complete Lean proof that
\[
\forall(n,k)\in\mathcal D,\qquad
|g(n,k)-M(n,k)|\le\frac1{100}.
\]
The error is measured in the unnormalized number of DNF terms. The approximation need not be integer-valued. This finite-parameter determination is an editorial extension of the source’s request to close the gap between exponential upper and lower bounds.
cards.why: The same Boolean function can have very different sizes in conjunctive and disjunctive normal form. This question measures the largest unavoidable number of DNF terms when only the input clause width and number of variables are fixed, separating an inherent representation cost from the performance of any particular conversion algorithm.

cards.title: Cutwidth
cards.formal:
Does there exist a uniform deterministic algorithm that computes the cutwidth of every finite simple undirected graph on \(n\) vertices in time \(O(c^n)\) for some fixed constant \(c<2\)?

Precisely, do there exist one machine \(A\), a rational constant \(c\) with \(1<c<2\), and an integer \(K\ge1\) such that, on every graph \(G\) encoded as below, \(A\) outputs \(\operatorname{cw}(G)\) and halts within \(Kc^n\) transitions? Neither \(c\) nor \(K\) may depend on the graph, its size, its cutwidth or any auxiliary parameter.
cards.why: Cutwidth measures how many connections must cross the busiest boundary in a sequential arrangement of a graph. Computing it requires coordinating a whole vertex order, and the standard subset-based running time has resisted a uniform exponential improvement. A faster exact algorithm would clarify how much of that subset enumeration is essential for a basic graph layout problem.

cards.title: Sub-base-two exact maximum acyclic subgraph
cards.formal: Do there exist constants \(1<c<2\), \(K\ge1\), an integer \(a\ge0\), and one uniform deterministic algorithm that, for every unweighted directed graph on \(n\) vertices, outputs a maximum-cardinality acyclic spanning subgraph in at most \(Kc^n(n+1)^a\) bit operations? The exponent parameter is the number of vertices, and the graph class and computational model are specified below.
cards.why: Many ordering problems admit exact algorithms whose time grows like two to the number of vertices. Maximum acyclic subgraph is a basic test of whether directed precedence constraints permit a fixed exponential improvement, without restricting the input graph or accepting an approximate ordering.

cards.title: Polynomial exact metric sparsifiers with a crossing-edge budget
cards.formal: Do there exist absolute constants \(C,c>0\) such that the following holds? For every finite simple undirected unweighted graph \(G=(V,E)\), terminal set \(T\subseteq V\) of size r, and integer \(p\ge 0\), there is a set \(Z\subseteq E\) with |\(Z|\le C(1+p+r)^{c}\) having this universal property: for every finite nonempty label set D, every metric \(\mu :D\times D\to R_{\ge 0}\), and every terminal labeling \(\tau :T\to D\), if there exists a labeling \(\lambda :V\to D\) extending \(\tau\) with at most p crossing edges, then some labeling \(\lambda\)* of minimum \(\mu\)-cost among all such budget-feasible extensions has all its crossing edges in Z. The same Z must work simultaneously for every \(D,\mu ,\tau\) and depends only on G,T,p. This is the polynomial-size version of the contraction-based metric-sparsifier property in the source’s Theorem 22; that theorem’s earlier quasipolynomial upper-bound claim was later retracted.
cards.why: Would determine whether a graph can be compressed once for every metric-labeling objective under a bounded number of label changes, a stronger form of reusable exact information than preserving ordinary terminal cut values.

cards.title: Disjoint-union closure of tractable forbidden patterns
cards.formal: For every pair of fixed nonempty finite simple graphs \(H_{1},H_{2}\), is the following implication true? If Independent Set parameterized by the requested set size k is fixed-parameter tractable on \(H_{1}\)-free graphs and is fixed-parameter tractable on \(H_{2}\)-free graphs, then it is fixed-parameter tractable on \((H_{1}\sqcup H_{2})\)-free graphs. Here exclusion is as an induced subgraph, ⊔ is disjoint union of the forbidden patterns, and fixed-parameter tractability has the deterministic meaning defined below. The two forbidden graphs may themselves be disconnected and may be isomorphic.
cards.why: A closure theorem would reduce the classification of parameterized Independent Set with one forbidden induced pattern to its connected components. It would organize many currently separate tractability results through one general structural principle.

cards.title: Expected FPT delay from small-witness decision
cards.formal: Does every self-contained \(k\)-witness problem whose decision version is fixed-parameter tractable admit an always-correct randomized enumeration algorithm with expected delay \(f(k)L^{O(1)}\), where \(L\) is the encoded input length and \(f\) is a computable function? The algorithm must output every distinct witness exactly once and terminate, with the same expected bound before the first output and after the last. This selects the expected-delay branch of the source question; deterministic delay and the weaker incremental bounds are distinct companion questions.
cards.why: Tests how far an efficient existence test can be converted into a reliably responsive generator of all small solutions. The distinction between total work and delays matters when a solution set is large and users need successive answers before enumeration finishes.

cards.title: Fixed-parameter tractability of Perfect Edge Deletion
cards.formal:
Is Perfect Edge Deletion fixed-parameter tractable when the only parameter is the number of edges allowed to be deleted?

Precisely, do there exist one uniform deterministic algorithm \(A\), an integer \(c\ge1\), and a total computable function \(f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N_{\ge1}\) such that, for every input \((G,k)\) of bit length \(L\), \(A\) decides within \(f(k)(L+1)^c\) steps whether there is a set \(S\subseteq E(G)\) satisfying
\[
|S|\le k
\quad\text{and}\quad
(V(G),E(G)\setminus S)\text{ is perfect}?
\]
The exponent \(c\) is independent of \(k\), and the same program and function must work on every input graph.
cards.why: Perfect graphs form a broad class on which fundamental optimization problems become tractable. An algorithm for repairing a graph by a small number of edge deletions would locate an important boundary of parameterized graph modification. The distinction from vertex deletion is substantive: the vertex problem already has strong parameterized hardness, while the edge problem has remained unresolved across successive surveys.

cards.title: Exact counting of linear extensions below base two
cards.formal: Does there exist a uniform deterministic algorithm \(A\), constants \(K>0\) and \(1<c<2\), and an integer \(n_0\), such that, for every \(n\ge n_0\) and every partial order \(P\) on \([n]\), \(A\) outputs the exact number \(e(P)\) of linear extensions using at most \(Kc^n\) bit-cost random-access steps? It must also terminate correctly on every smaller valid input. There is no restriction on the width, height, dimension, sparsity or a graph parameter of \(P\).
cards.why: The target asks whether a canonical exact counting problem can beat the all-subsets exponential barrier on every input, despite the ease of finding one feasible ordering. It connects precedence counting with the structure of exact exponential algorithms. The original target is retained historically because a checked 2026 preprint now answers it.

area: Approximation algorithms and hardness of approximation
label: Approximation algorithms and inapproximability

cards.title: Unique Games Conjecture
cards.formal:
Is the following proposition true? For every pair of rational constants \(\varepsilon,\delta>0\) with \(\varepsilon+\delta<1\), there exists an integer \(q\ge2\) such that it is NP-hard to distinguish the following two classes of explicitly listed Unique Games instances over the alphabet \([q]=\{1,\ldots,q\}\):
\[\text{YES: }\operatorname{val}(G)\ge1-\varepsilon,\qquad \text{NO: }\operatorname{val}(G)\le\delta.\]
NP-hardness here means a deterministic polynomial-time many-one reduction from 3SAT with the completeness and soundness guarantees defined below. The alphabet size and the reduction may depend on the two constants but must be fixed before the input size grows. The target is this hardness proposition itself, without assuming \(\mathrm P\ne\mathrm{NP}\).
cards.why: UGC would turn many conditional approximation thresholds into NP-hardness theorems and explain the optimality of a general SDP framework. Its very simple permutation constraints isolate a fundamental boundary between exact consistency, approximate consistency, and hardness amplification.

cards.title: Constant-factor approximation for Densest k-Subgraph
cards.formal:
Does Densest \(k\)-Subgraph have a deterministic polynomial-time constant-factor approximation on all explicitly given finite simple undirected unweighted graphs?

For \(n\ge1\), write \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). If \(G=([n],E)\) and \(1\le k\le n\), define
\[e_G(S)=|\{\{u,v\}\in E:u,v\in S\}|,\qquad \operatorname{OPT}(G,k)=\max_{\substack{T\subseteq[n]\\|T|=k}}e_G(T).\]
The proposition is that there exist one real constant \(C\ge1\), positive integer constants \(D,d\), and one deterministic multitape Turing machine \(A\) such that, on every encoded input of length \(L\), \(A\) halts within \(D(L+1)^d\) bit steps, and on every valid \((G,k)\) it outputs an explicitly represented set \(S\subseteq[n]\) satisfying
\[|S|=k\qquad\text{and}\qquad C\,e_G(S)\ge\operatorname{OPT}(G,k).\]
The same algorithm, constants and polynomial clock must work for all \(n,G,k\).
cards.why: Densest k-Subgraph asks whether a prescribed number of vertices can capture a constant fraction of the greatest possible internal connectivity. Its approximation landscape is a central gap between available algorithms, conditional hardness and what follows from the usual P-versus-NP assumption. The answer also matters for several graph optimization objectives linked to its approximability.

cards.title: Small-Set Expansion Hypothesis
cards.formal: For every rational constant \(\eta \in (0,1/2)\), is there a rational constant \(\delta \in (0,1/2)\) such that the following promise problem is NP-hard under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions? Given a regular graph G on n vertices with \(\delta n\) an integer, distinguish YES: some \(S\subseteq V(G)\) with |\(S|=\delta n\) has \(\Phi _{G}(S)\le \eta\), from NO: every \(S\subseteq V(G)\) with |\(S|=\delta n\) has \(\Phi _{G}(S)\ge 1- \eta\).
cards.why: A major proposed basis for hardness of graph partitioning and layout problems, with connections to Unique Games.

cards.title: Polylogarithmic approximation for Directed Steiner Tree
cards.formal:
Do there exist positive integers \(a,C,K,q\) and one uniform randomized classical algorithm \(A\) such that, for every feasible Directed Steiner Tree instance \(I\) of encoding length \(N\) with \(k\ge1\) terminals, every execution halts within \(K(N+1)^q\) bit steps and outputs a feasible arc subset \(F\), and
\[\Pr\!\left[c(F)\le a\bigl(\log_2(k+2)\bigr)^C\operatorname{OPT}(I)\right]\ge\frac23?\]
The probability is over the algorithm’s internal randomness, separately for each input. The graph is arbitrary and directed, with exactly represented nonnegative rational arc costs. All four constants and the program must be independent of the instance.
cards.why: A defining gap in directed network-design approximation: determine whether a shared directed connection network can be approximated within a polylogarithmic factor using only polynomial time.

cards.title: Constant-factor approximation for uniform Sparsest Cut
cards.formal:
Do there exist real constants \(C\ge1\) and \(K>0\), an integer constant \(d\ge1\), and one uniform classical randomized Turing machine \(A\) with the following property? For every finite simple undirected graph \(G\) on \(n\ge2\) vertices, every execution halts within \(K(n+1)^d\) bit operations and outputs a nonempty proper vertex set \(S\). For each fixed input graph,
\[
 \Pr\!\left[\varphi_G(S)\le C\operatorname{OPT}(G)\right]\ge\frac23,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{OPT}(G)=\min_{\varnothing\ne T\subsetneq V(G)}\varphi_G(T),
 \qquad
 \varphi_G(T)=\frac{|E(T,V(G)\setminus T)|}{|T|\,|V(G)\setminus T|}.
\]
The same machine and constants must work for all these graphs.
cards.why: A constant approximation would bound the quality loss for finding sparse graph separations independently of graph size, addressing a central question connecting approximation algorithms and metric geometry.

cards.title: Vertex Cover approximation below factor two
cards.formal:
Do there exist a rational constant \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\), a uniform deterministic algorithm \(A\), and integers \(B,k\ge1\) such that, on every explicitly encoded finite simple undirected graph \(G\) of input bit length \(L\), the algorithm halts within \(B(L+1)^k\) Turing-machine steps and returns a vertex cover \(S\) satisfying
\[|S|\le(2-\varepsilon)\tau(G),\qquad
\tau(G)=\min\{|T|:T\subseteq V(G),\ T\text{ is a vertex cover of }G\}?\]
The same positive improvement \(\varepsilon\) and the same algorithm must work for graphs of all sizes, with no structural promise. Vertices have unit cost. The question asks for an unconditional algorithm-existence theorem or its unconditional negation.
cards.why: Vertex Cover is a basic covering problem with a long-standing gap between its factor-two algorithmic benchmark and known unconditional hardness thresholds. A fixed improvement would distinguish the true computational limit from a barrier shared by many methods. Ruling out every such algorithm would require an unconditional complexity separation, so the logical strength of the chosen question must remain explicit.

cards.title: Subtour-LP integrality gap for metric TSP
cards.formal:
Determine, to absolute accuracy \(1/100\), the universal subtour-LP integrality gap for the symmetric metric traveling-salesperson problem:
\[
 \Gamma=\sup_{n\ge3}\ \sup_{c\in\mathcal M_n}
 \frac{\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{TSP}}(c)}{\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{LP}}(c)}.
\]
Here \(\mathcal M_n\) is the set of all metrics on \(n\) labeled vertices, and the two optima are defined below. The target is this one dimensionless real number over all finite sizes, not the gap for one fixed number of vertices or for a restricted metric family.
cards.why: The exact strength of the principal relaxation for a canonical optimization problem, joining polyhedral structure, probabilistic rounding and approximation. A resolution would explain a longstanding gap between fractional connectivity and integral tours.

cards.title: Constant-factor approximation for Directed Feedback Vertex Set
cards.formal:
Does there exist a uniform deterministic polynomial-time constant-factor approximation for minimum-weight Directed Feedback Vertex Set on arbitrary finite directed graphs?

Precisely, do there exist one machine \(A\) and integers \(C,K,d\ge1\) such that, for every valid input \((D,w)\) of bit length \(L\), the machine halts within \(K(L+1)^d\) transitions and outputs a set \(F\subseteq V(D)\) satisfying
\[
D-F\text{ is acyclic},\qquad
\sum_{v\in F}w(v)\le C\,\operatorname{OPT}(D,w)?
\]
The same \(C,K,d,A\) must work for every graph and every allowed assignment of weights.
cards.why: Deleting vertices to destroy every directed cycle is a basic optimization problem for cyclic dependencies. Its approximation behavior differs sharply from the undirected version: special directed graph classes admit constant factors, while the general case has resisted them and has strong conditional hardness. Resolving the unrestricted weighted target would clarify a central boundary of efficient approximation for directed graphs.

cards.title: Optimal polynomial-time approximation ratio for metric k-Median
cards.formal: Determine the real number \[\rho_{\mathrm{med}}=\inf\mathcal R,\qquad \mathcal R=\{r\in\mathbb R:r\ge1\text{ and an algorithm with guarantee }r\text{ below exists}\}.\] For each fixed \(r\), the guarantee requires one uniform classical randomized algorithm \(A\), a constant \(K\ge1\) and an integer \(b\ge1\) such that, for every valid metric k-Median input of bit length \(L\), every execution finishes within \(KL^b\) steps and returns a nonempty set \(S\subseteq F\) with \(|S|\le k\), while \[\Pr[\operatorname{cost}(S)\le r\operatorname{OPT}]\ge2/3.\] The program and constants may depend on \(r\), but not on the input, \(k\), metric size or distance precision. Determine \(\rho_{\mathrm{med}}\) with absolute error at most \(1/100\), without an additional unproved complexity assumption.
cards.why: A central unresolved approximation threshold for metric clustering, separating known coverage hardness from the best algorithms with a strict facility budget.

cards.title: Unconditional NP-hardness at the Goemans–Williamson Max-Cut threshold
cards.formal:
Let
\[
 \alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}=
 \min_{0<\theta\le\pi}\frac{2\theta}{\pi(1-\cos\theta)}.
\]
Is the following statement true? For every rational \(\varepsilon\) with \(0<\varepsilon<1-\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\), there exist rational constants \(0<b<a\le1\), with
\[
 \frac ba<\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}+\varepsilon,
\]
and a deterministic polynomial-time many-one reduction \(R_\varepsilon\) from 3-SAT to simple unweighted Max-Cut such that, for every 3-CNF formula \(\varphi\), its output graph has at least one edge and satisfies
\[
 \varphi\text{ satisfiable}\ \Longrightarrow
       \operatorname{val}(R_\varepsilon(\varphi))\ge a,
 \qquad
 \varphi\text{ unsatisfiable}\ \Longrightarrow
       \operatorname{val}(R_\varepsilon(\varphi))\le b?
\]
The statement assumes no hardness conjecture.
cards.why: An unconditional reduction at this threshold would explain the limit of a landmark semidefinite approximation algorithm using ordinary NP-hardness, without adding a separate hardness conjecture.

cards.title: Optimal polynomial-time approximation ratio for metric TSP
cards.formal:
Determine, to absolute accuracy \(1/100\), the optimal expected polynomial-time approximation ratio for symmetric metric traveling-salesperson problems:
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{TSP}}=\inf\mathcal R,
\qquad
 \mathcal R=\{r\in\mathbb R:r\ge1\text{ and }r\text{ is achievable as defined below}\}.
\]
The infimum ranges over all uniform classical randomized algorithms in the stated bit model and all finite input metrics. It is an unconditional real constant; no unproved complexity assumption is part of its definition.
cards.why: Determine the fundamental efficient-approximation limit of the canonical routing problem, beyond the guarantees of any one linear relaxation or rounding algorithm.

cards.title: Subtour-LP integrality gap for asymmetric TSP
cards.formal: Determine \(\Gamma _{\mathrm{ATSP}}=\sup\){\(\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{ATSP}}(c)/\mathrm{LP}_{\mathrm{ATSP}}(c): n\ge 2, c\) is a nonnegative directed metric on n vertices, \(\mathrm{LP}_{\mathrm{ATSP}}(c)>0\)}, using the tour and linear program below.
cards.why: Would identify the fundamental relaxation gap for asymmetric travelling salesman.

cards.title: Optimal general-domain CSP approximation under Unique Games hardness
cards.formal: Assuming the Unique Games Conjecture and \(\mathrm{NP}\not\subseteq\mathrm{BPP}\), determine up to universal constant factors the optimal expected approximation ratio \(\rho(k,d)\) for every fixed arity \(k\ge2\) and domain size \(d\ge2\). The source proposes the scale \[q(k,d)=\frac{\max\{k,\log d\}}{d^{k-1}},\] which is retained as context rather than assumed to equal the answer.
cards.why: The question asks how arity and the number of labels jointly control the best efficient approximation of arbitrary local constraints. Matching bounds would explain the transition between Boolean-like behavior and large-domain instances, with consequences for the quantitative strength of probabilistically checkable proofs.

cards.title: Min-CSP approximation at the SDP integrality gap
cards.formal:
For every fixed finite domain \(D\), positive arity \(k\), and finite set \(\Lambda\) of nonnegative rational cost functions \(f:D^k\to[0,1]\), is the following true? For every rational \(\varepsilon>0\), there is a randomized polynomial-time algorithm which, on every \(n\)-variable minimization \(\Lambda\)-CSP instance \(I\) with finite \(n\)-variable SDP integrality gap \(\alpha_\Lambda(n)\), returns an assignment \(\sigma\) such that
\[\Pr\bigl[\operatorname{cost}_I(\sigma)\leq (1+\varepsilon)\alpha_\Lambda(n)\operatorname{OPT}(I)\bigr]\geq\tfrac23?\]
The same algorithm handles all \(n\); it also halts and returns an assignment on the sizes where the gap is infinite, but no multiplicative guarantee is imposed there. The gap and the basic SDP are defined below.
cards.why: A universal theorem would extend the general SDP approximation framework to multiplicative minimization guarantees, including instances whose optimum vanishes with input size. It would connect a geometric obstruction of a standard relaxation to actual polynomial-time approximation across all finite cost languages. A counterexample would identify a limit to interpreting integrality gaps as achievable algorithmic benchmarks.

cards.title: Optimal polynomial-time approximation ratio for asymmetric TSP
cards.formal:
Determine the real constant \(\rho_{\mathrm{ATSP}}\), the infimum of achievable expected-cost approximation ratios for the asymmetric metric traveling salesman problem, under worst-case polynomial running time. Let \(\mathcal I\) be the set of valid rational distance-matrix instances and \(\mathcal A\) the class of uniform randomized, always-feasible algorithms defined below. Put
\[
\mathcal R=
\left\{r\in\mathbb R:\ r\ge1\ \land\ \exists A\in\mathcal A\ \forall I\in\mathcal I,
\quad\mathbb E_{\omega}\bigl[\operatorname{cost}_I(A(I;\omega))\bigr]
\le r\operatorname{OPT}(I)\right\},
\qquad
\rho_{\mathrm{ATSP}}=\inf\mathcal R.
\]
Supply a real value \(a\) with a complete Lean proof that
\[
\left|a-\rho_{\mathrm{ATSP}}\right|\le\frac1{100}.
\]
The algorithm and its polynomial time bound may depend on the achievable ratio \(r\), but must work for every valid instance. No complexity assumption is included in the target. The requested accuracy is additive error in the dimensionless approximation ratio.
cards.why: Asymmetric TSP is a central model of directed routing, where travel costs can depend on direction. Determining its efficient approximation threshold would measure how much optimality must be sacrificed for polynomial computation, beyond the breakthrough establishing that some constant factor is possible.

cards.title: Optimal polynomial-time approximation ratio for Steiner Tree
cards.formal:
Determine the real constant \(\rho_{\mathrm{ST}}\), the infimum of achievable expected-cost approximation ratios for undirected weighted Steiner Tree under worst-case polynomial running time. For the valid instances \(\mathcal I\) and the uniform randomized, always-feasible algorithms \(\mathcal A\) defined below, put
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathrm{ST}}=
\left\{r\in\mathbb R:
r\ge1\ \land\
\exists A\in\mathcal A\ \forall I\in\mathcal I,\
\mathbb E_{\omega}\!\left[\operatorname{cost}_I(A(I;\omega))\right]
\le r\,\operatorname{OPT}(I)\right\},
\qquad
\rho_{\mathrm{ST}}=\inf\mathcal R_{\mathrm{ST}}.
\]
Supply an unambiguous real value \(a\) and a complete Lean proof that
\[
\left|a-\rho_{\mathrm{ST}}\right|\le\frac1{100}.
\]
The algorithm and its polynomial time bound may depend on \(r\), but must work for every valid instance. The expectation concerns output cost, not running time. No complexity assumption is part of the definition. The requested error is additive in this dimensionless approximation ratio.
cards.why: Steiner Tree is a basic network-design problem and a recurring subproblem in more general connectivity objectives. Determining its efficient approximation threshold would establish how closely polynomial-time algorithms can approach optimal connection cost in unrestricted weighted graphs. The target compares all algorithms, making it broader than the accuracy of one method or the strength of one relaxation.

cards.title: Parameterized Inapproximability Hypothesis from \(\mathrm{FPT} \ne  \mathrm{W}[1]\)
cards.formal: Assuming \(\mathrm{W}[1]\ne \mathrm{FPT}\), is there an absolute constant \(\varepsilon \in (0,1)\) such that no deterministic fixed-parameter algorithm can distinguish a satisfiable binary constraint satisfaction instance on k variables from an instance in which every assignment violates at least an \(\varepsilon\) fraction of the constraints, with k as the parameter?
cards.why: Would supply a parameterized analogue of the PCP theorem from the standard exact-hardness assumption, giving a common basis for constant-gap inapproximability across many parameterized optimization problems.

cards.title: Optimal approximation for nonmonotone submodular maximization over a matroid
cards.formal:
Determine the optimal expected approximation ratio for maximizing a nonnegative, not necessarily monotone submodular set function subject to one matroid independence constraint, in the polynomial-time oracle model specified below.

For an instance \(J=(n,f,\mathcal I)\), write
\[
\operatorname{OPT}(J)=\max\{f(S):S\in\mathcal I\}.
\]
Let \(\mathscr A\) be the class of uniform randomized oracle algorithms defined below: each always outputs an independent set and has a polynomial bound on its total number of elementary operations, on every valid instance and every random tape. Define
\[
\mathcal R=\left\{\alpha\in[0,1]:
 \exists A\in\mathscr A\ \forall J\
 \mathbb E_{\omega}\!\left[f\!\left(A^{f,\mathcal I}(n;\omega)\right)\right]
 \ge \alpha\,\operatorname{OPT}(J)\right\},
\qquad
\rho_{\mathrm{mat}}=\sup\mathcal R.
\]
The universal quantifier ranges over every finite ground-set size, every nonnegative submodular function on that ground set, and every matroid on it. The approximation constant and algorithm are chosen before the instance. The target is the real number \(\rho_{\mathrm{mat}}\); it is not assumed that an algorithm attains the supremum. Supply a real answer \(a\) with a Lean-checked proof that
\[
|a-\rho_{\mathrm{mat}}|\le \frac{1}{100}.
\]
cards.why: This is a central approximation question for a general combinatorial optimization model, rather than a guarantee for one application or a running-time refinement. Matroids include cardinality, partition and linear-independence constraints, and submodularity encompasses many cut, coverage and information objectives. Determining the optimal guarantee would identify the inherent cost of combining diminishing returns, potentially harmful additions and independence constraints. Unlike several neighboring monotone or unconstrained models, the known algorithmic and information-theoretic bounds still leave a substantial gap.

cards.title: Does a fixed d-to-1 Games conjecture imply Unique Games?
cards.formal:
Is the following implication true for the classical constraint games and deterministic polynomial reductions defined below?
\[\bigl(\exists\,d\in\mathbb N,\ d\ge2\text{ and }D_d\bigr)\ \Longrightarrow\ \mathrm{UGC}.\]
Here \(D_d\) is the perfect-completeness \(d\)-to-one Games conjecture with \(d\) fixed independently of the soundness parameter; \(\mathrm{UGC}\) is the full near-perfect-completeness Unique Games conjecture. Equivalently, for every fixed \(d\ge2\), does \(D_d\) imply \(\mathrm{UGC}\)? The card retains the forward implication singled out in the saved source excerpt.
cards.why: An implication would connect exact satisfiability in many-to-one constraint games with the near-satisfiable permutation games used to predict sharp approximation thresholds. The new perfect-completeness four-to-one claim makes this relationship especially consequential: accepting that theorem would make the requested implication as strong as full UGC.

cards.title: Constant-factor approximation for Dasgupta’s hierarchical clustering objective
cards.formal: Do there exist real constants \(C\ge1\), \(K>0\), an integer \(a\ge1\), and one deterministic multitape Turing machine which, on every explicitly encoded nonnegative rational similarity graph \(G\), outputs a hierarchy \(T\) with \(\operatorname{cost}_G(T)\le C\operatorname{OPT}(G)\) within \(K(N+1)^a\) bit operations, where \(N\) is the total input bit length and the cost and allowed hierarchies are defined below?
cards.why: A hierarchy must represent similarity at every scale, so optimizing a single flat partition is insufficient. A constant approximation for this canonical objective would give a uniform quality guarantee on arbitrary similarity data and would cross a major graph-partitioning hardness barrier.

cards.title: Optimal polynomial-time approximation ratio for Euclidean k-means
cards.formal:
Determine the real constant
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{EucKM}}=
 \inf\left\{r\in[1,\infty):\begin{array}{l}
 \text{there is one uniform randomized polynomial-time algorithm }A\\
 \text{such that }\mathbb E[\operatorname{cost}_I(A(I))]
 \le r\operatorname{OPT}(I)\text{ for every valid instance }I
 \end{array}\right\}
\]
to absolute error at most \(1/100\), using the explicit rational-input, arbitrary-center and worst-case polynomial bit-time model below. Neither the number of clusters nor the dimension is fixed.
cards.why: Locate the computational approximation limit of a central clustering objective when neither dimension nor cluster count is a fixed parameter. This separates what any efficient algorithm can achieve from the performance of the current best technique.

cards.title: Almost 3-colorable graphs versus graphs with no large independent set
cards.formal: For every fixed pair of constants \(0<\eta <1\) and \(0<\varepsilon <(1- \eta )/3\), is it NP-hard to distinguish graphs G on N vertices in which an induced subgraph on at least \((1- \eta )N\) vertices is properly 3-colorable from graphs G with independence number \(\alpha (G)<\varepsilon N\)? This is the nonoverlapping promise range of the source’s Conjecture 23, whose intended demand is hardness for arbitrarily small positive \(\eta\) and \(\varepsilon\).
cards.why: Would strengthen almost-coloring hardness enough to improve a central Vertex Cover approximation barrier, linking graph coloring promises with independent-set soundness.

cards.title: Constant-factor approximation of graph crossing number
cards.formal: Do there exist a universal constant \(C\geq1\) and a uniform randomized polynomial-time algorithm that, on every finite undirected graph \(G\), outputs a drawing \(D\) in the plane satisfying \[\operatorname{cr}(D)\leq C\,\operatorname{cr}(G)\] with probability at least \(2/3\)?
cards.why: Crossing minimization is a basic graph-layout optimization problem with applications to drawing networks and circuit layouts. A constant approximation would establish a general algorithmic guarantee across sparse and dense inputs, beyond the degree-dependent and additive-error bounds currently available.

cards.title: A polynomial-time constant approximation for capacitated k-median without violations
cards.formal:
Do there exist an absolute rational constant \(\rho\ge1\), positive integers \(K,a\), and one classical randomized algorithm \(A\) such that every capacitated metric \(k\)-median instance of bit length \(L\) is processed in at most \(K(L+2)^a\) steps on every execution, with the following guarantee? Infeasibility is always reported correctly. On every feasible instance, every execution returns a feasible solution \((S,\phi)\), and
\[
\Pr\!\left[\sum_{c\in C}d(c,\phi(c))\le\rho\,\mathrm{OPT}\right]\ge\frac23.
\]
The solution must use at most \(k\) distinct facilities and respect every facility’s capacity exactly; neither constraint may be exceeded.
cards.why: This is a central facility-location approximation problem in which both resource constraints must be enforced. Resolving it would determine whether constant-factor metric clustering survives exact capacities and an exact bound on the number of open facilities in polynomial time.

cards.title: Square-root logarithmic approximation for metric labeling
cards.formal:
Do there exist absolute constants \(C,K\ge1\), an integer \(d\ge1\), and one uniform classical randomized algorithm such that on every metric-labeling instance of binary length \(L\) with \(k\ge1\) labels, every execution halts within \(K(L+1)^d\) bit steps and outputs a labeling \(f\) satisfying
\[
\Pr\!\left[\operatorname{cost}(f)\le C\sqrt{\log_2(k+2)}\,\operatorname{OPT}\right]\ge\tfrac23?
\]
The input graph, nonnegative rational edge weights and assignment costs, and full rational metric on the labels are arbitrary. The output is always a feasible labeling; \(\operatorname{OPT}\) is the least cost of any labeling.
cards.why: Close a major gap for a general labeling objective linking metric geometry and approximation.

cards.title: Optimal polynomial-time approximation ratio for metric k-means
cards.formal:
Determine, to absolute error at most \(1/100\), the constant
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{MetKM}}=
 \inf\left\{r\in[1,\infty):\begin{array}{l}
 \text{some uniform randomized polynomial-time algorithm }A\text{ always returns}\\
 \text{a feasible solution and satisfies }
 \mathbb E[\operatorname{cost}_I(A(I))]\le r\operatorname{OPT}(I)\\
 \text{for every valid explicitly encoded metric instance }I
 \end{array}\right\}.
\]
The metric, squared cost, candidate-center constraint and worst-case polynomial bit-time model are defined below.
cards.why: Determine the computational approximation limit of squared-distance clustering in general finite metrics. This isolates the cost of clustering without geometric assumptions while requiring an exact center budget on every execution.

cards.title: Configuration-LP gap for maximum generalized assignment
cards.formal:
Determine, with absolute error at most \(1/100\), the constant
\[
g_{\mathrm{GAP}}=\inf_{\substack{I\text{ a finite rational maximum}\text{ generalized-assignment instance}\\\mathrm{LP}(I)>0}}
\frac{\mathrm{OPT}(I)}{\mathrm{LP}(I)},
\]
where \(\mathrm{OPT}\) is the maximum total value of a feasible integral assignment and \(\mathrm{LP}\) is the configuration relaxation defined below. The convention is integral optimum divided by fractional optimum, so \(g_{\mathrm{GAP}}\in[0,1]\). The numbers of items and bins are unbounded.
cards.why: Configuration relaxations encode every feasible packing within each bin while retaining fractional conflicts between bins. Locating their unavoidable loss measures the strength of a central relaxation for allocation and distinguishes its limitations from those of particular rounding algorithms.

cards.title: Hardness of coloring 2-dicolorable digraphs with any fixed number of colors
cards.formal: For every fixed integer \(k\ge 4\), is it NP-hard under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions to distinguish digraphs with dichromatic number at most 2 from digraphs with dichromatic number greater than k?
cards.why: Tests how much approximation helps when searching for a partition into acyclic subgraphs. Constant-color hardness would establish a strong obstruction even when an optimal two-part partition is promised to exist.

cards.title: Subquadratic factor-three edit-distance approximation
cards.formal: Does there exist a classical randomized algorithm and constants \(\eta>0\) and \(C>0\) such that, for every pair of explicitly given strings \(X,Y\) of total length \(n\), the algorithm runs in at most \(C(n+2)^{2-\eta}\) time and, with probability at least \(2/3\), outputs an estimate \(\widehat d\) satisfying \[\operatorname{ED}(X,Y)\leq\widehat d\leq3\operatorname{ED}(X,Y)?\]
cards.why: Tests how much accuracy can be retained while obtaining a fixed polynomial speedup for a basic sequence-comparison problem. It separates the power of approximation from the quadratic barrier for exact computation, with relevance to algorithms for aligning and comparing strings.

cards.title: Matroid secretary conjecture
cards.formal:
Does there exist a finite universal real constant \(C\ge1\) such that, for every finite matroid \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\), there is a randomized online selection strategy \(\mathcal A_M\) satisfying
\[\forall w:E\to\mathbb R_{\ge0},\qquad
\mathbb E_{\pi,U}\!\left[\sum_{e\in S_{\mathcal A_M}(w,\pi,U)}w(e)\right]
\ge\frac1C\max_{I\in\mathcal I}\sum_{e\in I}w(e)?\]
The element weights are fixed adversarially before a uniformly random arrival permutation \(\pi\) and the strategy's independent randomness \(U\) are chosen. Each acceptance decision is irrevocable and must preserve independence. The same \(C\) must work for all matroids and all weights.
cards.why: This is a central question about the power of random arrival order in online selection under general independence constraints. A universal bound would apply across all matroids and is equivalent, through established reductions, to a general random-order contention-resolution guarantee.

cards.title: Optimal competitive ratio for convex body chasing
cards.formal:
Determine, up to universal constant factors as a function of \(d\), the optimal deterministic competitive ratio \(\mathcal C(d)\) for general convex body chasing in Euclidean space \(\mathbb R^d\). The domain is every integer \(d\ge1\).

An online strategy starts at \(x_0=0\), sees a nonempty compact convex set \(K_t\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) at round \(t\), and must immediately choose \(x_t\in K_t\) using only \(K_1,\ldots,K_t\). Its cost on a finite request sequence is \(\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|x_t-x_{t-1}\|_2\). Let
\[\operatorname{OPT}(K_1,\ldots,K_T)=\min_{y_t\in K_t,\ y_0=0}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\|y_t-y_{t-1}\|_2\]
and define
\[\mathcal C(d)=\inf\left\{c\ge1:\ \exists A\ \forall T\ge1\ \forall K_1,\ldots,K_T,\quad\operatorname{cost}_A(K_1,\ldots,K_T)\le c\,\operatorname{OPT}(K_1,\ldots,K_T)\right\}.\]
The strategy may depend on \(d\), but must serve all horizons and request sequences in that dimension. The target is the asymptotic order of this dimension-dependent ratio, resolving the source's gap between order \(\sqrt d\) and order \(d\).
cards.why: Convex body chasing isolates the movement cost of maintaining feasibility when constraints arrive without advance notice. The optimal dependence on dimension measures how much geometric complexity alone can penalize online decisions, independently of computational efficiency. Matching bounds would resolve a central quantitative gap between what convexity permits offline and what an online strategy can guarantee.

cards.title: Optimal approximation ratio for unrelated-machine makespan
cards.formal:
For offline makespan minimization on unrelated parallel machines, determine the real number
\[\rho_{\mathrm{unrel}}=\inf\mathcal R,\qquad \mathcal R=\Bigl\{r\in[1,\infty):\exists A\ \exists c,k\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\ \forall I\in\mathcal I,\ \begin{array}{l} A(I)\text{ halts in at most }c(L(I)+2)^k\text{ bit steps,}\\ A(I)\text{ outputs a feasible schedule }\sigma_I,\\ C_{\max}(\sigma_I)\le r\operatorname{OPT}(I)\end{array}\Bigr\}.\]
Here \(\mathcal I\) is the full class of finite rational processing-time matrices defined below, \(L(I)\) is the full binary input length, and \(A\) ranges over finite deterministic Turing-machine programs. Approximate \(\rho_{\mathrm{unrel}}\) within absolute error \(1/100\), with a complete Lean proof. No complexity hypothesis is included in the definition of this number.
cards.why: This is a central approximation question for allocating heterogeneous work to heterogeneous machines. The long gap between achievable guarantees and conditional hardness also has formal consequences for max-min fair allocation, making its resolution informative beyond scheduling.

cards.title: Randomized competitiveness of k-server
cards.formal:
Determine the growth, up to universal multiplicative constants, of the optimal randomized competitive ratio for \(k\)-server on all finite metrics against an oblivious adversary. For each integer \(k\ge2\), define
\[R_{\mathrm{rand}}(k)=\inf\mathcal R_k,\]
where \(\mathcal R_k\) is the set of real \(r\ge1\) such that
\[\forall (X,d)\in\mathcal M_k\;\forall C_0\in X^k\;\exists\mathcal A\;\exists\beta\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}\;\forall\sigma\in X^{<\omega},\qquad
\mathbb E_U[\operatorname{cost}_{\mathcal A}(\sigma;C_0,U)]
\le r\operatorname{OPT}(\sigma;C_0)+\beta.\]
Here \(\mathcal M_k\) consists of all finite metric spaces with at least \(k+1\) points, and \(\mathcal A\) is an online randomized strategy as defined below. Give an unambiguous positive function \(h\) on the integers \(k\ge2\) and fixed real constants \(0<a\le b<\infty\) such that
\[a h(k)\le R_{\mathrm{rand}}(k)\le b h(k)\qquad\text{for all integers }k\ge2.\]
The requested precision is matching asymptotic bounds, including any logarithmic dependence.
cards.why: A surviving central problem in randomized competitive analysis, beyond the refuted logarithmic k-server conjecture.

cards.title: Minimax dimension dependence in bandit convex optimization
cards.formal: Determine, up to universal constant factors jointly in dimension d and horizon T, the information-theoretic minimax expected regret \(R*(d,T)\) for one-point adversarial bandit convex optimization with losses in \([0,1]\). Use the oblivious-adversary, exact-feedback model and worst-case normalized convex body defined below; logarithmic dependence is part of the requested rate.
cards.why: Determines the price of limited feedback in a basic model of online convex optimization.

cards.title: Constant additive error for one-dimensional bin packing
cards.formal:
Do there exist an integer \(C\ge0\), a uniform randomized algorithm \(A\), and absolute integers \(K,d\ge1\) such that every explicitly listed one-dimensional bin-packing instance \(I\), of binary input length \(L\), satisfies all three conditions below?

Every execution of \(A(I)\) takes at most \(K(L+1)^d\) bit operations and outputs a feasible packing into bins of capacity one; and, writing \(B_A(I)\) for its number of nonempty bins,
\[
\Pr[B_A(I)\le\operatorname{OPT}(I)+C]\ge\frac23.
\]
The constants do not depend on the number of items, their sizes or precision, the number of distinct sizes, or the optimum. The entire input is available before any packing decisions are made.
cards.why: The question asks whether the absolute loss in a basic packing problem can be bounded independently of instance scale. Such a result would go beyond a ratio tending to one by controlling the number of extra bins itself, and would sharpen a longstanding boundary in approximation algorithms.

cards.title: Optimal approximation ratio for precedence-constrained makespan
cards.formal:
Determine the infimum approximation ratio achievable in deterministic polynomial time for nonpreemptive precedence-constrained makespan minimization on an input number of identical machines:
\[\rho_{\mathrm{prec}}=\inf\mathcal R,\]
where \(\mathcal R\) consists of all real \(r\ge1\) for which there exist one uniform deterministic algorithm \(A\) and constants \(K>0\), \(d\in\mathbb N\) such that for every valid instance \(I\) of bit length \(L\), the algorithm outputs a feasible schedule \(S_A(I)\) in at most \(K(L+1)^d\) steps and
\[C_{\max}(S_A(I))\le r\,\operatorname{OPT}(I).\]
The algorithm receives the entire instance before producing its schedule. The numerical answer must determine \(\rho_{\mathrm{prec}}\) to absolute error at most \(1/100\), with the proof requirement stated below. The infimum need not be attained by a single algorithm.
cards.why: Precedence constraints make scheduling depend on both how much work can run in parallel and which completions unlock later jobs. The optimal approximation ratio measures the algorithmic cost of coordinating these two effects. Pinning it down would settle a central scheduling approximation boundary whose basic factor-two guarantee dates to the 1960s.

cards.title: Additive-one approximation for bin packing
cards.formal:
Is there a polynomial-time approximation algorithm for one-dimensional offline bin packing that uses at most one more bin than optimum? Explicitly allowing randomization, the target is one uniform probabilistic algorithm \(A\) and a polynomial \(p\) such that, for every finite input list \(I=(s_{1},\ldots,s_{n})\) of rational sizes \(0<s_{i}\le1\), \(A\) runs within \(p(L)\) steps for every coin sequence, always outputs a feasible packing, and satisfies
\[
\Pr\bigl[B(A(I))\le\operatorname{OPT}(I)+1\bigr]\ge\tfrac23.
\]
Here \(L\) is the total binary input length, \(B\) is the number of bins used, and probability is over the algorithm’s independent fair random bits for each fixed input. A deterministic algorithm with the same bound on every input also qualifies.
cards.why: A one-extra-bin algorithm would show that a strongly NP-hard packing problem can nevertheless be solved to a uniformly tiny additive error. The question tests a much sharper notion of approximation than a ratio tending to one and is a long-standing benchmark for understanding the structure of feasible packings.

cards.title: Constant-factor online contention resolution for matroids
cards.formal:
Is there a finite universal real constant \(C\ge1\) such that the following holds? For every finite matroid \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\), every real \(\alpha\ge1\), and every probability distribution \(D\) on \(2^E\) that admits an offline \(\alpha\)-competitive contention-resolution map, there exists a randomized online random-order strategy \(\mathcal A\) which always returns an independent subset \(S\subseteq R\) and satisfies
\[\forall e\in E,\qquad \Pr[e\in S]\ge\frac{\Pr_{R\sim D}[e\in R]}{C\alpha}.\]
Here \(R\sim D\) is the active set, the elements of \(E\) arrive in an independent uniformly random order, and the strategy learns whether an element is active only when it arrives. The strategy knows \(M,D,\alpha\) in advance; \(C\) is independent of all of them. The target is unconditional existence, without assuming the matroid secretary conjecture.
cards.why: This question isolates the additional cost of making feasible selections online when the active set can have arbitrary correlations. Comparing with the best available offline balance avoids charging the online algorithm for distributional obstructions that already exist offline. Its constant-factor form is equivalent to the matroid secretary conjecture.

cards.title: Minimax rate of sequential binary calibration
cards.formal:
Determine the minimax expected ordinary calibration error
\[
C(T)=\inf_{P,A}\ \sup_B\ \mathbb E\!\left[\sum_{p\in P}\left|\sum_{\substack{1\le t\le T\\p_t=p}}(y_t-p)\right|\right]
\]
up to absolute multiplicative constants as the integer horizon \(T\) tends to infinity. The finite prediction set \(P\subseteq[0,1]\), forecaster \(A\) and adaptive adversary \(B\) use the simultaneous-move game below. The requested rate includes every logarithmic factor.
cards.why: A fundamental quantitative problem in sequential prediction, with consequences for calibrated learning and decision making.

cards.title: Optimal competitive ratio of online bin packing
cards.formal: Determine the infimum asymptotic competitive ratio R_BP of deterministic online bin packing.
cards.why: The constant measures the irreducible loss caused by committing to packing decisions without future items.

cards.title: Polynomial-time constant approximation for the General Scheduling Problem
cards.formal: For the explicitly encoded General Scheduling Problem below, is there a deterministic polynomial-time approximation with a universal constant factor?
cards.why: A constant approximation would unify many completion-time objectives under one general scheduling model.

cards.title: Polynomial-time unit-job precedence scheduling on fixed machines
cards.formal:
For every fixed integer \(k\ge3\), can the minimum makespan of unit-duration jobs with arbitrary precedence constraints be computed in deterministic polynomial time on \(k\) identical machines?

For a finite directed acyclic graph \(G\), let \(\mu_k(G)\) be the least number of time slots needed to execute all its vertices as jobs, using at most \(k\) jobs per slot and executing every job strictly after its predecessors. The precise target is
\[
\forall k\ge3\ \exists A_k,C_k,c_k\ \forall G,
\]
where \(A_k\) is one uniform deterministic algorithm, \(C_k,c_k\ge1\) are integers, and on every valid \(L\)-bit encoding of \(G\), \(A_k\) halts in at most \(C_k(L+1)^{c_k}\) steps and outputs a rational number \(a\) satisfying
\[
|a-\mu_k(G)|\le\frac1{100}.
\]
The numerical output convention is equivalent here to computing the optimum integer exactly, by rounding in polynomial bit time.
cards.why: With unit-duration jobs and identical machines, the only remaining source of scheduling difficulty is the interaction between a partial order and limited parallel capacity. Polynomial solvability for each fixed machine count would identify a major tractable boundary in precedence scheduling. The three-machine case has resisted classification since the classical scheduling complexity literature, despite the recent subexponential advance.

cards.title: Constant-factor related-machine precedence scheduling
cards.formal: Does nonpreemptive precedence-constrained makespan minimization on uniformly related parallel machines admit a deterministic polynomial-time approximation with a universal constant factor? Precisely, do there exist one algorithm \(A\), constants \(K\ge1,C>0\), and an integer \(b\ge1\), such that for every instance of binary encoding length \(L\) specified below, \(A\) returns a feasible schedule of makespan at most \(K\,\mathrm{OPT}\) in at most \(C(L+1)^b\) Turing-machine steps? All constants are independent of the numbers of jobs and machines, processing requirements, machine speeds and precedence graph.
cards.why: Identical machines already allow nontrivial parallelism constrained by a dependency graph, and different speeds add a global allocation choice. A universal constant approximation would show that this extra heterogeneity can be handled with bounded worst-case loss. A negative resolution would identify a basic source of approximation difficulty even though every job can run on every machine and execution times have the simple requirement-divided-by-speed form.

cards.title: Optimal prophet-secretary constant
cards.formal: Determine the optimal prophet-secretary constant α_PS for independent nonnegative integrable values arriving in uniformly random order with identities revealed.
cards.why: The prophet-secretary constant quantifies the value of distribution knowledge under random arrival.

cards.title: One forecaster with the optimal regret rate for every proper loss
cards.formal: For each fixed number \(K\ge 2\) of outcomes, does there exist one randomized online forecaster A, not given the loss function, such that for every bounded proper loss \(\ell\) its worst-case expected regret satisfies \(R_{A},\ell (T)\le C_{\ell},K\cdot (1+R*_{\ell},K(T))\cdot (\log (T+2))^{c_{\ell},K}\) for all \(T\ge 1\), for some constants \(C_{\ell},K>0\) and \(c_{\ell},K\ge 0\) independent of T? Here \(R*_{\ell},K\) is the minimax regret achievable by a forecaster tailored to that particular loss. This spells out the source’s “optimal up to constant or logarithmic factors in T” target; the additive one covers losses with zero or bounded optimal regret.
cards.why: Would establish whether a general-purpose probability forecaster can match every downstream user’s best possible learning rate without knowing that user’s loss. It refines universal sublinear regret into adaptation to the intrinsic difficulty of each scoring rule.

cards.title: Sublinear-in-q prophet inequalities for q-matroid intersection
cards.formal: Is there a function \(g:\mathbb N_{\ge1}\to[1,\infty)\) with \(\lim_{q\to\infty}g(q)/q=0\) such that, for every sequence of independent nonnegative random values and every feasibility constraint given by the intersection of \(q\) matroids, some online irrevocable selection strategy obtains expected reward at least \(1/g(q)\) times the expected offline optimum? The arrival order is fixed in advance, all value distributions and constraints are known to the strategy, and the guarantee is independent of the number of elements.
cards.why: A prophet knows all random values before choosing a feasible set, while an online selector must commit before later values arrive. Matroid intersections capture many simultaneous resource constraints. Determining whether the approximation loss can grow sublinearly in their number would distinguish a limitation imposed by lack of future information from the performance of existing selection guarantees.

cards.title: Randomized competitive ratio of list update
cards.formal: Determine the optimal randomized competitive ratio of online list update against an oblivious adversary in the full-cost model: \[\rho_{\mathrm{LU}}=\inf\{r\in[1,\infty):r\text{ is achievable under the definition below}\}.\] Give its value to absolute error at most \(1/100\). The same competitive factor must work for lists of every finite size, with an additive constant allowed to depend on the size and initial order. No predictions or advice about future requests are supplied.
cards.why: List update is a basic model of a data structure adapting to changing demand without knowing future accesses. Its optimal randomized ratio would quantify the value of randomization in a simple online problem whose deterministic analogue is well understood. The unresolved constant gap makes it a precise long-standing benchmark in competitive analysis.

cards.title: Optimal stretch for online bin stretching
cards.formal: Determine R_stretch=limsup_{m→∞} r_m for deterministic online bin stretching, where r_m is the best stretch for exactly m bins.
cards.why: This measures how much extra capacity is needed when the number of bins is fixed but item order is online.

cards.title: Sublogarithmic competitiveness for online metric TSP
cards.formal: Does there exist one deterministic online insertion algorithm \(A\), in the unrestricted-space model below, and a function \(\rho:\{2,3,\ldots\}\to[1,\infty)\) such that \(\lim_{n\to\infty}\rho(n)/\log_2 n=0\) and \(\operatorname{cost}_A(D)\le\rho(n)\operatorname{OPT}(D)\) for every \(n\ge2\) and every valid sequence of \(n\) metric arrivals? The algorithm knows \(n\), but receives distances only as points arrive and does not know the final offline optimum. Earlier relative-order decisions are irrevocable.
cards.why: An online tour can insert new points between old ones while keeping the old relative order. The question asks how costly that one irreversible choice is when future distances are unknown. Its resolution would identify whether the logarithmic guarantee reflects an inherent online limitation or a limitation of known ordering rules.

cards.title: Pinwheel Packing in NP
cards.formal:
Does ordinary Pinwheel Packing belong to \(\mathrm{NP}\)?

An instance is an explicit finite list of positive integers \(a_1,\ldots,a_k\), written in binary, with \(k\ge1\). It is feasible if there exists a schedule \(\sigma:\mathbb Z\to\{0,1,\ldots,k\}\) such that
\[
\forall i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\ \forall t\in\mathbb Z\
\exists j\in\{0,\ldots,a_i-1\},\qquad \sigma(t+j)=i.
\]
Thus one machine must execute task \(i\) at least once in every \(a_i\) consecutive time slots, forever.

Precisely, do there exist one uniform deterministic verifier \(V\) and integers \(C,c\ge1\) such that every valid encoded instance \(x\), of bit length \(L\), satisfies
\[
x\text{ is feasible}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists z\in\{0,1\}^{\ast}\ 
\bigl(|z|\le C(L+1)^c\ \text{and}\ V(x,z)=1\bigr),
\]
and \(V\) halts on every pair \((x,z)\) within \(C(|x|+|z|+1)^c\) steps?
cards.why: A compact list of recurring service requirements describes an infinite scheduling obligation. NP membership would show that feasibility always has a short, efficiently checkable finite explanation, even when a directly listed repeating schedule may be very long. Together with the 2026 hardness result, a positive answer would classify this long-studied perpetual scheduling problem as NP-complete.

cards.title: Adaptive regret in misspecified linear bandits
cards.formal: Do there exist universal constants \(C>0\) and an integer \(p\ge0\) such that, for every \(d,k,T\in\mathbb N\) with \(d,T\ge1\) and \(k\ge d^2\), and every known feature matrix \(\Phi\in\mathbb R^{k\times d}\), there is one bandit policy \(\pi\) satisfying, simultaneously for every unknown mean-reward vector \(\mu\in\mathbb R^k\) with \(\max_i\mu_i-\min_i\mu_i\le1\), \[R_T(\pi,\mu)\le C[\log(2kdT)]^p\min\left\{T,\ d\sqrt T+\varepsilon(\Phi,\mu)T\sqrt d,\ \frac{k}{d}\sqrt T\right\}?\] Here \(\varepsilon(\Phi,\mu)=\inf_{\theta\in\mathbb R^d}\|\Phi\theta-\mu\|_\infty\). The policy may depend on \(\Phi,d,k,T\), but cannot be given \(\mu\), a fitting parameter \(\theta\), the misspecification level \(\varepsilon\), or an upper bound on that level. Use the Gaussian-noise model below.
cards.why: Features let a learner transfer information between arms, but approximation errors can make that transfer misleading. A policy that adapts to unknown error while preserving a controlled fallback would identify how much statistical benefit an imperfect model can safely provide. The requirement that one policy meet the bound at every error level is central: independently choosing a policy after learning the true error would answer a different question.

cards.title: Three-competitive deterministic file migration
cards.formal: For every finite metric space and every integer D≥1, is deterministic online file migration 3-competitive with an input-independent additive constant?
cards.why: The target asks whether a canonical state-location problem reaches its known lower-bound ratio.

cards.title: Exact optimal stopping for mixtures of product distributions
cards.formal:
Do there exist two uniform deterministic algorithms \(P,E\) and positive integers \(C,a\) with the following property? For every rational mixture-of-scenarios instance \(I\) of binary length \(L\) defined below, \(P(I)\) constructs a binary policy description \(z_I\) in at most \(C(L+2)^a\) bit steps, and \(E(I,z_I,h)\) decides whether to stop at each observed history \(h\) within the same time bound. The resulting stopping time \(\tau\) must satisfy
\[
\mathbb E_I[X_\tau]=\max_{\sigma\text{ an online stopping rule}}\mathbb E_I[X_\sigma].
\]
The equality is exact. All constants, programs and polynomial exponents are independent of the number of scenarios, sequence length, support size and numerical precision.
cards.why: A small latent scenario model can describe exponentially many observation histories. The question asks whether this compact source of dependence still permits exact efficient decisions, separating concise distribution descriptions from concise optimal policies.

cards.title: Optimal bandit regret for paths in a directed grid
cards.formal:
Determine the minimax expected regret \(R(n,T)\) for paths from \((1,1)\) to \((n,n)\) in the directed square grid, with only total path loss observed, up to universal multiplicative constants, jointly for all integers \(n\ge2\) and \(T\ge1\). Specifically, supply an explicit asymptotic rate \(F(n,T)>0\) and constants \(0<c\le C<\infty\), independent of both parameters, such that
\[
cF(n,T)\le R(n,T)\le CF(n,T)
\]
throughout this domain. Edge losses lie in \([0,1]\), are fixed in advance, and the comparator is the best single path in hindsight. The precise minimax quantity is defined below.
cards.why: Paths overlap heavily in a grid, so treating them as unrelated arms discards useful information while observing only a total loss hides the responsible edges. This elementary network isolates how action geometry affects the limits of online exploration.

cards.title: Optimal deterministic price of obligatory testing
cards.formal: Determine R_det=inf_A sup_I cost_A(I)/OPT(I) for deterministic obligatory-test scheduling with arbitrary positive test durations.
cards.why: The problem quantifies the cost of acquiring information before scheduling work.

cards.title: Power of randomization in scheduling with obligatory tests
cards.formal: Determine R_rand=inf_A sup_I E[cost_A(I)]/OPT(I) for obligatory-test scheduling with t_j=1 and an oblivious adversary.
cards.why: This isolates the value of randomization in scheduling with compulsory information acquisition.

cards.title: Deterministic competitiveness of k-server
cards.formal:
For every integer \(k\ge1\), determine the universal deterministic competitive-ratio infimum
\[R_{\mathrm{det}}(k)=\inf\mathcal R_k,\]
where
\[\mathcal R_k=\Bigl\{r\in[1,\infty):\ \forall(M,d)\in\mathcal M_k\ \forall C_0\in M^k\ \exists A\ \exists\beta\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}\ \forall\sigma\in M^{<\omega},\quad
\operatorname{cost}_{A}(\sigma;C_0)\le r\operatorname{OPT}(\sigma;C_0)+\beta\Bigr\}.\]
Here \(\mathcal M_k\) consists of all finite or infinite metric spaces having at least \(k+1\) points, \(A\) is a deterministic online rule in the serving model below, and \(M^{<\omega}\) is the set of all finite request sequences, including the empty sequence. Give a real-valued function \(g\) and a complete Lean proof that
\[\forall k\in\mathbb N_{\ge1},\qquad |g(k)-R_{\mathrm{det}}(k)|\le\frac1{100}.\]
The tolerance is absolute in the competitive ratio and is the same for every \(k\).
cards.why: The k-server problem measures the movement cost of responding to demand without knowing future requests. It includes paging and serves as a basic problem in competitive analysis, with the same number of resources available to the online rule and the offline optimum.

cards.title: Optimal randomized competitive ratio of weighted k-server
cards.formal: Determine the asymptotic growth of \(R_{w}(k)\), the optimal randomized competitive ratio of the weighted k-server problem over all finite uniform metrics, up to universal multiplicative constants as the integer k tends to infinity. Use an oblivious request adversary and expected online cost, as defined below.
cards.why: The optimal randomized cost of heterogeneous servers is a central online resource-allocation question; the recent singly-exponential breakthrough leaves a substantial quantitative frontier.

cards.title: Average-case NP hardness from \(\mathrm{P} \ne  \mathrm{NP}\)
cards.formal:
Is the following implication true in the ordinary uniform Turing-machine model?
\[\mathrm P\ne\mathrm{NP}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\exists L\in\mathrm{NP}\ \exists S\in\mathrm{PSamp}\ :\ (L,D^S)\notin\mathrm{AvgP}.
\]
Here \(S\) is one exact polynomial-time sampler, \(D^S=(D^S_n)_{n\ge1}\) its output distribution ensemble, and \(\mathrm{AvgP}\) means deterministic, always-correct computation with the positive-moment runtime bound below. Thus the conclusion requires one fixed language and one fixed feasible sampling procedure for which no exact deterministic decider has average polynomial running time. No additional hardness or derandomization hypothesis may be assumed.
cards.why: Worst-case hardness alone does not explain whether feasible procedures can generate instances that remain difficult on average. Resolving this implication would connect the central decision-class separation to robust limits on exact computation under efficiently generated inputs.

cards.title: Planted clique conjecture
cards.formal: Is the following hardness statement true? For every fixed real \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)\), with \(k_n=\lfloor n^{1/2-\varepsilon}\rfloor\), there is no uniform classical randomized polynomial-time algorithm \(A\) for which \[\Pr[\widehat b=b]\geq\frac23\] in the balanced one-graph experiment below for every sufficiently large integer \(n\).
cards.why: A foundational average-case hardness hypothesis, planted clique isolates a gap between statistical information and efficient computation. The hidden clique is far larger than cliques arising by chance, yet no unrestricted polynomial-time detector is established in this regime. Related assumptions support hardness results for estimation, clustering and other inference tasks. Proving this formulation would imply Boolean \(\mathrm P\ne\mathrm{NP}\): a polynomial-time general clique decider would distinguish these distributions once \(k_n\) exceeds the typical null clique size.

cards.title: Exact random-order ratio of Best Fit bin packing
cards.formal: Determine the asymptotic random-order ratio \[R_{\mathrm{BF}}=\lim_{M\to\infty}\sup_{I:\operatorname{OPT}(I)\ge M}\frac{\mathbb E_{\pi}[\mathrm{BF}(I^\pi)]}{\operatorname{OPT}(I)}\] of the Best Fit bin-packing algorithm. Benchmark acceptance requires absolute error at most \(1/100\) in this dimensionless constant; exact determination also qualifies.
cards.why: The target measures how much a random arrival order improves a classical greedy packing rule.

cards.title: Computational threshold for tensor PCA
cards.formal: Is the following computational impossibility statement true? For every fixed integer \(k\ge3\), rational \(0<\varepsilon<(k-2)/4\), and rational \(0<c<1\), no uniform randomized polynomial-time classical algorithm can, for all sufficiently large \(n\), recover a vector with absolute correlation at least \(c\) with a uniformly random hidden unit direction from the single rounded tensor observation \[Y=\lambda_n v^{\otimes k}+Z,\qquad \lambda_n=n^{k/4-\varepsilon},\qquad v\sim\operatorname{Unif}(S^{n-1}),\] where all \(n^k\) ordered entries of \(Z\) are independent \(N(0,1)\) variables. Recovery must succeed with probability at least \(2/3\), averaged over the hidden direction, noise and algorithm coins. Rounding, output normalization and the uniform bit-cost model are defined below. The fixed power saving \(n^\varepsilon\) and the spherical prior are parts of the existing target, not replaced by a threshold for one algorithm family.
cards.why: Determine whether the canonical statistical–computational gap for a dense Gaussian tensor persists against all polynomial-time recovery algorithms.

cards.title: Computational Kesten–Stigum threshold
cards.formal:
Do there exist a fixed integer \(q\ge5\), fixed rational numbers \(a>b>0\), a fixed real \(\delta>0\), and one uniform randomized polynomial-time algorithm \(A\) such that
\[(a-b)^2<q\bigl(a+(q-1)b\bigr)\]
and, for every sufficiently large integer \(n\), the symmetric stochastic block model defined below satisfies
\[\mathbb E\bigl[\operatorname{ov}(A(G),\sigma)\bigr]\ge\frac1q+\delta?\]
All model parameters and the algorithm are chosen once, independently of \(n\). The expectation is over the planted labels, the graph and the algorithm's random bits.
cards.why: Determine whether the canonical local signal threshold is a true barrier for every efficient algorithm in a basic model of network inference.

cards.title: Polynomial-time refutation of random 3-SAT at constant density
cards.formal:
Do there exist an integer \(C\geq6\) and a uniform randomized polynomial-time algorithm \(A\) such that \(A\) never outputs \(\mathrm{UNSAT}\) on any satisfiable \(3\)-CNF formula, and
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\Pr_{F\sim R_3(n,Cn),\,\rho}
 [A(F;\rho)=\mathrm{UNSAT}]=1?
\]
The distribution \(R_3\), exact soundness, and worst-case time bound are defined below. The constant \(C\), machine and its time polynomial must be fixed before \(n\); the probability includes the algorithm’s independent random bits \(\rho\).
cards.why: This problem isolates the gap between knowing that a typical sparse formula is unsatisfiable and efficiently proving unsatisfiability without ever making a false claim. A resolution would identify a major limit of average-case certification or produce an algorithm beyond the methods underlying existing refutation barriers.

cards.title: Algorithmic threshold for random k-SAT
cards.formal: Does the randomized polynomial-time satisfying-assignment threshold for random \(k\)-SAT satisfy \[\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\alpha_{\mathrm{alg}}(k)}{2^{k}\ln(k)/k}=1?\] For each fixed \(k\), \(\alpha_{\mathrm{alg}}(k)\) is the supremum of constant clause densities at which some polynomial-time algorithm finds a satisfying assignment with probability tending to one as the number \(n\) of variables tends to infinity. The distribution and quantifiers are specified below.
cards.why: Pinpoints a possible computational barrier inside a regime where satisfying assignments typically exist. A resolution would clarify whether the geometry of random constraint problems predicts the power of arbitrary efficient algorithms, beyond individual heuristics and restricted computational models.

cards.title: Infinitely-often one-way functions from average-case NP hardness
cards.formal:
Does
\[
 \mathrm{DistNP}\not\subseteq\mathrm{HeurBPP}
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \text{an infinitely-often one-way function exists}
\]
hold under the uniform classical definitions below? In this card \(\mathrm{DistNP}\) uses exactly polynomial-time samplable input distributions, and infinitely-often security means that for every polynomial-time inverter and every inverse-polynomial success threshold there are arbitrarily large lengths at which the inverter's success falls below that threshold.
cards.why: It asks whether distributional hardness alone suffices for basic cryptography: a central connection between average-case complexity and cryptographic constructions.

cards.title: Exponential worst-case hardness implies mild average-case hardness in NP
cards.formal:
Is the implication \(H_{\mathrm{worst}}\Rightarrow H_{\mathrm{mild}}\) true, where
\[
H_{\mathrm{worst}}:\quad\exists L\in\mathrm{NP}\ \exists\alpha\in\mathbb Q\cap(0,1)\ \exists N\ge1\ \forall n\ge N\ \forall C\in\mathcal C(n,\lfloor2^{\alpha n}\rfloor)\ \exists x\in\{0,1\}^n:\ C(x)\ne1_L(x),
\]
and
\[
H_{\mathrm{mild}}:\quad\exists M\in\mathrm{NP}\ \exists\beta\in\mathbb Q\cap(0,1)\ \exists a,N'\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\ \forall n\ge N'\ \forall C\in\mathcal C(n,\lfloor2^{\beta n}\rfloor):\quad
\Pr_{x\sim U_n}[C(x)\ne1_M(x)]\ge n^{-a}?
\]
Here \(\mathcal C(n,s)\) is the class of deterministic Boolean circuits with \(n\) input bits and at most \(s\) gates, and \(U_n\) is the uniform distribution on those bits. No additional cryptographic, average-case or nondeterministic hardness assumption is permitted.
cards.why: A hard exceptional input does not explain why a uniformly sampled instance should be hard. The question asks whether exponential worst-case difficulty within NP necessarily supplies a language with a substantial density of hard inputs at the same exponential scale.

cards.title: Algorithmic threshold for the symmetric binary perceptron
cards.formal:
Does the Gaussian symmetric binary perceptron's polynomial-time search threshold satisfy
\[\alpha_{\mathrm{alg}}(\kappa)=\widetilde\Theta(\kappa^2)\qquad\text{as }\kappa\downarrow0?\]
Precisely, are there constants \(C\ge1\), an integer \(a\ge0\), and \(\kappa_0\in(0,1/2]\) such that for every rational \(\kappa\in(0,\kappa_0]\),
\[\frac{\kappa^2}{C(\log(1/\kappa))^a}\ \le\ \alpha_{\mathrm{alg}}(\kappa)\ \le\ C\kappa^2(\log(1/\kappa))^a?\]
For fixed margin \(\kappa>0\) and density \(\alpha>0\), an instance is an \(\lfloor\alpha n\rfloor\)-by-\(n\) matrix \(G\) with independent standard Gaussian entries. A successful search returns \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^n\) with
\[\max_{1\le i\le\lfloor\alpha n\rfloor}\left|\sum_{j=1}^{n}G_{ij}\sigma_j\right|\le\kappa\sqrt n.\]
The threshold is the supremum of fixed rational densities at which a uniform polynomial-time algorithm succeeds with probability tending to one as \(n\to\infty\), in the real-arithmetic model specified below.

The polylogarithmic tolerance restores the tilde lost in the imported excerpt. To make the source's informal efficient-algorithm class definite on exact Gaussian inputs, this card explicitly selects rational-constant randomized real-arithmetic computation. It does not assert equivalence with every discretized or machine-specific version of the conjecture.
cards.why: The symmetric binary perceptron is a basic random constraint model in which many solutions can exist while known algorithms reach much smaller densities. Locating the small-margin search scale tests whether the observed computational obstruction captures all efficient algorithms or only particular algorithm families. Its links to discrepancy, random solution geometry and worst-case lattice hardness make the threshold a substantial average-case complexity question.

cards.title: Optimization and certification of Max-Cut in random cubic graphs
cards.formal:
Determine the two-valued function \(F:\{\mathrm{optimization},\mathrm{certification}\}\to\mathbb R\) for Max-Cut on a uniformly random simple labeled \(3\)-regular graph:
\[
F(\mathrm{optimization})=a_*\qquad\text{and}\qquad F(\mathrm{certification})=b_*.
\]
Here \(a_*\) is the supremum of asymptotic cut sizes achievable with high probability by uniform randomized polynomial-time algorithms, and \(b_*\) is the infimum of asymptotic upper bounds obtainable with high probability by uniform randomized polynomial-time producers of always sound, polynomial-time-verifiable certificates. Both values count crossing edges per vertex. The definitions below fix the quantifiers without assuming that either computational optimum is attained.

This is the user-approved specialization, recorded on 16 September 2026, of the source’s broader program for unspecified sparse random CSP models. The general model parameter is deliberately replaced by this single distribution and this pair of optimal computational thresholds.
