cards.why: Random cubic Max-Cut is a concrete sparse optimization model in which excellent solutions and convincing upper certificates may have different computational limits. Determining both thresholds would measure that gap in a fixed distribution, test the limits of spectral and local methods, and clarify which information about a typical optimum can be made into an efficient proof for an individual instance.

cards.title: Polynomial smoothed complexity of FLIP for Max-Cut
cards.formal: Are there absolute constants \(C,a,b>0\) such that, for every \(n\ge 1\), every simple undirected graph G on n vertices, every \(\varphi \ge 1/2\) and every collection of independent edge-weight distributions supported on \([- 1,1]\) with probability densities bounded by \(\varphi\), the expected length of the longest strictly improving single-vertex-flip path is at most \(C(n+1)^{a}(1+\varphi )^{b}\)?
cards.why: A flagship unresolved explanation of why a canonical PLS local-search algorithm works efficiently on perturbed inputs.

cards.title: Optimal exponential hardness amplification for balanced NP languages
cards.formal:
Is \(H_{\mathrm{balanced}}\Rightarrow H_{\mathrm{strong}}\), where
\[
H_{\mathrm{balanced}}:\quad\exists L\in\mathrm{NP}\ \exists\alpha\in\mathbb Q\cap(0,1)\ \exists a,N\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}:\quad
\bigl(\forall n\ge1:\Pr_{x\sim U_n}[x\in L]=1/2\bigr)
\ \land\ 
\bigl(\forall n\ge N\ \forall C\in\mathcal C(n,\lfloor2^{\alpha n}\rfloor):\Pr_{x\sim U_n}[C(x)\ne1_L(x)]\ge n^{-a}\bigr),
\]
and
\[
H_{\mathrm{strong}}:\quad\exists M\in\mathrm{NP}\ \exists\beta\in\mathbb Q\cap(0,1)\ \exists N'\ge1\ \forall n\ge N'\ \forall C\in\mathcal C(n,\lfloor2^{\beta n}\rfloor):\quad
\Pr_{x\sim U_n}[C(x)\ne1_M(x)]\ge\frac12-2^{-\beta n}?
\]
The distribution \(U_n\) is uniform on all \(n\)-bit strings, and \(\mathcal C(n,s)\) consists of deterministic Boolean circuits of size at most \(s\). No additional hypothesis is allowed.
cards.why: Combining independent hard bits by parity amplifies prediction hardness, but NP is not known to preserve membership under such a combination. The question asks whether amplification that stays inside NP can nevertheless attain a truly exponential advantage bound without weakening the exponential circuit-size scale.

cards.title: Polynomial simplex complexity under zero-preserving perturbations
cards.formal:
Does there exist one randomized two-phase simplex algorithm \(\mathcal A\), in the exact model below, and fixed integers \(C,k\ge1\), such that for every \(m,d\ge1\), every real matrix \(\bar A\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}\), vectors \(\bar b\in\mathbb R^m,c\in\mathbb R^d\) with
\[
\max_{i\in[m]}\| (\bar A_{i,*},\bar b_i)\|_2\le1,
\qquad\|c\|_2\le1,
\]
and every \(0<\sigma\le1\),
\[
\mathbb E_{G,R}\,[T_{\mathcal A}(A,b,c,\sigma)]
\le C(m+d+\sigma^{-1}+1)^k?
\]
For each nonzero entry of \((\bar A,\bar b)\), independently add \(\sigma\) times a standard normal random variable; entries initially equal to zero remain exactly zero. The resulting data are \((A,b)\), and \(c\) is unchanged. The task is to solve \(\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b,\ x\in\mathbb R^d\}\) exactly, including infeasibility and unboundedness. The same program and constants must work for all dimensions, centers, zero patterns and noise scales. Expectation includes both the perturbations \(G\) and independent algorithmic fair coins \(R\). This is an explicitly disclosed specialization of the source's general direction to the fixed artificial-variable initialization and fair-bit program class below. It is not a claim about every pivot rule, and the specified class is not asserted to include all published shadow-vertex implementations.
cards.why: Zero coefficients encode much of the structure that makes large linear programs usable. A guarantee stable under preserving those zeros would test whether random-data explanations of simplex efficiency extend beyond dense perturbations. The question concerns the existence of an exact simplex implementation with a universal expected resource bound, and therefore separates a limitation of one pivot rule from a limitation of the whole specified algorithm class.

cards.title: Asymptotically optimal algorithms for random three-dimensional assignment
cards.formal: Is there a uniform polynomial-time algorithm \(A\) and a deterministic sequence \(\eta_n\ge0\) with \(\eta_n\to0\) such that, for an \(n\times n\times n\) array of independent mean-one exponential costs, \(A\) returns permutations \(\pi,\sigma\in S_n\) satisfying \[\Pr\!\left[\sum_{i=1}^n C_{i,\pi(i),\sigma(i)}\le(1+\eta_n)\operatorname{OPT}(C)\right]\longrightarrow1?\] The dimension is exactly three and the assignment is axial, as defined below.
cards.why: Random multidimensional assignment is a canonical test of how distributional structure changes optimization complexity.

cards.title: Polynomial-time exact optimization of random asymmetric TSP
cards.formal: Does there exist a uniform algorithm \(A\) and absolute constants \(C,c>0\) such that, for the complete directed graph on \([n]\), with mutually independent costs \(w_{ij}\sim\operatorname{Uniform}[0,1]\) for \(i\ne j\), the probability that \(A\) returns an exactly minimum-cost directed Hamiltonian cycle within \(Cn^c\) arithmetic operations tends to one as \(n\to\infty\)? The algorithm must be correct whenever it terminates and terminate almost surely on this input distribution.
cards.why: This asks whether random instances remove the worst-case obstacle to exact asymmetric traveling-salesman optimization.

cards.title: Average-case optimality of standard Shellsort
cards.formal: Does there exist a choice, for every \(n\ge2\), of a finite deterministic increment list \(h^{(n)}=(h_1,\ldots,h_p)\), with \(1\le h_i<n\) and \(h_p=1\), such that standard Shellsort with these increments uses at most \(Cn\log n\) key comparisons on average over a uniformly random permutation of \([n]\), for one absolute constant \(C\)? The list may depend on \(n\) but not on the input permutation.
cards.why: This would determine whether the original increment-based sorting method can be average-case optimal.

label: Sampling, Markov chains and mixing times

cards.title: Rapid mixing of Glauber dynamics with \(\Delta +2\) colours
cards.formal: Are there absolute constants \(C,c>0\) such that for every finite simple undirected graph \(G\) with \(n\ge1\) vertices and maximum degree \(\Delta\), and every integer \(q\ge\Delta+2\), the single-vertex heat-bath Glauber chain on proper labelled \(q\)-colourings satisfies \[t_{\mathrm{mix}}(1/4)\le Cn^c?\] The constants must be independent of the graph, its degree and the number of colours. This retains the previously selected degree-uniform polynomial target; the time unit is one vertex update, not a sweep or a bit operation.
cards.why: This tests whether the simplest local update rule samples proper colourings efficiently throughout the full range where it is guaranteed to move between all solutions. It connects random sampling, approximate counting and antiferromagnetic spin systems at a longstanding boundary for general graphs.

cards.title: Polynomial mixing of critical three-dimensional Ising dynamics
cards.formal:
For the zero-field nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic Ising model on the three-dimensional box \(V_L=\{1,\ldots,L\}^{3}\) with free boundary conditions, at the infinite-lattice critical inverse temperature \(\beta_c(\mathbb Z^3)\) defined below, is the worst-initial-state total-variation mixing time of random-site heat-bath dynamics polynomial in \(L\)? Precisely, do there exist constants \(C,a>0\) such that
\[\forall L\in\mathbb N,\ L\ge1,\qquad t_{\mathrm{mix}}(L,1/4)\le C(L+1)^a?\]
Time is counted in individual site-update attempts. The critical parameter is fixed independently of \(L\), and the target is the exact critical point, not a subcritical parameter approaching it at an unspecified rate.
cards.why: This is a basic question about whether a standard local sampling dynamics remains efficient at a phase transition in three dimensions. The equilibrium system has correlations on many scales, so high-temperature mixing guarantees do not directly apply. A polynomial bound or a superpolynomial obstruction would clarify the computational cost of critical fluctuations in one of the central lattice models.

cards.title: Kannan–Tetali–Vempala conjecture
cards.formal: Do universal constants \(K,c>0\) exist such that, for all \(r,s\ge 1\) and all nonnegative integer margins \(a\in \mathbb{N} ^{r},b\in \mathbb{N} ^{s}\) with a nonempty realization set \(\Omega (a,b)\), the lazy switch chain below satisfies \(t_{\mathrm{mix}}(1/4)\le K(r+s)^{c}\)?
cards.why: A general guarantee for a basic sampler that preserves individual degrees, with applications to network and fixed-margin statistical models. The reported solution would close the gap between eventual convergence and a uniform polynomial sampling bound.

cards.title: Cutoff for bounded-degree transitive expanders
cards.formal:
Does every sequence of bounded-degree vertex-transitive expander graphs exhibit total-variation cutoff for lazy simple random walk? More precisely, consider any sequence \((G_k)_{k\ge1}\) of finite connected undirected simple graphs, with \(N_k=|V(G_k)|\to\infty\). Assume each \(G_k\) is vertex-transitive, that there is a fixed integer \(D\ge3\) with \(3\le d_k\le D\) for its vertex degree \(d_k\), and that the lazy-walk spectral gaps satisfy \(\gamma_k\ge\delta\) for some constant \(\delta>0\) independent of \(k\). Must
\[\forall\varepsilon\in(0,1/2),\qquad\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{t_k(\varepsilon)}{t_k(1-\varepsilon)}=1?\]
The transition rule and worst-start mixing times \(t_k\) are defined below. The constants \(D\) and \(\delta\) may depend on the sequence. No quantitative cutoff window or common leading constant for different sequences is demanded.
cards.why: Expanders combine sparse connectivity with fast random-walk mixing and are central objects in algorithms and pseudorandomness. This conjecture asks whether spatial symmetry forces their approach to equilibrium to be abrupt. A resolution would separate the role of expansion in the speed of mixing from the role of symmetry in the shape of convergence.

cards.title: Stationary-start cover-time lower bound
cards.formal: For every irreducible reversible discrete-time Markov chain on n≥2 states, is E_π C≥(n−1)∑_{j=1}^{n−1}1/j?
cards.why: An exact extremal bound would identify how quickly a reversible exploration process can cover its state space.

cards.title: A single hard-core uniqueness threshold on the square lattice
cards.formal: Is there a finite λ_c>0 such that the hard-core model on Z² has a unique Gibbs measure for every 0<λ<λ_c and more than one Gibbs measure for every λ>λ_c?
cards.why: The lattice transition organizes the behavior of independent-set sampling and spatial correlations.

cards.title: Polynomial mixing of planar Ising dynamics with plus boundaries
cards.formal:
For every fixed finite inverse temperature \(\beta\in[0,\infty)\), does random-site heat-bath Glauber dynamics for the zero-field nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic Ising model on \(V_n=\{1,\ldots,n\}^{2}\), with all exterior boundary spins fixed to \(+1\), mix in time polynomial in \(n\)? Precisely, is it true that
\[\forall\beta\in[0,\infty)\ \exists C_\beta,a_\beta>0\ \forall n\ge1,\qquad t_{\mathrm{mix}}^+(n,\beta,1/4)\le C_\beta(n+1)^{a_\beta}?\]
The mixing time is worst-case over every initial configuration inside the box and counts individual site-update attempts. The constants may depend on the fixed temperature, but not on \(n\). The finite-temperature convention and the update rule are specified below.
cards.why: This question asks whether fixing a coherent boundary phase is enough to make local sampling efficient at every positive temperature. At low temperature, convergence from an opposing interior phase is controlled by the disappearance of large interfaces. A polynomial bound would quantify how boundary information removes the slow phase switching that occurs under other boundary conditions.

cards.title: Monotonicity of Ising spectral gaps
cards.formal:
Does strengthening any collection of ferromagnetic interactions always weakly decrease the spectral gap of zero-field random-site heat-bath Ising dynamics on a fixed finite vertex set? For every integer \(n\ge1\), put \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Let \(J=(J_{uv})_{u<v}\) and \(J'=(J'_{uv})_{u<v}\) be finite nonnegative real interaction strengths on the unordered vertex pairs. Is the following statement true?
\[\bigl[\forall u<v,\ 0\le J_{uv}\le J'_{uv}\bigr]\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\gamma(J')\le\gamma(J).\]
Here \(\gamma\) is the spectral gap per individual uniformly chosen site update, defined below. There is no external magnetic field or fixed boundary spin. This is the common interaction-strength generalization explicitly asked in Question 2 of the source.
cards.why: The conjecture asks whether stronger attractive interactions universally slow the relaxation of local sampling. A positive answer would give a comparison principle across both temperature and graph structure, while a counterexample would expose a limit of that basic physical intuition. The difficulty is a global dynamical property, even though each update uses only the neighboring spins.

cards.title: Mixing of the self-avoiding-walk pivot chain
cards.formal:
Determine, up to constant factors as \(n\to\infty\), the worst-initial-state total-variation mixing time \(t_{\mathrm{pivot}}(n)\) of the following pivot chain on rooted \(n\)-step self-avoiding walks in the square lattice. The target is an asymptotic order \(h:\mathbb N_{\ge1}\to\mathbb R_{>0}\) for which there exist constants \(c,C>0\) and \(n_0\ge1\) such that
\[c\,h(n)\le t_{\mathrm{pivot}}(n)\le C\,h(n)\qquad\text{for every }n\ge n_0.\]
A step is one attempted pivot, including a rejected proposal. The exact proposal distribution and the distance threshold \(1/4\) are fixed below. This is an explicitly selected asymptotic mixing-time formulation of the source’s broader request to analyze convergence.
cards.why: The pivot algorithm is a major sampling method for self-avoiding walks, a basic model of polymers with excluded volume. Its practical efficiency makes the absence of a matching rigorous convergence analysis especially consequential. Determining its mixing order would quantify when samples have forgotten an arbitrary initial shape, beyond the behavior of a few measured observables.

cards.title: Polynomial mixing at the four-state Potts critical point
cards.formal: Do there exist absolute constants C,c>0 such that t_mix(1/4)≤C L^c for critical four-state Swendsen–Wang dynamics on every square torus of side L≥3?
cards.why: This isolates the unresolved critical sampling threshold between established polynomial and quasipolynomial guarantees.

cards.title: Cluster sampling of graph colorings with \(\Delta+1\) colors
cards.formal: Are there universal C,c>0 such that WSK dynamics on every finite simple graph with n≥1 vertices and q≥max{2,Δ+1} colors satisfies t_mix(1/4)≤C(nq)^c?
cards.why: A sharp general-graph guarantee would establish when cluster updates overcome barriers facing single-vertex coloring samplers.

cards.title: Weakly negatively regressive sampling of matroid bases
cards.formal:
Does there exist a uniform randomized algorithm which, for every finite matroid \(M\) on \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) given by an independence oracle and every rational point \(p\) of its base polytope, samples a basis \(B\) with exact marginals
\[\Pr[i\in B]=p_i\quad(i\in[n])\]
and a weakly negatively regressive output distribution, in expected time polynomial in \(n\) and the binary encoding length of \(p\)?

Here weak negative regression (WNR) requires, simultaneously for every \(i\in[n]\) and every increasing function \(f:2^{[n]\setminus\{i\}}\to\mathbb R\),
\[\mathbb E[\mathbf 1_{\{i\in B\}} f(B\setminus\{i\})]\le p_i\,\mathbb E[f(B\setminus\{i\})].\]
The algorithm receives no objective function \(f\). One output law must satisfy all these inequalities.

This card selects WNR, the weakest of the three alternative dependence requirements in the source question. Negative association or negative regression would also suffice by implying WNR. The independence-oracle, rational-input and exact expected-time sampling conventions below make the source's efficiency question precise; they are explicit editorial conventions.
cards.why: Randomized rounding must reconcile combinatorial feasibility with the dependence created by exact marginal requirements. This question asks whether every matroid base point has an efficiently accessible law controlling all monotone effects of conditioning on one coordinate. Such a general sampling theorem would support objective-independent rounding and strong guarantees for nonlinear submodular objectives, beyond the linear expectations fixed by marginals alone.

cards.title: General characterization of parallel random-walk cover time
cards.formal: Editorial computational variant: does there exist a deterministic algorithm which, given a connected simple graph \(G\) and an integer \(k\ge1\), outputs a positive rational \(F(G,k)\) in time polynomial in \(|V(G)|+k\), with absolute constants \(0<c\le C<\infty\) such that \[cF(G,k)\le t_{\mathrm{cov}}^{(k)}(G)\le CF(G,k)\] for every input? The parallel cover time uses the worst starting tuple and independent lazy walks defined below.
cards.why: A graph-general cover-time law would quantify the speedup obtainable from parallel random exploration.

cards.title: Exact uniform spanning-tree sampling in linear time
cards.formal: Is there a uniform randomized word-RAM algorithm that, on every connected simple unweighted undirected graph G with m edges, outputs an exactly uniform spanning tree in expected \(O(m)\) total time?
cards.why: This asks whether exact random generation can match the cost of reading the graph.

cards.title: Deterministic approximation scheme for graph cover times
cards.formal:
Is there a deterministic polynomial-time approximation scheme for the expected cover time of simple random walk from a specified starting vertex of an arbitrary finite connected undirected simple graph? Specifically, does there exist one deterministic algorithm \(A\) such that, for every integer \(q\ge2\), there are constants \(C_q,a_q>0\) for which every allowed \(n\)-vertex input \((G,v,q)\) is processed within \(C_q(n+1)^{a_q}\) bit operations and the output rational number \(\widehat C\ge0\) satisfies
\[\left|\widehat C-C(G,v)\right|\le\frac{C(G,v)}q?\]
Here \(C(G,v)\) is defined below. The runtime is polynomial in graph size for every fixed accuracy \(1/q\); its exponent may depend on \(q\). This restores the relative-approximation question actually stated by Aldous and Fill, rather than the unsupported exact-output wording in the imported draft.
cards.why: Cover time is a global measure of how efficiently a random walk explores a network. It is readily estimated by randomized simulation, while deterministic evaluation must account for the distribution of entire exploration histories. A scheme for arbitrary graphs would resolve a concrete derandomization question about an important graph parameter, with accuracy beyond universal constant-factor estimates.

cards.title: Critical Swendsen–Wang spectral-gap exponent
cards.formal: For critical two-state Swendsen–Wang dynamics on square tori, does z=lim_{L→∞} log(1/gap(P_L))/log L exist, and if it does, determine z?
cards.why: The dynamic critical exponent measures the intrinsic cost of cluster sampling near a phase transition.

cards.title: Rapid cluster sampling of three-colourings on the square torus
cards.formal: Do there exist C,c>0 such that WSK dynamics on proper three-colorings of every even square torus of side N≥4 satisfies t_mix(1/4)≤C N^c?
cards.why: This tests whether cluster sampling remains efficient at a canonical antiferromagnetic critical point.

cards.title: FPRAS for counting perfect matchings
cards.formal:
Does there exist one uniform probabilistic algorithm \(A\) and integers \(C,k\ge1\) such that, for every finite undirected simple graph \(G\) and every rational \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\), \(A(G,\varepsilon)\) halts on every random tape within
\[C\bigl(L+\lceil1/\varepsilon\rceil+1\bigr)^{k}\]
Turing-machine steps and outputs a nonnegative rational \(\widehat Z\) satisfying
\[\Pr\bigl[(1-\varepsilon)Z(G)\le\widehat Z\le(1+\varepsilon)Z(G)\bigr]\ge\frac34?\]
Here \(Z(G)\) is the number of perfect matchings, \(L\) is the complete input bit length defined below, and, whenever \(Z(G)=0\), every run must output zero. This is the existence question for a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme on general unweighted graphs.
cards.why: A canonical unresolved problem in approximate counting, separating efficient existence testing from estimating the number of solutions. It also controls the approximability of other counting and partition-function problems through reductions.

cards.title: FPRAS for #BIS
cards.formal: Does \(\#\mathrm{BIS}\), counting all independent sets in an arbitrary finite simple bipartite graph, admit a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme? Precisely, do there exist one probabilistic Turing machine \(A\) and integers \(C,k\geq1\) such that, for every encoded bipartite graph \(G\) and rational \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\), the machine outputs a nonnegative rational \(\widehat Z\) within \(C(L+\lceil1/\varepsilon\rceil)^k\) steps on every random tape and satisfies \[\Pr\big[(1-\varepsilon)Z(G)\leq\widehat Z\leq(1+\varepsilon)Z(G)\big]\geq\tfrac34?\] Here \(Z(G)\) is the number of independent vertex subsets, \(L\) is the complete encoded input length, and the probability is over the algorithm’s independent fair coin bits.
cards.why: The canonical unresolved boundary in approximate counting: many counting problems share its approximation difficulty, while exact counting hardness does not settle whether a randomized relative approximation is efficient. A general scheme would transfer to problems reducible to it with preserved approximation guarantees; an impossibility proof would separate this central family from the counting problems with known fully polynomial schemes.

cards.title: FP versus #P
cards.formal:
Is every function in \(\#\mathrm P\) computable exactly in deterministic polynomial time? With the numerical function convention defined below, the proposition is
\[\#\mathrm P\subseteq\mathrm{FP}_{\mathbb N},\]
equivalently \(\#\mathrm P=\mathrm{FP}_{\mathbb N}\). Each function may have its own fixed machine and polynomial running-time bound. The output is the exact nonnegative integer in binary.
cards.why: This is the fundamental exact-counting analogue of P versus NP. It asks whether every efficiently checkable family of witnesses also admits efficient evaluation of its full multiplicity, and connects counting satisfiability, permanents and many discrete partition functions under one computational boundary.

cards.title: Deterministic FPTAS for the nonnegative permanent
cards.formal:
Does there exist one finite deterministic algorithm \(D\) and integers \(C,k\ge1\) such that, for every \(n\ge1\), every explicitly encoded matrix \(A\in\mathbb Q_{\ge0}^{n\times n}\), and every rational \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\), \(D(A,\varepsilon)\) halts within
\[C\bigl(L+\lceil1/\varepsilon\rceil+1\bigr)^{k}\]
Turing-machine steps and returns a nonnegative rational \(z\) satisfying
\[(1-\varepsilon)\operatorname{per}(A)\le z\le(1+\varepsilon)\operatorname{per}(A)?\]
Here \(L\) is the full binary input length, and the permanent is defined below. The guarantee must hold on every input without randomness.
cards.why: A landmark derandomization problem: match the accuracy and efficiency of the permanent FPRAS using deterministic computation on every nonnegative rational matrix.

cards.title: FP = #P from \(\mathrm{P} = \mathrm{NP}\)
cards.formal:
Does the following implication hold for ordinary uniform Turing computation?
\[\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\#\mathrm P\subseteq\mathrm{FP}_{\mathbb N}.\]
The conclusion means exact deterministic polynomial-time computation of every polynomially verifiable witness count, output as a binary nonnegative integer. Since \(\mathrm{FP}_{\mathbb N}\subseteq\#\mathrm P\) holds unconditionally, the conclusion is also written \(\#\mathrm P=\mathrm{FP}_{\mathbb N}\).
cards.why: The implication isolates the computational gap between learning that solutions exist and determining their exact number. A proof from the decision-collapse hypothesis would connect two central forms of computational tractability, while a negative answer would show that exact counting can remain hard even after all NP existence problems become easy.

cards.title: Deterministic relative counting for DNF
cards.formal:
Is there a deterministic fully polynomial-time approximation scheme for the number of satisfying assignments of an arbitrary explicitly given DNF formula? In the precise reciprocal-integer accuracy convention used here, do there exist a uniform deterministic algorithm \(A\) and positive integers \(C,a\) such that for every DNF formula \(\varphi\) of encoding length \(N\) over its declared \(n\) variables, and every integer \(q\ge2\), the algorithm outputs a nonnegative rational number \(\widehat Z\) with
\[|\widehat Z-Z(\varphi)|\le Z(\varphi)/q,\qquad Z(\varphi)=|\{x\in\{0,1\}^{n}:\varphi(x)=1\}|,\]
and halts within \(C(N+q+1)^a\) steps? The guarantee must hold on every input without randomness, advice or an oracle. There is no bound on term width or on the number of occurrences of a variable other than the explicit input length.
cards.why: DNF counting is a canonical approximate-counting problem for which randomization gives an efficient relative approximation even when direct random assignment sampling rarely finds a solution. A deterministic scheme would remove randomness from this basic union-counting task across all formula widths and occurrence patterns. It would strengthen the explicit derandomization tools available for both complexity theory and probabilistic data processing.

cards.title: Output-polynomial hypergraph transversal enumeration
cards.formal: Do a deterministic Turing algorithm \(A\) and absolute constants \(C,c>0\) exist such that, for every explicitly given finite hypergraph \(H\), \(A\) outputs every inclusion-minimal transversal exactly once and terminates within \(C(L(H)+L_{\mathrm{out}}(H)+1)^c\) bit steps?
cards.why: This central enumeration question governs the complexity of converting a hypergraph into the family of all its minimal hitting sets and underlies many enumeration reductions.

cards.title: Output-polynomial vertex enumeration
cards.formal:
Do there exist a uniform deterministic algorithm \(A\) and a polynomial \(p\) such that, for every rational matrix \(M\) and rational vector \(b\) for which
\[
P=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:Mx\leq b\}
\]
is bounded, \(A\) lists every vertex of \(P\) exactly once and halts in at most \(p(L+S)\) bit operations? Here \(L\) is the complete binary input length and \(S\) is the length of the required exact vertex list in the canonical encoding below. The dimension \(d\) is part of the input. Empty, lower-dimensional and degenerate polytopes are included.
cards.why: This is a basic unresolved question about converting between implicit and explicit representations of convex feasible regions. A general output-polynomial algorithm would make degeneracy and intermediate representation growth manageable at the level of total complexity, while an impossibility result would separate efficient linear optimization from full exact enumeration.

cards.title: Decision versus approximate counting for fixed-width SAT
cards.formal: For every fixed clause width \(k\geq3\), do randomized decision \(k\)-SAT and randomized multiplicative approximation of \(\#k\)-SAT have the same optimal exponential running-time rate in the number of variables? With \(d_k\) and \(a_k\) defined below, the target is \(a_k=d_k\) for every fixed \(k\geq3\). This makes “close the gap” precise at the exponential-rate level, as in the later source’s fixed-width question.
cards.why: Tests whether estimating the number of satisfying assignments intrinsically requires more exponential work than finding out whether any exist. Equality would transfer the leading exponential savings in fixed-width SAT to a broader counting task.

cards.title: FPRAS for counting undirected Euler tours
cards.formal:
Does the number of Euler tours of an arbitrary connected Eulerian undirected graph admit a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme? Using the labelled-edge, fixed-first-traversal normalization below, let \(Z(G)\) be the tour count. The question is whether there exist a uniform randomized algorithm \(A\) and constants \(C,a>0\) such that, for every allowed graph \(G\) and every integer \(q\ge2\), the algorithm outputs a nonnegative rational \(\widehat Z\) in at most \(C(N+q+1)^a\) bit operations on every random tape and
\[\Pr\!\left[\left|\widehat Z-Z(G)\right|\le\frac{Z(G)}q\right]\ge\frac34.\]
Here \(N\) is the input encoding length and the probability is over the algorithm’s independent fair random bits. The constants are independent of the graph and accuracy. There is no degree bound, planarity promise or prescribed sampling chain.
cards.why: Euler tours are elementary graph traversals whose existence is easy to decide, yet approximate enumeration remains a major counting question. A solution would clarify how much harder it is to impose one globally connected traversal than to satisfy local balance constraints on edge directions. This is a test case for the reach of randomized approximate counting beyond problems with tractable orientation or matching formulations.

cards.title: #BIS-easiness of Boolean log-supermodular counting CSPs
cards.formal:
For every fixed finite family \(\mathcal F\) of functions \(f:\{0,1\}^{r_f}\to\mathbb Q_{\geq0}\), where each arity \(r_f\geq0\) is fixed, does
\[\bigl[\forall f\in\mathcal F\ \forall x,y\in\{0,1\}^{r_f},\quad f(x\lor y)f(x\land y)\geq f(x)f(y)\bigr]\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\#\operatorname{CSP}(\mathcal F)\leq_{\mathrm{AP}}\#\mathrm{BIS}\ ?\]
Here \(\leq_{\mathrm{AP}}\) is a randomized approximation-preserving reduction for counting problems with the relative-error and polynomial-cost guarantees below. The family is fixed before instances arrive, and a reduction may depend on it.
cards.why: A positive answer would collapse the whole finite rational Boolean log-supermodular approximation region to the #BIS benchmark and sharpen the conservative counting-CSP classification. A negative answer would separate general log-supermodularity from that benchmark at the level of computational reductions, beyond the known separation in gadget expressibility.

cards.title: Fully polynomial randomized approximation of mixed discriminants
cards.formal: Does there exist a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for the mixed discriminant of every tuple of rational symmetric positive semidefinite matrices, with no restriction on dimension, rank or conditioning? The scheme must give arbitrarily small relative error with success probability at least \(3/4\), in the precise uniform bit model below.
cards.why: An FPRAS would extend the success of nonnegative permanent approximation to general positive semidefinite matrix tuples and improve the algorithmic understanding of constrained determinantal distributions. An impossibility result would identify a substantive boundary between determinant-based counting structures despite their nonnegative coefficients and useful convex relaxations.

cards.title: Parity subgraph-counting dichotomy
cards.formal:
Is the following statement true? For every computable class \(\mathcal H\) of finite simple graphs whose matching-split number is unbounded, the parameterized problem \(\oplus\mathrm{Sub}(\mathcal H)\) is complete for parity-\(\mathrm W[1]\) under deterministic fixed-parameter Turing reductions:
\[\oplus\mathrm{Clique}\ \leq^{\mathrm{fpt}}_T\ \oplus\mathrm{Sub}(\mathcal H)\ \leq^{\mathrm{fpt}}_T\ \oplus\mathrm{Clique}.\]
The input to \(\oplus\mathrm{Sub}(\mathcal H)\) is a pattern \(H\in\mathcal H\) and an arbitrary host graph \(G\); its output is the parity of the number of subgraphs of \(G\) isomorphic to \(H\), and its parameter is \(|V(H)|\). No closure property beyond invariance under isomorphism is imposed on \(\mathcal H\). This is the parity clause of the source conjecture, using the reduction convention made explicit in the later classification paper.
cards.why: A classification by a single structural parameter would identify exactly which graph-pattern families avoid the difficulty of parity counting, subject to the usual separation between fixed-parameter tractability and parity clique. This is a broad boundary theorem for counting complexity: taking counts modulo two can make families tractable even when exact counting remains hard. The unresolved scope is all computable pattern classes, beyond the substantial hereditary and tree cases.

cards.title: Treewidth classification of approximate counting CSP
cards.formal: Assume that parameterized Clique has no randomized fixed-parameter algorithm with bounded error. For every fixed recursively enumerable class C of finite relational structures with a uniform bound on relation arity, are the following equivalent: (1) counting homomorphisms \(A\to B\) for \(A\in C\) and arbitrary compatible B is exactly solvable in polynomial time; (2) this problem admits a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme; (3) it admits a fixed-parameter randomized approximation scheme with parameter \(\Vert A\Vert\); and (4) the Gaifman graphs of structures in C have bounded treewidth? The missing implication is \((3)\Rightarrow (4)\). No fan-grid containment, minor closure or other closure property is assumed for C. This is the source’s Theorem 3 with its fan-class hypothesis removed.
cards.why: Would determine whether approximation enlarges the tractable classes of structurally restricted counting CSPs, and whether treewidth remains the complete structural criterion.

cards.title: Finite-domain enumeration-CSP dichotomy
cards.formal:
Classify all finite constraint languages by whether their satisfying assignments can be enumerated with polynomial delay. More precisely, under the explicitly stated hypothesis \(\mathrm P\ne\mathrm{NP}\), determine the characteristic function
\[\chi_{\mathrm{Delay}}(D,\Gamma)=\begin{cases}1,&\operatorname{EnumCSP}(D,\Gamma)\in\mathrm{DelayP},\\0,&\operatorname{EnumCSP}(D,\Gamma)\notin\mathrm{DelayP},\end{cases}\]
for every finite nonempty domain \(D\) and every finite relational language \(\Gamma\) on \(D\), with absolute error at most \(1/100\). The requested dichotomy is a substantive structural characterization of the tractable class, with algorithms on that side and conditional exclusion of polynomial delay on the complementary side, in the model below.
cards.why: A full classification would identify exactly which finite local constraint languages support regular generation of every solution, rather than just deciding whether one exists. It would explain the extra algorithmic structure needed beyond the decision dichotomy, including languages that admit efficient enumeration despite hard pinning tests. This matters when applications must inspect alternatives without long pauses between outputs.

cards.title: Does P ≠ NP imply both polynomial-space enumeration separations?
cards.formal:
Is the following implication true for enumeration problems with polynomial-time checkable, polynomial-length solutions?
\[
\mathrm P\ne\mathrm{NP}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\left(\mathrm{DelayP}\ne\mathrm{DelayP}^{\mathrm{poly}}
\ \land\ 
\mathrm{IncP}\ne\mathrm{IncP}^{\mathrm{poly}}\right).
\]
Here DelayP permits polynomial delay and unrestricted working space, IncP permits incremental polynomial time and unrestricted working space, and the superscript poly requires the same enumerator to obey the timing guarantee while using only polynomial space in the input length. All classes use the deterministic RAM model defined below.
cards.why: The question tests whether space can be an essential resource for efficient enumeration even when each solution is short and easy to verify. Fixing P ≠ NP asks whether this familiar decision-complexity separation already forces a time–space distinction for producing many answers.

cards.title: Incremental polynomial-time binary-matroid circuit enumeration
cards.formal: Is there a deterministic algorithm that, for every explicitly given binary matrix \(A\in\mathbb F_2^{r\times m}\), enumerates all circuits of its column matroid exactly once in incremental polynomial time while using space polynomial only in the input length? Equivalently, does binary-matroid circuit enumeration belong to \(\mathrm{IncP}^{\mathrm{poly}}\) under the source’s conventions? The target permits any fixed polynomial exponent in the number of outputs; retaining the known quadratic incremental exponent is a stronger variant distinguished in the later source.
cards.why: This is a concrete test of whether the storage used by saturation-based enumeration is intrinsically necessary. A polynomial-space incremental algorithm would make all minimal binary linear dependencies accessible in output-sensitive time without retaining an exponentially large history, and could suggest methods for other closure-based enumeration problems.

cards.title: Nearly linear approximate counting for knapsack
cards.formal: Is there a randomized algorithm that, for n nonnegative integer weights and a nonnegative capacity T, outputs \(\widehat Z\) with \[\Pr[(1-\varepsilon)Z\le\widehat Z\le(1+\varepsilon)Z]\ge2/3,\qquad Z=|\{S\subseteq[n]:\sum_{i\in S}W_i\le T\}|,\] in \(O(n\varepsilon^{-a}\log^b(n/\varepsilon+2))\) time for some absolute constants a,b and all \(0<\varepsilon\le1/2\)?
cards.why: An input-linear approximate counter would sharpen the complexity of a basic counting problem beyond decision and optimization.

cards.title: Edge-exchange Gray codes for directed spanning trees
cards.formal: For every finite loopless simple directed graph and root r admitting an out-arborescence, do all spanning out-arborescences admit an arc-exchange listing?
cards.why: This extends minimal-change enumeration to rooted directed connectivity and implies the undirected pivot-exchange existence statement.

cards.title: A natural OutputP versus IncP separation from clique-free domination
cards.formal:
Does \(\mathrm{TFNP}\ne\mathrm{FP}\) imply that there is a fixed integer \(t\ge3\) for which enumerating all inclusion-minimal dominating sets of \(K_t\)-free graphs belongs to \(\mathrm{OutputP}\) but not to \(\mathrm{IncP}\)?

The graph is explicitly given. Enumeration is deterministic, without repetitions and in any order. Total output-polynomial time is already known for every fixed \(t\); the question is whether this specific family supplies the conditional failure of incremental polynomial time.
cards.why: This would locate the gap between efficient total enumeration and efficient initial output in a standard graph problem. The concrete candidate tests whether a known abstract total-search separation can be realized without constructing artificial padded solution sets.

cards.title: Pivot-exchange Gray codes for spanning trees
cards.formal: Does every finite connected simple undirected graph have a pivot-exchange listing of all its spanning trees?
cards.why: A pivot-exchange ordering would impose a much stronger locality condition than ordinary edge-exchange enumeration.

cards.title: Ranking and unranking a spanning-tree Gray code
cards.formal: Is there a uniformly polynomial-time rankable and unrankable edge-exchange ordering of the labeled spanning trees of K_n for every n≥2?
cards.why: This combines minimal-change generation with efficient random access to a fundamental combinatorial family.

cards.title: Polynomial-delay disjointness Gray codes for combinations
cards.formal: For every k≥1 and n≥2k+1 except (n,k)=(5,2), can all k-subsets of [n] be generated in a cyclic disjointness ordering with polynomial delay and polynomial workspace?
cards.why: The question separates existence of a combinatorial Gray cycle from its efficient generation.

cards.title: Ramanujan graphs of every degree
cards.formal: Do arbitrarily large d-regular Ramanujan graphs exist for every \(d\ge 3\)?
cards.why: Source selection: A landmark survey connecting expansion with combinatorics, algorithms and complexity.

cards.title: Hadwiger’s conjecture
cards.formal: Is the following proposition true? For every integer \(n\ge1\), every simple undirected graph \(G\) on \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and every integer \(t\ge1\), if \(\chi(G)\ge t\), then \(G\) contains \(K_t\) as an ordinary graph minor. Equivalently, \(h(G)\ge\chi(G)\) for every such graph, where \(h\) is the Hadwiger number defined below.
cards.why: Hadwiger’s conjecture proposes an exact relation between two basic graph parameters: the number of colors needed and the size of a complete graph obtainable by contraction. It extends the Four-Color Theorem and would turn exclusion of a complete minor into the sharp universal coloring bound. Its significance comes from this structural connection across all finite graphs, rather than from an algorithmic requirement in the question.

cards.title: Erdős–Hajnal conjecture
cards.formal: For each integer \(h\ge 2\) and each undirected simple graph \(H\) on \([h]\), is there a real constant \(c_H>0\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge 1\) and every undirected simple graph \(G\) on \([n]\) containing no induced copy of \(H\), \[\max\{\alpha(G),\omega(G)\}\ge n^{c_H}?\] The exponent is chosen after the entire forbidden graph \(H\) and before the host graph \(G\); the assertion must hold for all such \(H\).
cards.why: This central conjecture asks whether every proper hereditary restriction forces a polynomial-size clique or independent set, far beyond the logarithmic scale possible in arbitrary graphs. It would provide a common structural guarantee across all forbidden-induced-subgraph classes and clarify the relation between local exclusions, large nearly uniform vertex sets and neighborhood complexity. These are basic objects in structural and algorithmic graph theory; the assertion itself is an existence theorem, not an efficient clique or independent-set algorithm.

cards.title: Tutte’s 5-flow conjecture
cards.formal: Does every finite loopless bridgeless undirected multigraph \(G=(V,E)\) admit an orientation \(D\) of all its edges and a function \(f:E\to\{1,2,3,4\}\) such that, at every vertex \(v\in V\), \[\sum_{e\in E:\,\operatorname{head}_D(e)=v}f(e)=\sum_{e\in E:\,\operatorname{tail}_D(e)=v}f(e)\] as an equality of integers?
cards.why: The conjecture asks whether the necessary absence of bridges always permits bounded nonzero integer circulation, with the universal value limit improved from five to four. It connects flow existence with graph coloring through planar duality and has a quantitative consequence for packing sets of arcs that meet every directed cut.

cards.title: Erdős girth conjecture
cards.formal: For every integer \(k\ge 1\), do there exist constants \(c_{k}>0\) and \(N_{k}\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge N_{k}\), some simple undirected graph G on exactly n vertices has at least \(c_{k} n^{1+1/k}\) edges and contains no cycle of length less than \(2k+2\)? Equivalently, is \(M_{2k+2}(n)=\Omega _{k}(n^{1+1/k})\) for every fixed k, where \(M_{s}(n)\) is the maximum number of edges in an n-vertex graph with no cycle shorter than s?
cards.why: A central extremal graph question with direct consequences for compact routing and graph sparsification: it asks whether the standard density obstruction from short cycles is asymptotically tight at every fixed scale.

cards.title: Erdős girth conjecture
cards.formal:
Is the following assertion true?
\[
 \forall k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge2}\quad
 \exists c_k\in\mathbb R_{>0}\quad
 \forall N\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\quad
 \exists n\in\mathbb Z_{\ge N}\quad
 \exists G:\quad
 |V(G)|=n,\qquad |E(G)|\ge c_k n^{1+1/k},\qquad
 \operatorname{girth}(G)>2k,
\]
where \(G\) ranges over finite simple undirected graphs? In words, for every fixed \(k\ge2\), there must be graphs of unbounded order with no cycle of length at most \(2k\) and with a positive constant fraction of \(n^{1+1/k}\) edges.
cards.why: The conjecture asks whether graphs can attain the classical density scale while avoiding all short cycles. Its resolution would clarify the extremal limits of sparse graph representations that preserve distances.

cards.title: Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture
cards.formal:
Is the following proposition true? For every finite nonempty tree \(T\) and every integer \(r\ge1\), there exists an integer \(B\ge0\) such that every finite simple undirected graph \(G\) satisfies
\[\bigl(\omega(G)\le r\ \land\ G\text{ has no induced copy of }T\bigr)
\ \Longrightarrow\ \chi(G)\le B.\]
The quantifier order is \(\forall T\,\forall r\,\exists B\,\forall G\). The bound may depend on the entire tree \(T\) and on \(r\), but must be independent of the number of vertices and every other parameter of \(G\). No rate of growth or computational requirement on \(B\) is prescribed.
cards.why: Would characterize induced forests as the single forbidden patterns capable of bounding ordinary chromatic number in terms of clique number, clarifying a central structural obstruction to graph colouring and large independent sets.

cards.title: Reed’s conjecture
cards.formal: Does every nonempty finite simple undirected graph \(G\) satisfy \[\chi(G)\leq\left\lceil\frac{\Delta(G)+1+\omega(G)}{2}\right\rceil?\] The quantification is over every number of vertices and every edge set, with no restriction on maximum degree or graph class.
cards.why: A defining question about how a local degree constraint and a global clique obstruction jointly control ordinary graph colouring. A positive resolution would give a sharp universal guarantee for partitioning vertices into independent colour classes, while a counterexample would reveal a colouring obstruction beyond this proposed relationship among three basic graph parameters. Its significance is structural even without an efficient algorithm for finding the guaranteed colouring.

cards.title: Vertex reconstruction conjecture
cards.formal: For every integer \(n\ge 3\) and every pair of finite simple undirected graphs G,H on n vertices, does equality \(D(G)=D(H)\) of their vertex decks imply that G and H are isomorphic?
cards.why: The conjecture asks whether all overlapping one-vertex views determine an entire graph. It tests how much structural information survives deletion and loss of labels, and connects graph structure to reconstruction and isomorphism problems.

cards.title: List edge-coloring conjecture
cards.formal: For every finite loopless multigraph G and every assignment L of finite sets of colors to its edges with |\(\mathrm{L}(e)|\ge \chi ' (G)\) for every edge e, does there exist a proper edge coloring c with \(c(e)\in \mathrm{L}(e)\) for every e? Equivalently, is \(\chi ' _{\ell}(G)=\chi ' (G)\) for every such G?
cards.why: The conjecture asks whether local restrictions on available edge colors ever increase the number of choices each edge must receive beyond the optimum with a shared palette. It tests whether ordinary scheduling feasibility is robust to arbitrary per-job availability, across all finite loopless multigraphs.

cards.title: Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture
cards.formal:
For every integer \(n\ge2\), every integer \(r\) with \(1\le r\le n-1\), and every simple loopless digraph \(D=(V,A)\) on \(n\) vertices, does
\[\bigl(\forall v\in V:\ d_D^+(v)\ge r\bigr)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\bigl(\exists\text{ a directed cycle of length }\ell\le\lceil n/r\rceil\bigr)\]
hold? Opposite arcs are allowed, and a pair of opposite arcs counts as a directed cycle of length two. The bound is exact, for every permitted pair \((n,r)\), with no additive error.
cards.why: The conjecture asks whether a lower bound on every vertex’s number of outgoing neighbors forces a cycle at the sharp possible length. It would determine the exact universal relation between a local directed-degree condition and global cyclic structure. Even the dense regime that should force a directed triangle remains a major unresolved case, despite broad approximate bounds and results for symmetric graph classes.

cards.title: Seese’s conjecture
cards.formal:
For every isomorphism-closed class \(\mathcal C\) of finite simple undirected graphs, does
\[
\operatorname{Sat}_{\mathrm{MSO}_1}(\mathcal C)\ \text{decidable}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\exists k\ge1\ \forall G\in\mathcal C,\quad\operatorname{cw}(G)\le k
\]
hold?

The language \(\operatorname{Sat}_{\mathrm{MSO}_1}(\mathcal C)\) contains exactly the encoded vertex-set monadic second-order sentences satisfied by at least one graph in \(\mathcal C\). The bound \(k\) may depend on the whole class but must hold for every graph in it.
cards.why: The conjecture asks whether decidability of an expressive graph language forces a uniform structural restriction. It connects computability of theories to finite graph construction with a bounded number of labels, without assuming an efficient decision procedure or a restricted graph class.

cards.title: Optimal bounds in the Excluded Grid Theorem
cards.formal:
For every integer \(r\ge2\), define
\[f(r)=\min\{t\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}:\ \forall\text{ finite simple undirected graphs }G,\ \operatorname{tw}(G)\ge t\ \Longrightarrow\ Q_r\text{ is a minor of }G\},\]
where \(Q_r\) is the square grid of side length \(r\). Determine the asymptotic order of \(f(r)\) up to universal constant factors, including all logarithmic or other unbounded factors. In particular, supply an independently specified positive function \(h\) and prove
\[\exists a,b>0\ \exists r_0\ge2\ \forall r\in\mathbb Z_{\ge r_0}:\quad a\,h(r)\le f(r)\le b\,h(r).\]
The constants and the threshold \(r_0\) are independent of the host graph and of \(r\). The problem asks for the actual asymptotic order; it does not assume a quadratic or cubic conjectured answer.
cards.why: The Grid-Minor Theorem connects an abstract measure of graph connectivity with a concrete planar pattern. Its quantitative loss controls the strength of many structural and parameterized-algorithm results. Determining the optimal loss would identify how much treewidth is inherently needed to force a grid in unrestricted graphs, including whether the remaining logarithmic obstruction captures the whole difficulty.

cards.title: Berge–Fulkerson conjecture
cards.formal:
Does every finite loopless bridgeless cubic multigraph \(G=(V,E)\) admit a list of six perfect matchings \(M_1,\ldots,M_6\subseteq E\) such that
\[
\forall e\in E,\qquad
\bigl|\{i\in\{1,\ldots,6\}:e\in M_i\}\bigr|=2?
\]
The six entries may repeat. Their union must cover every edge, and every edge must occur in exactly two list positions.
cards.why: One perfect matching selects one incident edge at every vertex. The conjecture asks whether six globally consistent selections can always distribute their incidences evenly across the three edges at each vertex. This exact decomposition problem is central to matching and covering theory for cubic graphs, and it implies other long-standing matching conjectures.

cards.title: Barnette’s conjecture
cards.formal:
Is every finite simple undirected graph that is 3-connected, cubic, bipartite and planar Hamiltonian?

Equivalently, for every integer \(n\ge4\) and every graph \(G=([n],E)\) satisfying the four properties below, must there exist a bijection \(\pi:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to[n]\) such that
\[
\{\pi(j),\pi((j+1)\bmod n)\}\in E
\qquad\text{for every }j\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}?
\]
The cyclic order must use only edges of the original graph.
cards.why: The conjecture asks whether local degree and parity restrictions, together with planar structure and robust connectivity, force one global cycle through every vertex. It is a classical boundary problem for Hamiltonicity, with connections to graph drawing and partitions of planar dual graphs. A proof or counterexample would settle the full structural claim, beyond algorithms for individual instances or restricted families.

cards.title: Seymour’s second-neighborhood conjecture
cards.formal:
Does every finite nonempty oriented graph \(D=(V,A)\) contain a vertex \(v\) whose second out-neighborhood is at least as large as its first out-neighborhood?
\[
\forall D\ \exists v\in V,\qquad
|N_D^{++}(v)|\ge |N_D^+(v)|.
\]
Here \(N_D^+(v)\) contains vertices at directed distance one from \(v\), and \(N_D^{++}(v)\) contains vertices at directed distance exactly two, as defined below.
cards.why: The conjecture predicts a universal local expansion phenomenon even in sparse directed graphs with no connectivity assumptions. Its statement involves only two steps of reachability, but a proof must find a favorable vertex in every orientation without opposite arcs. It is a central structural question about how directed degree constraints force neighborhood growth.

cards.title: Lovász conjecture
cards.formal:
Does every finite nonempty connected vertex-transitive simple undirected graph have a Hamiltonian path? With the definitions below, prove or refute
\[
\forall n\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\ \forall E\subseteq\binom{[n]}2\quad
\bigl(\operatorname{Connected}([n],E)\land
\operatorname{VertexTransitive}([n],E)\bigr)
\Longrightarrow
\exists p\in S_n\ \forall i\in[n-1]\quad
\{p(i),p(i+1)\}\in E.
\]
There is no restriction on the number of vertices, degree, automorphism group or representation as a Cayley graph. The required spanning object is a path; its endpoints need not be adjacent. This is an existence assertion without a computational time bound or a requirement to find the path efficiently.
cards.why: A resolution would settle a central connection between graph symmetry and spanning structure. A proof would show that connectedness and vertex symmetry suffice for a spanning path across every finite simple undirected graph, beyond particular group constructions. A counterexample would identify an obstruction that survives complete vertex symmetry. The existence question remains meaningful without asking for a fast algorithm.

cards.title: Two-sided Ramanujan signings
cards.formal: Find two-lifts or adjacency signings with the stated two-sided Ramanujan spectral bounds.
cards.why: Source selection: A landmark survey connecting expansion with combinatorics, algorithms and complexity.

cards.title: Fat Minors
cards.formal: Fat Minors
cards.why: The significance of this particular question has not yet been individually assessed. The question concerns algorithmic solvability in a specified model. Its structural value is to locate the boundary between an effective procedure and a computational or logical obstruction.

cards.title: Sparsification conjecture
cards.formal:
Is every monadically stable class of finite simple undirected graphs structurally nowhere dense? Precisely, with the definitions below, prove or refute
\[
\forall\mathcal C\subseteq\mathfrak G\
\left[
\operatorname{MS}(\mathcal C)\Longrightarrow
\exists\mathcal D\subseteq\mathfrak G\ \exists T\
\left(
\operatorname{ND}(\mathcal D)\ \land\
\forall H\in\mathcal C\ \exists G\in\mathcal D\
H\in T(G)
\right)
\right].
\]
Here \(\mathfrak G\) is the set of finite simple undirected graphs up to isomorphism, \(\operatorname{MS}\) denotes monadic stability, \(\operatorname{ND}\) denotes nowhere denseness, and \(T\) is a single first-order transduction with finitely many unary colors and one vertex variable per output vertex.

The source class \(\mathcal D\), number of colors and formulas of \(T\) may depend on the whole target class \(\mathcal C\). They must be fixed for that class, independently of the size or identity of \(H\). The graph \(G\) and its coloring may depend on \(H\). The covering requirement is \(\mathcal C\subseteq T(\mathcal D)\); the transduction may also produce graphs outside \(\mathcal C\). Neither class is assumed closed under taking subgraphs or induced subgraphs, and neither is required to be decidable or effectively presented. This is an existence statement, with no time bound, bound on the size of a preimage, or algorithm for finding the preimage.
cards.why: A resolution would determine whether a central model-theoretic restriction on definable order patterns has an exact structural explanation in terms of sparse graphs. A positive answer would identify all monadically stable classes as logical images of nowhere dense classes, unifying two major descriptions of graph structure. A negative answer would exhibit a form of monadic stability that every such sparse representation misses. The target is the existence of a uniform representation for an entire class, a distinct structural issue from algorithms for evaluating first-order sentences.

cards.title: Cereceda’s conjecture
cards.formal:
For every fixed integer \(d\ge0\), does there exist an integer \(C_d\ge1\) such that every finite simple \(d\)-degenerate graph \(G\) on \(n\) vertices satisfies
\[
\operatorname{diam}\bigl(R_{d+2}(G)\bigr)\le C_d n^2?
\]
Here \(R_{d+2}(G)\) is the graph of proper colorings using the fixed palette \(\{1,\ldots,d+2\}\), with one move changing the color of exactly one vertex.

Equivalently, for every \(d\) there must be one \(C_d\) such that, for every \(n\ge0\), every such graph and every pair of its proper \((d+2)\)-colorings \(\alpha,\beta\), a sequence of at most \(C_d n^2\) valid single-vertex moves transforms \(\alpha\) into \(\beta\). The constant may depend on \(d\) and on nothing else.
cards.why: A coloring may need to change while every intermediate assignment remains valid. Cereceda’s conjecture asks whether one extra color beyond the greedy guarantee always permits a quadratic-length transition, even when local degrees are large. It is a central test of how sparsity controls the geometry of a solution space, beyond merely ensuring that all solutions are connected.

cards.title: Well-quasi-ordering by pivot-minors
cards.formal: Are all graphs well-quasi-ordered by pivot-minors?
cards.why: Source selection: A specialist survey covering both algorithmic and structural questions about rank-width.

cards.title: Tuza’s triangle packing–covering conjecture
cards.formal:
Is it true that every finite simple undirected graph \(G\) satisfies
\[
 \tau_{\triangle}(G)\le 2\nu_{\triangle}(G),
\]
where \(\tau_{\triangle}(G)\) is the minimum number of edges meeting every triangle of \(G\), and \(\nu_{\triangle}(G)\) is the maximum number of pairwise edge-disjoint triangles?
cards.why: The conjecture asks whether the cost of destroying every triangle is always at most twice the largest edge-disjoint triangle packing, the exact factor already forced by a small complete graph.

cards.title: Linear neighborhood complexity of hereditary small graph classes
cards.formal: Every hereditary small class of graphs has neighborhood complexity \(O(n)\).
cards.why: The significance of this particular question has not yet been individually assessed. The question concerns algorithmic solvability in a specified model. Its structural value is to locate the boundary between an effective procedure and a computational or logical obstruction.

cards.title: Bipartite circle pivot-minors from large rank-width
cards.formal: Large rank-width forces every fixed bipartite circle graph as a pivot-minor.
cards.why: Source selection: A specialist survey covering both algorithmic and structural questions about rank-width.

cards.title: Tree vertex-minors from large linear rank-width
cards.formal: Does sufficiently large linear rank-width force every fixed tree as a vertex-minor?
cards.why: Source selection: A specialist survey covering both algorithmic and structural questions about rank-width.

cards.title: Edge reconstruction conjecture
cards.formal: For every pair of finite simple undirected graphs G and H with at least four edges, does equality of their edge decks \(D_{E}(G)=D_{E}(H)\) imply \(G\cong H\)?
cards.why: A longstanding reconstruction principle that tests how much global graph structure survives individual edge losses.

cards.title: Constant-factor treewidth preservation by subcubic subgraphs
cards.formal:
Does there exist a real constant \(C\ge1\) such that every finite nonempty simple undirected graph \(G\) has a nonempty subgraph \(H\) satisfying
\[
\Delta(H)\le3
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\operatorname{tw}(H)\ge\frac{\operatorname{tw}(G)}{C}?
\]
Here \(H\) is obtained solely by deleting vertices and edges of \(G\), \(\Delta\) is maximum degree, and \(\operatorname{tw}\) is treewidth. The same constant \(C\) must work for all graphs.
cards.why: Treewidth is a central measure of graph structure. This question asks whether a graph can always retain a constant fraction of that structure after every vertex degree is reduced to at most three, regardless of its original degrees or density.

cards.title: Neumann–Lara conjecture
cards.formal:
Is it true that for every finite oriented graph \(D=(V,A)\) whose underlying undirected graph is planar, there exists a map \(c:V\to\{0,1\}\) such that
\[
 D[c^{-1}(0)]\quad\text{and}\quad D[c^{-1}(1)]
\]
are both acyclic?
cards.why: Determine whether two acyclic classes always suffice to organize the vertices of an oriented planar graph.

cards.title: Well-quasi-ordering Eulerian digraphs by weak immersion
cards.formal:
Is the class of all finite Eulerian directed multigraphs well-quasi-ordered by weak immersion?

Let \(\mathcal E\) be the set of graphs defined below: loops and parallel arcs are allowed, and every vertex has equal in-degree and out-degree. No connectivity, degree, width or surface-embedding restriction is imposed. Write \(H\preccurlyeq_{\mathrm{wi}}G\) when \(H\) has a weak immersion in \(G\), with directions and distinct arc identities respected.

The exact proposition is
\[
\forall (G_i)_{i\in\mathbb N}\in\mathcal E^{\mathbb N}\quad
\exists i,j\in\mathbb N\quad
i<j\ \land\ G_i\preccurlyeq_{\mathrm{wi}}G_j,
\]
where \(\mathbb N=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}\). The sequence is arbitrary and need not be computable. The earlier graph must immerse in the later graph in the order specified by the sequence. This is Conjecture 3.2 of the ICALP 2026 source, with the graph and immersion conventions supplied by its full version.
cards.why: A positive answer would extend a central type of structural graph-ordering theorem to the broad Eulerian directed setting. It would imply finite forbidden-immersion descriptions for properties closed under weak immersion within that class, with the fixed-property testing consequences explained by the source. General digraphs and strong immersions admit known ordering obstructions, so the balance condition and the precise weak relation are substantive. A counterexample would identify a fundamental obstruction that survives both restrictions.

cards.title: Boolean dimension of posets with planar cover graphs
cards.formal:
Does there exist an integer \(d\ge1\) such that, for every finite poset \(P=(V,<_{P})\) whose undirected cover graph is planar, there exist strict total orders \(L_1,\ldots,L_d\) on \(V\) and a Boolean function \(\varphi_P:\{0,1\}^{d}\to\{0,1\}\) satisfying
\[
\forall x,y\in V\ (x\ne y\Longrightarrow
\bigl[x<_{P}y\iff
\varphi_P(b_1(x,y),\ldots,b_d(x,y))=1\bigr]),
\]
where \(b_i(x,y)=1\) if \(x<_{L_i}y\), and \(b_i(x,y)=0\) otherwise? The integer \(d\) must be independent of the poset. The total orders and the Boolean function may depend on \(P\).
cards.why: This asks whether planar local cover relations force a uniformly bounded comparison description of the entire partial order, despite arbitrarily large ordinary order dimension. A positive answer would also give logarithmic-size reachability labels for planar directed graphs, connecting a structural question about orders with concise representations of global reachability.

cards.title: Polylogarithmic treewidth with forbidden induced minors
cards.formal: For every integer \(t\ge 2\), does there exist an integer \(c_{t}\ge 1\) such that every n-vertex graph G with \(n\ge 2\), no clique of size t and neither Kt,t nor Wt as an induced minor satisfies \(\operatorname{tw}(G)\le c_{t}(\log _{2} n)^{c_{t}}\)?
cards.why: Would yield a substantially stronger structural bound for graphs excluding two induced-minor patterns and large cliques. Polylogarithmic treewidth supports quasipolynomial algorithms for many problems whose dependence on treewidth is exponential, making the quantitative improvement algorithmically significant.

cards.title: Graph isomorphism in polynomial time
cards.formal: Does there exist a uniform deterministic Turing machine M and fixed positive integers C,k such that on every binary input x, M halts within \(C(|x|+1)^k\) transitions and accepts exactly when x encodes two isomorphic finite simple undirected graphs? Equivalently, is the language \(\mathrm{GI}\) defined below in deterministic polynomial time?
cards.why: Tests whether the central equivalence problem for finite combinatorial structures can be recognized in deterministic polynomial time after the quasipolynomial barrier was broken.

cards.title: Deterministic linear-time minimum spanning tree
cards.formal: Does there exist one uniform deterministic comparison-RAM algorithm that, for every finite connected simple undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) with arbitrary real weights \(w:E\to\mathbb R\), outputs a minimum spanning tree in \(O(n+m)\) worst-case total time, where \(n=|V|\) and \(m=|E|\)? The graph is explicitly listed, and weights are opaque keys that may only be copied and compared. The machine, output and quantifier conventions are fixed below; the bound counts all computation, not only weight comparisons.
cards.why: A central unresolved boundary between deterministic and randomized algorithms for a classical graph optimization problem, and a rare case where a provably optimal algorithm exists before its exact asymptotic complexity is understood.

cards.title: Almost-linear-time exact maximum matching in general graphs
cards.formal:
Does there exist one uniform randomized sequential word-RAM algorithm that, on every explicitly represented finite simple undirected graph \(G\), terminates almost surely, always outputs a valid matching when it terminates, and outputs a maximum-cardinality matching with probability at least \(2/3\), with expected running time
\[(n+m+2)^{1+o(1)}?\]
Here \(n=|V(G)|\), \(m=|E(G)|\), and the precise machine, input, probability and asymptotic conventions are below. In particular, the same program must meet every positive exponent slack; an algorithm chosen separately for each fixed slack is not the stated target.
cards.why: A major remaining exact graph-optimization problem beyond the almost-linear flow framework. It asks whether odd-cycle and blossom structure impose a real asymptotic cost, even when randomization is allowed.

cards.title: Exact directed maximum flow in \(O((m+n) \operatorname{polylog} n)\) time
cards.formal:
For every fixed integer \(a\ge1\), do there exist a uniform randomized word-RAM algorithm \(A_a\), integers \(B_a\ge a+3\), \(k_a\ge0\) and \(C_a\ge1\) with the following property? On every explicitly represented directed graph \(G\) with \(n\ge2\) vertices, \(m\) arcs, distinct terminals \(s,t\), and integer arc capacities
\[0\le u_e\le n^a,\]
the algorithm uses words of \(w=B_a\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\) bits, halts on every random execution within
\[C_a(m+n)\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil^{k_a}\]
word operations, and outputs an exact integral maximum \(s\)-\(t\) flow with probability at least \(2/3\)?
The output must give a flow value on every original arc. The algorithm, constants and logarithmic exponent may depend on \(a\), but not on the graph, its capacities, its terminal choices or its input ordering. The complete graph, flow and machine conventions are specified below.
cards.why: Maximum flow is a central primitive for routing, cuts and combinatorial optimization. Almost-linear algorithms have already removed a polynomial overhead. This question asks whether exact directed flow can be computed with only a fixed power of a logarithm beyond explicit input size, on all polynomial-capacity instances and with a complete flow as output.

cards.title: Linear-time directed shortest paths with nonnegative real weights
cards.formal: Do there exist an integer word-size constant \(B\ge3\), an absolute constant \(K>0\), and one uniform deterministic comparison-addition RAM algorithm that, on every explicitly given simple directed graph with \(n\ge2\) vertices and \(m\) arcs of arbitrary nonnegative real lengths, and every specified source vertex, outputs all exact source distances within \(K(n+m)\) instructions? The model below charges control, memory access, preprocessing and output as well as operations on real values.
cards.why: An optimal linear algorithm would determine whether directed shortest paths with general nonnegative numerical lengths can be computed at the cost of reading the graph.

cards.title: Deterministic almost-linear vertex connectivity
cards.formal:
Do there exist one uniform deterministic word-RAM algorithm \(A\), a real constant \(K>0\), an integer word-size constant \(d\ge4\), and a function \(h:\{2,3,\ldots\}\to[1,\infty)\) satisfying
\[
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log h(N)}{\log N}=0
\]
such that, for every explicitly given simple unweighted undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) with \(V=[n]\), \(n\ge2\), \(m=|E|\) and \(N=n+m\), the algorithm uses at most \(KNh(N)\) instructions and outputs both
\[
 \kappa(G)=\min\bigl\{|S|:S\subseteq V,
 G[V\setminus S]\text{ is disconnected or }|V\setminus S|\le1\bigr\}
\]
and a set \(S\) attaining this minimum?

The machine has word length \(w=d\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\) and the operations and charged costs below. No randomness is allowed.
cards.why: Determine whether randomness is needed for almost-linear exact computation of a basic measure of network resilience. Finding the weakest vertex separation uniformly over sparse and dense graphs remains different from handling only small cuts.

cards.title: Deterministic Exact Matching
cards.formal:
Do there exist a deterministic Turing machine \(A\), a real constant \(K>0\) and an integer \(d\ge1\) such that, for every explicitly given finite simple undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) with an even number \(n\ge0\) of vertices, every red-edge subset \(R\subseteq E\), and every integer \(0\le k\le n/2\), the machine halts within \(K(L+1)^d\) steps and outputs YES exactly when
\[
 \exists M\subseteq E:\qquad
 \bigl(\forall v\in V,\ |\{e\in M:v\in e\}|=1\bigr)
 \quad\text{and}\quad |M\cap R|=k?
\]
Here \(L\) is the input bit length under the explicit encoding below. No bipartition is promised.
cards.why: Determine whether randomness can be removed from a basic exact constraint on perfect matching. The problem connects combinatorial derandomization with algebraic algorithms while keeping a short, directly checkable input and feasibility condition.

cards.title: Almost-linear triangle detection
cards.formal: Does one uniform classical randomized word-RAM algorithm exist that, for every finite simple undirected graph with \(n\) vertices and \(m\) edges given by explicit adjacency lists, returns whether a triangle exists with probability at least \(2/3\), while every execution takes at most \((n+m+2)^{1+o(1)}\) word instructions? The running-time guarantee must cover all graph densities, all valid adjacency-list orders and every random tape.
cards.why: Determine whether detecting the simplest cyclic graph pattern requires a superlinear amount of computation beyond reading the input.

cards.title: Graph canonization versus graph isomorphism
cards.formal: Do there exist a deterministic oracle Turing machine A and a constant \(c\ge 1\) such that A, given any finite simple undirected graph G, computes a canonical form \(F(G)\) in at most \(O((N+1)^{c})\) steps using the graph-isomorphism decision oracle, where N is the input encoding length and F satisfies the conventions below?
cards.why: Distinguishes recognizing structural equivalence from efficiently choosing a unique representative of each equivalence class.

cards.title: Strongly explicit Ramanujan families for every degree
cards.formal: For every fixed integer \(d\ge 3\), is there one deterministic algorithm that computes the port rotation map of connected d-regular Ramanujan graphs for an unbounded set of vertex counts n in time polynomial in log n, with the effective family and graph conventions below?
cards.why: Combine extremal spectral quality with efficient local access for arbitrary constant-degree expanders.

cards.title: Strongly polynomial near-linear negative-weight shortest paths
cards.formal:
Do there exist one uniform classical randomized comparison-addition algorithm \(A\), constants \(C>0\), integers \(k\ge0\) and \(B\ge3\), and a polynomial \(p\) with the following property? For every directed graph with \(n\ge2\) vertices, \(m\) arcs, arbitrary real arc lengths and no negative directed cycle, and every specified source \(s\), every execution of \(A\) halts within
\[
 C(m+n)\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil^k
\]
instructions in the model below, and with probability at least \(2/3\) outputs all exact distances from \(s\)? The bound is uniform over all graph densities and real weight assignments and is independent of numerical magnitude or encoding length. On rational inputs the additional encoding-space bound is \(p(L)\), where \(L\) is the full binary input length.
cards.why: Removing numerical scaling dependence in a nearly input-linear bound would settle a central gap in exact shortest-path computation over arbitrary real data.

cards.title: Strongly polynomial maximum flow below the \(mn\) barrier
cards.formal:
Do there exist constants \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\), \(K>0\), an integer word-size constant \(B\ge3\), a polynomial \(p\), and one uniform classical randomized algorithm \(A\) such that, for every directed network in the domain below, every execution of \(A\) uses at most
\[
 K(mn)^{1-\varepsilon}
\]
arithmetic-RAM instructions, uses at most \(p(L)\) bits of space, and outputs an exact maximum flow with probability at least \(2/3\)? Here \(n\) and \(m\) count vertices and arcs, \(L\) is the full binary input length, and capacities are arbitrary nonnegative finite rationals. The constants, program and space polynomial must be the same for every network, every allowed density and every capacity encoding length.
cards.why: A polynomial improvement over the general strongly polynomial maximum-flow barrier would separate a central combinatorial optimization primitive from its longstanding arithmetic complexity bound.

cards.title: Polynomial-time detection of the seven-vertex tree H* as an induced minor — resolved
cards.formal: Let H* have vertex set {a₁,a₂,b,c,d,e₁,e₂} and edge set {a₁b,a₂b,bc,cd,de₁,de₂}. Is there a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that decides, for every finite simple undirected input graph G, whether H* is an induced minor of G? Answer: yes, by Eagling-Vose, Martin, Paulusma, and Trotignon (April 2026).
cards.why: This was the smallest unresolved forest-pattern case in induced-minor detection, a basic graph containment operation sitting between subgraph detection and ordinary minor detection. Its solution explains how forbidding unwanted cross-edges can remain algorithmically manageable. It is retained as a resolved historical benchmark, with its original identifier and source.

cards.title: Steiner Shortcut Conjecture
cards.formal:
Do there exist an absolute real constant \(C>0\) and integers \(a,b\ge0\) such that every finite simple directed graph \(G=(V,E)\) with \(n=|V|\ge2\), \(m=|E|\ge1\) and no isolated vertices admits finite sets of new vertices \(W\) and new arcs \(F\) satisfying all of the following?
\[
 W\cap V=\varnothing,\qquad
 H=(V\cup W,E\cup F),\qquad
 |F|\le C m\bigl(\log_2(n+2)\bigr)^a.
\]
For every ordered pair \(u,v\in V\), a directed path from \(u\) to \(v\) exists in \(H\) if and only if one exists in \(G\). Moreover, whenever such a path exists, \(H\) has a \(u\)-to-\(v\) path containing at most
\[
 C\bigl(\log_2(n+2)\bigr)^b
\]
arcs. There is no restriction on the number of consecutive new vertices along a path and no construction-time requirement.
cards.why: Determine whether a directed reachability relation always has a compact augmentation with short witnessing paths. The structural answer would clarify an obstacle behind fast parallel graph algorithms, while efficient construction remains a separate requirement.

cards.title: Single-exponential exact cut mimicking networks
cards.formal:
Does there exist an absolute real constant \(C>0\) such that, for every finite simple undirected graph \(G=(V,E,w)\) with finite nonnegative real edge weights and every specified terminal set \(T\subseteq V\) of size \(k\ge2\), there is a finite simple undirected graph \(H=(V_H,E_H,w_H)\) with nonnegative real edge weights such that
\[
 T\subseteq V_H,\qquad |V_H|\le2^{Ck},\qquad
 \forall\,\varnothing\ne A\subsetneq T,\quad
 \lambda_{H,T}(A)=\lambda_{G,T}(A)?
\]
Here the terminal cut value is
\[
 \lambda_{G,T}(A)=
 \min_{\substack{S\subseteq V\\ S\cap T=A}}
 \sum_{e\in\delta_G(S)}w(e),
\]
and the analogous formula defines \(\lambda_{H,T}\). The replacement graph is arbitrary and need not be a contraction, minor or subgraph of \(G\).
cards.why: Determine how compactly a network can encode every exact terminal separation cost. The question isolates the structural power of arbitrary replacement graphs beyond contractions and beyond preserving only pairwise cuts.

cards.title: Near-linear-space exact planar distance oracles with polylogarithmic queries
cards.formal: Does every directed planar graph with n vertices and nonnegative real edge weights admit a uniformly constructible exact distance oracle using \(O(n\log^c(2+n))\) cells, answering each distance query in \(O(\log^c(2+n))\) worst-case operations, and having expected polynomial preprocessing time, for one absolute constant c? Preprocessing may be Las Vegas randomized, but every returned oracle must answer all pairs exactly.
cards.why: This asks whether planarity permits simultaneously compact and fast exact distance queries.

cards.title: Bipartite Exact Matching: deterministic polynomial time
cards.formal: Do there exist one uniform deterministic Turing machine \(A\), a constant \(C\ge1\) and an integer \(d\ge1\) such that, for every finite simple bipartite graph \(G=(L\cup R,E)\) with \(|L|=|R|=n\ge0\), every red/blue coloring of its edges, and every integer \(0\le k\le n\), the machine decides within \(C(\ell+1)^d\) bit steps whether \(G\) has a perfect matching with exactly \(k\) red edges? Here \(\ell\) is the full explicit input encoding length. The answer must be correct on every allowed instance, with no randomness or additional promise.
cards.why: Determine whether randomness can be removed from an exact cardinality constraint on bipartite perfect matching, a concrete test case connecting combinatorial algorithms and polynomial identity testing.

cards.title: Polynomial-time computation of planar treewidth
cards.formal:
Is there a uniform deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that computes the exact treewidth of every finite planar graph?

Precisely, do there exist one deterministic multitape Turing machine \(M\) and integers \(C,k\ge1\) such that \(M\) halts on every binary input \(x\) within \(C(|x|+1)^k\) transitions and, for every finite simple planar graph \(G\) in the encoding below,
\[
M(\operatorname{enc}(G))=\operatorname{bin}_{\pm}(\operatorname{tw}(G))?
\]
