The output is the exact integer treewidth in the specified signed binary encoding. Graph size and treewidth are unrestricted; the polynomial is fixed independently of both. No planar embedding, tree decomposition or bound on treewidth is supplied with the graph.

This is the polynomial-time existence question stated in §4.6 of the 2016 seminar report. It asks for an exact algorithm, not an optimal numerical running-time exponent. A negative answer is the full negation of that existence assertion, not merely an NP-hardness theorem conditional on a separate complexity-class separation.
cards.why: Treewidth is a central measure connecting graph structure with algorithms for otherwise difficult graph problems. An exact polynomial-time algorithm on planar graphs would make optimal width accessible on a large and important sparse graph class. A negative answer would locate a fundamental limitation of planarity despite efficient algorithms for the related branchwidth parameter. The issue is distinct from using a decomposition once one has already been supplied.

cards.title: Optimal exact-distance label length for planar graphs
cards.formal: Determine the asymptotic growth of \(\ell_{\mathrm{planar}}(n)\) up to universal constant factors, where \(\ell_{\mathrm{planar}}(n)\) is the least integer \(b\ge0\) permitting labels of \(b\) bits that determine every pairwise distance in every connected unweighted simple planar graph on \(n\ge2\) vertices using only the two labels.
cards.why: Closing this polynomial gap would identify the information needed to distribute an entire planar graph metric into independent vertex labels.

cards.title: Almost-linear exact directed global minimum cut
cards.formal:
For every fixed integer \(a\ge1\), do there exist one uniform randomized algorithm \(A\), constants \(C\ge1\), an integer \(d\ge a+4\), and a function \(h:\mathbb N_{\ge2}\to[1,\infty)\) with
\[
\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log h(N)}{\log N}=0,
\]
such that every allowed directed graph on \(n\ge2\) vertices and \(m\) arcs is processed in at most \(C(m+n)h(m+n)\) word-RAM instructions on every random execution? Arc weights are positive integers at most \(n^a\). With probability at least \(2/3\), the output must be a nonempty proper set \(S\subset V\) minimizing
\[
\sum_{(u,v)\in E:\ u\in S,\ v\notin S}w(u,v)
\]
over all such sets, together with its exact integer value. There are no prescribed terminals.
cards.why: Exact global directed connectivity is a fundamental graph optimization problem whose unknown optimal terminals remain a major obstacle beyond fast single-pair flow.

cards.title: Almost-linear directed vertex connectivity
cards.formal:
Do there exist one uniform randomized algorithm \(A\), a constant \(C\ge1\), an integer word-size constant \(d\ge4\), and a function \(h:\mathbb N_{\ge2}\to[1,\infty)\) satisfying
\[
\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log h(N)}{\log N}=0,
\]
such that, on every simple unweighted directed graph \(G\) with \(n\ge2\) vertices and \(m\) arcs, every execution uses at most \(C(m+n)h(m+n)\) word-RAM instructions and, with probability at least \(2/3\), outputs the exact vertex connectivity \(\kappa(G)\) together with an attaining vertex set? Define
\[
\kappa(G)=\min\{|S|:S\subseteq V(G),\ G-S\text{ is not strongly connected or }|V(G)\setminus S|\le1\}.
\]
Both density and connectivity are unrestricted.
cards.why: A uniform almost-linear algorithm would settle the remaining general exact running-time gap for directed vertex robustness, a classical network problem.

cards.title: 3-colorability of diameter-two graphs
cards.formal: Does there exist one deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, for every finite simple connected undirected graph \(G\) of diameter at most \(2\), decides whether \(G\) has a proper vertex coloring with three colors? The input does not promise that such a coloring exists. Precisely, there must be one Turing machine and constants \(C>0,b\in\mathbb N\), independent of the graph, whose worst-case running time on every valid \(n\)-vertex graph is at most \(C(n+1)^b\), and whose output is correct on every such graph.
cards.why: Three-colorability is a basic constraint-satisfaction problem, and diameter is one of the simplest measures of graph connectivity. This single unresolved boundary tests whether very short distances enforce exploitable structure without any sparsity assumption. Either an algorithm or a hardness reduction would explain a fundamental limit of structural restrictions in graph algorithms.

cards.title: Dynamic optimality conjecture
cards.formal: Fix n ordered keys and an access sequence X. In the root-BST model, an access is served by rotations until its key is at the root; its cost is one plus the number of rotations. Let \(\operatorname{OPT}(X)\) minimize total cost over offline executions, allowing an optimal initial tree. Is there a universal constant C such that, for every initial splay tree \(T_{0}\) and every X, \(\mathrm{cost}_{\mathrm{splay}}(X;T_0)\le C(\mathrm{OPT}(X)+n)\)? The additive term allows an arbitrary initial configuration.
cards.why: It asks whether a simple local adjustment rule can match every legal strategy with complete knowledge of the future. The issue is fundamental to instance-sensitive data structures: success would replace a growing competitive penalty by a constant for all access patterns. A counterexample would identify a limitation of splaying that its many separate locality guarantees fail to reveal.

cards.title: Superlogarithmic static cell-probe lower bounds
cards.formal: Does there exist a fixed integer \(k\ge 2\) and a uniformly polynomial-time computable family of Boolean functions \(F_{n}\) on an n-word database and a \(k\lceil \log _{2} n\rceil\)-bit query such that its optimal deterministic static cell-probe query complexity \(t*F(n)\), with word size \(\lceil 4\log _{2} n\rceil\) bits and \(n\lceil \log _{2} n\rceil ^{2}\) memory cells, satisfies \(t*F(n)/\log _{2} n\to \infty\) as \(n\to \infty\)?
cards.why: A central unconditional lower-bound bottleneck for data structures: establish that a short, explicitly defined static query fundamentally needs more than logarithmically many memory accesses despite unrestricted preprocessing.

cards.title: Deterministic linear-time static dictionaries
cards.formal: Is the following proposition true? For every fixed integer \(d\ge 1\) there are uniform deterministic construction and query programs \(A_{d},Q_{d}\) and a constant \(C_{d}\ge 1\) such that, for every \(n\ge 2\), every word length \(\lceil \log _{2}(n+1)\rceil \le w\le d\lceil \log _{2}(n+1)\rceil\), and every n-record input with distinct w-bit integer keys and w-bit values, \(A_{d}\) builds a static dictionary in at most \(C_{d} n\) operations and \(C_{d} n\) words of total space, and \(Q_{d}\) answers every membership-and-value query in at most \(C_{d}\) operations.
cards.why: Exact constant-time lookup is a basic component of many larger data structures. The unresolved cost is obtaining the representation deterministically in optimal time, so a resolution would settle whether randomness is essential to this combination of construction, storage and lookup guarantees.

cards.title: Constant-time deterministic dynamic dictionaries
cards.formal:
Is the following statement true? For every fixed integer \(c\ge2\), there exist a uniform deterministic word-RAM program \(A_c\) and a constant \(C_c\ge1\) such that, for every integer capacity \(N\ge2\), with word size
\[
 w=\lceil c\log_2(N+2)\rceil,
\]
the program maintains a dictionary of at most \(N\) word-sized key–value pairs, starting empty, and satisfies all of the following guarantees for every valid online operation sequence: initialization costs at most \(C_cN\) instructions; at most \(C_cN\) words of space are used at any time; every lookup costs at most \(C_c\) instructions; and initialization together with every finite prefix containing \(q\) lookups and \(u\) insertions or deletions costs at most \(C_c(N+q+u)\) instructions? All answers must be exact.
cards.why: A fully deterministic dictionary with these guarantees would match the basic operation bounds of randomized dynamic hashing in linear space. An unconditional obstruction would establish a substantive limitation of determinism for this central data-structure interface.

cards.title: Multiphase conjecture
cards.formal:
Do there exist real constants \(\gamma>1\) and \(\delta>0\) such that every admissible uniform, always-correct randomized word-RAM algorithm for the following three-phase problem, with \(k=\lceil n^\gamma\rceil\), satisfies
\[
 \tau_A(n)=\Omega(n^\delta)?
\]
Phase I receives \(S_1,\ldots,S_k\subseteq[n]\) and preprocesses them. Phase II receives \(T\subseteq[n]\) and updates the retained state. Phase III receives \(i\in[k]\) and answers whether \(S_i\cap T=\varnothing\). The normalized expected overhead is
\[
 \tau_A(n)=\max\left\{1,\frac{t_1(n)}{kn},\frac{t_2(n)}n,t_3(n)\right\},
\]
where \(t_j(n)\) is the worst-input expected number of instructions used in Phase \(j\), as defined below. The lower bound must hold for all sufficiently large integer \(n\), with no restriction on query adaptivity.
cards.why: This staged problem is a candidate for unconditional polynomial operation lower bounds for dynamic data structures, including directed reachability. Its conjectured overhead is much larger than the logarithmic bounds accessible in general models.

cards.title: Polynomial lower bounds for adaptive dynamic data structures
cards.formal: Is there an explicit dynamic Boolean problem for which adaptive randomized polynomial-space cell-probe data structures require polynomial amortized cost? Precisely, seek one problem family for which, for every fixed space exponent s, there is \(\eta_s>0\) such that every structure using at most \(n^s\) cells incurs expected \(\Omega(n^{\eta_s})\) probes per operation on some polynomial-length operation sequence, for infinitely many n.
cards.why: A polynomial unconditional barrier would change the known limits of dynamic data structures beyond polylogarithmic lower bounds.

cards.title: Superlinear cell-probe lower bounds for succinct Boolean matrix-vector products
cards.formal:
For every family of deterministic exact static cell-probe data structures representing arbitrary matrices \(M\in\{0,1\}^{n\times n}\) in \(n^2+o(n^2)\) bits, with word length
\[w_n=\left\lceil\log_2(n^2+1)\right\rceil,\]
must its worst-case number \(T(n)\) of word probes for answering a Boolean matrix-vector query satisfy
\[T(n)=\omega(n)?\]
The representation may encode the whole matrix arbitrarily; it need not retain the original matrix as a separately readable array. Computation between probes and preprocessing time are uncharged, as specified below.
cards.why: A superlinear lower bound with almost no storage overhead would go beyond the standard static-data-structure barriers for this central problem. It would isolate an information-access obstruction independently of how much computation is performed between memory reads.

cards.title: Superconstant word-RAM time for prefix-\(U_1\)
cards.formal:
Is it impossible to maintain a length-\(n\) bit sequence under substitutions and answer prefix-AND queries using a deterministic uniform word-RAM data structure with \(O(n)\) preprocessing and \(O(1)\) worst-case time for each update and each query?

An update \(\operatorname{set}(i,b)\) replaces the bit at position \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) by \(b\in\{0,1\}\). A query at \(k\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\) must return
\[\operatorname{prefix}(k)=\bigwedge_{i=1}^{k}b_i,\qquad\operatorname{prefix}(0)=1.\]
The word length is \(w=\lceil c\log_2(n+2)\rceil\) for a fixed integer constant \(c\ge1\). The impossibility is to hold for every such fixed constant and every correct data structure in the model below.

This retains the source's worst-case time convention. The target is absence of any constant bound, not a prescribed logarithmic lower-bound rate or the stronger exclusion of amortized constant time.
cards.why: This small dynamic problem isolates whether maintaining even threshold information about a changing minimum requires more than a constant number of actual word operations. Its hardness would complete conditional classifications of dynamic regular-language membership, and newer work extends that connection to tree languages. The challenge concerns computation inside the machine as well as memory access, making it a foundational word-RAM question.

cards.title: Space-query exponent curve of 3SUM indexing
cards.formal:
Determine the query-exponent curve \(\tau_{\mathrm{3SI}}:[1,2]\to\mathbb R\) to absolute accuracy \(1/100\) at every point, where
\[
\tau_{\mathrm{3SI}}(s)=\inf\{t\ge0:\ \forall\eta\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\ \exists(P,Q)\text{ satisfying }S(n)=O(n^{s+\eta}),\ T(n)=O(n^{t+\eta})\}.
\]
Here \((P,Q)\) is a uniform randomized static index for the two-set sum-membership problem below. Space and query time obey their bounds on every random outcome, while each fixed input/query is correct with probability at least \(2/3\). Preprocessing time is unrestricted.
cards.why: The curve asks how much information about a quadratic family of sums must be stored to support reusable membership queries, a general representation barrier underlying several string indexes.

cards.title: Strong SetDisjointness conjecture
cards.formal: Is the following statement true? For every admissible uniform static word-RAM data structure for SetDisjointness, with worst-case retained space \(S(N)\) words and worst-case query time \(T(N)\) steps, there exist constants \(c>0\), \(b\in\mathbb N\), and \(N_0\ge2\) such that \(S(N)T(N)^2\ge cN^2/(\log_2(N+2))^b\) for every integer \(N\ge N_0\). For every integer \(N\ge2\), the input is a list \(A_1,\ldots,A_m\) of nonempty subsets of \([N]=\{1,\ldots,N\}\), with \(1\le m\le N\) and total size \(N=\sum_{i=1}^m|A_i|\). A query supplies indices \(i,j\in[m]\) and must return whether \(A_i\cap A_j=\varnothing\).
cards.why: This conjecture underlies many space-query conditional lower bounds for text indexes, graph oracles and set systems.

cards.title: Succinct dynamic rank/select in a polynomial universe — resolved
cards.formal: Can a dynamic set S⊆{0,…,U−1}, with n=|S| and polynomially larger universe U=n^(1+Θ(1)), be represented using H(n,U)+o(H(n,U)) bits while supporting insertion, deletion, rank and select in deterministic O(1+log n/log log(n+2)) worst-case time per operation on a word RAM with multiplication and word size Θ(log U)? Here H(n,U)=log₂ binom(U,n). Yes: Domingues’s 2026 construction implies this bound.
cards.why: Rank/select is a basic ordered-data interface. Achieving its optimal dynamic time together with near-minimum encoding space shows that compression need not cost an additional asymptotic slowdown, and distinguishes space spent on information from space spent on navigation.

cards.title: Randomized complexity of online labeling
cards.formal: Determine, up to constant factors, the optimal amortized expected number of relabelings per insertion or deletion for randomized online list labeling with at most \(n\) live items and labels in \([2n]\), against an oblivious adversary. The target is one asymptotic rate \(f(n)\) with a matching upper bound and lower bound in the model below.
cards.why: The problem measures the unavoidable movement needed to maintain a sorted array with spare capacity, a primitive used throughout ordered storage and indexing.

cards.title: Unified bound for binary search trees
cards.formal:
Does there exist one uniform deterministic online binary-search-tree program \(A\) in the model below and one integer \(C\ge1\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge1\), every integer \(m\ge0\), and every request sequence \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in[n]^m\), the program correctly completes all requests and
\[
T_A(n,X)\le C\bigl(n\log_2(n+2)+U_n(X)\bigr),
\qquad
U_n(X)=\sum_{t=1}^{m}\log_2\!\left(2+\min\left\{n,\min_{1\le s<t}(t-s+|x_t-x_s|)\right\}\right)?
\]
Here \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), an empty minimum is \(+\infty\), an empty sum is zero, and \(T_A\) includes initialization and all computation. The same program, its fixed storage constants, and \(C\) must work for all \(n,m,X\). The guarantee is total amortized cost for every finite sequence, including every finite prefix, with no worst-case bound on an individual request.
cards.why: The unified bound asks one search tree to exploit temporal and rank locality together, beyond separate working-set and dynamic-finger guarantees. Resolving whether that combined access bound is achievable would clarify a central limit of adaptive binary search trees.

cards.title: Deque conjecture
cards.formal:
Is there an absolute constant \(C\ge1\) such that, for every finite binary search tree \(T_0\) with \(n\ge0\) distinct ordered keys and every legal sequence \(\mathcal S\) of \(m\ge0\) deque operations, the specified bottom-up splay implementation satisfies
\[
W(T_0,\mathcal S)\le C(n+m)?
\]
The operations are insertion of a new minimum or maximum and deletion of the current minimum or maximum. Insertions make the new key the root; deletions splay the requested extremum to the root and remove it. The cost \(W\) counts operation overhead, search edges and rotations as defined below.
cards.why: I include this because it tests whether one general-purpose adaptive representation can recognize a workload whose optimal cost is linear. The remaining gap is tiny numerically but significant mathematically: a proof would explain why expensive local restructuring cannot accumulate across arbitrary alternations of the two ends.

cards.title: Amortized decrease-key complexity of standard pairing heaps
cards.formal:
Determine an explicit asymptotic growth rate \(f:\mathbb N_{\ge1}\to[1,\infty)\) that is a tight amortized decrease-key charge for the standard two-pass pairing heap. For every finite legal operation sequence \(\mathcal S\) starting from empty heaps and having at most \(N\) live items in all heaps combined, require
\[
W(\mathcal S)\le C\bigl(a(\mathcal S)+b(\mathcal S)\log_2(N+2)+c(\mathcal S)f(N)\bigr)
\]
for one absolute \(C\). Here \(a\) counts make-heap, insert, meld and find-min operations, \(b\) counts delete-min operations, and \(c\) counts decrease-key operations. Tightness means that every charge function satisfying such an inequality is \(\Omega(f(N))\), with the quantifiers specified below. The algorithm itself and the other-operation charges are fixed.
cards.why: A tight analysis would resolve the central complexity uncertainty for one of the simplest and most widely studied self-adjusting priority queues.

cards.title: Splay traversal conjecture
cards.formal: Is there an absolute C such that accessing the preorder of any n-key binary search tree by standard bottom-up Splay, starting from any other tree on those keys, costs at most Cn?
cards.why: The traversal conjecture is a classical structured-access barrier within the broader dynamic-optimality program.

cards.title: Logarithmic fully retroactive priority queues
cards.formal:
Does there exist one deterministic comparison pointer-machine program \(A\), with fixed constants \(C_t,C_s>0\), that implements the fully retroactive priority queue defined below on every valid finite sequence of commands? Starting with an empty history, it must insert and remove historical insertion or extract-min records, and return the minimum item immediately after any queried historical time. Write \(m_j\) for the number of historical records after command \(j\), \(m_0=0\), and \(M_j=\max\{m_{j-1},m_j\}\). For every \(q\ge0\), require
\[
T_A(q)\le C_t\left(1+\sum_{j=1}^{q}\log_2(2+M_j)\right),
\]
where \(T_A(q)\) counts initialization and all steps through the first \(q\) commands. During command \(j\), at most \(C_s(1+M_j)\) records may be allocated and not yet reclaimed; after it finishes, at most \(C_s(1+m_j)\) may remain. Initialization uses at most \(C_s\) records. Thus time is amortized over all edits and queries, while space is linear in the currently maintained history, including working storage.
cards.why: A single change to the past can alter which items many later extractions remove. Matching ordinary priority-queue costs despite this dependence would show that unrestricted historical access can be maintained without an asymptotic time or space penalty in the stated model.

cards.title: Optimal distance oracles that also report paths
cards.formal: Is there a uniform path-reporting distance-oracle construction for every finite simple undirected graph on \(n\ge2\) vertices with positive real edge weights and every integer \(2\le k\le n\), using at most \(Cn^{1+1/k}\) storage cells, that answers a connected-pair query \((u,v)\) with an estimate \(D\) in at most \(C\) operations and then reports a path \(P\) in at most \(C(1+|P|)\) further operations, with \[d_G(u,v)\le w(P)\le D\le(2k-1)d_G(u,v)?\] The constant \(C\) is absolute, independent of \(n,k\), the graph and its weights.
cards.why: This asks whether compact distance summaries can return actual routes without losing their best size and stretch guarantees.

cards.title: Truly subquadratic preprocessing for stretch-3 distance oracles
cards.formal: For every fixed \(\varepsilon\in(0,1]\), do there exist constants \(\delta>0\) and \(C\), and a uniform randomized preprocessing algorithm, such that every simple undirected nonnegatively weighted graph with \(n\) vertices and \(m\le n^{2-\varepsilon}\) edges can be turned in expected \(Cn^{2-\delta}\) time into a distance oracle using \(Cn^{3/2}\) cells and worst-case \(C\) query time, whose estimate satisfies \[d_G(u,v)\le D(u,v)\le3d_G(u,v)\] for every connected vertex pair? Constants may depend on \(\varepsilon\), but not on the graph, its weights or \(n\).
cards.why: The remaining stretch-three case tests whether compact distance oracles can be built genuinely faster than quadratic time on sparse inputs.

cards.title: Sorting-bound external-memory breadth-first search
cards.formal: Can exact single-source unweighted distances in every undirected graph be computed in O(S(n+m)) external-memory I/Os, even when M<n?
cards.why: This asks whether graph traversal can match the basic external-memory sorting bound.

cards.title: Sorting-bound external-memory weighted shortest paths
cards.formal: Can exact single-source distances in an arbitrary undirected graph with nonnegative real edge lengths be computed in O(S(n+m)) external-memory I/Os independently of weight ratios?
cards.why: The problem tests whether weighted graph exploration can be performed at sorting cost on external storage.

cards.title: Buffered fully persistent search trees
cards.formal:
For every fixed real \(0<\varepsilon<1\), does there exist one uniform deterministic comparison-based external-memory data structure and a constant \(c\ge1\) that maintain the fully persistent ordered-set interface below, for every integer block size \(B\ge2\), internal-memory capacity \(M\ge2B\), and every online operation history? Require correctness and termination, worst-case at most \(c\) I/Os for each explicit \(\operatorname{Clone}\), and the following joint amortized bound on every finite history \(H\):
\[
\operatorname{IO}(H)\le c\!\left(1+C_H+\sum_{j\in\mathcal U_H}B^{\varepsilon-1}L_j+\sum_{j\in\mathcal Q_H}L_j+\sum_{j\in\mathcal R_H}\frac{K_j}{B}\right),
\qquad L_j=1+\log_B(2+N_j).
\]
Here \(\mathcal U_H\) indexes insertions and deletions, \(\mathcal Q_H\) indexes successor and range queries, \(\mathcal R_H\subseteq\mathcal Q_H\) indexes range queries, \(C_H\) counts explicit clones, \(N_j\) is the size of the version accessed by operation \(j\), and \(K_j\) is that range query’s output size. At every point require at most
\[
c\!\left(1+\frac{U+C}{B}\right)
\]
external-memory blocks, including metadata and temporary storage, where \(U,C\) count update and clone operations begun by that point. The constants and program may depend on \(\varepsilon\), but not on the block parameters, history, keys or version sizes. This retains the card’s stated simultaneous quantitative sharpening of the source’s broader question about buffered full persistence and efficient cloning.
cards.why: Buffering reduces storage transfers for updates, while full persistence permits new branches from historical states. Combining them with queries measured by the accessed version’s size and space measured by the update history would provide both capabilities in one comparison-based storage index.

cards.title: Optimal randomized memory-reallocation overhead
cards.formal:
Determine, up to absolute constant factors as \(\varepsilon\to0^+\), the optimal worst-case expected overhead \(F(\varepsilon)\) for online memory reallocation at load at most \(1-\varepsilon\). In the model below,
\[
F(\varepsilon)=\inf_{\mathcal A}\ \sup_{M,\sigma,j}\ \mathbb E[\operatorname{cost}_{\mathcal A,M}(\sigma,j)],
\qquad 0<\varepsilon\le\tfrac12.
\]
The supremum ranges over positive integer capacities, nonempty valid finite request sequences fixed independently of the allocator's randomness, and one update in each sequence. All live objects occupy disjoint contiguous intervals.
cards.why: A tight result would establish the intrinsic price of fragmentation when a general-purpose allocator operates close to full capacity.

cards.title: Combined depth and size bounds for confluently persistent tries
cards.formal: For every fixed integer \(k\ge2\), does there exist a deterministic uniform functional trie representation and a constant \(C_k>0\) that supports the version, finger-navigation and subtree-copy interface below, with worst-case navigation time \(C_k\log_2(2+\Delta)\), no new permanent records from navigation, and both worst-case modification time and newly permanent record count at most \(C_k[1+\min\{D\log_2(2+\Delta),\log_2(2+N)\}]\) for every valid operation sequence?
cards.why: The question concerns whether persistent hierarchical data can exploit shallow or local changes while also protecting users against arbitrarily deep versions.

cards.title: Computing optimal generalized binary split trees
cards.formal: Is there a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, given rational successful-query probabilities \(p_1,\ldots,p_n\), constructs a generalized binary split tree minimizing \(\sum_{i=1}^n p_i(\operatorname{depth}_T(i)+1)\) over all correct such trees?
cards.why: This identifies the complexity of a basic comparison-search model whose formerly claimed polynomial algorithm was invalid.

cards.title: Fast insertion arbitrarily close to bucketized-cuckoo thresholds
cards.formal: For every bucket capacity b≥1 and rational 0<ε<c_b, is there a uniform randomized insertion algorithm that fills a two-choice cuckoo table to load c_b−ε in expected amortized time bounded by an explicit function of b,ε alone, with failure probability tending to zero as table size grows?
cards.why: This isolates the algorithmic gap between feasible hash-table load and efficient insertion.

cards.title: Rank error of MultiQueues under unrestricted insertion orders
cards.formal: Determine the worst-case per-deletion expected rank error R(q,T) of the sequential MultiQueue process, up to universal constant factors, for all q≥2 and T≥2.
cards.why: This asks how relaxed priority queues behave without favorable assumptions about the order of priorities.

cards.title: Constant-update working-set heaps on pointer machines
cards.formal:
Does there exist one deterministic online priority queue in the pointer-machine model below and an absolute constant \(C\ge1\) such that every legal sequence \(\sigma\) of \(M\ge1\) operations, starting with an empty queue, has total charged cost
\[
W_A(\sigma)\le C\left(M+\sum_{x\text{ extracted in }\sigma}\log_2\Gamma_\sigma(x)\right)?
\]
The operations are insert, find-min, decrease-key and extract-min, and
\[
\Gamma_\sigma(x)=1+\#\{\text{insertions strictly between the insertion and extraction of }x\}.
\]
Those later insertions count even if their items were already removed. All answers must be exact, and the same program and constant must work for every finite sequence and every ordered key domain.
cards.why: This is a basic test of whether temporal adaptivity and cheap priority changes can coexist without word-level machine tricks. A solution would clarify a model distinction in a fundamental graph-algorithm primitive. The small remaining factor makes it a sharper structural question than simply asking for a faster heap.

cards.title: Deterministic fully dynamic connectivity with polylogarithmic worst-case updates
cards.formal:
Does there exist a finite deterministic word-RAM program \(A\), with fixed positive integer constants \(C,c,d,a\), such that for every integer \(n\ge2\) it maintains an initially empty simple undirected graph on \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) under every finite valid online sequence of edge insertions, edge deletions and pairwise connectivity queries, with all the following guarantees?
\[\begin{aligned}
 \text{initialization time}&\le Cn^d,\\
 \text{total stored words at every time}&\le Cn^d,\\
 \text{time of each individual operation}&\le C(\log_2 n)^c.
\end{aligned}\]
Every query must return the exact connectivity bit. Initialization receives only \(n\); the word size is \(w=\lceil a\log_2 n\rceil\), and computation uses the machine conventions below. All constants and the same finite program are chosen before \(n\) or the operation sequence. Give a complete Lean proof of this existence proposition or its logical negation.
cards.why: Exact dynamic connectivity is a basic test of whether a graph data structure can guarantee uniformly low latency without randomness. The question separates efficient processing of a long sequence from a fast response after every individual change, and is relevant to graph algorithms that call connectivity as a subroutine.

cards.title: Fully dynamic near-optimal matching with polylogarithmic updates
cards.formal:
For every fixed rational \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) and every fixed integer \(a\ge1\), do there exist a uniform randomized fully dynamic algorithm \(A_{\varepsilon,a}\) and constants \(K,d,B\ge1\) with the following guarantees?

For every \(n\ge2\) and every valid oblivious sequence of \(T\le n^a\) edge insertions and deletions starting from the empty graph on \([n]\), the expected total initialization and update cost is at most
\[
K\left[n+T\bigl(\log_2(n+2)\bigr)^d\right].
\]
With probability at least \(1-n^{-3}\), after every update the algorithm maintains an explicit matching \(M\) in the current graph \(G\) such that
\[
|M|\ge\frac{\nu(G)}{1+\varepsilon},
\]
where \(\nu(G)\) is the maximum matching cardinality. The same constants apply to every \(n,T\) and sequence for the fixed \(\varepsilon,a\).
cards.why: A single insertion or deletion can change which edges should be used together in a large matching. The question asks whether a near-optimal explicit solution can be kept current at a cost that grows only polylogarithmically with graph size, combining approximation quality with efficient dynamic maintenance.

cards.title: Dynamic APSP with edge-linear updates
cards.formal:
For every fixed integer \(c\ge1\), do there exist integers \(a,d\ge1\) and \(B\ge c+3\), a real constant \(K\ge1\), and one uniform deterministic word-RAM data structure with the following guarantees for every \(n\ge2\) and supplied integer capacity \(n\le m\le n^2\)?

The data structure maintains a simple directed graph on the fixed vertex set \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with at most \(m\) live edges and edge weights in \(\{1,\ldots,n^c\}\), under online single-edge insertions, deletions and weight changes. It returns the exact current distance for every queried ordered vertex pair. Write \(\ell=\log_2(n+2)\). Preprocessing an arbitrary initial graph uses at most \(Kn^d\) instructions, and space is at most \(Kn^d\) words at every time. Every individual query uses at most \(K\ell^a\) instructions. After preprocessing, every finite valid sequence containing \(U\) updates and \(Q\) queries uses at most
\[
K\bigl(Um\ell^a+Q\ell^a\bigr)
\]
instructions in total. The constants and program may depend on \(c\), but not on \(n,m\), the initial graph or the operation sequence.
cards.why: This asks whether exact shortest-path information can be maintained at a cost reflecting the number of input edges, rather than all possible vertex pairs. It is a central dynamic-graph trade-off between update work, sparse structure, and immediate exact access to global information.

cards.title: Polylogarithmic worst-case updates for exact dynamic minimum spanning forests
cards.formal:
For every fixed pair of integers \(a,b\ge1\), does there exist a uniform randomized data structure that maintains the exact canonical minimum spanning forest of the graph below, with polynomial preprocessing and space and polylogarithmic worst-case time for each edge insertion or deletion? For every valid update sequence \(\sigma\) of length \(T\le n^a\) fixed independently of its randomness, require
\[\Pr_R\bigl[\widehat F_t=F(G_t)\text{ for every }0\le t\le T\bigr]\ge1-n^{-b}.\]
The event also requires every edge-change report to be valid as defined below. Here \(G_t\) is the graph after update \(t\), \(F(G_t)\) is its specified exact forest, and \(\widehat F_t\) is reconstructed from the reported edge changes. Each update must finish within its time bound on every execution, including executions on which the answer is wrong. The data structure receives no future updates in advance.
cards.why: A basic dynamic optimization problem with very small changes to its answer but potentially expensive global replacement searches. It tests whether amortized efficiency can be made reliable for every update.

cards.title: Polylogarithmic maintenance of the exact global minimum cut
cards.formal:
Does there exist a uniform randomized data structure maintaining the exact global minimum-cut value of a fully dynamic simple unweighted undirected graph with polylogarithmic expected amortized update time, polylogarithmic worst-case query time and polynomial space? Precisely, is there one algorithm \(A\) and fixed integers \(b\ge1,c\ge0\) such that, for every fixed integer confidence parameter \(a\ge1\), there is a constant \(C_a\ge1\) for which the following holds? For every \(n\ge2\), initialize on the empty graph on \([n]\). For every legal operation sequence \(\sigma\) fixed independently of the random bits, with \(U\) updates and \(Q\) queries and \(U+Q\le n^a\), require all of:
\[\text{space on every execution}\le C_a n^b\text{ words},\qquad \mathbb E[T_{\rm init}+T_{\rm updates}]\le C_a\bigl(n^b+U L^c\bigr),\]
\[\text{each query takes at most }C_aL^c\text{ steps on every execution},\qquad \Pr[\text{all }Q\text{ answers equal the current }\lambda(G)]\ge1-n^{-3},\]
where \(L=\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\) and the machine model and costs are defined below. The exponents \(b,c\) and program are independent of \(a,n,\sigma\) and all cut values; constants may depend on \(a\).
cards.why: A central exact dynamic graph problem asking whether a global measure of edge connectivity can be updated as efficiently as basic connectivity, across the full range of cut values.

cards.title: Near-linear incremental topological ordering
cards.formal:
Does there exist one uniform Las Vegas randomized word-RAM algorithm \(A\) that maintains a topological order of an initially empty directed graph on \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), under edge insertions promised to preserve acyclicity, with all the following guarantees? Order-comparison queries take \(O(1)\) worst-case time, space is \(O((n+m)(\log_2(n+2))^C)\) words for one fixed \(C\ge0\), and for every real \(\eta>0\) there is a constant \(K_\eta>0\) such that
\[
\mathbb E[\text{initialization and update instructions through any prefix}]
\le K_\eta(n+m)^{1+\eta}.
\]
Here \(m\) is the number of insertions in that prefix, and \(n\ge2\). The same algorithm must meet all exponents; \(q\) comparison queries add at most \(K_Qq\) instructions for one absolute constant \(K_Q\).
cards.why: Maintaining an actual vertex order remains a central gap between static graph processing and incremental graph maintenance, even as cycle detection itself has become almost linear.

cards.title: Polynomial-time query outside DynFO
cards.formal: Editorial uniform-initialization variant: is there an isomorphism-invariant polynomial-time Boolean query on some fixed finite relational vocabulary that is not maintainable by any first-order dynamic program with built-in order, addition and multiplication and first-order initialization from the empty input?
cards.why: An unconditional separation would establish a basic expressive limit of dynamic descriptive complexity.

cards.title: Worst-case dynamic Courcelle theorem at bounded treewidth
cards.formal: For every k and fixed CMSO₂ sentence φ, can its truth be maintained deterministically on graphs of treewidth at most k with f(k,φ) log^c(n+2) worst-case update time and O(1) truth queries?
cards.why: A worst-case dynamic Courcelle theorem would make logical tractability stable under every individual update.

cards.title: Worst-case polylogarithmic fully dynamic planarity testing
cards.formal: Is there a deterministic fully dynamic planarity structure with polylogarithmic worst-case edge-update time and constant-time planarity queries?
cards.why: This asks whether dynamic topological feasibility can avoid all occasional expensive updates.

cards.title: Dynamic spanning trees with polylogarithmic average stretch
cards.formal:
Is there a uniform randomized fully dynamic algorithm that maintains a spanning forest \(F_t\) of an unweighted simple graph \(G_t\) with polylogarithmic expected average stretch and sublinear expected amortized update time? Precisely, do there exist such an algorithm, constants \(C,a,c>0\), and a function \(u:\mathbb N_{\ge2}\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) with
\[\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{u(n)}n=0,\]
such that for every \(n\ge2\) and every finite oblivious sequence of \(T\) edge insertions and deletions starting from the empty \(n\)-vertex graph,
\[\mathbb E[\operatorname{avstr}_{F_t}(G_t)]\le C(\log_2(n+2))^c\quad(0\le t\le T),\]
and the expected total work for the updates is at most \(T u(n)\), after at most \(C n^a\) expected initialization work? The maintained object must always be an actual spanning forest using current graph edges.

For a connected graph, a spanning forest is a spanning tree. The componentwise convention below makes the target meaningful when a deletion disconnects the graph, as in the original dynamic low-stretch algorithm. This card chooses the first question in the workshop source, with the expectation and amortization conventions of that prior work; it does not also require resistance to adaptive updates.
cards.why: Low-stretch spanning trees replace a graph by a particularly simple subgraph while controlling average detours. They underpin graph optimization and linear-system algorithms. The question asks whether a polylogarithmic quality guarantee can survive repeated edge changes without spending a linear amount of work per update; it isolates the cost of requiring the approximation to remain a genuine subgraph.

cards.title: Polylogarithmic dynamic maximal matching against adaptive updates
cards.formal:
Does there exist a uniform randomized algorithm that explicitly maintains a maximal matching in a fully dynamic \(n\)-vertex simple graph against an adaptive adversary, with polylogarithmic expected amortized update time? More precisely, are there an algorithm and constants \(C,c>0\) such that, for every \(n\ge2\), every horizon \(T\ge1\), and every valid adaptive update strategy, the algorithm is always correct and its expected total update work is at most
\[C T(\log_2(n+2))^c,\]
after initialization in at most \(C n(\log_2(n+2))^c\) expected time? The graph starts empty and each update inserts or deletes one edge. The model and adversary are defined below. A deterministic algorithm is permitted as a special case.

This card selects the polylogarithmic question expressly included in the 2022 source. Its earlier sublinear-time question has since received positive answers; that weaker threshold is retained as dated progress rather than presented as open.
cards.why: Maximal matching is a basic dynamic graph primitive whose current answer can influence the next change to the graph. This problem asks whether the cost of responding to that feedback can be reduced to a polylogarithm. It would clarify a major difference between algorithms that assume an independently chosen update sequence and algorithms whose guarantees survive interaction.

cards.title: Logarithmic Las Vegas dynamic connectivity
cards.formal:
Do there exist a real constant \(K>0\), integers \(a\ge4\) and \(c\ge0\), and one uniform randomized online word-RAM data structure \(A\) with the following guarantees for every \(n\ge1\)?

Starting with the empty undirected simple graph on \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), it processes every finite valid operation sequence \(\sigma\), fixed independently of its randomness, consisting of edge insertions, edge deletions and connectivity queries. It is always correct, all operations terminate almost surely, and, writing \(u\) and \(q\) for the numbers of updates and queries and \(\lambda_n=\log_2(n+2)\),
\[
 \mathbb E[T_A(n,\sigma)]\le
 K\bigl(n\lambda_n^c+(u+q)\lambda_n\bigr).
\]
Every individual query uses at most \(K\lambda_n\) instructions on every execution. The structure uses at most \(K(n+m)\lambda_n^c\) words when the current graph has \(m\) edges, with workspace counted as specified below. Its word length is \(w=a\lceil\lambda_n\rceil\).
cards.why: Determine the logarithmic endpoint for a basic graph property under arbitrary edge insertions and deletions. It would close the remaining update-time gap to general information-access lower bounds under a precise, always-correct randomized guarantee.

cards.title: Fast constant-factor fully dynamic edit distance
cards.formal: Does there exist an absolute constant \(A\ge1\) and a randomized fully dynamic data structure that maintains two strings of length at most \(N\), after polynomial preprocessing and in polynomial space, under arbitrary single-character insertions, deletions and substitutions, with expected amortized update time \((\log(2+N))^{O(1)}\) and constant query time, returning \(D\) with \(\operatorname{ED}(X,Y)\le D\le A\operatorname{ED}(X,Y)\) with probability at least \(2/3\) at each specified query against an oblivious update sequence?
cards.why: This would make a fundamental sequence-distance estimate efficiently maintainable throughout an evolving input.

cards.title: Deterministic worst-case polylogarithmic dynamic 2-edge-connectivity
cards.formal: Does there exist a deterministic data structure for a simple undirected graph on a fixed vertex set \([n]\), with polynomial initialization and polynomial space, that supports edge insertion, edge deletion and pairwise two-edge-connectivity queries in \(O(\log^c(2+n))\) worst-case time each, for one absolute constant c?
cards.why: This asks whether resilience to one edge failure can be maintained without expensive occasional rebuilds.

cards.title: Polylogarithmic updates for the exact arboricity value
cards.formal: Can exact integral arboricity of a fully dynamic simple graph be maintained deterministically in polylogarithmic amortized update time with constant-time value queries?
cards.why: Value-only maintenance separates the intrinsic difficulty of arboricity from the cost of explicitly changing a forest decomposition.

cards.title: Logarithmic fully dynamic planar nearest neighbors
cards.formal: Does a uniform Las Vegas data structure maintain a finite set of planar points under insertions and deletions, answer exact Euclidean nearest-neighbor queries in \(O(\log(n+2))\) worst-case time, and support updates in expected amortized \(O(\log(n+2))\) time, using \(O((n+1)\log^c(n+2))\) space for some fixed constant \(c\)?
cards.why: A logarithmic fully dynamic structure would establish the natural two-dimensional counterpart of a basic ordered-search interface.

cards.title: Subquadratic exact fully dynamic weighted single-source distances
cards.formal: Do a constant \(\delta>0\) and a deterministic data structure exist that maintain exact distances from one fixed source in every fully dynamic undirected \(n\)-vertex graph with positive integer edge weights at most \(n^3\), using polynomial preprocessing and space, \(O(n^{2-\delta})\) worst-case update time and \(O(1)\) worst-case time per distance query in the word-RAM model below?
cards.why: Dynamic shortest paths asks how much computation can be reused as a network changes. Separating update cost, query cost, approximation and graph density is essential to deciding whether a data structure meaningfully improves on a static computation.

cards.title: Worst-case logarithmic dynamic planar convex hulls
cards.formal: Does there exist one uniform deterministic data structure and an absolute constant \(K\ge1\) that maintain a finite set \(P\subset\mathbb R^2\), initially empty, with the following guarantees on every finite valid online sequence? Each point insertion, point deletion and extreme-point query takes at most \(K\log_2(n+2)\) worst-case real-RAM steps, where \(n\) is the larger set size immediately before and after that operation. The stored representation uses at most \(K(1+|P|)\) cells. Given any \(u\in\mathbb R^2\setminus\{0\}\), an extreme-point query returns a point \(p\in P\) maximizing \(\langle u,p\rangle\), or an empty marker if \(P=\varnothing\).
cards.why: This asks whether optimal dynamic geometric query performance can be guaranteed for individual updates rather than only averaged over a sequence.

cards.title: DynProp maintenance of directed reachability
cards.formal: Can all-pairs directed reachability be maintained from the empty graph under individual edge insertions and deletions by a fixed finite program of quantifier-free updates to auxiliary relations of arbitrary fixed finite arity, allowing arbitrary initial auxiliary relations?
cards.why: This tests the expressive power of quantifier-free dynamic computation beyond known bounded-arity lower bounds.

cards.title: Polylogarithmic updates for bounded rank-width
cards.formal: Can a rank-decomposition of width at most C(k+1) be maintained in f(k) log^c(n+2) amortized update time under the promise that rank-width never exceeds k?
cards.why: This asks whether a structural graph parameter supports genuinely polylogarithmic dynamic maintenance.

cards.title: Optimal-query fully dynamic text indexing
cards.formal: Is there a deterministic fully dynamic index for a fixed-alphabet string with linear-word space, polylogarithmic amortized character edits and O(m+occ) worst-case pattern-reporting queries?
cards.why: This seeks an optimal reporting interface that survives arbitrary edits throughout a text.

cards.title: Dynamic edge coloring with sublinear additive slack
cards.formal:
Does there exist a uniform randomized fully dynamic edge-coloring algorithm and fixed constants \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), \(C\ge1\), and \(a,b\ge0\), such that for every \(n\ge2\), every fixed degree bound \(1\le\Delta\le n-1\), and every valid oblivious sequence of edge insertions and deletions, it explicitly maintains a proper coloring with at most
\[K(n,\Delta)=\Delta+\left\lceil C\Delta^{1-\gamma}(\log_2(n+2))^a\right\rceil\]
colors in expected amortized update time at most \(C(\log_2(n+2))^b\)? The algorithm must always return a valid coloring. The bound must hold uniformly in both \(n\) and \(\Delta\), with the same constants, not only at each fixed \(\Delta\).

This is the update-time question in the workshop report, with the polylogarithmic factors and probability/cost convention made explicit. The author's separate, weaker recourse-only question is context rather than the main target.
cards.why: The question asks whether a changing graph can stay close to the optimal edge-color bound while each update costs only a polylogarithm. Its central issue is the joint dependence on graph size and degree: bounds that are fast for fixed relative error can become slow when the allowed extra colors shrink by a power of the degree. A resolution would sharpen the resource tradeoff for dynamic conflict-free scheduling represented by edge coloring.

cards.title: DynFO maintenance of red-predecessor parity
cards.formal: Does there exist a DynFO program that maintains the Boolean query |\(\{y\in D:\exists x\in D (R(x)\land E(x,y))\}|\equiv 1\) mod 2 under arbitrary single-tuple insertions and deletions in a directed edge relation \(E\subseteq D^{2}\) and a red-vertex relation \(R\subseteq D\)? Use one fixed finite auxiliary relational vocabulary and fixed first-order update formulas for every finite domain D. All input and auxiliary relations are empty initially, and there are no built-in order or arithmetic relations. The program must be correct after every finite sequence of updates, with no bound on the length of that sequence.
cards.why: Would clarify whether first-order dynamic maintenance can express a basic combination of existential coverage and parity counting, beyond the already understood parity of a directly stored set.

cards.title: Deterministic \(\widetilde O(n^{5/2})\) worst-case dynamic APSP
cards.formal: Is there a deterministic fully dynamic exact all-pairs distance structure on a fixed universe of \(N\) vertex labels, for directed real-weighted graphs with no negative directed cycle, with polynomial initialization, \(O(N^2\log^c(2+N))\) space, \(O(N^{5/2}\log^c(2+N))\) worst-case time per vertex insertion or deletion, and O(1) time per distance query, for an absolute constant c?
cards.why: This isolates the cost of removing randomness from a central worst-case dynamic shortest-path bound.

cards.title: Fast dynamic vertex colouring against adaptive updates
cards.formal: Can a Las Vegas randomized fully dynamic structure maintain a proper (Δ+1)-coloring against adaptive updates in expected amortized polylogarithmic time with constant-time color queries?
cards.why: Adaptive robustness is a central obstacle to making very fast randomized dynamic colorings reliable in interactive use.

cards.title: Low-loss deterministic reduction from weighted to unweighted dynamic matching
cards.formal:
Is there a uniform deterministic black-box transformation that converts every explicit fully dynamic \(\alpha\)-approximate maximum-cardinality matching algorithm into a fully dynamic \(\alpha(1-1/q)\)-approximate maximum-weight matching algorithm on general graphs, for every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1]\) and integer \(q\ge2\), with only an accuracy-dependent polylogarithmic overhead in update time and with preservation of worst-case as well as amortized bounds?

The precise overhead and interfaces are specified below. The transformation must work at the original approximation ratio \(\alpha\); it may not demand a stronger unweighted algorithm with approximation approaching one as \(q\) grows. This card selects the deterministic, fully dynamic version of the source’s broader feature-preserving conversion question. Randomized and partially dynamic extensions are not part of this chosen statement.
cards.why: A low-loss conversion would transfer a broad range of dynamic matching improvements from counting matched edges to optimizing their weights. The central unresolved scope includes algorithms with fixed approximation ratios such as one half or two thirds, not only near-optimal algorithms. Preserving determinism and time guarantees would make the conversion useful across existing algorithmic tradeoffs without redesigning each algorithm.

cards.title: Fully dynamic linear programming with outliers
cards.formal: Can fully dynamic planar linear programming with at most k violated halfplanes be maintained with (k+1)^{O(1)} polylogarithmic amortized update time and near-linear-plus-polynomial-in-k space?
cards.why: This asks whether robust optimization can support arbitrary deletions without advance lifetime information.

cards.title: Logarithmic dynamic convex-hull line intersection queries
cards.formal: Can a dynamic planar point set support insertions and deletions in O(log(n+2)) amortized time and exact convex-hull line-section queries in O(log(n+2)) worst-case time, using O(n+1) space?
cards.why: The line-intersection interface asks for geometric information not covered by optimal extreme-point query bounds.

cards.title: Faster approximate dynamic distances on monotone grids
cards.formal: Can (1+ε)-approximate opposite-corner distances in a weighted directed square grid be supported with offline-known weight updates at polylogarithmic amortized update cost and square-root query cost?
cards.why: The proposed tradeoff connects dynamic geometric distances to faster approximate time-series alignment.

cards.title: Constant-factor edit-distance approximation in \(O(n\operatorname{polylog} n)\) time
cards.formal:
Do there exist absolute real constants \(C\geq1\), \(K>0\), \(d\geq0\), an integer word-size constant \(B\geq3\), and one uniform classical randomized algorithm \(A\) such that for every integer \(n\geq1\) and all explicitly given \(x,y\in\{0,1,\ldots,n^2+1\}^n\), every execution uses at most
\[Kn\bigl(\log_2(n+2)\bigr)^d\]
word-RAM instructions and its integer output \(D\) satisfies
\[\Pr\bigl[\operatorname{ED}(x,y)\leq D\leq C\operatorname{ED}(x,y)\bigr]\geq\frac23?\]
The constants and program are chosen once for all input lengths and all pairs. The distance is unit-cost Levenshtein distance; the probability is over the algorithm’s internal randomness on that fixed pair.
cards.why: This asks whether allowing one universal constant loss of alignment accuracy reduces worst-case sequence comparison to the cost of reading the input, apart from a fixed polylogarithmic overhead. The result would locate a basic computational boundary that remains beyond the known fast constant-factor algorithms. Even a large universal factor would resolve this existence question.

cards.title: Optimal approximation ratio for shortest common superstring
cards.formal:
Determine, with absolute error at most \(1/100\), the real number
\[
\rho_{\mathrm{SCS}}=\inf\mathcal R,\qquad
\mathcal R=\{r\ge1:r\text{ is an achievable approximation ratio}\}.
\]
A ratio is achievable if one uniform deterministic polynomial-bit-time algorithm outputs, on every instance \(I\), a common superstring \(w\) with \(|w|\le r\operatorname{OPT}(I)\).
The input alphabet and strings are explicit, and the algorithm may be any algorithm in the model below. This is the best possible approximation ratio for shortest common superstring, not the worst-case ratio of maximum-overlap greedy.
cards.why: A long-standing approximation threshold for a basic string-assembly problem with direct algorithmic genomics and compression motivation.

cards.title: Almost-linear-time \((1+\varepsilon)\)-approximation of edit distance
cards.formal:
For every fixed rational \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\), does there exist one uniform classical randomized algorithm \(A_\varepsilon\) which, on every pair of explicitly given strings \(x,y\) of total length \(n=|x|+|y|\geq2\), outputs an integer \(D\) such that
\[\Pr\bigl[\operatorname{ED}(x,y)\leq D\leq(1+\varepsilon)\operatorname{ED}(x,y)\bigr]\geq\frac23,\]
and has worst-case running time \(n^{1+o(1)}\) in the word-RAM model below? Here \(\operatorname{ED}\) is unit-cost Levenshtein distance, the probability is only over the algorithm’s independent random bits, and the time bound must hold on every execution. For each fixed accuracy, the same algorithm must satisfy every positive fixed exponent slack.
cards.why: Edit distance captures sequence alignment under insertions and deletions as well as replacements. The question asks whether every pair of long sequences can be compared with arbitrarily small fixed relative error while the worst-case time exponent approaches the input-reading exponent one. It would resolve a central joint accuracy–runtime frontier beyond both constant-factor approximation and a fixed saving over quadratic time.

cards.title: Worst-case sample complexity of trace reconstruction
cards.formal: For every fixed deletion probability \(\delta\in(0,1)\), determine the worst-case sample-complexity function \(N_\delta(n)\) up to multiplicative constant factors as \(n\to\infty\). This is the least number of independent deletion traces from which one estimator can reconstruct every unknown \(n\)-bit string exactly with probability at least \(2/3\). Computation is unrestricted, the original length and deletion probability are known, and constants may depend on \(\delta\).
cards.why: Determine the intrinsic amount of information needed to recover an arbitrary string when repeated observations lose the positions of deleted symbols. This separates the statistical cost of hidden alignment from the computational cost of processing the observations.

cards.title: Constant-factor approximation of the smallest grammar
cards.formal:
Do there exist absolute constants \(C\ge1\), \(K\ge1\), an integer \(d\ge1\), and one uniform deterministic algorithm \(A\) such that, for every \(n\ge1\) and explicitly supplied string \(s\in\{1,\ldots,n\}^n\), the algorithm outputs an acyclic grammar \(G\) generating exactly \(s\), with
\[
|G|\le C\,g^*(s),
\]
in at most \(K(L(s)+1)^d\) Turing-machine bit steps? Here \(|G|\) is the total number of terminal and nonterminal occurrences on all right-hand sides, \(g^*(s)\) is the minimum such size among grammars generating \(s\), and \(L(s)\) is the explicit binary input length.
cards.why: This is a fundamental compression-versus-optimization question: can an efficient procedure recover a representation within a fixed factor of the best hierarchical description? It also supplies a benchmark for compressed-data algorithms, whose costs often depend on grammar size rather than on the original string length.

cards.title: Optimal \(\ell_{1}\) distortion of binary edit distance
cards.formal: For each integer \(n\ge2\), let \(X_n=\{0,1\}^{n}\) and define \[D_{\mathrm{ED}}(n)=\inf\bigl\{D\in[1,\infty):\ \exists m\in\mathbb N_{\ge1},\ \exists f:X_n\to\mathbb R^m,\ \exists a>0,\ \forall x,y\in X_n,\ a\,\mathrm{ED}(x,y)\le\|f(x)-f(y)\|_1\le D a\,\mathrm{ED}(x,y)\bigr\}.\] Determine the asymptotic growth of \(D_{\mathrm{ED}}(n)\) up to universal multiplicative constants as \(n\to\infty\).
cards.why: Determining this distortion would explain how closely the geometry of binary sequence editing can be represented by sums of coordinate differences, closing a longstanding gap between metric embeddings and their obstructions.

cards.title: Breaking two for sum-of-pairs multiple sequence alignment
cards.formal: Does there exist a rational constant \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) and a uniform deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that returns a \((2-\varepsilon)\)-approximation for minimum sum-of-pairs alignment of any number of strings under an input metric substitution-and-gap cost?
cards.why: This is a principal approximation barrier for a basic bioinformatics optimization problem, requiring an improvement that survives as the number of sequences grows.

cards.title: Truly subquadratic \((1+\varepsilon)\)-approximation of edit distance
cards.formal:
For every fixed rational \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\), do there exist real constants \(\delta_\varepsilon\in(0,1)\), \(K_\varepsilon>0\) and one uniform classical randomized algorithm \(A_\varepsilon\) such that, for every integer \(n\geq1\) and every pair of length-\(n\) strings \(x,y\), every execution uses at most \(K_\varepsilon(n+2)^{2-\delta_\varepsilon}\) word-RAM instructions and its integer output \(D\) satisfies
\[\Pr\bigl[\operatorname{ED}(x,y)\leq D\leq(1+\varepsilon)\operatorname{ED}(x,y)\bigr]\geq\frac23?\]
The distance is unit-cost Levenshtein distance, the alphabet and computational model are specified below, and probability is over independent internal random bits for each fixed input pair.
cards.why: This asks whether any fixed tolerance for a relative alignment error permits a fixed polynomial saving from the quadratic time scale on arbitrary sequences. Exact edit distance has strong conditional hardness evidence, while fast coarse approximations already exist. The question isolates whether near-exact approximation can cross the fixed-exponent boundary for every desired fixed accuracy.

cards.title: Almost-linear constant-factor approximation of LCS
cards.formal:
Do there exist absolute real constants \(C\ge1\) and \(K>0\), an integer \(d\ge8\), a function \(h:\{2,3,\ldots\}\to[1,\infty)\) with
\[
 \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log h(n)}{\log n}=0,
\]
and one uniform classical randomized word-RAM algorithm \(A\) such that, for every pair of explicitly given strings \(x,y\) of total length \(n=|x|+|y|\ge2\) over the integer alphabet \(\{0,\ldots,n^2-1\}\), every execution of \(A\) uses at most \(Knh(n)\) instructions, outputs a valid common subsequence \(z\) of \(x,y\), and satisfies
\[
 \Pr\bigl[|z|\ge \operatorname{LCS}(x,y)/C\bigr]\ge\frac23?
\]
The machine has word length \(w=d\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\), and all input, initialization and output costs are charged as specified below.
cards.why: Determine whether a basic sequence-similarity measure admits a constant-quality witness in time close to reading the input, even when the alphabet grows. The combined approximation and time target separates the general problem from easy fixed-alphabet guarantees.

cards.title: Linear-space encoding from smallest string attractors
cards.formal:
Do there exist a constant \(C\ge1\) and two uniform deterministic computable functions \(E,D\) such that, for every \(n\ge1\) and every string \(T\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}^n\),
\[
D(E(T))=T
\quad\text{and}\quad
|E(T)|\le C\,\gamma(T)\,\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil?
\]
Here \(E(T)\) is a finite binary code, its length \(|E(T)|\) includes all metadata, and \(\gamma(T)\) is the minimum string-attractor size defined below. The decoder receives only the complete binary code. No time bound is imposed on encoding or decoding. Equivalently, the target is \(O(\gamma(T))\) words of \(\Theta(\log n)\) bits for a lossless representation.
cards.why: An attractor measures how a small set of positions witnesses all distinct substrings, independently of a particular compressor. If its size always controls description length to within a constant number of words, it supplies a general measure of how much information repetitive strings contain. A failure would expose a gap between substring coverage and lossless representability.

cards.title: Text-to-pattern Hamming distances below the square-root barrier
cards.formal:
Do there exist absolute constants \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)\), \(K>0\), an integer \(B\ge8\), and one uniform classical Las Vegas word-RAM algorithm \(A\) such that, for all integers \(n\ge2\), \(1\le m\le n\), every text \(T\in\{0,\ldots,n^2-1\}^{n}\) and pattern \(P\in\{0,\ldots,n^2-1\}^{m}\), it outputs every exact distance
\[
 h_i=|\{j\in\{0,\ldots,m-1\}:T[i+j]\ne P[j]\}|
 \quad (i=0,\ldots,n-m)
\]
and satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E[\operatorname{time}_A(T,P)]
 \le Knm^{1/2-\varepsilon}?
\]
The expectation is over internal randomness for each fixed input. The word length is \(w=B\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\), and correctness is required on every terminating execution.
cards.why: Computing exact mismatch counts at every alignment is a basic string-processing task with a long-standing square-root dependence on the pattern length. A fixed exponent saving would also advance closely related restricted arithmetic-counting computations.

cards.title: Almost-quadratic unweighted tree edit distance
cards.formal:
Is there one uniform deterministic algorithm \(A\), an integer word-size constant \(B\ge8\), a constant \(K>0\), and a function \(g:\{2,3,\ldots\}\to[1,\infty)\) satisfying
\[
 \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log g(n)}{\log n}=0,
\]
such that, for every two nonempty rooted ordered labelled trees with a total of \(n\ge2\) vertices, \(A\) outputs their exact unit-cost tree edit distance using at most
\[
 Kn^2g(n)
\]
word-RAM instructions in the worst case? Each vertex label is an integer in \(\{0,\ldots,n^2-1\}\), both trees are explicitly supplied, and the word length is \(B\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\).
cards.why: Tree edit distance compares hierarchical labelled data using local structural edits. An almost-quadratic exact algorithm would clarify how much ordered branching adds to the cost of ordinary string comparison and improve a basic structured dynamic-programming task.

cards.title: Linear-space LZ77 random access
cards.formal: Do there exist uniform deterministic preprocessing and query algorithms and absolute constants \(C,K>0\), integers \(a\ge1,b\ge2\), such that, for every string \(S\in[1..N]^N\) with \(N\ge1\), its greedy overlapping LZ77 parse with \(z\) phrases can be preprocessed in at most \(K(N+1)^a\) bit operations into a representation supporting every character query \(i\in[1..N]\) with exact answer \(S[i]\), worst-case query time at most \(C(1+\log_2 N)\), and at most \(Cz\) machine words in total at query time? A word has \(w=b\lceil\log_2(N+2)\rceil\) bits, and query time counts the word-RAM operations below.
cards.why: Random access is a basic interface for computation on compressed texts. Linear storage in the LZ77 phrase count would preserve the benefit of repetition while making individual characters accessible without expanding the text.

cards.title: Linear-time LZ77 pattern matching
cards.formal: For every fixed integer \(c\ge1\), do there exist constants \(K\ge1\), an integer \(B\ge c+8\), and one uniform deterministic algorithm \(A\) with the following property? Given any valid \(z\)-phrase LZ77 representation of a text \(T\) of length \(N\ge1\), and an explicit nonempty pattern \(P\) of length \(m\), with symbols in \(\{1,\ldots,(z+m)^c\}\), the algorithm decides whether \(P\) occurs contiguously in \(T\) using at most \(K(z+m)\) word-RAM instructions and \(K(z+m)\) working words. Self-referential copy phrases are allowed, the word size is \(w=B\lceil\log_2(N+m+2)\rceil\), and all preprocessing is included.
cards.why: This is a basic test of whether computation can follow the compressed input size rather than the size of the object it describes. Settling it would also clarify whether the representation gap between LZ77 and grammars creates an unavoidable algorithmic cost for a fundamental string operation.

cards.title: Linear-space k-mismatch indexing with fast queries
cards.formal:
For every fixed integer \(k\ge2\), do there exist constants \(C_k,K_k>0\), integers \(p_k\ge1\) and \(B_k\ge8\), and one uniform deterministic static indexing algorithm \(A_k\) with the following properties? For every \(n\ge2\) and text \(T\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}^n\), it constructs an index in at most \(K_kn^{p_k}\) word-RAM instructions using at most \(C_kn\) retained words. Every subsequently supplied pattern \(P\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}^m\), \(1\le m\le n\), has all its occurrences with at most \(k\) mismatches reported exactly in at most
\[
K_k\left(m+\bigl(\log_2(n+2)\bigr)^k
                  \log_2\log_2(n+2)+\mathrm{occ}\right)
\]
worst-case instructions. The index together with all temporary query work uses at most \(C_kn\) words. Here \(\mathrm{occ}\) is the number of reported positions and the word length is \(B_k\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\).
cards.why: Approximate text indexing serves many patterns against the same stored text. The question asks whether the fast fixed-error query interface can be kept in linear word space even when the alphabet grows, removing the storage overhead that can dominate large indexes.

cards.title: Space-query exponent curve of gapped string indexing
cards.formal:
Determine the dimensionless space exponent \(s_{\mathrm{gap}}(\delta)\) for every real \(\delta\in[0,1]\). For each such \(\delta\), let
\[
s_{\mathrm{gap}}(\delta)=\inf\{s\in[1,\infty):\ \forall\eta\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\ \exists\mathcal D,K,C_0,h,d\text{ satisfying the bounds below}\}.
\]
Here \(\mathcal D=(P,Q)\) is a uniform randomized static indexing scheme in the stated word-RAM model, \(K,C_0\ge1\) are constants, and \(h\ge1,d\ge8\) are integers. For every \(n\ge2\), every length-\(n\) text, and every valid query, preprocessing takes at most \(C_0(n+2)^h\) steps; the index together with query workspace uses at most \(Kn^{s+\eta}\) words; and the query takes at most
\[
K\bigl(m_1+m_2+n^{\delta+\eta}(1+\mathrm{occ})\bigr)
\]
steps. Each bound holds for every outcome of the random choices. For each fixed text and query, the complete output is correct with probability at least \(2/3\), over preprocessing and query randomness. The chosen programs and constants may depend on \(\delta,s,\eta\), but not on the text, its length, or a query. The requested answer is a real-valued function \(g\) on \([0,1]\), certified to satisfy \(\lvert g(\delta)-s_{\mathrm{gap}}(\delta)\rvert\le1/100\) at every point.
cards.why: An optimal storage-versus-query curve would identify the limits of reusing a preprocessed text for paired-pattern searches with query-dependent distance constraints. This is a basic indexing primitive motivated by motif searches and co-occurrence analysis.

cards.title: Fully functional suffix trees in BWT-run-linear total space
cards.formal:
Do there exist constants \(C,K>0\), integers \(c\ge0\), \(p\ge1\), \(B\ge8\), and one uniform deterministic static data structure such that, for every \(n\ge2\) and every explicitly given text
\[
T\in\{0,1\}^{n-1}\#,
\]
it constructs a representation of the compact suffix tree in at most \(Kn^p\) word-RAM instructions, retains at most \(Cr\) words, and answers each operation specified below exactly in at most
\[
K\bigl(\log_2(n+2)\bigr)^c
\]
worst-case instructions, while the retained representation together with all temporary query work uses at most \(Cr\) words? Here \(r\) is the number of runs in the Burrows–Wheeler transform of \(T\), including its unique sentinel, and the word length is \(B\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\). All constants and programs are chosen once, independently of the text and its length.
cards.why: A complete navigation index lets algorithms work directly on highly repetitive text without retaining an expanded tree. The question is whether this general interface, including direct suffix and text access, can fit at the same run-count scale as more specialized search indexes.

cards.title: Grammar random access in \(O(g\log g)\) bits
cards.formal: Do there exist absolute constants \(K\ge1\), integers \(d\ge1\) and \(B\ge d+8\), and uniform deterministic construction and query algorithms with the following guarantee? For every binary straight-line program \(G\) with \(g\ge1\) reachable rules generating a binary string \(T\) of length \(N\), construction from \(G\) takes at most \(K(g+1)^d\) word-RAM instructions and produces a representation occupying at most \(Kg\log_2(g+2)\) persistent bits. Given any \(1\le i\le N\), a query returns \(T[i]\) in at most \(K\log_2(N+2)\) instructions. The word size is \(w=B\lceil\log_2(N+g+2)\rceil\); the space bound includes the retained grammar, every auxiliary index and final-word padding.
cards.why: Random access is the simplest useful operation on a compressed string. Resolving this target would determine whether the extra address-length information is an inherent price of efficient access or an artifact of current representations, and would make the distinction between compressed bits and machine words precise.

cards.title: Polyloglogarithmic suffix-array access in compact space
cards.formal:
Do there exist two deterministic finite word-RAM programs \(P,Q\), integers \(a,c\ge1\) and \(d\ge8\), and constants \(C,K>0\), such that the following holds simultaneously for every integer \(n\ge2\), every binary string \(T\in\{0,1\}^{n}\), and every rank \(i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\)?
The preprocessing program \(P\), given \(n\) and the packed bits of \(T\), constructs a static index \(I_T\) in at most \(K(n+2)^a\) operations. Given only \(n,i,I_T\), the query program \(Q\) returns the exact value \(\operatorname{SA}_T[i]\) in at most
\[
K\bigl(1+\log_2\log_2(n+2)\bigr)^c
\]
operations. At every point of a query, the index and all query working storage together use at most \(Cn\) bits in the model below. The same programs and constants must work for every input length; all bounds are worst-case.
cards.why: A text contains enough information to determine the full suffix order, but explicitly storing every starting position costs an extra logarithmic factor in bits. This question asks whether that factor can be removed while each rank-to-position lookup takes only a fixed polynomial in the double logarithm of the text length.

cards.title: Preprocessing exponent of binary jumbled indexing
cards.formal:
Determine, to absolute error at most \(1/100\), the real number
\[
 \alpha_{\mathrm{BJ}}=inf\{a\in[1,\infty):
 \text{for every rational }\eta>0\text{ there is an admissible index with}
 \text{ preprocessing time }O(n^{a+\eta})\}.
\]
An admissible index is a uniform deterministic static index for every binary string of length \(n\ge2\), using \(O(n)\) stored words and answering each exact histogram-existence query in \(O(1)\) worst-case time. The input, query, machine model and quantifiers are specified below.
cards.why: Binary histogram queries isolate a basic form of order-insensitive search while keeping queries and the stored index small. Determining the construction exponent would clarify the real cost of preparing all such queries and its connection to structured convolution.

cards.title: General-alphabet Hamming oracles with optimal preprocessing
cards.formal: Is there a uniform deterministic data structure which, for every pair of strings of lengths \(n,m\ge1\) and every integer \(1\le x\le\min(n,m)\), uses \(\widetilde O(nm/x)\) preprocessing time and stored words and answers exact substring Hamming-distance queries in \(O(x)\) worst-case time?
cards.why: This isolates the cost of reusable exact similarity queries and tests whether large alphabets create an inherent preprocessing penalty.

cards.title: Certifying Karp–Rabin fingerprints
cards.formal:
For every fixed integer \(c\ge2\), do there exist a constant \(K\ge1\) and one uniform randomized algorithm \(A\) with this guarantee? Its input is \(n\ge2\), an alphabet size \(2\le\sigma\le n^c\), a string \(T\in\{0,\ldots,\sigma-1\}^n\) and a supplied prime \(2\le p\le n^c\). Every execution takes at most \(Kn\log_2(n+2)\) word-RAM instructions. It outputs CERTIFIED or REJECT for the single fingerprint
\[
h_p(T[i..i+\ell-1])=\sum_{a=0}^{\ell-1}T[i+a]\sigma^a\pmod p.
\]
If any two unequal equal-length substrings collide, every execution must output REJECT. If no such pair exists, the probability of CERTIFIED must be at least \(2/3\). All lengths \(1\le\ell\le n\) are included; the supplied base and prime remain fixed.
cards.why: Efficient certification could turn a widely used probabilistic string primitive into a reliable one while preserving a chosen fingerprint representation.

cards.title: Input-optimal construction of compact inverse suffix arrays
cards.formal: Do there exist a uniform deterministic construction algorithm \(B\), a uniform deterministic query algorithm \(A\), and constants \(C_B,C_S,C_A>0\), such that for every \(n\ge2\) and every packed binary text \(T\in\{0,1\}^n\), \(B\) constructs a static index in at most \(C_B(1+n/\log_2(n+2))\) worst-case word-RAM steps, the retained index and query workspace together occupy at most \(C_S n\) bits, and \(A\) answers every query \(i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\) with \(\operatorname{ISA}_T[i]\) in at most \(C_A\) worst-case steps? All three constants and the programs are independent of \(n,T,i\). Both algorithms use the common word model specified below.
cards.why: An inverse suffix-array query identifies the lexicographic position of a suffix without storing all ranks explicitly. A compact index with constant query time would be especially useful if its construction were as fast as processing the packed representation. The remaining construction gap tests a substantive barrier shared with other packed-string tasks.

cards.title: Optimal top-k document retrieval in compact space
cards.formal:
Do there exist one uniform deterministic static indexing algorithm, one uniform deterministic query algorithm, absolute constants \(C,K>0\), and fixed integers \(p\ge1\), \(B\ge8\), with the following guarantees? For every ordered collection of \(d\ge1\) nonempty strings of total length \(n\ge2\) over an alphabet \(\{0,\ldots,\sigma-1\}\), where \(2\le\sigma\le n\), preprocessing takes at most \(K(n+1)^p\) word-RAM instructions and produces an index occupying at most
\[
 Cn\lceil\log_2\sigma\rceil\ \text{bits}.
\]
For every packed nonempty pattern \(P\) of length \(1\le m\le n\) and every \(1\le k\le d\), the index returns the top-\(k\) documents by occurrence frequency, in the specified order, within
\[
 K\left(1+\frac{m}{\log_\sigma n}+k\right)
 \quad\text{word-RAM instructions in the worst case}?
\]
The word length is \(w=B\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\). All constants and programs must be independent of the collection and all query parameters.
cards.why: An index should rank documents containing an arbitrary substring without storing a word-sized record for every text position. Simultaneously attaining the packed-input query bound and space proportional to the text is a central time–space question for exact retrieval on string collections.

cards.title: Polynomial-time construction of minimum-density DNA minimizers
cards.formal:
Do there exist a constant \(K>0\), an integer \(C\ge1\), and one uniform deterministic algorithm \(A\) such that, for every pair of integers \(k,w\ge2\), it outputs a total order \(\rho\) of all \(4^k\) DNA strings of length \(k\) satisfying
\[
d_{k,w}(\rho)=\min_{\pi}d_{k,w}(\pi)
\]
in at most \(K(4^k+w)^C\) bit-computation steps? The minimum ranges over all total orders of those same strings, and \(d_{k,w}\) is the density defined below. The input encodes \(k\) in binary and \(w\) in unary; the output explicitly lists the \(4^k\) strings from lowest to highest rank. The constants and algorithm are independent of \(k,w\).
cards.why: Minimizers choose seeds used throughout sequence processing, and lower density reduces the number retained under the same window guarantee. The question asks whether a provably best order can be generated efficiently relative to its explicit representation, separating exact optimization from practical low-density designs.

cards.title: A fixed exponent improvement for elastic-degenerate string intersection
cards.formal:
Do there exist constants \(0<\varepsilon<1\), \(K>0\), an integer \(d\ge0\), an integer \(B\ge8\), and one uniform classical randomized word-RAM algorithm \(A\) such that, on every pair of explicitly represented elastic-degenerate strings \(E_1,E_2\) defined below, every execution takes at most
\[
K\left(N_1+N_2+n_2N_1^{\omega-1-\varepsilon}
                 +n_1N_2^{\omega-1-\varepsilon}\right)
\bigl(\log_2(N_1+N_2+2)\bigr)^d
\]
instructions and outputs the correct answer to
\[
\mathcal L(E_1)\cap\mathcal L(E_2)\ne\varnothing
\]
with probability at least \(2/3\)? Here \(n_i\) is the number of segments, \(N_i\) their total number of explicitly stored characters, and \(\omega\) is the rational algebraic matrix-multiplication exponent specified below. The word length is \(B\lceil\log_2(N_1+N_2+2)\rceil\). All constants, including the positive exponent saving, are chosen once for the algorithm.
cards.why: A sequence of alternative fragments represents many possible full strings without listing them all.
