Faster exact intersection would improve a basic comparison operation on these representations, including simplified pangenomes, while clarifying the role of segment count versus explicitly stored length.

area: Algorithmic game theory, mechanism design and fair division
label: Game theory, social choice and fair division

cards.title: Existence of complete EFX allocations for additive valuations
cards.formal: For all integers \(n\ge4\) and \(m\ge0\), and every matrix \((v_{ig})_{i\in[n],g\in[m]}\) of nonnegative real values, does there exist a complete allocation \((A_1,\ldots,A_n)\) such that \(\sum_{h\in A_i}v_{ih}\ge\sum_{h\in A_j\setminus\{g\}}v_{ih}\) for every \(i,j\in[n]\) and every \(g\in A_j\) satisfying \(v_{ig}>0\)?
cards.why: Asks whether an indivisible allocation can always control every agent’s envy after the removal of any positively valued good, while distributing all goods. It tests a stronger fairness guarantee than EF1 even before imposing computational efficiency.

cards.title: Constant-factor universally truthful auctions for submodular bidders
cards.formal:
Does there exist a universal constant \(C\ge1\) and one uniform randomized combinatorial-auction mechanism with polynomial worst-case communication which is universally truthful and, for every number \(n\ge1\) of bidders, number \(m\ge1\) of items, public precision bound \(B\ge1\), and admissible normalized monotone submodular valuation profile \(v\), satisfies
\[\mathbb E_r\!\left[\sum_{i=1}^n v_i(S_i(v;r))\right]
\ \ge\ \frac{\operatorname{OPT}(v)}{C}?\]
The constant is independent of \(n,m,B\). The expectation is over report-independent mechanism randomness. For each fixed random realization the allocation and payment rule must satisfy the dominant-strategy inequality below. Communication is measured in bits, with unlimited terminating local computation and arbitrary interactive messages, including demand queries.
cards.why: Determine whether exact truthful incentives inherently cause an unbounded loss of allocative efficiency, even when arbitrary compact communication and unlimited local optimization are available.

cards.title: Constant-factor approximation for Santa Claus
cards.formal:
Does there exist a universal constant \(C\ge1\), one uniform randomized algorithm \(A\), and constants \(K>0\), \(d\in\mathbb N\), such that for every explicit nonnegative rational additive valuation matrix \(I=(v_{ij})\) of bit length \(L\), the algorithm always outputs a feasible allocation within \(K(L+1)^d\) steps and
\[\Pr\!\left[\min_{i\in[n]}\sum_{j:\,A(I)(j)=i}v_{ij}
\ \ge\ \frac{\operatorname{OPT}(I)}{C}\right]\ge\frac23?\]
The probability is over the algorithm’s internal fair random bits and concerns one allocation serving all agents simultaneously. The constants and program must work for every number of agents and items and every permitted valuation matrix. The optimum is the largest achievable minimum agent value under the same indivisibility constraints.
cards.why: The central unresolved max-min allocation question: can all agents be protected to within a constant factor when indivisible resources have arbitrary heterogeneous additive values?

cards.title: Randomized truthful unrelated-machine scheduling
cards.formal:
Determine, up to universal constant factors as the integer number of machines \(m\to\infty\), the optimal worst-case expected-makespan ratio \(R(m)\) of truthful-in-expectation mechanisms for unrelated-machine scheduling. For each \(m\ge2\), the mechanism must handle every finite job count \(n\ge1\) and every matrix of finite nonnegative real processing times. It may use payments and arbitrary correlated random assignments, with no computational or communication restriction.
\[R(m)=\inf_{M\in\mathcal M_m}\ \sup_{\substack{n\ge1,\ t\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{m\times n}\\\operatorname{OPT}(t)>0}}
\frac{\mathbb E[C(M_{m,n}(t),t)]}{\operatorname{OPT}(t)}.\]
Here \(\mathcal M_m\) consists of the families satisfying the incentive and zero-optimum conditions below. The question includes deciding whether \(R(m)=\Theta(1)\), but a negative answer to that special possibility alone does not determine the requested asymptotic order.
cards.why: Quantifies how much load-balancing efficiency must be lost solely to multidimensional private costs when randomization and unrestricted payments are available. Matching asymptotic bounds would show whether expected-utility incentives can overcome the linear loss now known for deterministic truthful scheduling.

cards.title: Constant-factor truthful subadditive combinatorial auctions
cards.formal: Is there a polynomial-time, polynomial-demand-query truthful-in-expectation mechanism with a universal constant welfare approximation for arbitrary subadditive bidders?
cards.why: This targets the welfare attainable from strategic bidders with broad complement-free preferences.

cards.title: Black-box conversion to dominant-strategy truthfulness without expected-welfare loss
cards.formal: For the finite rational single-parameter model below, is there a polynomial-query black-box transformation to dominant-strategy truthfulness in expectation that loses no expected welfare?
cards.why: This asks whether algorithmic welfare can be retained when incentives are strengthened beyond Bayesian truthfulness.

cards.title: Universal maximin-share approximation for additive goods
cards.formal: Determine the universal maximin-share approximation constant for additive indivisible goods, \[\alpha_{\mathrm{MMS}}=\sup\bigl\{\alpha\in[0,1]:\ \forall n\ge1\ \forall m\ge0\ \forall v\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{n\times m}\ \exists(A_1,\ldots,A_n)\in\Pi_n([m])\ \forall i\in[n],\ v_i(A_i)\ge\alpha\,\mu_i(v)\bigr\}.\] Here \(n,m\) range over integers, \(v_i(S)=\sum_{g\in S}v_{ig}\), and \(\mu_i(v)=\max_{(P_1,\ldots,P_n)\in\Pi_n([m])}\min_{j\in[n]}v_i(P_j)\). The benchmark asks for this one dimensionless constant with absolute error at most \(1/100\), together with a complete Lean-checked proof of the error bound.
cards.why: Maximin share gives each agent a fairness benchmark determined by their own values, independent of how the other agents evaluate the goods. These personal guarantees can conflict when objects are indivisible. The universal constant measures the unavoidable loss from satisfying all agents simultaneously, separating a limitation of fairness itself from a limitation of available algorithms. It is a central quantitative threshold for additive fair division, with significance across instances and arbitrary numbers of participants.

cards.title: Polynomial query complexity of exact envy-free cake cutting
cards.formal:
Do there exist absolute integers \(C,d\ge1\) and one uniform deterministic Robertson–Webb protocol which, for every integer \(n\ge1\) and every profile of \(n\) nonatomic additive cake valuations, makes at most \(Cn^d\) queries and produces a partition \((A_1,\ldots,A_n)\) of the entire cake satisfying
\[
 \mu_i(A_i)\ge\mu_i(A_j)\qquad\text{for every }1\le i,j\le n?
\]
Every allocated piece may be a finite union of intervals. The allocation must be complete and exactly envy-free on every profile and for every valid choice of cut-query responses.
cards.why: The question asks how much preference information is necessary to divide a continuous resource exactly without anyone preferring another person’s share. A polynomial query bound would separate the information needed for fairness from the enormous bounds in existing general protocols.

cards.title: Constant-factor welfare from posted item prices
cards.formal: Is there a universal α>0 such that every independent prior over subadditive buyers admits fixed anonymous item prices achieving expected welfare at least α E[OPT] for every fixed arrival permutation?
cards.why: This asks whether a simple posted-price interface can match the welfare power of richer allocation mechanisms.

cards.title: Constant price of stability for undirected network design
cards.formal: Is the price of stability of undirected equal-cost-sharing network design games bounded by a universal constant?
cards.why: The price of stability asks how much inefficiency is unavoidable even in the best stable outcome.

cards.title: Pure positional Nash equilibria in reachability games
cards.formal:
Does every finite deterministic turn-based multiplayer game with a designated initial vertex and a reachability objective for each player admit a pure positional Nash equilibrium?

The equilibrium is evaluated from that one initial vertex. A unilateral deviating strategy may depend on the complete finite history, even though every strategy in the proposed equilibrium must depend only on the current vertex.
cards.why: A positional strategy stores no history and is directly implementable as one choice per vertex. The question asks whether all players can always make mutually stable choices of this form when their goals are to reach target sets, despite the extra power available to a deviating player who remembers the past.

cards.title: EF1 existence for arbitrary mixed-item utilities
cards.formal: For every integer \(n\ge 3\), every finite item set M and every profile of utility functions \(u_{i}:2^{M}\to \mathbb{R}\) with \(u_{i}(\varnothing )=0\), does there exist a complete allocation \(A=(A_{1},\ldots ,A_{n})\) such that for every ordered pair of agents i,j there is a set \(X\subseteq A_{i}\cup A_{j}\) with |\(X|\le 1\) satisfying \(u_{i}(A_{i}\setminus X)\ge u_{i}(A_{j}\setminus X)\)?
cards.why: Tests whether one-item envy relief remains possible when item values have unrestricted interactions and may change sign across bundles. A positive answer would extend a basic fairness guarantee far beyond additive goods and chores; a negative answer would identify a limit of that guarantee itself.

cards.title: EF1 and Pareto optimality for additive mixed items
cards.formal: Does every finite instance of indivisible mixed-item allocation with \(n\ge3\) agents and arbitrary real additive utilities admit a complete allocation that is both envy-free up to one item (EF1) and Pareto optimal (PO)? The item removed to eliminate an agent’s envy may come from the envied bundle or from the envious agent’s own bundle, with at most one item removed in total.
cards.why: Fairness and efficiency can conflict when an indivisible item benefits one participant and burdens another. This question asks whether one standard minimal relaxation of envy is always compatible with the absence of a Pareto improvement. Resolving it would determine whether a central fairness–efficiency guarantee survives unrestricted mixed valuations beyond the now-understood pure-goods and pure-chores existence settings.

cards.title: Polynomial-time EF1 and Pareto-optimal goods allocation
cards.formal:
Is there a uniform deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, for every explicitly given instance of indivisible goods with nonnegative additive valuations, outputs an allocation that is both envy-free up to one good (EF1) and Pareto optimal (PO)?

Precisely, do there exist one algorithm \(A\) and integers \(C,c\ge1\) such that, for every \(n\ge1\), \(m\ge0\), and matrix
\[
(v_{ig})_{i\in[n],\,g\in[m]}\in\mathbb Q_{\ge0}^{n\times m},
\]
\(A\) outputs a complete integral allocation satisfying the two conditions below in at most \(C(L+1)^c\) bit steps, where \(L\) is the full binary input length? The same program, constant and exponent must work for every number of agents and goods.
cards.why: Fairness and efficiency can each be obtained quickly, and an allocation satisfying both always exists. The unresolved computational question asks whether the two can be reconciled without time proportional to numerical value magnitudes or an exponent growing with the number of participants. It is a basic boundary between existence and efficient construction in discrete fair division.

cards.title: Optimal universal approximation factor for EFX
cards.formal:
Determine the universal additive-goods EFX approximation constant
\[\alpha_* = \sup\{\alpha\in[0,1]:\ \forall n\ge1\ \forall m\ge0\ \forall v\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{n\times m}\ \exists A\in\mathcal A_{n,m},\ A\text{ is }\alpha\text{-EFX for }v\}.\]
Here \(n,m\) are integers, \(\mathcal A_{n,m}\) is the set of complete allocations of \(m\) goods to \(n\) agents, and \(\alpha\)-EFX uses the positive-good convention defined below. The requested benchmark precision is absolute error at most \(1/100\): supply a real number \(a\) and prove \(|a-\alpha_*|\le1/100\). This is an existence constant with unrestricted allocation computation, not a polynomial-time approximation threshold.
cards.why: This constant measures how much of the demanding EFX fairness comparison can always be guaranteed when all indivisible goods must be assigned. It gives a quantitative target even if exact EFX existence is unresolved. Its scope is every number of agents and every additive valuation profile, so improvements for special structures do not alone determine the universal guarantee.

cards.title: Polynomial-time approximation of EFX
cards.formal: Determine \(\alpha _{\mathrm{alg}} = \sup\){\(\alpha \in [0,1]\) : there is a deterministic algorithm that, on every finite instance of nonnegative rational additive goods, returns a complete \(\alpha -\mathrm{EFX}\) allocation in time polynomial in the binary input length}. The number of agents is unbounded and part of the input.
cards.why: Separates the efficiently attainable fairness guarantee from the purely existential EFX frontier.

cards.title: Multiplicative MMS guarantee for chores
cards.formal: Determine the smallest real \(\alpha \ge 1\) such that, for every finite instance of nonnegative additive chores with any number of agents, there is a complete allocation \((A_{1},\ldots ,A_{n})\) satisfying \(c_{i}(A_{i})\le \alpha \mu _{i}\) for every agent i, where \(\mu _{i}\) is that agent’s minimax share. Denote this universal factor by \(\alpha\)*.
cards.why: Seeks the intrinsic loss required for fair allocation of indivisible burdens.

cards.title: Polynomial-time mixed equilibria in coordination polymatrix games
cards.formal: Is there a uniform deterministic algorithm that, for every finite rational coordination-only polymatrix game, outputs an exact mixed Nash equilibrium in time polynomial in the complete binary input length?
cards.why: Locate the tractability boundary for exact mixed equilibrium when every pairwise interaction has common payoffs, distinguishing the complexity of network coordination from general games and from pure local-search equilibria.

cards.title: Existence of pairwise maximin-share allocations
cards.formal:
Does every finite instance of indivisible goods and nonnegative additive valuations admit a complete pairwise maximin-share allocation? Precisely, for all integers \(n\ge1\), \(m\ge0\), and every matrix \(v\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{n\times m}\), is there a partition \((A_1,\ldots,A_n)\) of the goods such that
\[
\forall i,j\in[n],\ i\ne j:\quad
v_i(A_i)\ge\mu_i(A_i\cup A_j,2),
\]
with the two-part maximin value \(\mu_i\) defined below? This preserves the exact existence question from Open Problem 8 of the 2022 survey. It is a historical question now answered negatively; no approximation or epistemic variant is substituted.
cards.why: The question asked whether a demanding pairwise fairness guarantee could always be achieved when resources cannot be divided. It connected two-person maximin guarantees with fairness across a larger society and with stronger versus weaker envy conditions. The negative resolution establishes a limitation of this exact guarantee even for three agents and strictly positive additive values.

cards.title: Nash equilibria in concurrent terminal-reward games
cards.formal: Does every finite two-player concurrent game with nonnegative terminal rewards admit an exact Nash equilibrium in randomized strategies that depend on the history of visited states? Play may continue forever, in which case both players receive zero. Existence is required from every specified initial state; strategies may use unbounded memory.
cards.why: Tests whether nonnegative eventual rewards suffice for exact strategic stability in the simplest concurrent infinite-duration setting. It separates the existence of stable behavior from restrictions on memory, computation or approximate incentives.

cards.title: Randomized metric distortion in social choice
cards.formal: Determine the infimum D* of the universal worst-case metric distortion achievable by any randomized ordinal voting rule, when the rule sees every voter’s full ranking and minimizes expected total distance to voters. The infimum ranges over all rules for all finite positive numbers of voters and candidates, with the model and zero-cost convention below.
cards.why: A defining limit on how much welfare can be recovered from ordinal preferences.

cards.title: Polynomial-time EFX for three additive agents
cards.formal: Do there exist a deterministic Turing machine A and constants \(C,k\ge 1\) such that, for every finite set of goods and every three nonnegative rational additive valuations, A returns a complete EFX allocation in at most \(C(N+1)^{k}\) steps, where N is the binary input length and EFX has the all-goods convention below?
cards.why: The smallest unresolved computational case for exact EFX after existence for three agents was established.

cards.title: Bounded protocols for connected envy-free proportional cake cutting
cards.formal: For every fixed integer \(n\ge 4\), does there exist a deterministic Robertson–Webb protocol \(\mathrm{P}_{n}\) and a finite integer \(B_{n}\) such that, for every profile of n nonatomic additive cake valuations and all valid query answers, \(\mathrm{P}_{n}\) uses at most \(B_{n}\) queries and returns disjoint connected bundles \(A_{1},\ldots ,A_{n}\) satisfying \(\mu _{i}(A_{i})\ge \mu _{i}(A_{j})\) for all i,j and \(\mu _{i}(A_{i})\ge 1/n\) for all i, while permitting unallocated cake?
cards.why: Asks whether discarded cake permits exact fairness together with geometric simplicity in finite interaction.

cards.title: Polynomial-time stable matching in unimodular hypergraphs
cards.formal: Is there one deterministic algorithm and constants \(C>0\), \(k\ge1\) as below that, for every explicitly given finite hypergraph with totally unimodular incidence matrix and strict vertex preferences, returns a stable matching in at most \(C(L+1)^k\) steps, where \(L\) is the full input bit length?
cards.why: Tests whether a strong integrality promise can turn guaranteed coalition stability into an efficient algorithm. It extends the computational perspective of classical stable matching while keeping the target independent of optimization over stable outcomes.

cards.title: Optimal truthful pricing from one sample
cards.formal: Determine the best prior-independent expected revenue ratio ρ_MHR attainable by a randomized posted price based on one independent sample, for the continuous MHR class specified below.
cards.why: This measures the value of a single observation in a basic truthful pricing problem.

cards.title: Optimal randomized truthful two-facility location
cards.formal: Determine the optimal worst-case expected social-cost approximation ratio of truthful-in-expectation two-facility mechanisms on the real line without payments.
cards.why: The sharp ratio would quantify the efficiency cost of truthful location reporting for multiple public facilities.

cards.title: Optimal truthful approximation for multi-hospital kidney exchange
cards.formal: Determine the optimal worst-case expected approximation ratio for truthful two-way kidney-exchange mechanisms with arbitrarily many hospitals allowed to hide vertices.
cards.why: The ratio quantifies the welfare cost of strategic participation by institutions in exchange networks.

cards.title: Sharp selfishness threshold for manipulation-resistant tournaments
cards.formal: For every n≥1, is there a monotone Condorcet-consistent randomized tournament rule satisfying 2-NM₁?
cards.why: A sharp incentive threshold would identify how much internal sacrifice is needed to prevent collusion in tournament selection.

cards.title: Matrix multiplication exponent
cards.formal: Determine, with the absolute \(1/100\) acceptance precision below, the matrix multiplication exponent \(\omega=\inf\{\tau\in\mathbb R:\exists C>0\ \forall n\in\mathbb N,\ n\ge2\Rightarrow s(n)\le Cn^\tau\}\). Here s(n) is the minimum number of arithmetic gates in a circuit computing all entries of the product of two arbitrary n by n complex matrices exactly, in the model below.
cards.why: This exponent measures the asymptotic arithmetic cost of a fundamental operation and governs many other algebraic and graph algorithms. Determining its value would locate the limit of savings from shared computation.

cards.title: Bit complexity of integer multiplication
cards.formal: Determine, up to constant factors as \(n\to \infty\), the optimal worst-case running time for exactly multiplying two n-bit nonnegative binary integers by one uniform deterministic multitape Turing machine. The target is an attainable asymptotic upper bound with a matching lower bound for every correct machine in this model.
cards.why: One of the most basic unresolved limits of exact computation, affecting fast arithmetic throughout algorithms.

cards.title: Derandomizing polynomial identity testing
cards.formal: Is polynomial identity testing for explicitly represented arithmetic circuits over the integers in deterministic polynomial time? More precisely, do a deterministic multitape Turing machine \(A\), a real constant \(C>0\) and an integer \(k\ge1\) exist such that, on every valid circuit encoding of bit length \(N\), \(A\) decides whether the output is the zero formal polynomial and halts within \(C(N+2)^k\) steps?
cards.why: Polynomial identity testing is a central concrete derandomization problem: a polynomial may be identically zero because of cancellations invisible in the circuit syntax. A deterministic polynomial-time test would affect symbolic computation and numerous algebraic algorithms, and is known to imply major circuit lower bounds. This places the question at the intersection of efficient verification of algebraic identities and fundamental complexity limitations.

cards.title: Deterministic polynomial-time factorization over finite fields
cards.formal:
Does there exist one deterministic Turing algorithm \(A\) and absolute integers \(K,d\ge1\) such that, for every valid explicit field representation \(\mathbb F_q=\mathbb F_p[t]/(h(t))\) and every dense polynomial \(f\in\mathbb F_q[x]\) of degree \(n\ge1\), the algorithm outputs the complete irreducible factorization of \(f\) in at most
\[
K\bigl(n+\lceil\log_2q\rceil+1\bigr)^d
\]
bit operations?

The input includes the prime \(p\), the supplied monic irreducible field modulus \(h\), and every coefficient of \(f\). The algorithm and the constants are independent of \(n,p,h\) and \(f\), and no unproved number-theoretic assumption is allowed.
cards.why: Finite-field factorization is a basic operation in computer algebra and coding theory. Randomized polynomial-time algorithms are available, while a deterministic algorithm must handle every coefficient list and every characteristic without trying a number of possibilities proportional to the field size. The question isolates a central derandomization gap in an exact algebraic task.

cards.title: Word problem for one-relation monoids
cards.formal: Is the uniform word problem for ordinary one-relation monoids decidable? Does there exist one deterministic Turing machine which, given any finite alphabet \(A\) and four finite words \(u,v,s,t\in A^*\), always halts and decides whether \(s\) and \(t\) represent the same element of the monoid \(\langle A\mid u=v\rangle\)? The presentation and the word pair are all parts of the input; no running-time bound is prescribed.
cards.why: A foundational decidability boundary for rewriting: can reachability under one literal reversible string rule already escape every terminating uniform algorithm?

cards.title: Sum-of-square-roots problem
cards.formal:
Does the sum-of-square-roots decision problem belong to deterministic polynomial time? An instance explicitly gives an integer \(n\ge1\), signed integers \(c_1,\ldots,c_n\), and positive integers \(a_1,\ldots,a_n\), all in binary. The required answer is whether
\[
E(c,a)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_i\sqrt{a_i}\ \ge0,
\]
where each square root is the nonnegative real square root. There is no promise that \(E\ne0\), that the radicands are distinct or square-free, or that their magnitudes are polynomial in \(n\). The target is one uniform deterministic algorithm with a polynomial bound in the total input bit length. This selects the standard algorithmic question explicitly stated in the newer sources; the original TOPP entry principally asks for tight separation bounds, a related quantitative question distinguished below.
cards.why: This is a basic barrier between exact geometric algorithms and computation on finite binary inputs. A general polynomial-time comparison procedure would remove a recurring obstacle to placing geometric decision and verification tasks in familiar discrete complexity classes. The problem also connects algebraic-number representation, exact numerical computation and the complexity of arithmetic circuits.

cards.title: Polynomial-time finite-group isomorphism in the Cayley-table model
cards.formal:
Is isomorphism of finite groups given by their complete multiplication tables decidable in deterministic polynomial time?

Precisely, do there exist one uniform deterministic machine \(A\) and integers \(C,c\ge1\) such that, on every binary input of length \(L\), \(A\) halts within \(C(L+1)^c\) steps and outputs YES exactly when the input encodes two finite groups \(G,H\) and there is a bijection \(\varphi:G\to H\) satisfying
\[
\forall x,y\in G,\qquad
\varphi(x\cdot_G y)=\varphi(x)\cdot_H\varphi(y)?
\]
The constants and program are independent of the orders and structure of both groups.
cards.why: Group isomorphism asks whether two complete finite algebraic structures differ only in their element names. Even with every multiplication available explicitly, a polynomial-time algorithm for arbitrary groups has resisted decades of work. Resolving it would clarify both the complexity of finite algebra and a central algebraic special case of graph isomorphism.

cards.title: Conjugacy problem for one-relator groups
cards.formal:
Does there exist a single total deterministic Turing algorithm which, given any finite presentation with one relator
\[
G=\langle x_1,\ldots,x_k\mid r=1\rangle
\]
and two finite words \(u,v\) in those generators and their inverses, decides whether
\[
\exists w\in\{x_1,x_1^{-1},\ldots,x_k,x_k^{-1}\}^*,
\qquad w^{-1}uw=_Gv?
\]
The presentation is part of the input. There is no prescribed time or space bound, but the algorithm must halt correctly on both conjugate and nonconjugate pairs for every such presentation.
cards.why: One defining relation permits complicated infinite groups while still allowing ordinary word equality to be decided. Conjugacy adds an unrestricted search for a change of representative. Resolving its uniform decidability would locate a basic boundary between effective equality and effective existential questions in finitely presented algebra.

cards.title: Isomorphism problem for one-relator groups
cards.formal: Does there exist one deterministic Turing machine \(A\) that, for every pair of finite one-relator presentations \[P=\langle x_1,\ldots,x_k\mid r=1\rangle,\qquad Q=\langle y_1,\ldots,y_\ell\mid s=1\rangle,\] where \(k,\ell\ge1\) and \(r,s\) are arbitrary explicitly written words in their respective generators and inverses, halts and outputs \(1\) exactly when \(G_P\cong G_Q\), and outputs \(0\) otherwise? Isomorphism is of abstract groups, with no condition on the images of the displayed generators. There is no running-time bound, promise on the presented groups, or restriction on the number of generators.
cards.why: One of the central decision problems for finitely presented groups, testing whether a single defining relation permits effective recognition of abstract algebraic structure.

cards.title: Derandomizing black-box depth-four PIT
cards.formal: Does there exist one deterministic uniform polynomial-time construction of hitting sets for all size-\(s\), \(n\)-variable \(\Sigma\Pi\Sigma\Pi\) arithmetic circuits, in the field-operation model specified below? Precisely, one algorithm and constants \(C>0,b\in\mathbb N\) must work for every \(n,s\ge1\), every working field \(K\), and every supplied list \(T\) of \(2s^2+1\) distinct elements of \(K\). In at most \(C(n+s+1)^b\) operations it must output a list \(H\subseteq K^n\) such that every nonzero formal polynomial computed by any allowed circuit over \(K\) has a nonzero evaluation at some point of \(H\). The algorithm receives no circuit description, coefficients, or evaluation oracle for a particular polynomial.
cards.why: Identity testing asks whether a compact arithmetic computation represents the zero polynomial. A uniform collection of evaluations would remove randomness without inspecting the computation itself. The depth-four case is especially consequential because of its established relationship to much more general arithmetic circuits, and its unrestricted fan-ins distinguish it from several recent positive results.

cards.title: Linear-size circuits for integer multiplication
cards.formal: Do there exist a real constant \(C>0\) and an integer \(n_0\ge1\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge n_0\), some Boolean circuit with at most \(Cn\) gates computes the exact product of every pair of unsigned \(n\)-bit integers, outputting all \(2n\) product bits? The gates are binary AND and OR and unary NOT; fan-out and depth are unrestricted, and the circuit family need not be uniform.
cards.why: Determine whether multiplication has the same order of Boolean hardware complexity as addition, or provide an explicit superlinear lower bound in the unrestricted circuit model.

cards.title: Tensor decomposition at Kruskal’s uniqueness threshold
cards.formal: Does there exist one uniform randomized algorithm that, for every real third-order tensor having a decomposition satisfying Kruskal’s condition, recovers its rank decomposition in polynomial time in the exact algebraic model specified below? More precisely, are there constants \(C,c>0\) and one finite program whose cost is at most \(C(N+1)^c\) on every run and whose probability of outputting a correct decomposition is at least \(2/3\) on every promised input, where \(N=n_1n_2n_3\) is the number of input entries? The number of components and all Kruskal ranks may grow with the dimensions and are not supplied to the program.
cards.why: Kruskal’s condition guarantees that latent factors are mathematically determined by their tensor, but uniqueness alone does not provide an efficient recovery algorithm. Polynomial-time recovery throughout that regime connects identifiability with computation in models used for learning and signal analysis.

cards.title: Decidability of freeness in automaton groups
cards.formal: Is abstract freeness of an automaton group decidable? Does one deterministic Turing machine, given any finite complete deterministic invertible Mealy automaton \(\mathcal A\), always halt and return YES exactly when \[\exists r\in\mathbb N\quad G(\mathcal A)\cong F_r,\] where \(G(\mathcal A)\) is generated by all state transformations and their inverses and \(F_r\) is the free group of rank \(r\)? Rank zero, the trivial group, is included. The question does not require the supplied state transformations themselves to be a free basis.
cards.why: Automata give finite descriptions of groups that can have complex infinite structure and need not have finite presentations by relations. Recognizing a free group tests a fundamental structural property in this representation. The problem isolates the effect of invertibility on decidability and distinguishes structural recognition from equality of individual represented elements.

cards.title: Membership in \(2\times 2\) integer matrix semigroups
cards.formal:
Does there exist an algorithm which, for every finite list \(A_1,\ldots,A_k\in\mathbb Z^{2\times2}\), with \(k\ge1\), and every target \(B\in\mathbb Z^{2\times2}\), decides whether
\[
\exists \ell\ge1\ \exists i_1,\ldots,i_\ell\in\{1,\ldots,k\}:
A_{i_1}A_{i_2}\cdots A_{i_\ell}=B?
\]
All matrix entries are arbitrary signed integers; singular and nonsingular generators may occur together. The algorithm must halt on both positive and negative instances.
cards.why: Dimension two is a sharp unresolved boundary for exact reachability by integer matrix products. The combination of rank loss and determinant growth escapes algorithms for several important restricted matrix classes.

cards.title: Deterministic noncommutative circuit identity testing in polynomial size and degree
cards.formal:
Do there exist integers \(a,B\ge1\), a real constant \(K>0\), and one uniform deterministic algorithm which, given the complete description of a size-\(s\) noncommutative arithmetic circuit over \(\mathbb Q\) and an integer \(D\ge0\), decides whether its output is the zero formal polynomial in at most
\[
K(s+D+2)^a
\]
operations in the exact arithmetic model defined below, whenever the output polynomial has degree at most \(D\)? The degree promise includes the zero polynomial. Circuit depth, sharing and intermediate degrees are unrestricted.
cards.why: Deterministic identity testing asks whether the structure of an arithmetic computation can replace random evaluation. Ordered products retain information that scalar substitutions lose, while unrestricted reuse of intermediate computations prevents known formula algorithms from directly settling the circuit problem.

cards.title: Polynomial-time feasibility of integer min-plus linear systems
cards.formal:
Does there exist a deterministic algorithm that, given arbitrary integer matrices \(A=(a_{ij}),B=(b_{ij})\in\mathbb Z^{m\times n}\), with \(m,n\ge1\) and all entries in binary, decides in polynomial bit time whether there is \(x\in\mathbb Z^n\) satisfying
\[
\min_{1\le j\le n}(a_{ij}+x_j)
=\min_{1\le j\le n}(b_{ij}+x_j)
\qquad(1\le i\le m)?
\]
cards.why: Min-plus linear equations connect algebraic feasibility to two-player mean-payoff games. The challenge is to obtain a running time polynomial in the written input rather than in the magnitudes of its coefficients.

cards.title: Exact Kronecker-polytope membership in polynomial time
cards.formal:
Does there exist a deterministic polynomial-bit-time algorithm which, given three partitions \(\lambda,\mu,\nu\) of the same positive integer \(k\), each as a list of \(n\) nonnegative binary integers, decides whether
\[
\left(\frac{\lambda}{k},\frac{\mu}{k},\frac{\nu}{k}\right)\in\Delta_n,
\]
where \(\Delta_n\) is the Kronecker polytope defined below? The dimension \(n\) is part of the input, and membership is exact, including points on the boundary.
cards.why: Kronecker polytopes connect representation-theoretic multiplicities with possible spectra of quantum subsystems. Exact efficient membership would go beyond known certificate bounds and numerical scaling methods while avoiding the harder task of evaluating individual multiplicities.

cards.title: Bounded-interval zero testing for exponential-trigonometric polynomials
cards.formal:
Is the following proposition true? For every computable discrete subfield \(K\subseteq\mathbb R\) with a fixed effective presentation, there exists an algorithm which, given a constant-coefficient homogeneous linear differential equation with coefficients and initial values in \(K\), together with \(T\in\mathbb Q_{\ge0}\), decides whether its unique solution \(f\) satisfies
\[
\exists t\in[0,T]\quad f(t)=0.
\]
The order of the equation is part of the input and has no fixed upper bound. The algorithm may depend on the presented field, but must halt correctly on every valid equation and endpoint over that field. No unproved number-theoretic hypothesis is assumed.
cards.why: Exact zero detection is a basic reachability question for linear continuous dynamics. A bounded interval removes long-term behavior but still requires deciding tangential contact with zero, which numerical approximation alone need not certify.

cards.title: Polynomial-time dimension expansion over finite fields
cards.formal: Is there a uniform deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, given an explicitly represented finite field \(\mathbb F_q\), integers \(n\ge2,d\ge1\), and arbitrary matrices \(A_1,\ldots,A_d\in\mathbb F_q^{n\times n}\), computes the rational number \[\alpha(A_1,\ldots,A_d)=\min_{\substack{V\le\mathbb F_q^n\\1\le\dim V\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor}}\frac{\dim(A_1V+\cdots+A_dV)}{\dim V}\] exactly? Polynomial time is measured in the total input bit length, uniformly over the field, dimension and number of maps. This is the finite-field polynomial-time branch of the source’s broader computation-complexity question.
cards.why: The expansion guarantee quantifies over every low-dimensional subspace, including subspaces with no coordinate description. Explicit constructions can prove that certain families expand without yielding an efficient procedure to evaluate arbitrary supplied matrices. The question asks whether this global algebraic property has a polynomial-time exact evaluation algorithm.

cards.title: Polynomial-time computation of addition-chain length
cards.formal: Do there exist constants \(K>0\), \(a\in\mathbb N\) and one deterministic multitape Turing machine that, on every positive integer \(n\) supplied in binary, outputs the exact shortest addition-chain length \(\ell(n)\) in binary within \(K(b+1)^a\) steps, where \(b=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1\) is the input length?
cards.why: Addition chains express reuse in multiplication-only exponentiation. Their optimal length is small enough to have short certificates, yet finding that length for an arbitrary binary exponent has resisted a general complexity classification.

cards.title: Linear-time unit-Monge distance multiplication
cards.formal:
Do there exist absolute constants \(K,C>0\), an integer \(B\ge8\), and one uniform deterministic word-RAM algorithm which, for every integer \(n\ge2\) and all permutations \(\pi,\tau\) of \(\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\), outputs a permutation \(\rho\) of that set in at most \(Kn\) instructions using at most \(Cn\) working words, such that
\[
 A_\rho(i,j)=\min_{0\le h\le n}
 \bigl(A_\pi(i,h)+A_\tau(h,j)\bigr)
 \qquad(0\le i,j\le n),
\]
where
\[
 A_\nu(i,j)=|\{t\in\{i,\ldots,n-1\}:\nu(t)<j\}|?
\]
The input and output are permutation arrays, not explicitly written dense matrices. The word length is \(B\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\).
cards.why: This compact matrix operation combines many sequence-comparison values and is reused in alignment, subsequence and compressed-string algorithms. Removing its logarithmic overhead would improve an underlying primitive while matching the linear size of its representation.

cards.title: Efficient LRS evaluation
cards.formal: Does there exist one deterministic algorithm that, given a rational linear recurrence and a nonnegative index \(n\) in binary, decides whether its \(n\)-th term is exactly zero in time polynomial in the total input bit length? Both the recurrence and its initial values are part of the input, and its order is unrestricted.
cards.why: A single term of a rational recurrence has a compact arithmetic representation even when its expanded numerator is enormous. This question isolates whether exact zero testing for that representation can be performed efficiently without randomness.

cards.title: Deterministic divisibility testing by a constant-degree polynomial
cards.formal: For every fixed integer \(\delta \ge 2\), is there a deterministic algorithm using \(\operatorname{poly}(n,s,d)\) arithmetic operations over Q that, given an explicitly s-sparse polynomial \(f\in Q[x_{1},\ldots ,x_{n}]\) of total degree at most d and a nonzero polynomial \(g\in Q[x_{1},\ldots ,x_{n}]\) of total degree at most \(\delta\), decides whether g divides f?
cards.why: Tests whether even a supplied low-degree factor of a sparse multivariate polynomial can be verified efficiently without randomness, a basic obstruction in deterministic factorization.

cards.title: A uniform exponent saving for arbitrary generalized convolution
cards.formal: Does there exist an absolute \(\varepsilon >0\) such that, for every fixed finite domain D with \(d=|D|\ge 2\) and every fixed function \(f:D\times D\to D\), the entire f-convolution of two integer tables on \(D^{n}\) can be computed exactly in \(\widetilde{O}\)\((d^{(2- \varepsilon )n}\cdot \operatorname{polylog}(2+M))\) time? The same \(\varepsilon\) must work for all domains and operations; n is unbounded and M bounds the absolute input values. No associativity, commutativity or algebraic structure of f is assumed.
cards.why: Would give a broadly applicable improvement for table-merging computations without requiring an algebraic law on the state-combination operation, strengthening a common primitive in exact and parameterized algorithms.

cards.title: Uniform compressed word problem for graph groups
cards.formal: Is there a single deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, given a finite simple graph \((A,I)\) and a straight-line program \(S\) over \(A^{\pm1}\), decides whether \(\operatorname{val}(S)=1\) in the graph group \(G(A,I)=\langle A\mid ab=ba\text{ for }(a,b)\in I\rangle\)? The time bound must be polynomial in the combined encoded size of the graph and the program, uniformly over all graphs. This is the polynomial-time branch of the source question; membership in NP is its separate, weaker intermediate target.
cards.why: Asks whether efficient algebraic computation survives when both a compressed group element and the commutation structure of its ambient group vary. It isolates a uniformity obstacle that remains after fixed-group algorithms and more restricted compressed representations have been handled.

cards.title: Polynomial-time sign testing of matrix powers in every fixed dimension
cards.formal:
Is it true that for every fixed integer dimension \(d\ge1\), there is a deterministic polynomial-bit-time algorithm which, given matrices \(M,W\in\mathbb Z^{d\times d}\) and an exponent \(n\ge0\), all in binary, decides whether
\[
\sum_{i=1}^{d}\sum_{j=1}^{d} W_{ij}(M^n)_{ij}\ge0?
\]
The algorithm and the degree of its polynomial running-time bound may depend on \(d\), but not on the entries of \(M,W\) or on \(n\).
cards.why: Matrix powering compactly describes integers with exponentially many output bits. Deciding one exact sign tests whether low-dimensional algebraic structure permits efficient computation without expanding those integers.

cards.title: Collapse of rational recurrence systems to single recurrences
cards.formal: Does every rationally recursive sequence \(u:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Q\) admit a single finite-depth rational recurrence? Explicitly, for every such \(u\), must there exist an integer \(d\geq1\) and polynomials \(A,B\in\mathbb Q[y_{0},\ldots,y_{d-1}]\) such that, for all \(n\geq0\), \[B(u_{n},\ldots,u_{n+d-1})\ne0,\qquad u_{n+d}=\frac{A(u_{n},\ldots,u_{n+d-1})}{B(u_{n},\ldots,u_{n+d-1})}?\]
cards.why: Asks whether auxiliary state increases the expressive power of rational recurrences, or whether finite memory of the observed sequence always suffices. It is a basic structural question about discrete algebraic dynamics and the sequence models underlying weighted and polynomial automata.

cards.title: VP versus VNP
cards.formal:
Over the complex field \(\mathbb C\), do there exist integers \(B,k\ge1\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge1\), some arithmetic circuit with at most \(B(n+1)^k\) operation gates computes the permanent polynomial
\[\operatorname{perm}_n(X)=\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\prod_{i=1}^{n}x_{i,\sigma(i)}\ \in\mathbb C[x_{ij}:1\le i,j\le n]?\]
Circuits are division-free, have binary addition, subtraction and multiplication gates, allow arbitrary complex constants and unrestricted reuse, and compute exact formal polynomials. No uniform construction of the circuits is required. Equivalently, is \(\mathrm{VP}_{\mathbb C}=\mathrm{VNP}_{\mathbb C}\), with the classes defined below? The usual conjecture is that the answer is no.
cards.why: This is the central equality question for general arithmetic computation. It asks whether a polynomial-size algebraic computation can always absorb a sum over exponentially many Boolean witnesses, with the permanent serving as a complete concrete target. A separation would establish a general limitation despite arbitrary constants, cancellations and reuse; equality would give polynomial-size circuits for every polynomial family in VNP.

cards.title: Superpolynomial arithmetic formula lower bounds
cards.formal:
Is the permanent family outside polynomial-size arithmetic formulas over \(\mathbb C\)? Precisely, is the following assertion true?
\[
\forall K,C\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\ \exists n\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\
\forall F,\qquad
\llbracket F\rrbracket=\operatorname{Perm}_n
\ \Longrightarrow\ \operatorname{size}(F)>K n^C,
\]
where \(F\) ranges over the arithmetic formulas defined below and
\[
\operatorname{Perm}_n(X)=\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\prod_{i=1}^{n}x_{i,\sigma(i)}
\in\mathbb C[x_{ij}:i,j\in[n]]?
\]
This card fixes the standard complex-field \(\mathrm{VNP}\)-versus-formula interpretation of the source’s broadly phrased explicit lower-bound challenge. By the permanent’s completeness under polynomially bounded projections, this asks whether some family in \(\mathrm{VNP}_{\mathbb C}\) lacks polynomial-size formulas; it does not impose a separate uniform construction condition on the family of small formulas being ruled out. The source’s Open Problem 8 does not itself name a field or a particular hard family, so this precise choice is an explicit editorial specification.

Superpolynomial means that no single polynomial bound works for all dimensions. It does not demand one particular exponential rate or an eventually pointwise lower bound exceeding every polynomial. There are \(n^2\) input variables; \(n\) in the displayed size bound is the matrix dimension.
cards.why: Separating polynomial-size formulas from VNP would establish a basic limit of unrestricted algebraic expression trees for an explicit central polynomial. Formulas already allow arbitrary constants and cancellations, so their limitations are considerably harder to prove than those of many restricted algebraic models. This is a foundational lower-bound target within the hierarchy of algebraic complexity and is weaker than separating unrestricted circuits from VNP.

cards.title: Permanent versus determinant
cards.formal: Over \(\mathbb C\), is the determinantal complexity of the permanent not bounded above by any polynomial? Precisely, writing \(d_n=\operatorname{dc}_{\mathbb C}(\operatorname{perm}_n)\) as defined below, is it true that for every triple of integers \(B,k,N\ge1\) there is an integer \(n\ge N\) with \(d_n>B(n+1)^k\)? The matrices in the definition are unrestricted exact affine-linear representations over \(\mathbb C\).
cards.why: The permanent and determinant have almost identical permutation formulas, but the determinant is a basic efficiently computable polynomial whereas the permanent encodes algebraic counting. This conjecture asks whether enlarging the matrix and changing all its entries to affine forms can bridge that difference at polynomial cost. A superpolynomial lower bound would exclude an entire central model of algebraic computation, including polynomial-size algebraic branching programs and formulas.

cards.title: VP versus VBP over the complex numbers
cards.formal: Is \(\mathrm{VP}_{\mathbb C}=\mathrm{VBP}_{\mathbb C}\)? More explicitly, let \((m_n,f_n)_{n\ge1}\) be any family with integers \(m_n\ge0\) and commutative polynomials \(f_n\in\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_{m_n}]\). Suppose that some positive integer \(a\) satisfies \[m_n\le(n+2)^a,\qquad \deg f_n\le(n+2)^a,\qquad c(f_n)\le(n+2)^a\quad\text{for all }n\ge1,\] where \(c\) is minimum arithmetic-circuit size in the model below. Must there exist a positive integer \(b\), depending on the whole family, such that \[\operatorname{abp}(f_n)\le(n+2)^b\quad\text{for all }n\ge1?\] Computation is exact and nonuniform over the complex field, and the competing branching programs are unrestricted.
cards.why: The question compares unrestricted arithmetic circuits with path-sum computation inside the class of efficiently representable polynomials. Equality would make polynomial-size determinants of affine matrices sufficient to express every polynomial-degree circuit family. Inequality would establish a fundamental separation within efficient algebraic computation, isolating power supplied by general multiplication together with reuse of intermediate results.

cards.title: Polynomial-size arithmetic formulas for the determinant
cards.formal:
Do there exist positive integers \(K,C\) such that for every integer \(n\ge1\) there is an arithmetic formula \(F_n\) over \(\mathbb C\) satisfying
\[\operatorname{size}(F_n)\le K n^C,\qquad \llbracket F_n\rrbracket=\operatorname{Det}_n(X),\]
where \(\llbracket F_n\rrbracket\) is its output as a formal commutative polynomial and
\[\operatorname{Det}_n(X)=\sum_{\pi\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)\prod_{i=1}^{n}x_{i,\pi(i)}?\]
The formula is a binary expression tree with arbitrary complex constants and addition, subtraction and multiplication. Computations may use cancellations, but intermediate expressions cannot be shared. The same constants \(K,C\) must work for all dimensions.
cards.why: The canonical test of whether reusing intermediate expressions gives a superpolynomial advantage over arithmetic expression trees, even for an efficiently computable polynomial.

cards.title: Shub–Smale \(\tau\)-conjecture
cards.formal: Does there exist an integer \(C\geq1\), independent of the polynomial, such that every nonzero \(f\in\mathbb Z[x]\) satisfies \[z_{\mathbb Z}(f)\leq(1+\tau(f))^C,\] where \(z_{\mathbb Z}(f)\) is the number of distinct integer roots and \(\tau(f)\) is the minimum number of additions, subtractions and multiplications needed to construct \(f\) from only \(1\) and \(x\)?
cards.why: The conjecture asks whether a polynomial compressed into a short arithmetic computation can nevertheless have very many distinct integer zeros. Its elementary statement links arithmetic structure to fundamental lower bounds in algebraic computation. A proof would imply separation of polynomial-time nondeterministic and deterministic computation over the complex numbers, as well as important constant-free circuit separations; neither consequence is presently supplied by the conjecture itself.

cards.title: Explicit univariate arithmetic circuit lower bounds
cards.formal: Does there exist a family \(f=(f_d)_{d\ge2}\in\mathcal E\) whose arithmetic circuit complexity over \(\mathbb C\) is not \(O(\log d)\)? Precisely, \[\exists f\in\mathcal E\ \forall K\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\ \forall D\in\mathbb N_{\ge2}\ \exists d\in\mathbb N,\ d\ge D:\ S_{\mathbb C}(f_d)>K\log_2 d.\] Every \(f_d\in\mathbb Z[x]\) has degree exactly \(d\); \(\mathcal E\) is the class with the uniform coefficient-bit algorithm and polynomial coefficient-length bound defined below. Circuits are unrestricted binary addition/multiplication circuits with arbitrary complex constants, and \(S_{\mathbb C}\) counts wires. This is a disclosed editorial specialization of Wigderson's Open Problem 12.1: it retains the not-\(O(\log d)\) threshold, selects the complex field permitted by the source, and makes explicitness precise using ITCS 2021 Definition 1.
cards.why: This target asks whether efficiently accessible integer coefficients force unrestricted arithmetic computation beyond the elementary logarithmic degree bound, even with one variable and arbitrary complex constants. A solution would expose a source of circuit hardness that survives sharing and cancellation, providing a focused test of algebraic lower-bound techniques.

cards.title: Superlinear constant-degree arithmetic circuit lower bounds
cards.formal:
Does there exist a fixed integer \(d\ge2\) and a uniformly explicit family of polynomials
\[
f_n\in\mathbb Q[x_1,\ldots,x_n],\qquad \deg(f_n)\le d\quad(n\ge2),
\]
whose arithmetic circuit sizes over \(\mathbb C\) are not \(O(n)\)? Precisely, require
\[
\forall L\ge1\ \forall N\ge2\ \exists n\ge N:
\operatorname C_{\mathbb C}(f_n)>Ln,
\]
where \(L,N,n\) are integers and explicitness means that one deterministic polynomial-time Turing machine outputs the full rational coefficient list of \(f_n\). Circuit depth, sharing and complex constants are unrestricted.
cards.why: This isolates one of the most basic explicit arithmetic lower-bound barriers: even when polynomial degree is fixed, it is difficult to prove that unrestricted circuits require more than a linear number of gates. The target asks for any unbounded improvement over linear size.

cards.title: Explicit three-dimensional tensors of superlinear rank
cards.formal: Do there exist one deterministic multitape Turing machine \(A\), a real constant \(K>0\) and an integer \(a\ge1\) such that, for every \(n\ge1\), on input \(1^n\) it outputs all entries of a rational tensor \(T_n\in\mathbb Q^{n\times n\times n}\) within \(K(n+1)^a\) bit operations, and \[\forall B\in\mathbb R_{>0}\ \exists N\ge1\ \forall n\ge N:\quad \operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb C}(T_n)\ge Bn?\] Here rank is ordinary tensor rank over the complex numbers. Thus the required ratio \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb C}(T_n)/n\) tends to infinity, with no prescribed rate.
cards.why: Tensor rank measures the number of independent bilinear products needed to express a computation. Explicit superlinear-rank families would turn generic hardness into concrete examples and yield lower bounds for the corresponding constant-degree arithmetic computations.

cards.title: Strassen’s asymptotic rank conjecture
cards.formal:
Work over the complex field \(\mathbb C\). Is the following general cubic formulation of the asymptotic rank conjecture true?
\[\forall n\in\mathbb N_{>0}\ \forall T\in\mathbb C^n\otimes\mathbb C^n\otimes\mathbb C^n:\quad \bigl(\operatorname{rank}F_1(T)=\operatorname{rank}F_2(T)=\operatorname{rank}F_3(T)=n\bigr)\ \Longrightarrow\ \widetilde R(T)=n,\]
where \(F_i(T)\) are the three matrix flattenings and
\[\widetilde R(T)=\lim_{k\to\infty}R(T^{\boxtimes k})^{1/k}=\inf_{k\ge1}R(T^{\boxtimes k})^{1/k}?\]
Here \(R\) is exact tensor rank, and \(\boxtimes\) groups corresponding factors of tensor products. The tensor \(T\) and its dimension \(n\) are fixed while \(k\) tends to infinity. The quantifier covers all complex tensors satisfying the flattening condition; no additional symmetry, support or computational promise is imposed.
cards.why: The conjecture asks whether every bilinear operation attains, in the exponential growth rate of jointly processed copies, the elementary lower bound already visible from matrices. A positive answer would force matrix multiplication exponent two and impose a simple common asymptotic law on all concise tensors. A negative answer would exhibit an obstruction that survives arbitrarily many grouped copies, beyond the familiar difficulty of decomposing a single tensor.

cards.title: Explicit rigidity at rank n over log log n
cards.formal:
Do there exist a real constant \(0<\varepsilon<1\), constants \(K>0\), \(b\in\mathbb N\), and one deterministic Turing machine which, for every integer \(n\ge4\), outputs a matrix \(A_n\in\mathbb F_2^{n\times n}\) within \(Kn^b\) steps, such that
\[
\forall c>0\ \exists N_c\ge4\ \forall n\ge N_c:
R_{A_n}^{\mathbb F_2}\!\left(
\min\!\left\{n,\left\lfloor\frac{cn}{\log_2\log_2 n}\right\rfloor\right\}
\right)\ge n^{1+\varepsilon}?
\]
Here \(c\) is real, \(N_c,n\) are integers, and \(R^{\mathbb F_2}\) is the minimum number of entries that must be changed to reduce rank to the indicated value. The same matrix family and the same \(\varepsilon\) must work for every fixed \(c\).
cards.why: A sufficiently rigid explicit binary matrix gives a linear transformation whose computation resists linear-size logarithmic-depth circuits. Random matrices have strong rigidity, but obtaining the required guarantees from a uniform deterministic construction remains a central explicit lower-bound challenge.

cards.title: Superpolynomial noncommutative circuit lower bounds
cards.formal:
Does there exist a family
\[
f_n\in\mathbb Q\langle x_1,\ldots,x_n\rangle\qquad(n\ge2)
\]
of polynomial degree with uniformly polynomial-time computable word coefficients, such that
\[
\forall k\ge1\ \forall N\ge2\ \exists n\ge N:
\operatorname{NC}_{\mathbb C}(f_n)>n^k?
\]
Here \(k,N,n\) are integers and \(\operatorname{NC}_{\mathbb C}\) is minimum size among unrestricted noncommutative arithmetic circuits with arbitrary complex constants. The family can be chosen freely subject to the explicitness and degree requirements below; it is not required to be a particular permanent or determinant family.
cards.why: Noncommutative computation retains the order of products and already supports strong formula lower bounds. Proving a superpolynomial bound that survives unrestricted reuse would establish a major circuit lower-bound milestone for an explicitly specified family.

cards.title: Superpolynomial multilinear circuit lower bounds
cards.formal:
Does there exist a family of multilinear polynomials \(f_n\in\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), \(n\ge2\), belonging to \(\mathrm{VNP}_{\mathbb C}\), such that
\[
\forall k\ge1\ \forall N\ge2\ \exists n\ge N:
\operatorname{MC}(f_n)>n^k?
\]
All three quantified parameters are integers, and \(\operatorname{MC}(f_n)\) denotes the minimum size of a semantically multilinear arithmetic circuit over \(\mathbb C\) computing \(f_n\). Thus the target is a VNP family for which no polynomial-size family of gatewise multilinear circuits exists. The family is not required to be the permanent.
cards.why: Unbounded-depth multilinear circuits form a major frontier between successful restricted algebraic lower bounds and general circuit complexity. Requiring a VNP family makes the target a lower bound for algebraically structured polynomials, rather than the nonconstructive existence of hard coefficient tables.

cards.title: Unrestricted arithmetic lower bounds for the discrete Fourier transform
cards.formal: Let \(S(n)\) be the minimum size of a complex arithmetic straight-line program that computes all n coordinates of the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) exactly, in the model below. Do constants \(c>0\) and N exist such that \(S(n)\ge c n \log _{2}n\) for every power of two \(n\ge N\), with no bound on the magnitudes of the constants used in the program?
cards.why: Tests whether the central FFT upper bound is inherently necessary in unrestricted arithmetic computation.

cards.title: Algebraic branching programs versus formulas
cards.formal: For a fixed field F, is \(VF_{F} a\) proper subclass of \(VBP_{F}\)? Equivalently, is there a family \((f_{n})\) of polynomials of polynomially bounded degree in polynomially many commuting variables that has polynomial-size algebraic branching programs over F but no polynomial-size algebraic formulas over F? The field is a parameter of the question, as in the source; a result must state the fields to which it applies.
cards.why: Separates two fundamental models of algebraic computation and asks whether sharing path computations gives a polynomial-versus-superpolynomial advantage over arithmetic trees.

cards.title: NP-hardness of PosSLP
cards.formal: Is \(\mathrm{PosSLP}\) NP-hard under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions? Concretely, does there exist one deterministic Turing-computable map \(g\) and constants \(C>0,d\in\mathbb N\) such that \(g\) runs in time at most \(C(N+1)^d\) on every input of bit length \(N\), outputs a valid integer straight-line program, and for every encoded 3-CNF formula \(F\), \[F\text{ is satisfiable}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{value}(g(F))>0?\] The reduction must be unconditionally correct on all inputs, with no algebraic conjecture, randomness, oracle or advice. Malformed input encodings are treated as no-instances and must also map to nonpositive outputs.
cards.why: A short sequence of elementary integer operations can represent numbers whose binary expansions are enormous. PosSLP isolates the task of deciding the sign of such a number. Its connections to numerical computation make a conventional hardness classification consequential well beyond the particular instruction format.

cards.title: Uniform exact permanent circuits below base two
cards.formal:
Does there exist a rational \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\), an integer \(C\ge1\), and one deterministic circuit generator \(G\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge1\), \(G(1^{n})\) outputs a division-free rational arithmetic circuit \(\mathcal C_{n}\) with at most \(C(2-\varepsilon)^{n}\) nodes, within at most \(C(2-\varepsilon)^{n}\) Turing-machine steps, and
\[\forall K\text{ of characteristic zero}\ \forall A\in K^{n\times n},\qquad \mathcal C_{n}(A)=\operatorname{per}(A)=\sum_{\pi\in S_{n}}\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}A_{i,\pi(i)}?\]
Here \(S_{n}\) is the set of permutations of \(\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\), and every rational circuit constant is interpreted through the canonical embedding \(\mathbb Q\to K\). This fixes the uniform rational-circuit version of the saved characteristic-zero arithmetic-operation question.
cards.why: A canonical exponential-time algebraic computation barrier dating to Ryser's formula.

cards.title: Multilinear versus general arithmetic circuits
cards.formal:
Does there exist a family of multilinear polynomials \(f_n\in\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), indexed by integers \(n\ge2\), and an integer \(a\ge1\), such that
\[
\operatorname{C}(f_n)\le n^a\qquad\text{for every }n\ge2,
\]
while
\[
\forall k\ge1\ \forall N\ge2\ \exists n\ge N:
\operatorname{MC}(f_n)>n^k?
\]
The quantified \(k,N,n\) are integers. Here \(\operatorname{C}\) is unrestricted arithmetic circuit size and \(\operatorname{MC}\) is semantically multilinear arithmetic circuit size, both over \(\mathbb C\). Thus the outputs must have polynomial-size unrestricted circuits but no polynomial-size family of circuits that remain multilinear at every gate.
cards.why: This asks whether leaving the multilinear class during an exact algebraic computation can provide a superpolynomial advantage even though the final answer is multilinear. It tests the gap between a central restricted circuit model and general algebraic computation, where cancellation and sharing may interact in ways current lower-bound methods do not capture.

cards.title: Semantic versus syntactic multilinear circuits
cards.formal: Is there a field \(F\), fixed independently of \(n\), and a family \(f_n\in F[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), \(n\ge1\), that has polynomial-size semantically multilinear arithmetic circuits over \(F\) but has no polynomial-size family of syntactically multilinear arithmetic circuits over that same field? Semantic multilinearity is required at every gate. The question uses nonuniform circuit size and allows arbitrary field constants.
cards.why: Many arithmetic lower bounds are proved under syntactic restrictions that make the variables entering a multiplication disjoint. Semantic multilinearity permits the same polynomial property to hold after cancellation and sharing of intermediate computations. Determining whether this distinction changes polynomial circuit power would clarify the scope of a central restricted model of algebraic computation.

cards.title: Permanent lower bounds from black-box identity testing
cards.formal:
Does the following implication hold over the rational field \(\mathbb Q\)?
\[
\mathsf{HIT}_{\mathbb Q}\ \Longrightarrow\ \mathsf{PERMHard}_{\mathbb Q}.
\]
The premise \(\mathsf{HIT}_{\mathbb Q}\) says that there are a single deterministic algorithm \(G\) and positive integers \(A,a\) such that, for every \(n,d,s\ge1\), on unary input \((1^{n},1^{d},1^{s})\), algorithm \(G\) outputs a finite list \(H_{n,d,s}\) of points in \(\mathbb Q^{n}\) within \(A(n+d+s)^{a}\) bit operations, with the property
\[
\forall f\in\mathbb Q[x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}],\quad
\bigl(f\ne0\ \land\ \deg f\le d\ \land\ L_{\mathbb Q}(f)\le s\bigr)
\ \Longrightarrow\
\exists h\in H_{n,d,s},\quad f(h)\ne0.
\]
Here \(L_{\mathbb Q}(f)\) is the minimum number of edges in a division-free arithmetic circuit over \(\mathbb Q\) computing \(f\), in the model below; rational constants of arbitrary bit length are allowed in those circuits.

The conclusion \(\mathsf{PERMHard}_{\mathbb Q}\) says that the permanent polynomial family has no polynomial-size circuits in that same algebraic model. Explicitly, with
\[
\operatorname{Perm}_{m}(X)=\sum_{\pi\in S_{m}}\prod_{i=1}^{m}x_{i,\pi(i)},
\]
the conclusion is
\[
\forall B,b\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\ \forall m_{0}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\
\exists m\ge m_{0},\qquad
L_{\mathbb Q}(\operatorname{Perm}_{m})>Bm^{b}.
\]
Prove this implication or its logical negation. The source asks a more general question about circuit classes; this card selects its explicitly published general-circuit black-box instance and fixes the rational field and bit-cost convention as disclosed below.
cards.why: This question asks whether derandomizing algebraic identity testing forces hardness for the permanent, a canonical polynomial encoding counting, rather than merely for less explicitly describable polynomials. A resolution would clarify the strength of the connection between algorithms for detecting algebraic cancellation and nonuniform arithmetic lower bounds, a central barrier in algebraic complexity.

cards.title: Optimal multilinear-formula size of the permanent
cards.formal:
Determine the asymptotic growth of \(\log_2 F(n)\), up to universal multiplicative constants, where \(F(n)\) is the minimum size of a multilinear arithmetic formula over \(\mathbb C\) computing the permanent of an \(n\times n\) matrix of independent variables.

More precisely, give an explicitly characterized positive scale \(g:\{2,3,\ldots\}\to\mathbb R_{>0}\) and prove that there exist constants \(a,A>0\) and an integer \(n_0\ge2\) such that
\[
2^{a g(n)}\le F(n)\le2^{A g(n)}
\qquad\text{for every integer }n\ge n_0.
\]
The scale must determine the growth rate, rather than restating \(F(n)\) or another unresolved minimum-formula-size quantity.
cards.why: Establish a qualitatively stronger explicit algebraic lower bound in one of the few models already admitting superpolynomial separations.

cards.title: Cubic min-plus circuit lower bounds for shortest paths
cards.formal:
For \(n\ge2\), let \(K_n\) be the complete undirected graph on vertices \(1,\ldots,n\), with an arbitrary finite nonnegative real weight \(x_{ij}=x_{ji}\) on each edge \(\{i,j\}\). Let
\[
f_n(x)=\min_{P:\,1\leadsto n\text{ a simple path}}\sum_{e\in P}x_e.
\]
Write \(s(n)\) for the smallest number of binary gates in a circuit using only \(\min\) and addition, with optional constants \(0,+\infty\), that outputs \(f_n(x)\) exactly for every such weight assignment. Do there exist constants \(c>0\) and an integer \(n_0\ge2\) such that
\[
\forall n\ge n_0:\quad s(n)\ge c n^3?
\]
There is one output, with unrestricted circuit depth and reuse of intermediate values.
cards.why: This is a basic unconditional lower-bound question for dynamic programming. A resolution would clarify whether the standard cubic relaxation computation is intrinsically necessary even for one distance when computation is restricted to minimum and addition, and would illuminate why monotone lower-bound methods struggle with paths of varying lengths.

cards.title: VP factor closure in positive characteristic
cards.formal:
Is \(\mathrm{VP}_{F}\) closed under polynomial factors for every field \(F\) of positive characteristic? Explicitly, quantify first over every prime \(p\), every field \(F\) with \(\operatorname{char}(F)=p\), every function \(m:\mathbb N_{\ge1}\to\mathbb N\), and every two polynomial families
\[
f_n,g_n\in F[x_1,\ldots,x_{m(n)}]\qquad(n\ge1).
\]
Does the following implication always hold?
\[
\begin{split}
&\left[\ \forall n\ge1,\ f_n\ne0\text{ and }g_n\mid f_n\ \right]\\
&\quad\land\left[\ \exists A,k\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\ \forall n\ge1,\
\max\{m(n),\deg(f_n),L_F(f_n)\}\le A(n+1)^k\ \right]\\
&\qquad\Longrightarrow\left[\ \exists B,\ell\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\ \forall n\ge1,\
L_F(g_n)\le B(n+1)^{\ell}\ \right]?
\end{split}
\]
Here \(L_F\) is exact algebraic circuit size as defined below, and degree means total degree. The field is fixed throughout each family. Constants in the polynomial bounds may depend on the field and the families but not on \(n\). There is no restriction on factor multiplicities, including multiplicities divisible by \(p\).
cards.why: Factor closure asks whether multiplication can conceal a polynomial that is substantially harder to compute than the resulting product, even when all output degrees remain polynomially bounded. It is a structural question about the standard class of efficiently computable polynomial families. Its positive-characteristic form is also relevant to the scope of algebraic hardness-versus-randomness results, where extracting factors from circuit identities connects lower bounds with polynomial identity testing.

cards.title: VBP factor closure in positive characteristic
cards.formal:
For every field \(F\) of positive characteristic, do there exist a real constant \(K_F>0\) and an integer \(a_F\ge1\) such that for every integer \(n\ge1\) and all nonzero polynomials \(f,g\in F[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) with \(g\mid f\),
\[
\operatorname{ABP}_F(g)\le
K_F\bigl(\operatorname{ABP}_F(f)+n+1\bigr)^{a_F}?
\]
Here \(\operatorname{ABP}_F\) denotes minimum size of a commutative arithmetic branching program over the same field \(F\), as defined below. Factors of arbitrary multiplicity are included. The constants may depend on the fixed field, but not on the polynomials, their coefficients, the number of variables, or their degrees.
cards.why: Branching programs are a central algebraic model between formulas and unrestricted circuits. Understanding whether taking factors preserves their polynomial size in positive characteristic would complete an important structural closure property beyond the characteristic-zero theorem.

cards.title: Containment of presentable border VP in VNP over every field
cards.formal:
Is
\[
\mathrm{VP}^{\varepsilon}_F\subseteq\mathrm{VNP}_F
\]
true for every field \(F\), where \(\mathrm{VP}^{\varepsilon}_F\) is the presentable border class defined below? The same field is used for approximation and for the VNP representation. It is fixed throughout each polynomial family. The question includes infinite fields of every characteristic.
cards.why: Charging for approximation coefficients gives an intermediate model between exact circuits and unrestricted border complexity. Understanding whether its limits admit small algebraic verifiers tests how much power approximation adds when its coefficients have compact circuits.

cards.title: Arithmetic circuit closure under pth roots
cards.formal:
For every prime \(p\), do there exist constants \(K_p>0\) and integers \(a_p\ge1\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge1\) and every polynomial \(g\in\overline{\mathbb F_p}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\),
\[
\operatorname C_p(g)\le K_p\bigl(\operatorname C_p(g^p)+n+1\bigr)^{a_p}?
\]
Here \(\operatorname C_p\) is division-free arithmetic circuit size over the algebraic closure of the prime field, with arbitrary constants from that same field. The constants may depend on \(p\), but not on \(n\), \(g\), its coefficients or its degree. There is no degree parameter in the size bound.
cards.why: In positive characteristic, taking a power can conceal the coefficient structure needed for circuit factorization and hardness-to-randomness arguments. Removing such powers with polynomial size overhead would eliminate a basic inseparability obstacle in algebraic complexity.

cards.title: Explicit rigid matrices over low-degree number fields
cards.formal:
Does there exist a deterministic polynomial-time construction of matrices \(A_n\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}\), for integers \(n\ge4\), whose entries lie in a common number field of degree polynomial in \(n\), together with a constant \(0<\varepsilon<1\) such that
\[
\forall c>0\ \exists N_c\ge4\ \forall n\ge N_c:
R_{A_n}^{\mathbb C}\!\left(
\min\!\left\{n,\left\lfloor\frac{cn}{\log_2\log_2 n}\right\rfloor\right\}
\right)\ge n^{1+\varepsilon}?
\]
The same construction and \(\varepsilon\) must work for every fixed real \(c>0\). Rigidity is measured against all low-rank complex replacement matrices. Polynomial-time construction and the common field are specified by the exact representation below.
cards.why: Rigidity offers a route to lower bounds for linear computations of logarithmic depth. Allowing algebraic entries in small number fields relaxes the most restrictive coefficient choices while still demanding an efficient exact construction; known generic large-field constructions do not answer that challenge.

cards.title: Tensor orbit-closure intersection in \(\mathrm{NP}\cap\mathrm{coAM}\)
cards.formal:
Is the tensor orbit-closure intersection language \(L_{\mathrm{OCI}}\) defined below in \(\mathrm{NP}\cap\mathrm{coAM}\)? Equivalently, does it have both polynomially bounded certificates for yes-instances and a two-message public-coin Arthur–Merlin protocol for no-instances, with the completeness and soundness conditions below?

A valid input specifies positive integers \(n,m\) and two triples \(X=(X_{1},X_{2},X_{3})\) and \(Y=(Y_{1},Y_{2},Y_{3})\) of \(nm\)-by-\(nm\) matrices with coefficients in \(\mathbb Q(i)\), given by their full lists of entries. On the ambient complex vector space
\[
\mathcal X_{n,m}=\bigl(\mathbb C^{nm\times nm}\bigr)^{\oplus3},
\]
the group \(G_{n,m}=\mathrm{GL}_{n}(\mathbb C)\times\mathrm{GL}_{m}(\mathbb C)\) acts by
\[
(A,B)\cdot(X_{1},X_{2},X_{3})=
\bigl((A\otimes B)X_{1}(A\otimes B)^{-1},
      (A\otimes B)X_{2}(A\otimes B)^{-1},
      (A\otimes B)X_{3}(A\otimes B)^{-1}\bigr).
\]
The input belongs to \(L_{\mathrm{OCI}}\) exactly when
\[
\overline{G_{n,m}\cdot X}^{\,\mathrm{Zar}}
\cap
\overline{G_{n,m}\cdot Y}^{\,\mathrm{Zar}}
\ne\varnothing.
\]
Invalid encodings do not belong to the language. Both dimensions and all coefficient bit lengths are unbounded parts of the input; the number of matrices in each triple is fixed at three. Prove membership in both complexity classes, or prove that membership in their intersection fails. This is the tensor-class specialization of the explicit certificate question in the source, selected from its broader exact-complexity discussion.
cards.why: Tensor orbit-closure intersection captures when allowed basis changes can bring two algebraic objects to a common limit. Locating this class within NP and coAM would determine whether both sides of a broad family of geometric equivalence problems admit short, efficiently checkable evidence, connecting invariant theory with the certificate structure familiar from graph isomorphism.

cards.title: Homogeneous versus unrestricted arithmetic formulas
cards.formal:
Does there exist a family of homogeneous polynomials \(f_n\in\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), indexed by integers \(n\ge2\), and an integer \(a\ge1\), such that
\[
\operatorname{F}(f_n)\le n^a\qquad\text{for every }n\ge2,
\]
but
\[
\forall k\ge1\ \forall N\ge2\ \exists n\ge N:
\operatorname{HF}(f_n)>n^k?
\]
Here \(k,N,n\) are integers, \(\operatorname{F}\) is unrestricted arithmetic formula size and \(\operatorname{HF}\) is homogeneous arithmetic formula size over \(\mathbb C\), as defined below. In other words, can homogeneous outputs have polynomial-size general formulas but no polynomial-size homogeneous formulas?
cards.why: Homogenization is a central bridge between restricted algebraic lower bounds and general formula complexity. A superpolynomial separation would show that insisting on a single degree at every intermediate computation loses essential power, even when the final polynomial is homogeneous.

cards.title: A qAC⁰ versus NL-complete dichotomy for Cayley semigroup membership
cards.formal:
For every pseudovariety \(\mathcal V\) of finite semigroups, does its Cayley-table membership promise problem \(\operatorname{Memb}_{\mathrm{CT}}(\mathcal V)\), defined below, satisfy at least one of these two alternatives?
\[
\operatorname{Memb}_{\mathrm{CT}}(\mathcal V)\in\mathrm{qAC}^{0}
\qquad\text{or}\qquad
\operatorname{Memb}_{\mathrm{CT}}(\mathcal V)\text{ is NL-complete under uniform AC}^{0}\text{ many-one reductions}.
\]
Use uniform circuit classes and reductions that always output valid promised instances. The pseudovariety is fixed separately for each problem, not part of the input.
cards.why: Finite semigroup membership ranges from very shallow parallel computation to directed reachability. A dichotomy would organize this complexity landscape by algebraic closure properties, extending the structural understanding beyond known compression-friendly classes.

cards.title: Efficient equations for VP with unrestricted complex coefficients
cards.formal: For every fixed integer \(c\ge 1\), do there exist nonzero polynomials \(\mathrm{P}_{n}\) in \(N_{n}=\operatorname{binom}(n+n^{c},n)\) coefficient variables, with degree and algebraic circuit size at most \(C_{c} N_{n}^{a_{c}}\), such that for every fixed integer \(b\ge 1\) there is \(n_{0}(c,b)\) for which \(\mathrm{P}_{n}\)(\(coeff(f)\))=0 whenever \(n\ge n_{0}(c,b)\) and \(f\in \mathbb{C} [x_{1},\ldots ,x_{n}]\) has total degree at most \(n^{c}\) and an algebraic circuit of size at most \(n^{b}\)? Constants \(C_{c},a_{c}\) and the family \((\mathrm{P}_{n})\) may depend on c, but not on b. Coefficients of f may be arbitrary complex numbers. This expresses the source’s eventual vanishing on every polynomial-size family, without demanding a common finite threshold across all circuit-size exponents.
cards.why: Would clarify whether a broad family of algebraic lower-bound certificates can recognize all efficiently computable polynomials once arbitrary coefficients are allowed.

cards.title: Approximate polynomial satisfiability in AM under GRH
cards.formal: Assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, is approximate polynomial satisfiability for rational-coefficient arithmetic circuits in AM? An instance consists of division-free circuits computing \(f_{1},\ldots ,f_{m}\in \mathbb{Q} [x_{1},\ldots ,x_{n}]\). It is a YES instance if, for every real \(\eta >0\), there is a point \(a\in \mathbb{C} ^{n}\) with \(\max _{i} |f_{i}(a)|<\eta\); otherwise it is a NO instance. Equivalently, for every polynomial \(A\in \mathbb{Q} [y_{1},\ldots ,y_{m}]\), the identity \(A(f_{1},\ldots ,f_{m})=0\) must imply \(A(0,\ldots ,0)=0\). This equivalent decision predicate is AnnAtZero. Ask for one uniform public-coin protocol with verifier time, random-tape length and prover-message length polynomial in the full binary input length, with completeness at least \(2/3\) and soundness at most \(1/3\) on every instance.
cards.why: Would place a fundamental decision problem about limiting algebraic solutions inside a low level of interactive complexity rather than merely polynomial space. This would clarify the computational cost of passing from exact algebraic objects to their closures, a central operation in border complexity and geometric complexity theory.

cards.title: Does explicit multivariate hardness imply univariate hardness over F₂?
cards.formal:
Over the two-element field \(\mathbb F_2\), is the following implication true?
