cards.formal: Do there exist an absolute integer \(C\geq3\) and a uniform randomized polynomial-time algorithm that, on every finite simple undirected graph promised to be \(3\)-colourable, outputs a proper colouring using at most \(C\) colours with probability at least \(2/3\)? The same palette bound and finite program must work for all graph sizes. This card retains the explicitly adopted randomized version of the constant-palette problem.
cards.why: A defining promise-CSP problem: determine whether relaxing an NP-hard colouring task to any fixed larger palette permits efficient construction of a valid solution.

cards.title: Bodirsky–Pinsker conjecture
cards.formal:
For every countable finitely bounded homogeneous relational structure \(A\) over a finite signature, and every first-order reduct \(B\) of \(A\) with a finite relational signature, is
\[\operatorname{CSP}(B)\in\mathrm P\quad\lor\quad\operatorname{CSP}(B)\text{ is NP-complete}\ ?\]
NP-completeness uses deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions. The templates are fixed before the finite input is supplied. This is the unconditional complexity dichotomy, without requiring an algebraic criterion identifying the two sides.
cards.why: The main tractability-classification conjecture for well-behaved infinite-domain CSPs. It links algorithm design, universal algebra and model theory, and would extend the finite-domain dichotomy to substantially richer constraint languages.

cards.title: Search-to-decision equivalence for finite promise CSPs
cards.formal: For every fixed pair \((A,B)\) of finite nonempty relational structures over the same finite signature with \(A\to B\), does polynomial-time solvability of the decision promise problem \(\operatorname{PCSP}(A,B)\) imply polynomial-time solvability of its search version? Decision must accept every finite \(X\) with \(X\to A\) and reject every \(X\) with \(X\not\to B\). Search receives \(X\) with the promise \(X\to A\) and must output an explicit homomorphism \(X\to B\). Both algorithms are deterministic and have polynomial worst-case running time on all inputs; the programs and polynomial bounds may depend on \(A,B\).
cards.why: Many applications need an assignment rather than recognition that an assignment must exist. A universal implication would connect tractability classifications of promise decision problems to actual construction across finite local constraint languages. A separation would identify a fixed finite promise problem whose decision gap is efficiently recognizable while its promised solutions resist every deterministic polynomial-time search algorithm.

cards.title: Logarithmic-color approximation of 3-colorable graphs
cards.formal:
Is there a uniform randomized polynomial-time algorithm that, for every \(n\)-vertex graph promised to be \(3\)-colourable, produces a proper colouring using \(O(\log n)\) colours in expectation? More precisely, do there exist such an algorithm \(A\) and an absolute integer \(K\geq1\) for which
\[
\mathbb E_{\rho}\big[\kappa(A(G;\rho))\big]\leq K\max\{1,\log_2 n\}
\]
for every nonempty \(3\)-colourable graph \(G\), where \(\kappa\) counts distinct colours used? Randomization and expected performance follow the source’s approximation-algorithm convention; deterministic algorithms are included. Properness is always required, and the time bound is worst case as specified below.
cards.why: Logarithmic colouring would be a major improvement for a canonical approximation problem whose positive guarantees still grow as powers of the input size. It would show that a hidden partition into three independent sets can be replaced efficiently by a very small exact partition without needing to recover the original three classes.

cards.title: Hardness of 6-coloring 3-colorable graphs
cards.formal:
Is there a uniform deterministic polynomial-time many-one reduction \(R\) from Boolean \(3\)-SAT to finite simple undirected graphs such that, for every \(3\)-CNF formula \(F\),
\[
F\text{ is satisfiable}\ \Longrightarrow\ \chi(R(F))\leq3,
\qquad
F\text{ is unsatisfiable}\ \Longrightarrow\ \chi(R(F))>6?
\]
Equivalently, is the promise decision problem \(\operatorname{PCSP}(K_3,K_6)\) NP-hard under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions? This is the previously approved gap-decision formulation of the six-colouring hardness question.
cards.why: The three-versus-six gap is a concrete fixed-template question in approximate colouring and promise constraint satisfaction. An established reduction would supply a fundamental obstruction to algorithms producing six-colour solutions on promised three-colourable inputs; the newly claimed all-constant result directly addresses this target.

cards.title: NP-intermediate \(\omega\)-categorical CSPs
cards.formal:
Assume \(\mathrm P\ne\mathrm{NP}\). Does there exist a countable \(\omega\)-categorical relational structure \(\Gamma\) in a finite relational signature such that its fixed-template constraint satisfaction problem is NP-intermediate? Explicitly, the required three conditions are
\[\operatorname{CSP}(\Gamma)\in\mathrm{NP},\qquad\operatorname{CSP}(\Gamma)\notin\mathrm P,\qquad\operatorname{CSP}(\Gamma)\text{ is not NP-complete}.\]
Completeness uses deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions, as in the source’s hardness constructions. No effective presentation or uniform construction of the infinite template is required.
cards.why: This asks whether the principal symmetry condition for infinite-domain CSP algebra allows intermediate NP complexity at all. An example would locate a precise limit of tractability-versus-completeness classifications; a negative answer would establish a much broader NP dichotomy than the currently conjectured finitely bounded homogeneous framework.

cards.title: Dichotomy for finite-domain restricted CSPs
cards.formal:
Assume \(\mathrm P\ne\mathrm{NP}\). For every finite relational signature \(\tau\), every finite \(\tau\)-structure \(A\), and every possibly infinite \(\tau\)-structure \(B\) for which \(\operatorname{CSP}(B)\) is decidable, must \(\operatorname{RCSP}(A,B)\) be either polynomial-time solvable or NP-hard in the source’s completion sense? Explicitly, let
\[\mathcal S_{A,B}=\{S\subseteq\{0,1\}^*:S\text{ is decidable and }S\cap\operatorname{CSP}(B)=\operatorname{CSP}(A)\cap\operatorname{CSP}(B)\}.\]
Is it always true that
\[\bigl(\exists S\in\mathcal S_{A,B}:S\in\mathrm P\bigr)\quad\lor\quad\bigl(\forall S\in\mathcal S_{A,B}:S\text{ is NP-hard}\bigr)?\]
The input is a finite structure \(X\) promised to map homomorphically to \(B\); on that promise the decision is whether \(X\) maps to \(A\).
cards.why: This asks whether the finite-domain CSP dichotomy survives every decidable restriction described by homomorphisms into a fixed, possibly infinite structure. A positive answer would sharply constrain the complexity introduced by such promises. A counterexample would demonstrate intermediate promise behaviour even though all satisfying assignments still use a fixed finite domain.

cards.title: Boolean decision-Holant dichotomy
cards.formal:
Classify the polynomial-time solvable Boolean decision-Holant problems for all fixed finite families of Boolean relations. More precisely, under \(\mathrm P\ne\mathrm{NP}\), determine the entire characteristic function
\[\chi_{\mathrm H}(\mathcal F)=\begin{cases}1,&\operatorname{DecHolant}(\mathcal F)\in\mathrm P,\\0,&\operatorname{DecHolant}(\mathcal F)\notin\mathrm P,\end{cases}\]
with absolute error at most \(1/100\) at every finite family \(\mathcal F\). The answer must give a substantive structural criterion on the allowed relations, with algorithms and complementary lower bounds, rather than merely restating the definition of polynomial-time solvability. The model is the source’s Boolean edge-CSP interpretation of decision Holant, specified below.
cards.why: A full classification would explain exactly which local Boolean constraints remain tractable when each variable has two incidences. The unresolved region contains broad generalizations of matching rather than only the standard Boolean CSP algorithms. Resolving it would connect delta-matroid structure with the boundary between polynomial-time graph algorithms and NP-hardness.

cards.title: Universal representation of NP by \(\omega\)-categorical CSPs
cards.formal:
For every language \(L\subseteq\{0,1\}^*\) in \(\mathrm{NP}\), does there exist a countable \(\omega\)-categorical relational structure \(\Gamma\) in a finite relational signature such that
\[L\equiv_T^p\operatorname{CSP}(\Gamma)\ ?\]
The relation \(\equiv_T^p\) means deterministic polynomial-time Turing reductions in both directions. This reduction convention follows the source’s accompanying non-dichotomy results and the explicit definition in the later monograph; Question 2 itself abbreviates it as polynomial-time equivalence.
cards.why: The question tests whether the symmetry framework that supports infinite-domain algebraic CSP methods is computationally universal for NP under the source’s equivalence convention. A positive answer would place every NP degree into that framework; a negative answer would exhibit a complexity limitation imposed by omega-categoricity itself.

cards.title: Common polynomial exponent for tractable digraph CSPs
cards.formal: Does there exist an integer \(c\geq1\) such that, for every fixed finite digraph \(H\) for which \(\operatorname{CSP}(H)\) is in \(\mathrm P\), there are a deterministic algorithm \(M_{H}\) and a constant \(C_{H}\geq1\) that decide whether an input digraph \(G\) admits a homomorphism to \(H\) in at most \(C_{H}(L+1)^{c}\) bit steps, where \(L\) is the input encoding length? The exponent must be independent of \(H\), while both the machine and multiplicative constant may depend on \(H\).
cards.why: The finite CSP dichotomy classifies each fixed set of local relations qualitatively. A common exponent would add a quantitative uniformity principle to this classification. Its failure would show that polynomial-time digraph CSPs can require arbitrarily large exponents even though every individual template is tractable.

cards.title: VCSP tractability over the countable random graph
cards.formal:
Let \(\mathbb R=(D;E)\) be the countable random graph. Is it true that for every valued structure \(\mathcal A=(D;f_1,\ldots,f_s)\) with a finite signature and \(\operatorname{Aut}(\mathbb R)\subseteq\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal A)\),
\[
\mathcal A\text{ does not pp-construct }K_3
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{VCSP}(\mathcal A)\in\mathsf P?
\]
All cost functions take values in \(\mathbb Q\cup\{\infty\}\). The valued decision problem and the precise pp-construction condition are defined below. The template \(\mathcal A\) is fixed for each decision problem; the claim is not a uniform algorithm taking arbitrary templates as part of its input.
cards.why: This asks whether the known expressibility obstruction completely determines tractability for a major new class of infinite-domain optimization problems. A positive answer would extend the algebraic classification of valued CSPs beyond ordered domains to graph-invariant costs; a counterexample would expose a failure of the proposed general obstruction.

cards.title: Search tractability of BLP-solvable promise CSPs
cards.formal: For every fixed pair \((A,B)\) of finite relational structures of the same finite signature, with nonempty domains and a homomorphism \(A\to B\), suppose that the basic linear programming relaxation solves the decision problem \(\operatorname{PCSP}(A,B)\). Must there exist a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, on every finite input structure \(X\) promised to satisfy \(X\to A\), outputs a homomorphism \(X\to B\)? The algorithm and its polynomial bound may depend on \(A,B\); the promised homomorphism to \(A\) is not supplied.
cards.why: BLP is a central general-purpose tractability criterion for promise constraints. Determining whether its decision power always entails efficient promised search would clarify when an efficiently recognizable relaxation gap can also support construction of the relaxed object. A separation would expose a basic limitation of decision-to-search equivalence even for finite local relations.

cards.title: Super-log-logarithmic colouring hardness for two-colourable triple systems
cards.formal:
Is there an integer-valued function \(f:\mathbb N_{\ge1}\to\mathbb N_{\ge2}\) with
\[\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{f(N)}{\log_2\log_2(N+4)}=+\infty\]
and a deterministic quasipolynomial-time many-one reduction from Boolean 3-SAT to the following promise problem on explicitly represented \(N\)-vertex three-uniform hypergraphs \(H\):
\[\text{YES: }\chi(H)\le2;\qquad \text{NO: }\chi(H)>f(N)?\]
This accepts either hardness level offered in the source: a polynomial-time reduction is a stronger special case of the permitted quasipolynomial-time reduction. No particular growth function \(f\) is prescribed in advance.
cards.why: This asks for a quantitative hardness barrier at the smallest hyperedge size where even a hidden bipartition can be difficult to find. It separates the three-vertex constraint frontier from much stronger results for larger edges and tests how far approximation hardness can grow with input size.

cards.title: Characterizing CSP languages with linear non-redundancy
cards.formal: Characterize all finite constraint languages \(\Gamma\) over arbitrary finite nonempty domains for which every \(n\)-variable formula has a subformula with at most \(C_\Gamma n\) constraints and exactly the same set of satisfying assignments, for some constant \(C_\Gamma\) independent of the formula and \(n\). Equivalently, determine the class-membership function \(\chi_{\mathrm{lin}}\) on all such finite languages, taking value \(1\) when this property holds and \(0\) otherwise. The target is the full classification from Question 8; it is not restricted to Boolean domains or to a proposed sufficient condition.
cards.why: A full classification would explain which systems of local relations always have a linear-sized exact description using their own constraints. It would organize connections among logical redundancy, sparsification, preprocessing and algebra across all finite domains. The distinction between existence of a small subformula and efficiently finding it is essential to interpreting the result.

cards.title: Polynomial kernels for Boolean MinCSP
cards.formal: Classify all fixed finite Boolean constraint languages \(\Gamma\) for which \(\operatorname{MinCSP}(\Gamma)\), parameterized by the allowed number \(k\) of violated constraints, admits a randomized polynomial kernel. Equivalently, determine the membership function \(\chi_{\mathrm{ker}}(\Gamma)\in\{0,1\}\) of this class for every finite Boolean language. Deterministic kernels also qualify; the target retains the full language classification and the allowance for randomization in PACS 2024 Question 9.
cards.why: This would classify the full preprocessing power of finite Boolean constraint languages after the fixed-parameter solvability boundary is known. It asks which nearly satisfiable systems admit a compact equivalent core whose size depends only polynomially on the repair budget. The source allows randomization so that the classification addresses this compression boundary without also demanding derandomization of established kernels.

cards.title: Exact exponential-time equivalence for nonnegative Boolean Max-CSP
cards.formal: Does the following extension of the source’s degree-based classification hold? For every fixed finite Boolean constraint language \(\Gamma\) that is neither 0-valid, 1-valid, nor 2-monotone, let \(d=\deg (\Gamma )\). For every fixed real \(\alpha >1\), if Max \(\mathrm{CSP}(\Gamma ,N,c)\) has an exact deterministic algorithm running in \(\alpha ^{n}n^{O(1)}\) time for every fixed constant \(c\ge 1\), must Max d-CNF-SAT with nonnegative integer weights of total weight at most \(n^{c}\) also have an exact deterministic \(\alpha ^{n}n^{O(1)}\)-time algorithm for every fixed \(c\ge 1\)? The same base \(\alpha\) is required. Algorithms and polynomial factors may depend on \(\Gamma ,\alpha ,c\). This formulates the conclusion’s speedup question as extending Theorem 6.2 to all NP-hard nonnegative-weight languages; tractable languages are explicitly excluded.
cards.why: Would show whether the algebraic degree of a Boolean constraint language determines its exact exponential-time complexity even when every constraint has the usual nonnegative weight.

cards.title: Polynomial-time tractability testing for core crisp CSP languages
cards.formal: Is there one deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, given a finite crisp constraint language \(\Gamma\) over an explicitly given finite domain D and promised that \(\Gamma\) is a core, decides whether \(\Gamma\) admits an idempotent Siggers polymorphism? Equivalently on the core promise, decide whether \(\Gamma\) is solvable in the algebraic sense of the finite-domain CSP dichotomy. The polynomial must be uniform in the entire input, including |D|, the number of relations, their arities and their listed tuples; neither a polymorphism nor a tractability certificate is supplied.
cards.why: Would make the finite-domain CSP tractability criterion efficiently recognizable when the core is already given, connecting the structural dichotomy to algorithms whose template also varies as input.

area: Database theory and finite model theory
label: Database theory

cards.title: Decidability of conjunctive-query entailment in SROIQ
cards.formal:
Is Boolean conjunctive-query entailment for classical SROIQ decidable under semantics allowing both finite and infinite models? Precisely, does there exist one deterministic Turing machine \(D\) such that for every finite legal SROIQ knowledge base \(K\) and every Boolean conjunctive query \(q\), in the syntax and semantics below, \(D(K,q)\) halts with a bit satisfying
\[D(K,q)=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad K\models q?\]
Both \(K\) and \(q\) are input. Query atoms may use non-simple roles, including roles made transitive or affected by legal role chains. There is no bound on the size of models and no finite-model, named-witness, Horn or simple-query-role restriction. No running-time bound is requested beyond termination on every legal pair.
cards.why: A basic decidability boundary for querying expressive ontologies: the logic has decidable consistency, but unrestricted conjunctive-query entailment still lacks a general resolution.

cards.title: Conjunctive-query containment under bag semantics
cards.formal:
Does there exist one deterministic Turing machine that halts on every pair \((q_1,q_2)\) of finite conjunctive queries with the same output arity and correctly decides whether
\[
 \forall\text{ finite bag databases }D\quad
 \forall a\in U_D^r:\qquad q_1(D)(a)\le q_2(D)(a),
\]
with the unrestricted syntax and natural-number sum-product semantics defined below? Both input relations and query answers retain multiplicities.
cards.why: Bag semantics captures duplicate-sensitive query behavior, and containment is a basic correctness test for query optimization. Its unknown decidability marks a fundamental gap between simple positive query syntax and unbounded counting over finite structures. The problem also connects database theory with homomorphism inequalities and arithmetic decision problems.

cards.title: Constant-delay conjunctive-query classification
cards.formal:
Does there exist a total deterministic algorithm which, given any finite conjunctive query \(q\), decides whether all distinct answers to \(q\) can be enumerated on every finite database \(D\) with \(O_q(N)\) preprocessing time and \(O_q(1)\) worst-case delay?

Self-joins and projection are allowed. Here \(N\) is the database size defined below; the enumeration model is the specified deterministic word-RAM. The classifier has no prescribed running-time bound.
cards.why: Database queries can have far more answers than input tuples. Constant delay after linear preprocessing gives both output-sensitive total time and a bounded wait for each answer. A complete effective classification would identify exactly which query patterns allow this guarantee, including repeated uses of the same relation.

cards.title: Dichotomy for consistent query answering under primary keys
cards.formal:
For every fixed finite relational schema with one designated nonempty primary key for each relation, and every fixed Boolean conjunctive query \(q\) over that schema, is the language \(\operatorname{CERTAINTY}(q)\) either in deterministic polynomial time or coNP-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions?

The input to this language is an explicitly represented finite database \(D\), possibly violating its keys. It is accepted exactly when \(q\) is true in every inclusion-maximal subdatabase of \(D\) that satisfies the keys. Repeated occurrences of a relation in \(q\), called self-joins, are allowed.
cards.why: Conflicting primary-key records are routine in integrated data. This question asks whether every fixed database query is either efficiently answerable with certainty across all repairs or computationally complete for a standard hard class.

cards.title: Dichotomy for deletion resilience of relational queries
cards.formal:
For every fixed finite relational schema and every fixed Boolean union of conjunctive queries \(q\), is \(\operatorname{RES}(q)\) either in deterministic polynomial time or NP-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions?

An input consists of a finite bag database \(D\) and a nonnegative integer \(k\). It belongs to \(\operatorname{RES}(q)\) if at most \(k\) individual tuple occurrences can be deleted so that \(q\) becomes false. All occurrences may be deleted, and all relation arities and self-joins are allowed.
cards.why: Resilience measures how fragile a database answer is under deletion of records. A complete complexity dichotomy would identify whether all such fixed-query deletion problems have a tractable or NP-complete behavior, including repeated tables and higher-arity relations.

cards.title: Computability of entropic query-size bounds
cards.formal:
Is the logarithmic entropic query-size bound uniformly computable? More precisely, does a single deterministic Turing machine, given any finite set of degree constraints \(\mathcal D=\{(X_i,Y_i,b_i):1\leq i\leq k\}\) on \([n]\) with nonnegative rational logarithmic budgets, and any \(m\in\mathbb N\), halt and output either \(+\infty\) when \(E(\mathcal D)=+\infty\), or a rational \(q\) satisfying \(|q-E(\mathcal D)|\leq 2^{-m}\) when
\[E(\mathcal D)=\sup\{h([n]):h\in\overline{\Gamma_n^*},\ h(Y_i)-h(X_i)\leq b_i\ (1\leq i\leq k)\}<+\infty?\]
Here \(\overline{\Gamma_n^*}\) is the closure of the discrete entropy region defined below; \(n\) is part of the input.
cards.why: The strongest information-theoretic query estimates are useful algorithmically only if their numerical values can be obtained effectively. A computability theorem would make this extremal use of arbitrary discrete distributions accessible to uniform algorithms; a noncomputability theorem would identify a fundamental limit on exact information-theoretic database estimation, even with unlimited running time.

cards.title: BDD/FC conjecture
cards.formal: Is every finite set \(R\) of existential tuple-generating dependencies with bounded derivation depth finitely controllable? Use the precise query-rewriting definition of bounded derivation depth below. The required conclusion is that for every finite database \(I\) and every Boolean conjunctive query \(q\), \[(I,R)\models q\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad(I,R)\models_{\mathrm{fin}}q.\] The left side quantifies over all models extending \(I\) and satisfying \(R\); the right side quantifies only over finite such models. The conjecture quantifies over every finite relational signature of arbitrary finite arities, and permits conjunctions of several atoms in rule heads.
cards.why: Bounded derivation depth permits queries under existential rules to be answered through finite positive rewritings on the original database. Finite controllability asks whether considering only finite possible worlds changes those answers. Connecting the two would clarify when this useful query-processing property also supports finite-model semantics, across arbitrary relational arities.

cards.title: Decidability of query answering with linear rules and transitivity
cards.formal:
Is there one algorithm that, given a finite relational database \(D\), a finite set \(\Sigma\) of single-head linear existential rules and binary transitivity assertions, and a Boolean conjunctive query \(q\), decides whether \(D\cup\Sigma\models q\)?

Entailment ranges over all models, including infinite ones. The relation arities, rule set and query are part of the input; there is no bound on arity and no safety restriction on the linear rules.
cards.why: Incomplete databases often combine rules that imply missing records with transitive relations such as reachability. The question asks whether that combination still allows a general terminating procedure for answering multi-atom queries.

cards.title: Linear-round convergence over stable semirings
cards.formal:
Does there exist a universal real constant \(C\ge1\) such that, for every integer \(p\ge0\), integer \(n\ge1\), commutative \(p\)-stable semiring \(S\), and polynomial map \(F:S^n\to S^n\) with coefficients in \(S\), the synchronous sequence
\[
x^{(0)}=(0,\ldots,0),\qquad x^{(t+1)}=F(x^{(t)})
\]
satisfies \(x^{(t+1)}=x^{(t)}\) for some integer \(0\le t\le C(p+1)n\)? The constant must be independent of the semiring, coefficients, number of monomials and polynomial degrees. Only the number of rounds is measured.
cards.why: The problem asks whether local algebraic stability imposes a sharp global limit on recursive evaluation. A universal linear bound would explain why a broad class of annotated recursive computations needs only an output-scale number of rounds, while a separation would expose a fundamental cost of nonlinear interactions.

cards.title: Uniform reliability of homomorphism-closed queries
cards.formal: Is the following dichotomy true? For every finite relational signature \(\sigma\) of arbitrary fixed finite arities and every homomorphism-closed Boolean query \(Q\) on finite \(\sigma\)-instances, at least one of the following holds: (i) \(Q\) is equivalent on all finite instances to a finite union of conjunctive queries \(U\) for which exact tuple-independent probabilistic query evaluation \(\mathrm{PQE}(U)\) is computable in deterministic polynomial time; (ii) the function \(\mathrm{UR}_Q(I)=|\{J\subseteq I:Q(J)=1\}|\) is \(\#\mathrm P\)-hard under polynomial-time Turing reductions. This is the semantic formulation below of the source's proposed safe-UCQ versus hardness dichotomy; it retains arbitrary homomorphism-closed \(Q\), not only queries expressed by a UCQ.
cards.why: A complete dichotomy would identify exactly when independently retaining each database fact with probability one half permits tractable exact query evaluation. It would connect finite logical descriptions and recursive query behavior to the complexity of counting possible databases, extending the established weighted-query theory to a basic unweighted model.

cards.title: Entropic width versus submodular width
cards.formal:
Does there exist a finite hypergraph \(H=(V,E)\), with \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \(n\ge1\), nonempty hyperedges and \(\bigcup E=V\), such that
\[
\operatorname{entw}(H)<\operatorname{subw}(H)?
\]
For a set function \(h:2^V\to\mathbb R\), define
\[
w_H(h)=\min_{(T,\chi)\in\operatorname{TD}(H)}\ \max_{t\in V(T)}h(\chi(t)),\qquad
\mathcal E_H=\{h:h(e)\le1\text{ for all }e\in E\}.
\]
The two widths are
\[
\operatorname{entw}(H)=\max_{h\in\overline{\Gamma_n^*}\cap\mathcal E_H}w_H(h),\qquad
\operatorname{subw}(H)=\max_{h\in\Gamma_n\cap\mathcal E_H}w_H(h),
\]
where \(\Gamma_n\) is the cone of normalized monotone submodular functions and \(\overline{\Gamma_n^*}\) is the closure of finite-alphabet entropy vectors, defined below. Any strictly positive gap suffices; no minimum gap such as \(1/100\) is prescribed.
cards.why: Submodular width optimizes over a relaxation of all possible joint information profiles. Entropic width admits only limits of realizable profiles. Whether this relaxation changes the best decomposition cost is a structural question linking information inequalities to query complexity.

cards.title: Fractional-edge-cover load for general-message parallel joins
cards.formal:
For every fixed finite natural-join schema \(Q\), is there a randomized MPC algorithm computing its full join in a constant number of communication rounds with load
\[
\widetilde O_Q\!\left(\frac{m}{p^{1/\rho(Q)}}\right)
\]
on every database instance of total input size \(m\), using \(p\) machines with \(2\le p\) and \(p^3\le m\)?

Precisely, for every \(Q\) and every fixed word-size multiplier \(a\ge1\), must there exist one algorithm \(A_{Q,a}\), constants \(C_{Q,a}>0\), and integers \(R_{Q,a},d_{Q,a}\ge1\), such that it halts within \(R_{Q,a}\) rounds on every execution and, for each valid instance and initial distribution, with probability at least \(1-p^{-2}\) both outputs exactly the join and has load at most
\[
C_{Q,a}\frac{m}{p^{1/\rho(Q)}}
       \bigl(\log_2(m+2)\bigr)^{d_{Q,a}}?
\]
Messages may encode arbitrary information; they are not restricted to complete input tuples. This broader model is the explicit user choice.
cards.why: Parallel join processing must distribute related information so that machines can produce all compatible output tuples. The fractional edge-cover number captures a fundamental structural feature of the query. Whether it still suffices for communication with unrestricted messages separates a general information limit from limitations of algorithms that move database rows intact.

cards.title: Complexity of polymatroid query-size bounds
cards.formal:
Is computing the general polymatroid query-size bound NP-hard? Use the following exact comparison formulation and deterministic polynomial-time Turing reductions. Given \(n\geq1\), a finite list \(\mathcal D=\{(X_i,Y_i,b_i):1\leq i\leq k\}\) of rational logarithmic degree constraints and a rational threshold \(t\), let
\[P(\mathcal D)=\sup\{h([n]):h\in\Gamma_n,\ h(Y_i)-h(X_i)\leq b_i\text{ for all }i\},\]
where \(\Gamma_n\) is the cone of normalized monotone submodular set functions on \([n]\). Is the language
\[\mathrm{POLYBOUND}=\{\langle n,\mathcal D,t\rangle:P(\mathcal D)\geq t\}\]
NP-hard under the reduction convention below, when dimension and all constraints are part of the input?
cards.why: A general polynomial-time procedure would make a broad information-theoretic relaxation available for query planning without enumerating exponentially many subset entropies. A hardness theorem would explain why the known algorithms require special dependency structure. Determining which conclusion is justified separates a useful compact optimization method from a bound whose direct formulation is mainly an existential certificate.

cards.title: Tractable probability without polynomial-size deterministic decomposable lineage
cards.formal:
Does there exist a finite relational signature \(\sigma\) and a fixed Boolean union of conjunctive queries \(q\) over \(\sigma\) with both following properties?

First, a deterministic Turing machine computes the exact probability \(\Pr[q(I_p)]\) in time polynomial in the entire binary input length, for every finite explicitly given database \(I\) and every assignment of rational inclusion probabilities \(p_t\in[0,1]\) to its facts \(t\in I\), retained independently in \(I_p\).

Second, the lineage functions have no polynomial size bound in deterministic decomposable Boolean circuits with arbitrary internal negations:
\[
\forall C,c\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\ \exists I:\quad
\operatorname{ddsize}(\operatorname{Lin}(q,I))>C\bigl(N(I)+1\bigr)^c.
\]
Here \(N(I)\) is the unweighted database encoding length and the circuit model is defined below. The query and signature are fixed before all databases and probability assignments; no unproved complexity assumption is part of the question.
cards.why: Probability evaluation can combine numerical cancellations that may not correspond to a small reusable Boolean explanation. A separation would show that efficient numerical inference is strictly more general than the existence of compact deterministic decomposable lineage.

cards.title: Does extension preservation eliminate stratified intensional negation?
cards.formal: For every finite input schema and every generic query q expressible by a safe, constant-free stratified Datalog program with disequality, suppose that q is preserved under induced extensions of finite database instances. Must q be expressible by a safe, constant-free semi-positive Datalog program with disequality over the same input schema and with the same output arity? In the source’s notation, is Str-\(Datalog(\ne ) \cap  E = Sp-Datalog(\ne )\)? Preservation under induced extensions is defined below. The inclusion from right to left is known; the question is the converse.
cards.why: Would characterize when a semantic guarantee about growing databases suffices to remove negation between recursive stages, clarifying the expressive resources needed for distributed queries.

cards.title: Unconditional constant-delay lower bound for the two-step query
cards.formal:
Is it true, without any unproved complexity assumption, that the fixed query
\[
q_R=\{(x,y)\in[n]^2:\exists z\in[n],\ (x,z)\in R\ \land\ (z,y)\in R\}
\]
has no uniform deterministic constant-delay enumeration algorithm after linear preprocessing in the model below? Equivalently, is there no pair of finite programs \((P,E)\) and no integers \(B,c,d,s\ge1\), with \(B\ge2\), such that for every explicitly listed binary relation \(R\subseteq[n]^2\), \(P\) uses at most \(cN\) word-RAM instructions and \(E\) then outputs exactly \(q_R\), without repetition, with worst-case delay at most \(d\) and at most \(s\) additional working words? Here \(N=n+|R|+1\) and words have \(B\lceil\log_2(N+2)\rceil\) bits.
cards.why: Checking a particular two-edge walk is easy, but listing all endpoint pairs must suppress potentially many witnesses for the same output. The target asks for an unconditional obstruction to combining that task with linear preparation and constant time between outputs.

cards.title: Sunflower conjecture
cards.formal:
For every integer \(r\ge3\), does there exist a real constant \(C_r\ge1\) such that, for every integer \(k\ge1\), every finite set \(X\), and every family \(\mathcal F\subseteq\{S\subseteq X:|S|=k\}\),
\[
|\mathcal F|>C_r^k\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\exists\text{ distinct }S_1,\ldots,S_r\in\mathcal F\ \exists K\subseteq X\ \forall i\ne j:\ S_i\cap S_j=K?
\]
The constant may depend on \(r\) but not on the set size \(k\), the ground set or the family. The conclusion is the existence of an ordinary \(r\)-sunflower.
cards.why: A general combinatorial principle with established applications to computational lower bounds and parameterized reductions.

cards.title: \(1/3\)–\(2/3\) conjecture
cards.formal: For every integer \(n\ge 2\) and every partial order \(\mathrm{P}=([n],\le _{\mathrm{P}})\) that is not a total order, do there exist incomparable elements \(x,y\in [n]\) such that \(e(\mathrm{P})/3\le e_{\mathrm{P}}(x,y)\le 2e(\mathrm{P})/3\)?
cards.why: Asks for the sharp universal quality of a comparison when sorting with partial information. It connects uncertainty among compatible rankings to an extremal property of every finite partial order.

cards.title: Frankl's union-closed sets conjecture
cards.formal: For every finite set \(U\) and every family \(\mathcal F\subseteq 2^U\) containing a nonempty member and closed under union, is there an element \(u\in U\) belonging to at least \(|\mathcal F|/2\) members of \(\mathcal F\)?
cards.why: A basic closure principle for set systems, connected to information inequalities through entropy methods.

cards.title: Hadamard matrices of every order divisible by four
cards.formal: For every positive integer \(n\), does there exist a \(4n\)-by-\(4n\) matrix \(H\) whose entries belong to \(\{-1,1\}\) and satisfy \(HH^{\mathsf T}=4nI_{4n}\)?
cards.why: Orthogonal sign patterns are basic objects in coding, signal design and combinatorial constructions.

cards.title: Rota's basis conjecture for matroids
cards.formal: For every integer \(n\ge1\), every finite matroid of rank n, and every n bases \(B_1,\ldots,B_n\), can the elements in each B_i be ordered as \(b_{i,1},\ldots,b_{i,n}\) so that, for every j, the set \(\{b_{1,j},\ldots,b_{n,j}\}\) is also a basis?
cards.why: A universal exchange principle for independence systems underlying greedy algorithms and matroid optimization.

cards.title: Shannon capacity of \(C_{7}\)
cards.formal: Determine the zero-error Shannon capacity \[\Theta(C_7)=\sup_{t\ge1}\alpha(C_7^{\boxtimes t})^{1/t}\] of the seven-cycle, in distinguishable symbols per channel use, with the graph power defined below.
cards.why: The smallest odd-cycle zero-error capacity left unresolved after Lovasz's pentagon theorem.

cards.title: Asymptotic exponent of the largest cap set
cards.formal:
Determine, to additive accuracy \(0.01\), the exponent
\[\gamma=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log_3 M(n)}{n},\]
where \(M(n)\) is the largest size of a subset \(A\subseteq\mathbb F_3^n\) such that \(x+y+z=0\) for \(x,y,z\in A\) implies \(x=y=z\).
cards.why: This asks for the quantitative limit of the polynomial method in additive combinatorics, a source of techniques for algorithms and lower bounds.

cards.title: Feige's small-deviation conjecture
cards.formal:
For every positive integer n and independent nonnegative real random variables \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) with \(\mathbb E X_i\le1\), is
\[\mathbb P\!\left[\sum_{i=1}^n X_i<\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbb E X_i+1\right]\ge e^{-1}?\]
cards.why: A sharp probability bound for sums with minimal hypotheses, arising in randomized algorithms and probabilistic combinatorics.

cards.title: Nivat's conjecture on rectangular pattern complexity
cards.formal: Let \(A\) be a finite nonempty alphabet and \(c:\mathbb Z^2\to A\) a configuration. If for some positive integers m,n the number \(P_c(m,n)\) of distinct m-by-n rectangular patterns occurring in c is at most mn, must c have a nonzero global period?
cards.why: This connects the information in local pictures to global regularity, extending a central theorem about words to two-dimensional symbolic systems.

cards.title: Lonely runner conjecture
cards.formal:
For every integer \(k\ge1\) and all distinct positive integers \(v_1,\ldots,v_k\), does there exist a real number \(t\ge0\) such that
\[\min_{1\le i\le k}\|tv_i\|_{\mathbb R/\mathbb Z}\ge\frac1{k+1}?\]
cards.why: A simultaneous separation question linking number theory, discrete geometry and graph coloring.

cards.title: Erdős's distinct subset sums conjecture
cards.formal: Does there exist an absolute real constant \(c>0\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge1\) and every increasing sequence of positive integers \(a_1<\cdots<a_n\) with all \(2^n\) subset sums distinct, one has \(a_n\ge c\,2^n\)?
cards.why: How economically can binary choices be encoded by adding integer weights? This is an extremal counterpart of subset-sum encoding.

cards.title: Period-104 highway conjecture for Langton's ant
cards.formal: Does every finite initial set of black cells in the standard two-color Langton ant process eventually produce a period-104 diagonal highway? Precisely, do there always exist an integer \(T\ge0\) and \(v\in\{(-2,-2),(-2,2),(2,-2),(2,2)\}\) such that for every \(t\ge T\), the ant's position and direction satisfy \(p_{t+104}=p_t+v\) and \(d_{t+104}=d_t\)?
cards.why: A concrete prediction problem for a tiny computational dynamical system: does every finite perturbation eventually organize into a repeating drifting walk?
